Note: You may need to press ENTER to turn on Forms mode if it did not automatically activate.</p></li> <li><p>Press TAB to move to the menu listing the different settings categories.</p></li> <li><p>Press DOWN ARROW to move to Search engine and press ENTER.</p></li> <li><p>Press TAB to move to the combo box that lists all of the search engines that can be used in the address bar and use the ARROW keys to select a different search engine.</p></li> <li><p>Press CTRL+F4 to close the Settings page and your changes are automatically saved. <a href="javascript:unhide('ChangeFirefox');">Change the Default Search Engine in Firefox</a></p></li> </ul> <h6 id="change-the-default-search-engine-in-firefox">Change the Default Search Engine in Firefox</h6> <ul> <li><p>Press ALT+T to open the Tools menu and press S to open the Settings page.</p></li> <li><p>Press SHIFT+TAB to move to the list of categories. Note: You may need to press ENTER to turn on Forms mode if it did not automatically activate.</p></li> <li><p>Press DOWN ARROW to select Search and press ESC to turn off Forms mode.</p></li> <li><p>Press H to move to the Default Search Engine heading.</p></li> <li><p>Press C to move to the combo box that lists all of the search engines that can be used in the address bar. Press ENTER to turn on Forms mode and use the ARROW keys to select a different search engine.</p></li> <li><p>Press CTRL+F4 to close the Settings page and your changes are automatically saved.</p></li> </ul> <h5 id="going-beyond-the-search-engine-results-page">Going Beyond the Search Engine Results Page</h5> <p>OK, so what happens when you choose one of the links you find on a search engine page? What strategies do you use to find the information you were initially searching for on the resulting page?</p> <p>ANSWER: All of the strategies you learned in this series of Surf’s Up lessons, including:</p> <ul> <li>Use N to jump past a series of links to move to the next block of text that has at least 25 characters without a link.</li> <li>Use the list of links (INSERT+F7) to look for links that begin with specific words.</li> <li>Use the list of headings (INSERT+F6) to look for structure in the headings on a page.</li> <li>Use the JAWS Find to search for words or phrases on a web page.</li> <li>Look for regions.</li> <li>Use the JAWS Quick Settings dialog box (INSERT+V) to change things as needed such as: <ul> <li>Stop page refreshes</li> <li>Search for <title> attributes, acronyms, abbreviations, and more.</li> </ul></li> <li>Use the Custom Label feature of JAWS to label unlabeled links or unlabeled form fields on pages that you visit often.</li> </ul> <h3 id="using-the-jaws-find-command">Using the JAWS Find Command</h3> <h4 id="using-the-jaws-find-command-1">Using the JAWS Find Command</h4> <p>You can use the JAWS Find command to find specific words or phrases on a Web page. This works on long Web pages even if that information is not currently in view on the screen. The Find command searches from the location of the cursor to the bottom of the document by default, so it is best to start at the top of the page by pressing CTRL+HOME.</p> <ul> <li><p>Open the sample page <a href="JimsCafe.htm">Jim’s Cafe at Innisport</a> and press CTRL+HOME to go to the top of the page.</p></li> <li><p>Press CTRL+F to open the JAWS Find dialog box. Focus is in an edit box where you can type a search keyword or phrase. You can press the TAB key to move from one control to another within the dialog box. The different controls include:</p> <ul> <li>Find what edit box. Press the DOWN or UP arrow keys to move to previously searched for items. You can also open a list of the items in the combo box by pressing ALT+DOWN ARROW and then use first letter navigation to move to an item more quickly. It contains a history of the last 20 entries searched for.</li> <li>Context Specific History check box. This check box controls whether or not the Find history is context specific for the current site. The check box is selected by default.</li> <li>Maintain history of recent finds. This check box controls whether or not the Find What combo box maintains a history of items searched for. The default is checked.</li> <li>Direction radio buttons, the default is to search forward</li> <li>Ignore case checkbox, the default is checked, and</li> <li>Find, Delete, Clear Find History, and Cancel buttons. The default is the Find button. NOTE: The JAWS find is the default find in Internet browsers where the virtual cursor is supported. If you want to use the application’s native find dialog box, first press INSERT+3 on the numbers row (JAWS pass through keystroke), followed by the keystroke CTRL+F.</li> </ul></li> <li><p>Let’s say you heard that Jim’s Cafe offers a really great club sandwich. Do the following to search to see if that is listed on this page. Type the words “club sandwich” and press ENTER. If you started at the top of the page, the words “club sandwich” are not visible on the screen. They are further down on the page. JAWS moves to the phrase and reads the line where the search phrase is found.</p></li> <li><p>Use the JAWS Say Word command (INSERT+NUMPAD 5). You should hear the word “club” spoken.</p></li> <li><p>Use the JAWS Next Word command (INSERT+RIGHT ARROW). You should hear JAWS say, “sandwich.” JAWS moved you to the phrase right at the beginning of the word “club.”</p></li> <li><p>Press CTRL+HOME to move back to the top of the page.</p></li> <li><p>Open the JAWS Find dialog box again by pressing CTRL+F and search for the word “town.” You hear that the words around the word you searched for are “sleepy town of Innisport.”</p></li> <li><p>Press the keystroke to repeat the Find command (F3). You hear that the words around your search word now are “in downtown Innisport.” Notice that your search word is actually part of a larger word in this instance.</p></li> <li><p>Press F3 again and listen to the text you find.</p></li> <li><p>Continue pressing F3 until you get a message that says, “wrapping to top,” which indicates JAWS reached the last instance of the word “town” on this particular Web page and continued the search back at the top of the page again. JAWS also wraps when searching backward from the top of the page using SHIFT+F3. When searching for words or phrases with JAWS, the important keystrokes to remember are:</p></li> <li><p>CTRL+F to open the JAWS Find dialog box.</p></li> <li><p>F3 to repeat the search in the forward direction.</p></li> <li><p>SHIFT+F3 to repeat the search in the backward direction. NOTE: The JAWS find dialog box is different from the regular find dialog box in other programs. When you are in programs that have their own find dialog box you can still choose the JAWS find command as an alternative if you wish to. In those instances, use the JAWS keystroke INSERT+CTRL+F.</p></li> </ul> <p>Continue to experiment with this handy feature of JAWS. You will find this a very useful way of searching Web pages for specific information.</p> <h3 id="vispero-software-solutions">Vispero Software Solutions</h3> <h4 id="vispero-software-solutions-1">Vispero Software Solutions</h4> <p>Product: JAWS for Windows</p> <p>Description: The most popular screen reader worldwide, JAWS® screen reading software works with your computer to provide access to today’s software applications and the Internet. With its internal software speech synthesizer and the computer’s sound card, information from the screen is read aloud, providing technology to access a wide variety of information, education and job related applications. JAWS also outputs to refreshable braille displays, providing unmatched braille support of any screen reader on the market. Free Basic Training is included in full text and audio format DAISY books.</p> <p>Product: Fusion</p> <p>Description: Fusion provides the best of both worlds � ZoomText®, with its screen magnification and visual enhancements for screen viewing ease, coupled with the power and speed of JAWS® for screen reading functionality. A single installer and one license gives you access to both ZoomText and JAWS individually, or together when run as the combined solution � Fusion.</p> <p>Product: ZoomText Screen Magnification</p> <p>Description: ZoomText® screen magnification software combines great magnification features with true low vision screen reading when purchased with the speech option. It gives you the ability to choose the information you want read from the screen as you navigate your applications. ZoomText is easy to use with its talking large print installation, new user interface and hot keys that avoid conflicts with Windows and popular software applications.</p> <p>Product: OpenBook</p> <p>Description: OpenBook® scanning and reading software allows you to convert printed documents or graphic based text into an electronic text format using accurate optical character recognition and quality speech. The many powerful low vision tools of OpenBook allow you to customize how the document appears on your screen, while other features provide portability.</p> <p>For more information on these and other great products, please visit www.Vispero.com.</p> <h3 id="web-page-elements">Web Page Elements</h3> <h4 id="web-page-elements-1">Web Page Elements</h4> <p>Elements are used to create the structure of a web page and are used to present information in various ways. JAWS interacts with these elements to provide the information you need to access the page contents. Some of the most common web page elements you will encounter include:</p> <ul> <li>Links</li> <li>Paragraphs</li> <li>Headings</li> <li>Numbered and bulleted lists</li> <li>Tables</li> <li>Regions</li> <li>Images</li> <li>Form controls including radio buttons, edit fields, check boxes, combo boxes, list boxes, and buttons JAWS provides easy to use and remember commands called Navigation Quick Keys for quickly moving to various elements on a web page. Press a single letter on your keyboard and move right to an item. For example, you can press T for tables, F for form controls, V for visited links, H for headings, and so on. Add SHIFT to any navigation quick key to move to the previous element of that type.</li> </ul> <p>For instance, a sighted user can visually scan through headings on a page until they find the one they want and then focus in on the text in that section. Similarly, using JAWS, you can press H to quickly move through all of the headings on a page until you locate the one you want and then start reading with the ARROW keys.</p> <h5 id="viewing-lists-of-elements">Viewing Lists of Elements</h5> <p>JAWS can look at a web page and compile lists of paragraphs, links, headings, form fields, and other elements so you can quickly find what you need and move to information. Press INSERT+F3 to open the Virtual HTML Features dialog box. This dialog box allows you to choose from a variety of lists containing information about different types of elements on the current page. Select an item and press ENTER to view a list of all those elements.</p> <p>You can also use the following commands to quickly display lists of the following important HTML elements:</p> <ul> <li>Form Fields - Press INSERT+F5</li> <li>Headings - Press INSERT+F6</li> <li>Links - Press INSERT+F7 In addition, if you hold down CTRL+INSERT and press one of several Navigation Quick Keys, JAWS displays a list of those elements on the current page. For example, to display a list of check boxes on the current page, press CTRL+INSERT+X.</li> </ul> <p>Use the UP and DOWN ARROW keys to move through the lists and select items. Alternatively, press the first letter of an item to move right to it. Press ENTER to move to the selected item’s location on the page.</p> <h3 id="the-web-track-sample-form">The Web Track Sample Form</h3> <h4 id="the-web-track-sample-form-1">The Web Track Sample Form</h4> <p>Online Customer Tracking System</p> <h2 id="training-and-certification">Training and certification</h2> <h3 id="certification-training-and-certification">Certification (Training and certification)</h3> <h4 id="certification">Certification</h4> <p>The JAWS® and ZoomText® Certification programs are online knowledge-based exams for JAWS Screen Reader and ZoomText Magnifier/Reader. Each product has its own test and certification. The certification programs are designed for consultants, trainers, agency staff, and users to demonstrate proficiency in using JAWS and ZoomText software applications.</p> <p>Read the <a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/certification/certification-details/">exam details and FAQs</a> to prepare for the exams. These pages provide exam preparation resources, exam categories to focus on, cost, and frequently asked questions.</p> <p>Currently there is not a separate certification exam or program for Fusion™, but successful completion of both the JAWS and ZoomText certifications is a strong indicator of proficiency with Fusion.</p> <h5 id="list-of-certified-individuals">List of certified individuals:</h5> <ul> <li><a href="https://support.freedomscientific.com/Services/TrainingAndCertification/JAWSCertifiedIndividuals">JAWS Certified Individuals</a></li> <li><a href="https://support.freedomscientific.com/Services/TrainingAndCertification/ZoomTextCertifiedIndividuals">ZoomText Certified Individuals</a></li> </ul> <h5 id="one-exam-for-both-initial-certification-and-renewal">One Exam for Both Initial Certification and Renewal</h5> <p>There is a single exam for both the Initial Certification as well as Certification Renewals. Taking the exam is free. After successfully passing the exam, you will automatically receive a free electronic certificate of completion which can be displayed in your web browser and printed as needed. You will also have an opportunity to confirm if you would like your name included on the website of certified individuals. Inclusion on this website helps to enhance exposure of certified individuals as knowledgeable in the features and use of the JAWS screen reader and/or ZoomText Magnifier/Reader.</p> <p>If you are interested in purchasing a high-quality print copy of your Certificate for proudly displaying in your home or office (JAWS certificates also include braille), two options exist:</p> <ul> <li>Initial Certification – $49.00. For first-time certifications, a user needs to purchase the “Initial Certification.”</li> <li>Certification Renewal – $29.00. For successive certifications, a user can purchase the “Certification Renewal” at this lower cost.</li> </ul> <h5 id="exam-links">Exam Links</h5> <ul> <li><a href="http://hosted.onlinetesting.net/FreedomScientific2/login.pl/JAWSCertification">JAWS Certification Exam</a></li> <li><a href="http://hosted.onlinetesting.net/FreedomScientific2/login/ZoomText-Certification">ZoomText Certification Exam</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/certification/certification-details/">Certification Details</a></li> </ul> <h3 id="certification-program-details">Certification Program Details</h3> <p>Skip to content</p> <p>Need Support? <a href="tel:+18004444443">1(800) 444-4443</a></p> <h4 id="certification-program-details-1">Certification Program Details</h4> <p>This page contains details about the JAWS Certification Program, including topics covered, expected proficiency, cost, how the exam works, and resources for studying for the exam.</p> <p><a href="http://www.freedomscientific.com/Services/TrainingAndCertification/JAWSCertifiedIndividuals">JAWS Certified Individuals</a> who have purchased the certificate.</p> <ul> <li>Certification Program Goals</li> <li>Expected Capabilities after Successful Completion</li> <li>JAWS Exam Categories</li> <li>Cost for Certification</li> <li>Exam Resources</li> <li>Taking the Exam</li> <li>Certification Logos</li> <li>FAQs</li> </ul> <h5 id="certification-program-goals">Certification Program Goals</h5> <p>The JAWS Certification Program is an online knowledge-based exam for consultants, trainers, agency staff, and JAWS users. The purpose is to:</p> <ul> <li>Help JAWS trainers and consultants validate their understanding of the software for companies, agencies, and consumers</li> <li>Increase people’s general knowledge of JAWS software</li> <li>Expand skills and abilities into new product features</li> <li>Present a comprehensive look at all the free training resources provided online and within JAWS</li> <li>Enhance exposure for certified individuals by listing them on the Freedom Scientific website</li> </ul> <h5 id="expected-capabilities-after-successful-completion">Expected Capabilities after Successful Completion</h5> <ul> <li>Product installation and setup, including <ul> <li>Installation software for JAWS</li> <li>Training materials</li> <li>Synthesizers</li> <li>Braille displays (for JAWS)</li> </ul></li> <li>Thorough understanding of location and availability of training materials and resources, including <ul> <li>DAISY, MP3, HTML, and help files</li> <li>Archives of free webinars</li> </ul></li> <li>Product knowledge, including <ul> <li>Basic to advanced product skills</li> <li>JAWS keystrokes for both laptop and desktop layout</li> <li>How to identify and use key combinations for JAWS functions</li> </ul></li> </ul> <h6 id="jaws-exam-categories">JAWS Exam Categories</h6> <p>The JAWS certification exam covers a wide range of product knowledge. It is not limited to just using the product, but enhancing your knowledge, from installation procedures to where to look when you need to access product information. A variety of questions are drawn from the following categories:</p> <ul> <li>JAWS Features — includes in-depth questions on JAWS features and using Braille with JAWS</li> <li>New Features— includes questions on the new features in the latest JAWS version</li> <li>Headquarters — includes what is available on our web resource pages, along with questions on contacting Technical Support and basic troubleshooting</li> <li>Installation — includes all aspects of both typical and custom installation and activation of JAWS</li> <li>Training — includes questions on Freedom Scientific’s training resources, JAWS Tandem, and Terminal Services</li> <li>Keyboard Knowledge — includes questions on specific desktop and laptop keyboard commands</li> <li>HTML — includes questions on all aspects of navigating, reading, and customizing HTML pages</li> <li>Learning JAWS — includes the basics of JAWS and customizing an initial JAWS setup Do you want to share a success story involving your JAWS Certification? We would love to hear from you. Submit your comments.</li> </ul> <h5 id="cost-for-certification">Cost for Certification</h5> <p>There is no cost to study the materials and take the exam. Once you complete the exam with a passing score, you will be given the opportunity to purchase an official certificate from Freedom Scientific. The initial certification is $99 for each product, with a $39 renewal fee if you choose to update your certification later. To qualify for the $39 renewal fee, you must retake the exam and earn a passing score.</p> <p>Your purchase of a JAWS Certificate also entitles your name to be on our lists of <a href="JAWSCertifiedIndividuals">JAWS Certified Individuals</a>.</p> <h5 id="exam-resources">Exam Resources</h5> <p>The study materials are available in the current version of JAWS and on the Freedom Scientific website. If you have a current version of JAWS and a connection to the Internet, then you already have what you need to study for the exam. No additional study materials are required. The exam questions are based on guides, help topics, DAISY training materials, and web resources.</p> <p>The study time for each exam is approximately 10 hours. That time is based on listening to all basic training material and suggested DAISY books, reading the guides and websites, and studying the exact JAWS help topics. Study time will vary with your experience, and you may need to concentrate on some areas more than others. It is recommended that you take your time and become familiar with all the study materials before you take the exam.</p> <h6 id="resources-for-jaws">Resources for JAWS</h6> <p>JAWS Tandem Quick Start Guide — available from within the JAWS program window. Open the Utilities menu, open the JAWS Tandem submenu, and then open the Quick Start Guide.</p> <p>JAWS Quick Start Guide — available from within the start menu, Utilities - JAWS 20xx program group, and then open Explore the Manuals. This folder contains the JAWS Quick Start Guide.</p> <p>JAWS Basic Training Materials — the books are in DAISY format and can be reviewed using FSReader. The basic training materials are a collection of nine books. The total listening time is approximately 5 hours and 45 minutes. If your copy of JAWS is the downloaded version, you may not have the basic training materials. To download these and other training materials, visit the <a href="http://www2.freedomscientific.com/downloads/training/training-downloads.asp">Freedom Scientific Training Downloads</a> page.</p> <ul> <li>Select the DAISY books from the list.</li> <li>Select Install to begin the download. DAISY Books — the books are available to review using FSReader. FSReader can be opened from within the JAWS program window. Open the Help menu and press ENTER on the Training menu item and FSReader opens. If these books are not installed, pressing ENTER on a link in the JAWS Basic Training Table of Contents causes FSReader to download and install them automatically from the Freedom Scientific web site.</li> </ul> <p>Web Resources — available from within the JAWS program window. Open the Help menu, then open the Web Resources submenu. It is recommended that you familiarize yourself with the choices in the Web Resources submenu. Spend additional time focusing on JAWS Headquarters, Technical Support pages, Training and Certification pages, and Surfing the Internet.</p> <p>JAWS Help — JAWS Help topics are found in JAWS F1 Help. It is recommended that you become familiar with the JAWS Help topics. Open JAWS Help by pressing F1 from within the JAWS program window. To quickly find a topic, move to the Search tab, and type the topic name in the search field.</p> <h5 id="taking-the-exam">Taking the Exam</h5> <p>When you are confident that you have spent adequate time covering all study materials, it is time to take the exam. Be prepared to set aside 60 minutes without interruptions to take the exam. Please note — you will not be able to stop the clock on the exam once you begin.</p> <p>A web page link will take you to the exam log-on page.</p> <p>You must complete your full name and email address in the edit fields, select your country, and then press TAB to move to the Start Test button. Your exam page will load, followed by a dialog notifying you that you have 60 minutes to complete your exam. Press the OK button and begin.</p> <h6 id="exam-navigation">Exam Navigation</h6> <p>The exam is a web page, so standard JAWS navigation keys in HTML documents apply. For JAWS, pressing P to move by paragraph moves you between the questions and possible answers.</p> <h6 id="during-the-exam">During the Exam</h6> <p>At the mid-point of the exam, a dialog will appear to alert you that you are at the halfway point in the exam. You have 30 more minutes from that point. Press the OK button and continue your exam.</p> <p>The time remaining may show on the status bar in Internet Explorer, depending on your security settings. You can read this by pressing INSERT+PAGE DOWN at any time during the exam.</p> <p>If you are using JAWS to take the exam, you can also use the virtual cursor to read the time even if it is not visible on the status bar. Do this by pressing CTRL+END to move to the bottom of the exam page. Before you move from where you are, you can set a temporary PlaceMarker on the question to easily move back to your spot in the exam. Press CTRL+WINDOWS Key+K to set the temporary PlaceMarker or move it to another spot later in the exam. Press K to move back to your spot after checking the time.</p> <p>At the end of each question a Resource for that exam question will be noted. It will appear like this: (Resource: JAWS Help). This is a reference for you.</p> <h6 id="submitting-your-exam">Submitting Your Exam</h6> <p>When you complete the test, press the Submit Exam Now button at the end of the web page. Please note — if you do not press the Submit Exam Now button, your exam results will not be recorded. When the Submit Exam Now button is pressed and there are unanswered questions, the exam displays the message, “You have left some questions unanswered. Press OK to submit your test now or Cancel to move to the next unanswered question.” Choose the Cancel button to move to the first unanswered question and continue from there. If you choose the Submit Exam Now button again and there are other unanswered questions, you get a chance to move to the next unanswered question. When you move to the unanswered question, focus is on the first control, i.e., radio button or check box, so just press UP ARROW to read the question.</p> <p>If you do not finish the exam in the allotted time, a dialog appears at the end of 60 minutes and tells you your time is up. Press OK on the dialog button. Your exam will be submitted automatically.</p> <p>When you submit your exam, the exam page closes and you are taken to another web page with your results. From there, you can read your final score percentage and review your scores in each of the different categories. For passing scores you may choose the link in the results page to go directly to the online store to purchase your Certificate. For non-passing scores you may choose the link in the results page to go back to the Certification page for further review.</p> <h5 id="certification-logo-and-inclusion-on-web-site">Certification Logo and Inclusion on Web Site</h5> <p>There is now one exam for both the initial Certification as well as Certification Renewals. Taking the exam is free. After successfully passing the exam and purchasing into the Certification Program, the certified individual receives an official Certificate from Freedom Scientific, and his/her name is included on the website of JAWS Certified Individuals. Inclusion on this website helps to enhance exposure of certified individuals as knowledgeable in the features and use of the JAWS screen reader. If you have not yet taken and passed the exam, visit the Certification information page for full details. Two options exist when making a purchase:</p> <ul> <li>Initial Certification - For first-time certifications, a user needs to purchase the “Initial Certification.”</li> <li>Certification Renewal - For successive certifications, a user can purchase the “Certification Renewal” at a lower cost. NOTE: Users who purchase the Certification Program will be validated to ensure they successfully completed the exam. Only individuals that have previously purchased the Initial Certification are eligible to purchase the Renewal Certification.</li> </ul> <p>When you pass the Certification exam and purchase an official JAWS Certificate, you are entitled to be listed on our Certified Individuals page. Additionally, you are granted the right to use the new JAWS Certification Logo in your correspondence, email signature, or website.</p> <h5 id="faqs">FAQs</h5> <h6 id="what-if-i-accidentally-close-my-browser-while-taking-the-exam">What if I accidentally close my browser while taking the exam?</h6> <p>If your Internet browser closes, or if you have an equipment failure that interrupts your timed exam session, the portion of the exam you took will not be saved. You will have to start the exam again from the beginning.</p> <h6 id="is-it-okay-to-guess-if-i-am-not-sure-of-an-answer">Is it okay to guess if I am not sure of an answer?</h6> <p>Yes. If you do not record an answer for an exam question, then that question will be marked incorrect. If you are not sure, you may try eliminating the choices that you know are wrong. You are then left with choices that could be correct. From the remaining choices, select the choice that you think is the best answer.</p> <h6 id="what-if-i-am-in-the-middle-of-answering-a-question-and-the-60-minutes-are-up-can-i-finish-the-question-i-was-working-on">What if I am in the middle of answering a question and the 60 minutes are up, can I finish the question I was working on?</h6> <p>No. When the 60 minutes have elapsed, the focus shifts from the exam question you were working on to a dialog telling you your time is up. You will not be able to go back and finish. Please note - make sure you follow the instructions from that point so that your exam results will be saved.</p> <h6 id="do-i-get-a-reminder-of-how-much-time-has-elapsed">Do I get a reminder of how much time has elapsed?</h6> <p>At the halfway point, a dialog will appear letting you know that you have 30 minutes remaining in your exam. The time remaining may show on the status bar in Internet Explorer, depending on your security settings. You can read this by pressing INSERT+PAGE DOWN at any time during the exam.</p> <h6 id="are-there-any-short-answer-or-essay-questions">Are there any short answer or essay questions?</h6> <p>No. Exam questions are formatted as multiple choices, true or false, and check all that apply.</p> <h6 id="can-i-go-back-and-change-my-answers">Can I go back and change my answers?</h6> <p>During the 60 minutes you can go back and change or review your answers. It is recommended that you go back and review your exam if you finish before the time expires, to ensure that you are satisfied with the choices you made.</p> <h6 id="how-do-i-view-my-results">How do I view my results?</h6> <p>Your results are available as soon as you submit your exam. After you submit your results, a web page opens with the results page. You will be given an overall score and shown how you scored in each of the categories.</p> <h6 id="how-do-i-submit-my-exam">How do I submit my exam?</h6> <p>When you are ready to submit your exam, you must press the Submit button at the end of the exam web page. Please note - if you do not press the Submit button, your exam results will not be saved.</p> <h6 id="at-the-end-of-each-exam-question-there-is-a-resource.-what-does-that-mean">At the end of each exam question there is a resource. What does that mean?</h6> <p>The resource tells you which study materials that exam question was taken from. For example, a resource could be listed like this: (Resource: JAWS Help). This reference tells you that the exam question was taken from one of the JAWS F1 Help topics.</p> <h6 id="the-exam-is-85-questions-but-my-overall-score-showed-that-i-had-118-correct-out-of-147.-why-is-the-number-higher-than-85">The exam is 85 questions, but my overall score showed that I had 118 correct out of 147. Why is the number higher than 85?</h6> <p>There are 85 questions. The questions are a random selection of multiple choices, true or false, or check all that apply. The “check all that apply” questions are worth more points. Each correct check box is a point. For example, assume you had one “check all that apply” question in your exam and that question had five check boxes. That exam would be scored out of 89 not 85. Note that the exam will have more than one “check all that apply” question.</p> <h6 id="how-many-times-can-i-take-the-exam">How many times can I take the exam?</h6> <p>You may take the exam as many times as you wish.</p> <h6 id="does-a-certification-mean-i-can-train-the-product">Does a Certification mean I can train the product?</h6> <p>NO, the JAWS Certification does not mean you are capable of training the product. The certification validates your expertise and knowledge of JAWS, but does not in any way confirm your ability to teach the software to other individuals.</p> <h3 id="digital-accessibility-that-grows-with-your-organization">Digital Accessibility that grows with your organization</h3> <h4 id="digital-accessibility-that-grows-with-your-organization-1">Digital Accessibility that grows with your organization</h4> <p>Speak with an expert</p> <p>Find the right starting point</p> <p>Digital accessibility shouldn’t be an afterthought. Whether you need a quick VPAT for a procurement deadline or a complete overhaul of your design workflow, Vispero handles the heavy lifting. We don’t just audit your site and leave—our team provides the training, long-term governance, and consulting needed to make accessibility a natural part of your daily development cycle. Let’s build digital experiences that work for everyone.</p> <h5 id="find-the-right-starting-point">Find the right starting point​​</h5> <h6 id="every-accessibility-journey-starts-somewhere">Every accessibility journey starts somewhere</h6> <p>Organizations rarely begin with a fully developed accessibility program. Most start with an immediate need: a digital accessibility audit, VPAT, accessibility consulting, remediation guidance, or a compliance requirement. A procurement team requests a VPAT. A website redesign is underway. A customer reports an accessibility barrier. Leadership wants to better understand accessibility risk before launching a new digital experience. Whatever brings your organization to accessibility, it’s a valid place to begin. Choose the solution that best matches your current needs.</p> <h6 id="i-need-an-accessibility-audit">I need an accessibility audit</h6> <p>Understand your current accessibility posture through expert manual testing, assistive technology evaluation, and practical recommendations.</p> <h6 id="i-need-a-vpat">I need a VPAT</h6> <p>Support procurement with an independent VPAT 2.5 evaluation and Accessibility Conformance Report (ACR).</p> <h6 id="i-need-a-roadmap">I need a roadmap</h6> <p>Create a practical accessibility plan aligned with your business priorities, available resources, and long-term goals.</p> <h6 id="i-need-help-fixing-accessibility-issues">I need help fixing accessibility issues</h6> <p>Turn audit findings into prioritized remediation guidance that helps your team make meaningful progress.</p> <h6 id="i-need-accessibility-expertise-for-my-team">I need accessibility expertise for my team</h6> <p>Build accessibility knowledge through role-based training, expert guidance, and ongoing support.</p> <h6 id="i-need-an-ongoing-accessibility-partner">I need an ongoing accessibility partner</h6> <p>Build governance, internal capability, and sustainable accessibility practices that grow with your organization.</p> <h5 id="digital-accessibility-isnt-a-project.-its-an-organizational-capability.">Digital Accessibility isn’t a project. It’s an organizational capability.</h5> <p>Most organizations begin with a specific accessibility need. The organizations that make the greatest long-term progress do something more: they build accessibility into the way digital experiences are planned, designed, developed, tested, and maintained.</p> <p>Rather than treating accessibility as a series of isolated projects, they establish the people, processes, governance, and expertise needed to support accessibility as digital experiences, technologies, and organizational priorities evolve.</p> <p>This shift—from completing accessibility projects to building accessibility capability—helps organizations make steady progress, strengthen digital experiences, and create a foundation for long-term accessibility success.</p> <p>Learn how to build an accessibility program</p> <h5 id="how-organizations-build-accessibility-over-time">How organizations build accessibility over time</h5> <p>There is no single path to accessibility maturity, but organizations that make lasting progress typically move through the same stages as they strengthen accessibility across their digital experiences.</p> <h6 id="understand-your-current-state">Understand your current state</h6> <ul> <li>Accessibility audits</li> <li>Manual testing</li> <li>Assistive technology evaluation</li> <li>VPATs and ACRs</li> </ul> <h6 id="prioritize-what-matters-most">Prioritize what matters most</h6> <ul> <li>Understand risk</li> <li>Plan remediation</li> <li>Align resources</li> <li>Build a roadmap</li> </ul> <h6 id="build-organizational-capability">Build organizational capability</h6> <ul> <li>Governance</li> <li>Training</li> <li>Accessibility consulting</li> <li>Continuous testing</li> <li>Program support</li> </ul> <h6 id="sustain-accessibility-over-time">Sustain accessibility over time</h6> <ul> <li>Monitor progress</li> <li>Strengthen processes</li> <li>Expand accessibility knowledge</li> <li>Support evolving digital experiences</li> </ul> <h6 id="not-sure-where-to-begin">Not sure where to begin?</h6> <p>Learn how to identify the right next step for your organization. <a href="https://vispero.com/digital-accessibility-services-old/digital-accessibility-program-partner/">Explore our Digital Accessibility Program ></a></p> <h5 id="digital-accessibility-expertise-informed-real-world-assistive-technology">Digital Accessibility expertise informed real-world assistive technology</h5> <p>Meeting digital accessibility standards is important. Creating digital experiences that work for people is the ultimate goal.</p> <p>As the company behind JAWS®, the world’s leading screen reader, Vispero brings a perspective few digital accessibility consulting firms can offer. Our experts understand how people who rely on assistive technology navigate websites, applications, digital documents, kiosks, and other digital experiences every day.</p> <p>That real-world insight helps organizations move beyond technical conformance to create digital experiences that are more usable, more effective, and more inclusive. By combining assistive technology leadership with digital accessibility expertise, Vispero helps organizations build sustainable digital accessibility practices that continue to deliver value as technologies, teams, and customer expectations evolve.</p> <h6 id="assistive-technology-leadership">Assistive technology leadership</h6> <p>Digital accessibility guidance informed by decades of innovation in screen readers and other assistive technologies used every day by people who are blind or have low vision.</p> <h6 id="practical-digital-accessibility-expertise">Practical digital accessibility expertise</h6> <p>Digital accessibility audits, WCAG consulting, VPATs, remediation guidance, governance, training, and strategic planning that help organizations make measurable determine the best approach for your organization.</p> <h6 id="understanding-digital-accessibility-consulting">Understanding digital accessibility consulting</h6> <p>Learn what to look for in a WCAG consultant and how digital accessibility consulting supports long-term accessibility success.</p> <p><a href="https://vispero.com/resources/hub/digital-accessibility-and-compliance/">View all resources</a></p> <h5 id="frequently-asked-questions-1">Frequently asked questions</h5> <p>What makes Digital Accessibility Services different from one-off audits?</p> <p>Audits identify issues. Digital Accessibility Services operationalizes accessibility—assigning ownership, prioritizing work, enabling teams, verifying fixes, and governing outcomes over time.</p> <p>Can Digital Accessibility Services align with our sprint and release cadence?</p> <p>Yes. We integrate with your backlog, ceremonies, and tooling to deliver guidance where teams work.</p> <p>How does Digital Accessibility Services reduce risk for Legal and Compliance?</p> <p>We help you move toward conformance with globally recognized accessibility standards such as WCAG, Section 508, and EN 301 549, document your progress, and provide governance data executives can trust.</p> <p>Do you support assistive-technology-informed QA?</p> <p>Yes, our consulting team includes people with lived experience of disability. We can conduct AT user flow testing of key user flows or full usability testing to complement our standards-based audits.</p> <p>What if priorities shift mid-year?</p> <p>Our flexible service menu allows reallocation—e.g., from audits to training or from component reviews to regression checks.</p> <p>How are Digital Accessibility Services programs priced?</p> <p>Transparent, multi-year options that lock in value and align to budget cycles (including government funding models).</p> <p>Can we start small and scale over time?</p> <p>Yes. Digital Accessibility Services is designed to be flexible. You can start with a smaller package and increase coverage as your needs grow.</p> <p>How do you work with our internal teams?</p> <p>We embed accessibility expertise into your process, collaborate with developers and designers, and equip your teams with actionable guidance and training.</p> <p>Do we get reports and metrics?</p> <p>Yes. You receive regular reports, prioritized issue lists, and dashboards to track progress and measure impact.</p> <p>How does Vispero measure ROI?</p> <p>We report on reduced tech debt, fewer regressions, improved time-to-market, and increased customer satisfaction — giving you clear evidence of business impact.</p> <p><a href="https://vispero.com/speak-with-an-expert/?form_cta=accessibility-services">Still have questions? Contact us</a></p> <h5 id="ready-to-move-digital-accessibility-forward">Ready to move digital accessibility forward?</h5> <p>Whether you’re responding to a compliance requirement, preparing for procurement, or building a long-term accessibility program, Vispero can help you identify the right next step.</p> <p><a href="https://vispero.com/speak-with-an-expert/?form_cta=accessibility-services">Speak with a Digital Accessibility expert</a></p> <h3 id="fusion-training-training-and-certification">Fusion Training (Training and certification)</h3> <h4 id="fusion-training">Fusion Training</h4> <h5 id="getting-started-with-fusion">Getting Started with Fusion</h5> <p>Have you just installed your brand new copy of Fusion® on your Windows computer? Our Basic Training will help get you up and running with this powerful screen magnification and screen reader combination.</p> <p><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/fusion/getting-started/">Fusion Getting Started</a></p> <h5 id="fusion-videos">Fusion Videos</h5> <p>Check out and subscribe to the <a href="https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLk-npwu4WEBSwNNSROcuZZnsI-ElqsLCT">Freedom Scientific Training YouTube channel</a>. Our videos offer quick tips and hints for both new and experienced Fusion users. Watch a video to learn something new or refresh your skills.</p> <h5 id="fusion-faqs">Fusion FAQs</h5> <p>Need help accessing a particular feature of Fusion? Want to get more out of your user experience? Check out our Fusion training FAQs for answers to your burning questions.</p> <p><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/fusion/frequently-asked-questions/">Fusion FAQs</a></p> <h5 id="fusion-the-ultimate-accessibility-tool-1">Fusion, the Ultimate Accessibility Tool</h5> <p>Fusion combines two of the best vision accessibility tools available – ZoomText® Magnifier/Reader and JAWS® for Windows screen reader – into a single installation.</p> <p>Need more information on how to use the visual aspects of Fusion? We’ve compiled a trove of ZoomText resources to get you started and answer your most pressing ZoomText questions. To learn more, visit our <a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/zoomtext/">ZoomText Training Resources.</a></p> <p>From experienced JAWS users who are just venturing into a world of magnification with their residual vision, to beginners who have never used speech; our JAWS training covers it all. Once you’ve mastered the visual aspects of Fusion, visit our <a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/jaws/">JAWS Training Resources</a> to learn more and continue harnessing the power of Fusion.</p> <h5 id="fusion-hotkeys">Fusion Hotkeys</h5> <p>Fusion uses a combination of ZoomText magnification hotkeys and JAWS screen reading hotkeys to control magnification and speech.</p> <p><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/fusion/hotkeys/">Fusion Hotkeys</a></p> <p><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/">Back to Training Center﻿</a></p> <ul> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/fusion/getting-started/">Getting Started with Fusion</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/fusion/frequently-asked-questions/">Fusion FAQ</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/fusion/hotkeys/">Fusion Hotkeys</a></li> </ul> <h3 id="getting-started-with-zoomtext-training-and-certification">Getting Started with ZoomText (Training and certification)</h3> <p>Skip to content</p> <p>Need Support? <a href="tel:+18004444443">1(800) 444-4443</a></p> <h4 id="getting-started-with-zoomtext">Getting Started with ZoomText</h4> <p>The following is an overview of how ZoomText works along with instructions for setting up basic visual and voice settings.</p> <h5 id="how-zoomtext-works">How ZoomText Works</h5> <p>Most of the time ZoomText works in the background providing a magnified and enhanced view that follows all of your activity. So as you move the mouse pointer, type text, and navigate your applications, your point of interest is always in view. If you are running ZoomText Magnifier/Reader, ZoomText also echoes and narrates what you are doing, audibly confirming where you are, what you type, and more.</p> <h5 id="starting-zoomtext">Starting ZoomText</h5> <p>When you first start ZoomText, the ZoomText toolbar appears, and your screen displays in Full view mode with 2x magnification. If you are running ZoomText Magnifier/Reader, speech is also enabled. If you need to briefly silence speech, press CTRL.</p> <h5 id="the-zoomtext-toolbar">The ZoomText Toolbar</h5> <p>The ZoomText toolbar has a streamlined layout that makes it easy to learn and fast to use. You can access and operate the entire toolbar using the mouse or the keyboard.</p> <p>Using the arrow keys on your keyboard, you can navigate the ZoomText menu, toolbar tabs, toolbar controls, and button menus. When the focus is on a split button, pressing the ENTER key toggles the feature, while pressing the Down arrow expands a list of settings.</p> <p>When the focus is in the Zoom Level box (on the Magnifier tab) or the Rate box (on the Reader tab), pressing the Up and Down arrow buttons adjust the zoom and rate values and pressing the Left and Right arrow buttons move the focus to the next control. Pressing the ENTER key on the Zoom Level box will also toggle the Zoom to 1x magnification.</p> <h5 id="setting-up-screen-brightness-and-magnification">Setting Up Screen Brightness and Magnification</h5> <p>Since the primary purpose of ZoomText is to make everything larger and easier to see, the first task is to adjust the zoom level (magnification) and screen colors for comfortable viewing.</p> <h6 id="step-1.-screen-brightness">Step 1. Screen Brightness</h6> <p>Let’s start by inverting screen brightness. The idea is to reduce glare and provide contrast to make it easier to view items on the screen.</p> <ul> <li>Press and hold the CAPS LOCK key and then press C, or</li> <li>Click the top half of the Color button on the Magnifier tab</li> </ul> <h6 id="step-2.-zoom-level">Step 2. Zoom Level</h6> <p>The next step is to find a zoom level that works best for you. When you start ZoomText for the first time, it magnifies the entire screen at 2x magnification. Magnification values range from 1.0x to 60x with incremental steps between 1.0x and 5.0x.</p> <ul> <li>To zoom in, press CAPS LOCK+UP ARROW</li> <li>To zoom out, press CAPS LOCK+DOWN ARROW</li> <li>You can also use the Zoom Level box on the Magnifier tab to change zoom levels. Note: To toggle between the current magnification level and 1x magnification, press CAPS LOCK+ENTER. This is a handy way of comparing how much of the display you can actually see when it is magnified.</li> </ul> <h5 id="setting-up-voice-and-echo-features">Setting up Voice and Echo Features</h5> <p>If you are running ZoomText Magnifier/Reader, ZoomText audibly echoes and narrates everything you do, so your second task is to adjust ZoomText’s voice rate and echo settings so that ZoomText speaks program activity the way you like. This includes how the keyboard is echoed when you type, and how ZoomText’s program echo announces menus, dialog boxes and other controls as you navigate through your applications.</p> <h6 id="step-1.-voice-rate">Step 1. Voice Rate</h6> <p>The first thing to decide with speech is how fast or slow you want ZoomText to speak. Initially, you may want to decrease the voice rate until you are comfortable with both listening to ZoomText speak and following where focus is on the screen.</p> <ul> <li><p>To increase the voice rate, press CAPS LOCK+ALT+UP ARROW</p></li> <li><p>To decrease the voice rate, press CAPS LOCK+ALT+DOWN ARROW Note: If speech becomes overwhelming at first, press CTRL to momentarily stop speech</p></li> <li><p>You can also change the voice rate using the Rate box on the Reader tab</p></li> </ul> <h6 id="step-2.-echo-features">Step 2. Echo Features</h6> <p>The mouse echo and keyboard echo settings let you control how much detail is spoken as you type on the keyboard and use the mouse. Try experimenting with these features to see if it is something that you want to use now or in the future.</p> <p>ZoomText can read the word or the line of text that you point to with the mouse pointer. This is known as mouse echo.</p> <ul> <li><p>To cycle through the different mouse echo settings, press CAPS LOCK+ALT+M</p></li> <li><p>You can also select the Mouse button on the Reader tab to change mouse echo features Keyboard echo is another echo feature that lets you hear characters, words, or both as you type.</p></li> <li><p>To cycle through the different keyboard echo settings, press CAPS LOCK+ALT+K</p></li> <li><p>You can also select the Keyboard button on the Reader tab to change keyboard echo features</p></li> </ul> <h5 id="the-next-step">The Next Step</h5> <p>The information provided above should allow you to start working productively in all of your applications. But there are many other features and settings to be learned that will help you optimize your use of ZoomText even more. So we recommend that you invest some time in exploring the entire help system to learn more about how to use ZoomText.</p> <h3 id="jaws-and-zoomtext-certification">JAWS and ZoomText Certification</h3> <p>Skip to content</p> <p>Need Support? <a href="tel:+18004444443">1(800) 444-4443</a></p> <h4 id="jaws-and-zoomtext-certification-1">JAWS and ZoomText Certification</h4> <p>The JAWS® and ZoomText® Certification programs are online knowledge-based exams for JAWS Screen Reader and ZoomText Magnifier/Reader. Each product has its own test and certification. The certification programs are designed for consultants, trainers, agency staff, and users to demonstrate proficiency in using JAWS and ZoomText software applications.</p> <p>Read the JAWS exam details and FAQs or the <a href="https://www.zoomtext.com/lessons/certification-faqs/">ZoomText exam details and FAQs</a> to prepare for the exams. These pages provide exam preparation resources, exam categories to focus on, cost, and frequently asked questions.</p> <p>Currently there is not a separate certification exam or program for Fusion™, but successful completion of both the JAWS and ZoomText certifications is a strong indicator of proficiency with Fusion.</p> <p>List of certified individuals:</p> <ul> <li><a href="http://www.freedomscientific.com/Services/TrainingAndCertification/JAWSCertifiedIndividuals">JAWS Certified Individuals</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.zoomtext.com/lessons/zoomtext-certified-individuals/">ZoomText Certified Individuals</a></li> </ul> <h5 id="one-exam-for-both-initial-certification-and-renewal-1">One Exam for both Initial Certification and Renewal</h5> <p>There is a single exam for both the Initial Certification as well as Certification Renewals. Taking the exam is free. After successfully passing the exam and purchasing into the Certification Program, the certified individual receives an official Certificate from Freedom Scientific, and his/her name is included on the website of certified individuals. Inclusion on this website helps to enhance exposure of certified individuals as knowledgeable in the features and use of the JAWS screen reader and/or ZoomText Magnifier/Reader.</p> <p>Two options exist when purchasing the product certification:</p> <ul> <li>Initial Certification - For first-time certifications, a user needs to purchase the “Initial Certification.”</li> <li>Certification Renewal - For successive certifications, a user can purchase the “Certification Renewal” at a lower cost.</li> </ul> <h5 id="exam-links-1">Exam Links</h5> <ul> <li><a href="http://hosted.onlinetesting.net/FreedomScientific2/login.pl/JAWSCertification">JAWS Certification Exam</a></li> <li><a href="http://hosted.onlinetesting.net/FreedomScientific2/login/ZoomText-Certification">ZoomText Certification Exam</a></li> </ul> <h3 id="jaws-certified-individuals">JAWS Certified Individuals</h3> <p>Skip to content</p> <p>Need Support? <a href="tel:+18004444443">1(800) 444-4443</a></p> <h4 id="jaws-certified-individuals-1">JAWS Certified Individuals</h4> <p>The following individuals have received official JAWS Certification from Freedom Scientific. Passing the JAWS Certification exam guarantees that each individual above is knowledgeable about JAWS and knows where to find the different resources they may need to help others.</p> <h5 id="contact-the-freedom-scientific-training-department">Contact the Freedom Scientific Training Department</h5> <p>Phone: 800-444-4443 or 727-803-8000</p> <p>Fax: 727-803-8001</p> <p>You may also request help by completing the Training Information contact form.</p> <h3 id="jaws-training-training-and-certification">JAWS Training (Training and certification)</h3> <h4 id="jaws-training">JAWS Training</h4> <p>The JAWS® Training page is your one-stop source for finding free training materials, in a variety of formats, and on a range of topics.</p> <h5 id="getting-started-with-jaws">Getting Started with JAWS</h5> <p>Just installed your brand-new copy of JAWS on your Windows computer? Our Basic Training will help get you up and running with this powerful screen reader. This training is available for download in DAISY (Digital Accessible Information System), MP3, and HTML formats for you to listen to or read at your convenience.</p> <p><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/jaws/getting-started/">JAWS Getting Started</a></p> <h5 id="jaws-training-bundle">JAWS Training Bundle</h5> <p>You can also download the complete <a href="https://support.freedomscientific.com/Training/JAWS-Basic-Training.zip">JAWS Basic Training</a> as a ZIP file that you can extract to any location on your computer. It contains the entire Basic Training in MP3 and HTML format so you can listen or read at your convenience.</p> <h5 id="jaws-training-videos">JAWS Training Videos</h5> <p>Check out and subscribe to the <a href="https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCLlctxRAroB4ApeQd5b_I6A/videos?view=0&sort=dd&shelf_id=1">Freedom Scientific Training YouTube channel</a>. Our videos offer quick tips and hints for both new and experienced JAWS users. Watch a video to learn something new or refresh your skills.</p> <h5 id="additional-jaws-training">Additional JAWS Training</h5> <p>Learn more about using several popular JAWS features and how you can use them in various applications to increase your productivity. These lessons are available for download in both DAISY (Digital Accessible Information System) and MP3 format.</p> <p><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/jaws/additional-jaws-training-downloads/">Additional JAWS Training</a></p> <h5 id="surfs-up-browsing-the-web-with-jaws-1">Surf’s Up, Browsing the Web with JAWS</h5> <p><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/jaws/surfs-up/">Surf’s Up</a> is a series of self-guided lessons that teach you to read and navigate the web using JAWS. Get started now.</p> <p>Don’t have time to review the lessons online? <a href="https://support.freedomscientific.com/SurfsUp/ZIP_Surfs_Up.zip">Download Surf’s Up</a> and learn offline at your own pace.</p> <p>Watch a brief <a href="https://youtu.be/ZAVFzQl8wYU">introduction to Surf’s Up</a> on our YouTube channel.</p> <h5 id="new-and-improved-features-in-jaws">New and Improved Features in JAWS</h5> <ul> <li>The <a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/jaws/picture-smart-ai/">Picture Smart AI</a> feature allows you to submit a photo to be analyzed and then displays a description of the picture in the JAWS Results Viewer window.</li> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/jaws/fscompanion/">FSCompanion</a> is an AI assistant that helps you quickly find JAWS, ZoomText, and Fusion features, keystrokes, and task instructions across multiple applications—without searching through multiple documents or web pages.</li> </ul> <h5 id="jaws-faqs">JAWS FAQs</h5> <p>Find answers to some of the most commonly asked questions about using JAWS.</p> <p><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/jaws/frequently-asked-questions/">JAWS FAQs</a></p> <h5 id="jaws-hotkeys">JAWS Hotkeys</h5> <p>JAWS has an extensive list of keyboard commands. Keyboard key combinations (called keystrokes or commands) provide quick and effective access to the entire scope of Windows features. Programs are opened, used, and closed. Letters are written and edited. Spreadsheets are compiled and calculated. Files are created, modified, and deleted. The Internet is browsed, and files and programs are downloaded. Through extensive use of keystrokes, the limitations of a graphical user environment are overcome.</p> <p><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/jaws/hotkeys/">JAWS Hotkeys</a></p> <h5 id="jaws-touch-gestures">JAWS Touch Gestures</h5> <p>If you have a computer running Windows that includes a touch screen, such as the Surface™ Pro tablet from Microsoft, you can control JAWS directly from the touch screen.</p> <p>Performing JAWS and Windows commands from a touch screen is accomplished by different touch gestures using one or more fingers. Gestures include taps, flicks, swipes, rotating, and pinching.</p> <p><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/jaws/jaws-touch-gestures/">JAWS Touch Gestures</a></p> <p><a Passing the ZoomText Certification exam guarantees that each individual above is knowledgeable about ZoomText and knows where to find the different resources they may need to help others.</p> <h5 id="contact-the-freedom-scientific-training-department-1">Contact the Freedom Scientific Training Department</h5> <p>Phone: 800-444-4443 or 727-803-8000</p> <p>Fax: 727-803-8001</p> <p>You may also request help by completing the Training Information contact form.</p> <h3 id="zoomtext-faqs">ZoomText FAQs</h3> <p>Skip to content</p> <p>Need Support? <a href="tel:+18004444443">1(800) 444-4443</a></p> <h4 id="zoomtext-faqs-1">ZoomText FAQs</h4> <p>ZoomText Basic FAQs</p> <p>What is ZoomText?</p> <p>Who is ZoomText for?</p> <p>What operating systems does ZoomText work with?</p> <p>What versions of Microsoft Office does ZoomText support?</p> <p>What web browsers does ZoomText work with?</p> <p>Does ZoomText read PDF documents?</p> <p>Can I read my email with ZoomText?</p> <p>Magnification and Speech</p> <p>What is the difference between ZoomText Magnifier and ZoomText Magnifier/Reader?</p> <p>Is ZoomText Magnifier/Reader intended to be a complete magnification and screen reading solution?</p> <p>Licensing and Purchasing</p> <p>Where can I buy ZoomText?</p> <p>If I already own ZoomText, can I upgrade to ZoomText Magnifier/Reader or to Fusion?</p> <p>Is ZoomText available in languages other than English?</p> <p>Is a ZoomText demo available?</p> <h5 id="zoomtext-basic-faqs">ZoomText Basic FAQs</h5> <h6 id="what-is-zoomtext">What is ZoomText?</h6> <p>ZoomText is screen magnification software for the Microsoft Windows operating system. It allows you to change screen colors and magnification levels, customize the mouse pointer and text cursor to make it easy to find them, and turn on a focus rectangle to help you track where you are on the screen. Additionally, ZoomText is available with some basic speech features for reading documents, web pages, and email, as well as hearing what you are typing or what is under the mouse pointer.</p> <h6 id="who-is-zoomtext-for">Who is ZoomText for?</h6> <p>ZoomText is for any user with enough vision to see a computer screen, but requires extra visual enhancements to be able to more comfortably read screen content.</p> <h6 id="what-operating-systems-does-zoomtext-work-with">What operating systems does ZoomText work with?</h6> <p>ZoomText installs and works with Windows 10, Windows 8.1, and Windows 7. Note that as Windows continues to change, new ZoomText features may not be available in older versions of Windows.</p> <h6 id="what-versions-of-microsoft-office-does-zoomtext-support">What versions of Microsoft Office does ZoomText support?</h6> <p>ZoomText works with Microsoft Office 365, or Microsoft Office 2016 and later. ZoomText also supports older versions of Office (2013 and 2010), however, there are no further enhancements coming for these older versions.</p> <p>ZoomText has been tested to perform best with the latest Windows operating systems and software applications. As new versions of Freedom Scientific products are released, support for older software may not continue.</p> <h6 id="what-web-browsers-does-zoomtext-work-with">What web browsers does ZoomText work with?</h6> <p>ZoomText visually tracks as you navigate websites in Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, and Internet Explorer. Support for Microsoft Edge is continuing to improve as well. Web pages are also read aloud if you have ZoomText Magnifier/Reader.</p> <h6 id="does-zoomtext-read-pdf-documents">Does ZoomText read PDF documents?</h6> <p>Yes. ZoomText’s visual features work to help you navigate in PDF documents. If you have ZoomText Magnifier/Reader, the document will also be read aloud.</p> <h6 id="can-i-read-my-email-with-zoomtext">Can I read my email with ZoomText?</h6> <p>Yes. Special attention has gone into the design of ZoomText to make sure you have full access to email, especially with Microsoft Outlook from Office 365.</p> <h5 id="magnification-and-speech">Magnification and Speech</h5> <h6 id="what-is-the-difference-between-zoomtext-magnifier-and-zoomtext-magnifierreader">What is the difference between ZoomText Magnifier and ZoomText Magnifier/Reader?</h6> <p>ZoomText Magnifier contains all of the visual enhancements necessary to help make content on your computer screen easier to see. These include selection of the zoom level, zoom window types, screen enhancements, and navigation options. No speech feedback is available.</p> <p>ZoomText Magnifier/Reader offers all of the features of ZoomText Magnifier with the addition of speech features including typing, mouse and program echo; the AppReader and Reading Zones tools, and the Text Cursor and commands for speaking certain items like the window title and the time or date.</p> <h6 id="is-zoomtext-magnifierreader-intended-to-be-a-complete-magnification-and-screen-reading-solution">Is ZoomText Magnifier/Reader intended to be a complete magnification and screen reading solution?</h6> <p>No. ZoomText Magnifier/Reader is still primarily for low vision users with some added speech functionality to help with certain tasks like reading documents and web pages, echoing your typing or mouse movement, and speaking other essential program activity. If your vision has deteriorated enough where you need more speech feedback than what is provided by ZoomText Magnifier/Reader, then you should check out Fusion which combines both ZoomText and JAWS for the best in screen magnification and screen reading functionality.</p> <h5 id="licensing-and-purchasing">Licensing and Purchasing</h5> <h6 id="where-can-i-buy-zoomtext">Where can I buy ZoomText?</h6> <p>ZoomText is available from Freedom Scientific or your local Freedom Scientific dealer. Visit the Dealer Locator page to find out who serves your area.</p> <h6 id="if-i-already-own-zoomtext-can-i-upgrade-to-zoomtext-magnifierreader-or-to-fusion">If I already own ZoomText, can I upgrade to ZoomText Magnifier/Reader or to Fusion?</h6> <p>Absolutely! Contact Freedom Scientific or your local dealer for details and to place your order.</p> <h6 id="is-zoomtext-available-in-languages-other-than-english">Is ZoomText available in languages other than English?</h6> <p>ZoomText is available in many languages, some of which can be obtained from the Freedom Scientific downloads pages. Additional languages are also available directly from your local distributor in many countries.</p> <h6 id="is-a-zoomtext-demo-available">Is a ZoomText demo available?</h6> <p>Yes, like other Freedom Scientific products, ZoomText can be installed and will work in a 40-minute mode. When that expires, reboot and it will work again in the same way. And, if an update comes out, it will alert you and allow it to update just as it does for licensed software.</p> <h3 id="zoomtext-training-resources-1">ZoomText Training Resources</h3> <p>Skip to content</p> <p>Need Support? <a href="tel:+18004444443">1(800) 444-4443</a></p> <h4 id="zoomtext-training-resources-2">ZoomText Training Resources</h4> <h5 id="getting-started-with-zoomtext-1">Getting Started with ZoomText</h5> <p>ZoomText lets you change screen colors and magnification levels, customize the mouse pointer and text cursor to make it easy to find them, and turn on a focus rectangle to help you track where you are on the screen.</p> <p>ZoomText Getting Started</p> <h5 id="zoomtext-faqs-2">ZoomText FAQs</h5> <p>Stuck on something? Need a quick reminder about that handy feature you used a few weeks ago, but can’t remember how to do it? Then checkout our training FAQs for quick answers to those who, what, when, where, why, and, most importantly, how questions.</p> <p>ZoomText FAQs</p> <h5 id="zoomtext-videos">ZoomText Videos</h5> <p>Check out and subscribe to the <a href="https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCLlctxRAroB4ApeQd5b_I6A">Freedom Scientific Training YouTube channel</a>. Our videos offer quick tips and hints for both new and experienced ZoomText users. Watch a video to learn something new or refresh your skills.</p> <h2 id="training-resources">Training resources</h2> <h3 id="activating-software-licenses">Activating Software Licenses</h3> <ul> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/enterprise/">Enterprise</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/enterprise/activating-software-licenses/">Activating Software Licenses</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/enterprise/installation/">Software Installation Guide</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/enterprise/using-jaws-zoomtext-and-fusion-with-remote-access-software/">Using JAWS, ZoomText, and Fusion with Remote Access Software</a></li> </ul> <h4 id="activating-software-licenses-1">Activating Software Licenses</h4> <p>Before activating, your Freedom Scientific software (JAWS, ZoomText, or Fusion) will run in 40-minute demo mode, after which you will need to reboot the computer to use the software again. Once activated, the software will no longer time out. Internet License Manager (ILM) allows you to quickly activate your Freedom Scientific software using the Internet. There are three types of ILM licenses available: single-user, non-network multi-user, or network multi-user.</p> <h5 id="single-and-non-network-multi-user-activation">Single and Non-Network Multi-User Activation</h5> <p>Since most companies and organizations most likely have several users who need to access JAWS, ZoomText, or Fusion, you will most likely be dealing with a multi-user license. For non-network licenses, you need to activate the license on each computer that will be running the software. For example, if you have a five-user license for Fusion, you will perform the activation process on the five computers where you installed Fusion.</p> <h5 id="internet-activation">Internet Activation</h5> <p>Before performing these steps, make sure you have the 20-digit authorization number for the license you are activating.</p> <ul> <li>Launch your Freedom Scientific software.</li> <li>Select Activate.</li> <li>Select Internet as your method of activation.</li> <li>Follow the instructions on the screen. A message will inform you when the activation is successful.</li> </ul> <h5 id="manual-activation">Manual Activation</h5> <p>If you do not have an Internet connection on the computer you would like to activate, the best option is to use another computer with internet access to get the activation license code required to activate on the offline computer.</p> <ul> <li><p>Launch the Freedom Scientific software.</p></li> <li><p>Select Activate.</p></li> <li><p>Instead of selecting Internet as your activation method, select Manual.</p></li> <li><p>Note the 9-character locking code (including the dash) from the Manual screen. You will need this in conjunction with the 20-digit authorization number. You now need to obtain the activation license code. This is a combination of over 100 numbers, characters, spaces, and punctuation symbols. The easiest way to transfer that code is to copy it to a USB thumb drive, then bring it back to the computer you’d like to activate.</p></li> <li><p>Insert a USB thumb drive into the computer with Internet access.</p></li> <li><p>Go to <a href="https://fsactivate.freedomscientific.com/">fsactivate.freedomscientific</a><a href="https://fsactivate.com/">.com</a>.</p></li> <li><p>Select the <a href="https://fsactivate.freedomscientific.com/Activation/RetrieveActivationLicenseCode">Retrieve an Activation License Code</a> option.</p></li> <li><p>Enter the 20-digit authorization number in the Authorization number edit field.</p></li> <li><p>Enter the 9-character locking code into the Locking code edit field. Include the dash, for example, “100-D2C7F”.</p></li> <li><p>Select the Submit license request button.</p></li> <li><p>Select the button to copy the license activation code to your clipboard.</p></li> <li><p>Open a text editor, such as Notepad.</p></li> <li><p>Press CTRL+V to paste the license code into a new document. Do not add any additional spaces or text.</p></li> <li><p>Press CTRL+S to open the Save As dialog box. Type a name for this file, such as JAWS Activation, and save it to the USB thumb drive. You can now use the activation code you copied to the thumb drive to activate the software on the offline computer.</p></li> <li><p>Insert the USB thumb drive containing the file that you created.</p></li> <li><p>Open the file in Notepad and copy the entire activation code. If the only text in the document is the code, you can use CTRL+A to select all, then CTRL+C to copy it.</p></li> <li><p>With the Manual Activation dialog box open, navigate to the License code edit field and use CTRL+V to paste the code.</p></li> <li><p>You do not have to enter the 20-digit authorization code in the Authorization number field as it is not needed to complete activation.</p></li> <li><p>Select Next to complete the activation. Note: The activation license code always ends with the word “exclusive”. After pasting the entire code into Notepad, make sure you do not add or delete any characters or spaces. This will make it easier for copying and then pasting the correct code into the License code field of the Manual Activation dialog box.</p></li> </ul> <h5 id="automatic-ilm-activation">Automatic ILM Activation</h5> <p>In situations where your non-network multi-user license uses the same 20-digit authorization code for all seats in the license, you can have the software silently activate following a clean install by providing the authorization code when running the setup package. If you are running the April 2023 releases or later of JAWS, ZoomText, or Fusion, you can do one of the following:</p> <ul> <li>If you are installing the software using the AdditionalSettings.ini file as described on the <a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/enterprise/installation/">Software Installation Guide</a> page, there is a setting called ILMAuthorize. This setting takes the product to be authorized and the 20-digit authorization code. For example, ILMAuthorize=<a href="#fusion">Fusion</a>,[xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx].</li> <li>Run the setup package with the /ILMAuthorize command line option. This takes both the product being authorized and the 20-digit authorization code. For example, c:.exe /ILMAuthorize Fusion XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX. When the software is launched following the installation, and it detects there is no authorization available, it will silently activate using the information provided during setup without the need for user intervention.</li> </ul> <h5 id="network-multi-user-license-activation">Network Multi-User License Activation</h5> <p>A network license requires that you set up a license server on a computer that will be accessed by other computers on the same network running the Freedom Scientific software. The software installed on each computer will get its authorization from the license server up to the maximum number of allowed users. For example, if you have a five-user network Fusion license, up to five installations of Fusion can be running as authorized versions. If a sixth computer running Fusion attempts to obtain authorization from the license server, it will fail to authorize, unless one of the currently authorized copies of Fusion is shut down so it is no longer connected to the license server.</p> <p>Refer to the <a href="https://fsactivate.freedomscientific.com/Activation/Network">Network License Server Activation</a> page for more details on downloading and setting up the license server.</p> <p>Use our <a href="https://fsactivate.freedomscientific.com/Activation/ILMTroubleShootingGuide">Software Activation Troubleshooting Guide</a> to help resolve any issues you may encounter during the activation process.</p> <h3 id="additional-jaws-training-1">Additional JAWS Training</h3> <h4 id="additional-jaws-training-2">Additional JAWS Training</h4> <p>These training resources offer in-depth demonstrations of a variety of popular JAWS® features. From using Research It to browse the news or look up a definition, proofreading a document using Text Analyzer, or customizing how JAWS behaves through Settings Center, there’s something here for every user.</p> <p>These Training files are available in DAISY (Digital Accessible Information System) format and contain both text and audio. You can read them using the FSReader DAISY reader included with JAWS or using any other hardware or software DAISY player. For your convenience, some files are also available in MP3 audio if you would prefer to listen to them on an MP3 player or another device.</p> <h5 id="daisy-training-files-for-jaws">DAISY Training
