</ul> <h3 id="ai-terminology">AI Terminology</h3> <ul> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/learnai/">Learn AI</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/learnai/ai-terminology/">AI Terminology</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/learnai/breaking-down-barriers-practice-exercises/">Breaking Down Barriers: An Introduction to Using AI with JAWS, ZoomText, and Fusion Practice Exercises</a></li> </ul> <h4 id="ai-terminology-1">AI Terminology</h4> <p>This glossary explains common AI terms in plain language. These words come up often when using tools like ChatGPT, Gemini, or Copilot.</p> <h5 id="a">A</h5> <p>AI (Artificial Intelligence): Technology that can do things that normally need human thinking—like writing, planning, or answering questions.</p> <p>Automation: Letting technology handle a task for you. AI can help automate writing emails, scheduling meetings, or creating reports.</p> <h5 id="b">B</h5> <p>Bias: Sometimes AI gives unfair or unbalanced results because of patterns in its training data. It might favor one idea or group without meaning to.</p> <h5 id="c">C</h5> <p>Chatbot: An AI tool you can talk to through typing. ChatGPT is one example.</p> <p>Context Window: The limit to how much the AI can “remember” in one session. If the conversation gets too long, it might forget earlier parts.</p> <h5 id="d">D</h5> <p>Data Privacy: Keeping your personal or work info safe when using AI. Don’t share passwords, private data, or anything confidential with a chatbot.</p> <h5 id="f">F</h5> <p>Fine-tuning: Giving the AI extra training to help it do better in a certain topic or task.</p> <h5 id="g">G</h5> <p>Generative AI: AI that creates things—like writing, code, images, or music. ChatGPT is generative because it writes new content.</p> <h5 id="h">H</h5> <p>Hallucination: When the AI gives an answer that sounds real but isn’t true. It doesn’t mean to lie—it just gets things wrong sometimes.</p> <h5 id="i">I</h5> <p>Inference: The process the AI uses to figure out a good response based on your prompt.</p> <h5 id="l">L</h5> <p>LLM (Large Language Model): A type of AI that’s trained to understand and generate language. These models are what tools like ChatGPT are built on.</p> <h5 id="m">M</h5> <p>Model: The part of the AI that does the thinking. It reads your prompt and figures out how to respond.</p> <h5 id="n">N</h5> <p>Natural Language Processing (NLP): How AI reads, understands, and writes human language.</p> <h5 id="p">P</h5> <p>Personalization: Adjusting the AI’s response by giving it details about who you are or what you need. Example: “Write a thank-you note from a customer support rep.”</p> <p>Prompt: A message or instruction you give to the AI. It can be a question, a request, or a short description of what you need.</p> <h5 id="q">Q</h5> <p>Query: Another word for your question or search request. A prompt and a query are often the same thing.</p> <h5 id="t">T</h5> <p>Token: A piece of text the AI reads. Words and punctuation are broken into tokens. The more tokens, the longer or more detailed the response.</p> <p>Training Data: All the text the AI learned from—like books, articles, and websites. This helps it understand how language works.</p> <h5 id="u">U</h5> <p>Use Case: A real example of how AI is used. Example: Using AI to summarize long emails is a common use case.</p> <h5 id="w">W</h5> <p>Workflow: A set of steps you take to get something done at work. AI can help make some steps faster or easier.</p> <p><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/learnai">Back to Learn AI</a></p> <h3 id="blackboard-with-jaws-tutorials">Blackboard with JAWS Tutorials</h3> <ul> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/resources/">Resources</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/resources/blackboard-with-jaws-tutorials/">Blackboard with JAWS Tutorials</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/resources/use-jaws-with-canvas/">Use JAWS with the Canvas Learning Management System</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/resources/voice-assistant-in-the-classroom/">Voice Assistant in the Classroom</a></li> </ul> <h4 id="blackboard-with-jaws-tutorials-1">Blackboard with JAWS Tutorials</h4> <p>Blackboard is a learning management system (LMS) that colleges and universities use to host online classes and course content. These videos will show you how to use Blackboard with JAWS. A new video will be added each month to teach you different tasks in Blackboard.</p> <h5 id="using-blackboard-with-jaws">Using Blackboard with JAWS</h5> <p>Watch or download the video using the links below. Click or to watch the video in full screen. Press ESC to exit full screen.</p> <p>Download <a href="https://support.freedomscientific.com/training/resources/blackboard/Using-Blackboard-with-JAWS.mp4">Using Blackboard with JAWS (MP4)</a></p> <p>Note: If you want to save the MP4 and watch it later, select the link to start the MP4 and then press CTRL+S.</p> <h5 id="access-a-course-in-blackboard-with-jaws">Access a Course in Blackboard with JAWS</h5> <p>Watch or download the video using the links below. Click or to watch the video in full screen. Press ESC to exit full screen.</p> <p>Download <a href="https://support.freedomscientific.com/training/resources/blackboard/Access-a-Course-in-Blackboard-with-JAWS.mp4">Access a Course in Blackboard with JAWS (MP4)</a></p> <p>Note: If you want to save the MP4 and watch it later, select the link to start the MP4 and then press CTRL+S.</p> <p><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/resources/">Back to Resources page</a></p> <h3 id="braille-commands">Braille Commands</h3> <h4 id="braille-commands-1">Braille Commands</h4> <p>JAWS® supports a series of keystrokes that allow you to input braille commands and also control your computer (see BrailleIn™ description below). Below are keystrokes that support Freedom Scientific’s Focus braille displays. For other braille displays, contact the manufacturer for a list of keystrokes.</p> <p>Many commands listed here include the word “CHORD.” To perform a chorded command, you always include the SPACEBAR as part of the command. For example, L CHORD or DOTS 1-2-3 and the SPACEBAR.</p> <h5 id="modifier-keys">Modifier Keys</h5> <p>Use the modifier keys to simulate key combinations (keystrokes) that include CTRL, ALT, WINDOWS Key, SHIFT, or the JAWS Key (INSERT). To use these modifiers when typing a keystroke, do the following:</p> <ul> <li>Hold down DOT 8 CHORD and then press the corresponding modifier keys in the keystroke. Modifier keystrokes are listed in the following table.</li> <li>After you create the modifier portion of the keystroke, release the keys and press the remaining part of the keystroke. For example, to perform the keystroke CTRL+SHIFT+V, you press DOTS 3-7-8 CHORD, release the keys, and then press V (DOTS 1-2-3-6). Key Name</li> </ul> <p>Keystroke</p> <p>Function Keys (F1 through F12)</p> <p>For more information, see the Function Keys description.</p> <p>DOT 1</p> <p>INSERT</p> <p>DOT 2</p> <p>CTRL</p> <p>DOT 3</p> <p>WINDOWS Key</p> <p>DOT 4</p> <p>JAWS Key</p> <p>DOT 5</p> <p>ALT</p> <p>DOT 6</p> <p>SHIFT</p> <p>DOT 7</p> <p>Instead of memorizing these keys by their dot position, it may be easier to learn the finger with which each key would be associated. When all of your fingers are on the braille keyboard, the layout would be:</p> <p>Key Name</p> <p>Finger position</p> <p>Function Keys (F1 through F12)</p> <p>Left index finger</p> <p>WINDOWS Key</p> <p>Right index finger</p> <p>INSERT</p> <p>Left middle finger</p> <p>JAWS Key</p> <p>Right middle finger</p> <p>CTRL</p> <p>Left ring finger</p> <p>ALT</p> <p>Right ring finger</p> <p>SHIFT</p> <p>Left little finger</p> <p>Notice that you can create a rather loose correlation between pairs of fingers in this description. For example, the left index finger is Function Keys while the right index finger is the WINDOWS key. A stronger correlation can be made with the left and right middle fingers. The left is the INSERT Key and the right is the JAWS key, both often serving the same purpose in JAWS usage. Finally, the left and right ring fingers are the CTRL and ALT keys respectively, which make these two positions easier to remember.</p> <p>Once this layout is understood, it is easy to grasp that Any time a modifier key, or combination of modifier keys is used as part of a command, DOT 8 CHORD will always be included.</p> <p>Finally, pressing any of these modifier keys with DOT 8 CHORD is the same as pressing and holding any of the equivalent keys on the QWERTY keyboard. The computer is waiting for the key or keys which the modifier keys will modify. So, pressing DOTS 3-8 CHORD is the same as pressing the CTRL key. Windows then waits for the key which will complete the CTRL combination, such as the letter A to make CTRL+A to select all, or the letter C to make CTRL+C to copy the selected text to the clipboard. Repetition of frequently used keystrokes such as the CTRL key combinations already mentioned, Windows commands such as WINDOWS Key+M, and JAWS commands such as INSERT+T should imprint these key associations firmly in your memory.</p> <h6 id="function-keys">Function Keys</h6> <p>To simulate the function keys (F1 through F12), press DOTS 1-8 CHORD followed by A through L (which correspond to 1 through 12). For example, to simulate the F6 key, press DOTS 1-8 CHORD, then F (DOTS 1-2-4). If the function key is part of a key combination, add the appropriate modifiers while holding down DOTS 1-8 CHORD. For example, to simulate the keystroke INSERT+F2, press DOTS 1-2-8 CHORD, then B (DOTS 1-2).</p> <h5 id="special-keys">Special Keys</h5> <p>Use these keystrokes to simulate certain keys that are not available on the Focus braille keyboard. Contracted Braille</h5> <p>The BrailleIn feature lets you type in contracted braille using your Perkins-style keyboard. The input is immediately translated back as normal text in your current e-mail, document, or form. If an application or specific edit box does not support contracted braille, JAWS announces “Computer Braille” when tutor messages are enabled. In addition, the Computer Braille start symbol, dots 4-5-6 followed by dots 3-4-6, is shown on the braille display to indicate when Computer Braille is required.</p> <p>Computer braille input is selected by default. To use contracted braille, do the following:</p> <ul> <li>Press INSERT+F2, and select Settings Center.</li> <li>To apply changes to all applications, press CTRL+SHIFT+D to load the JAWS default settings. To apply changes to a specific application, select it from the Applications combo box.</li> <li>In the Search edit box, type “Translation” without the quotes.</li> <li>Press DOWN ARROW to move to Translation in the filtered search results in the tree view and press ENTER to move focus to the Translation group. Press RIGHT ARROW to expand the group.</li> <li>Press SPACEBAR to cycle through the different settings in the Output combo box to configure the mode for reading braille on your display.</li> <li>The first option is always Computer Braille. The other available options depend on the currently selected language. For example, when the language is set to English United States, which is the default setting, the available output modes are U.S. English Grade 1, U.S. English Grade 2, Unified English Braille Grade 1, and Unified English Braille Grade 2. If you set the language to French, the available modes are French Grade 1 and French Grade 2. The default output mode is Computer Braille.</li> <li>Press SPACEBAR to cycle through the different settings in the Input combo box to specify the input mode used when typing braille from the Perkins-style keyboard on your display.</li> <li>The first option is always Computer Braille. The other available option depends on the currently selected output mode. For instance, if you have chosen to display Unified English Braille Grade 2, then you can choose to type in either Computer Braille or Unified English Braille Grade 2. The default input mode is Computer Braille. This setting is not available if the selected output mode is Computer Braille, or the selected output mode does not support input.</li> <li>Choose OK to save your changes and close Settings Center.</li> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/braille/focus/focus-user-guide/">Focus Blue User Guide</a></li> <li><a Hotkeys</a></li> </ul></li> </ul> <h4 id="braille-training-1">Braille Training</h4> <p>Welcome to the Braille training pages where you can learn more about our braille displays and other braille products.</p> <h5 id="focus-blue-braille-displays-1">Focus Blue Braille Displays</h5> <p>Visit the <a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/braille/focus/">Focus Blue training pages</a> to watch product tutorials, get answers to frequently asked questions, and review user guides to help set up and use Focus Blue braille displays.</p> <h5 id="elbraille-portable-braille-device">ElBraille Portable Braille Device</h5> <p>Visit the <a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/braille/elbraille/">ElBraille training pages</a> to review the user guide and get answers to frequently asked questions.</p> <p>We are continually adding training material and resources, so check back regularly for updates.</p> <h3 id="breaking-down-barriers-an-introduction-to-using-ai-with-jaws-zoomtext-and-fusion-practice-exercises">Breaking Down Barriers: An Introduction to Using AI with JAWS, ZoomText, and Fusion Practice Exercises</h3> <ul> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/learnai/">Learn AI</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/learnai/ai-terminology/">AI Terminology</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/learnai/breaking-down-barriers-practice-exercises/">Breaking Down Barriers: An Introduction to Using AI with JAWS, ZoomText, and Fusion Practice Exercises</a></li> </ul> <h4 id="breaking-down-barriers-an-introduction-to-using-ai-with-jaws-zoomtext-and-fusion-practice-exercises-1">Breaking Down Barriers: An Introduction to Using AI with JAWS, ZoomText, and Fusion Practice Exercises</h4> <p>Project: Create a workplace mentor program Using AI</p> <h5 id="task-one-draft-and-send-an-initial-project-proposal-email">Task One: Draft and Send an Initial Project Proposal Email</h5> <p>Using ChatGPT, draft a company-wide email to gauge interest in a new mentorship program. The goal is to propose a basic idea and gather initial feedback from potential participants. To do this:</p> <ul> <li>Go to <a href="https://openai.com/chatgpt/overview/">ChatGPT</a>.</li> <li>Copy the following prompt and paste it in the edit box.</li> <li>Draft a company-wide email to gauge interest in a new mentorship program. The goal is to propose a basic idea and gather initial feedback from potential participants.</li> <li>After pasting the prompt, press ENTER.</li> <li>Make sure Forms Mode is not activated by pressing ESC, then Press H to navigate to the heading containing the result. It should be the last heading on the page.</li> <li>Read the email ChatGPT drafted. You can continue chatting with ChatGPT to refine your email. For example, tell ChatGPT to make the email more exciting or informative, provide additional details to add to the email, etc.</li> </ul> <h5 id="task-two-analyze-colleague-feedback">Task Two: Analyze Colleague Feedback</h5> <p>Collect all the responses from the initial email and analyze them to shape the final program design. Since you have not sent out an actual email, use AI to generate these responses. To do this:</p> <ul> <li>Use the same ChatGPT conversation you created to generate the email. Tell ChatGPT to provide feedback on this email from colleagues. Include specific details such as the number of feedback responses you want it to generate or the type of information you want the feedback to contain.</li> <li>Copy this feedback into a document to use for the analysis.</li> <li>Go to <a href="https://gemini.google.com/app">Gemini</a>. Type a prompt in the edit box asking it to analyze the following feedback you received about a company-wide email regarding a new mentorship program. Paste the feedback from your document directly after your prompt and press ENTER.</li> <li>Make sure Forms Mode is not activated by pressing ESC, then Press H to navigate to the heading containing the result. It should be the last heading on the page.</li> <li>You can continue refining the analysis by asking Gemini to sort the feedback into categories or display it in a table for easy comparison.</li> <li>Copy and paste the feedback analysis in a document to use in the next steps.</li> </ul> <h5 id="task-three-create-a-program-outline-and-timeline">Task Three: Create a Program Outline and Timeline</h5> <p>Based on the feedback analysis, create a concrete plan for the program’s structure, key activities, and deadlines. To do this:</p> <ul> <li>Using <a href="https://copilot.microsoft.com/chats/hWdYb7Fcw6BY23vGeR7zM">Copilot</a>, create a concrete plan for the program’s structure, key activities, and deadlines. Enter this prompt into the Edit box.</li> <li>Create a plan for a new mentorship program using the following feedback analysis. Include how the program should be structured, key activities participants will take part in, and a timeline for implementation.</li> <li>Press ENTER to submit your prompt.</li> <li>Continue refining the timeline by changing deadlines or adding activities.</li> </ul> <h5 id="task-four-draft-and-send-a-follow-up-announcement-email">Task Four: Draft and Send a Follow-Up Announcement Email</h5> <p>Use the outline and timeline you just created to draft a final announcement email. This email will officially launch the program and provide all the necessary details. To do this:</p> <ul> <li>Still using <a href="https://copilot.microsoft.com/chats/hWdYb7Fcw6BY23vGeR7zM">Copilot</a>, create a prompt asking it to draft an announcement email to colleagues about the mentorship program using the outline and timeline you just created.</li> <li>This email should clearly outline the program launch, explain how it will work, and provide all details colleagues need to know to participate.</li> <li>Continue chatting with Copilot to revise your email. For example, specify additional information you want to include or refine it to be more concise. <a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/learnai/">Back to Learn AI</a></li> </ul> <h3 id="certification-training-resources">Certification (Training resources)</h3> <h4 id="certification-2">Certification</h4> <p>The JAWS® and ZoomText® Certification programs are online knowledge-based exams for JAWS Screen Reader and ZoomText Magnifier/Reader. Each product has its own test and certification. The certification programs are designed for consultants, trainers, agency staff, and users to demonstrate proficiency in using JAWS and ZoomText software applications.</p> <p>Read the <a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/certification/certification-details/">exam details and FAQs</a> to prepare for the exams. These pages provide exam preparation resources, exam categories to focus on, cost, and frequently asked questions.</p> <p>Currently there is not a separate certification exam or program for Fusion™, but successful completion of both the JAWS and ZoomText certifications is a strong indicator of proficiency with Fusion.</p> <h5 id="list-of-certified-individuals-1">List of certified individuals:</h5> <ul> <li><a href="https://support.freedomscientific.com/Services/TrainingAndCertification/JAWSCertifiedIndividuals">JAWS Certified Individuals</a></li> <li><a href="https://support.freedomscientific.com/Services/TrainingAndCertification/ZoomTextCertifiedIndividuals">ZoomText Certified Individuals</a></li> </ul> <h5 id="one-exam-for-both-initial-certification-and-renewal-2">One Exam for Both Initial Certification and Renewal</h5> <p>There is a single exam for both the Initial Certification as well as Certification Renewals. Taking the exam is free. After successfully passing the exam, you will automatically receive a free electronic certificate of completion which can be displayed in your web browser and printed as needed. You will also have an opportunity to confirm if you would like your name included on the website of certified individuals. Inclusion on this website helps to enhance exposure of certified individuals as knowledgeable in the features and use of the JAWS screen reader and/or ZoomText Magnifier/Reader.</p> <p>If you are interested in purchasing a high-quality print copy of your Certificate for proudly displaying in your home or office (JAWS certificates also include braille), two options exist:</p> <ul> <li>Initial Certification – $49.00. For first-time certifications, a user needs to purchase the “Initial Certification.”</li> <li>Certification Renewal – $29.00. For successive certifications, a user can purchase the “Certification Renewal” at this lower cost.</li> </ul> <h5 id="exam-links-2">Exam Links</h5> <ul> <li><a href="http://hosted.onlinetesting.net/FreedomScientific2/login.pl/JAWSCertification">JAWS Certification Exam</a></li> <li><a href="http://hosted.onlinetesting.net/FreedomScientific2/login/ZoomText-Certification">ZoomText Certification Exam</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/certification/certification-details/">Certification Details</a></li> </ul> <h3 id="certification-details">Certification Details</h3> <h4 id="certification-details-1">Certification Details</h4> <p>This page contains details about the Certification Programs for JAWS® and ZoomText®, including topics covered, expected proficiency, cost, how the exam works, and resources for studying for the exam.</p> <ul> <li>Certification Program Goals</li> <li>Expected Capabilities after Successful Completion</li> <li>Exam Categories</li> <li>Cost for Certification</li> <li>Exam Resources</li> <li>Taking the Exam</li> <li>Certification Logos</li> <li>FAQs</li> </ul> <h5 id="certification-program-goals-1">Certification Program Goals</h5> <p>The Certification Program is an online knowledge-based exam for consultants, trainers, agency staff, and JAWS and ZoomText users. The purpose is to:</p> <ul> <li>Help trainers and consultants validate their understanding of the software for companies, agencies, and consumers</li> <li>Increase people’s general knowledge of JAWS and ZoomText software</li> <li>Expand skills and abilities into new product features</li> <li>Present a comprehensive look at all the free training resources provided online and within the software</li> <li>Enhance exposure for certified individuals by listing them on the Freedom Scientific website</li> </ul> <h5 id="expected-capabilities-after-successful-completion-1">Expected Capabilities after Successful Completion</h5> <p>Product installation and setup, including:</p> <ul> <li><p>Software installation</p></li> <li><p>Training materials</p></li> <li><p>Synthesizers</p></li> <li><p>Braille displays (for JAWS) Thorough understanding of location and availability of training materials and resources, including:</p></li> <li><p>Help files</p></li> <li><p>DAISY and MP3 files (for JAWS)</p></li> <li><p>Archives of recorded webinars</p></li> <li><p>Product videos Product knowledge, including:</p></li> <li><p>Basic to advanced product skills</p></li> <li><p>JAWS keystrokes for both laptop and desktop layout</p></li> <li><p>ZoomText keystrokes for carrying out ZoomText commands</p></li> <li><p>How to identify and use key combinations for various functions</p></li> </ul> <h5 id="exam-categories">Exam Categories</h5> <p>The certification exams cover a wide range of product knowledge. It is not limited to just using the product, but enhancing your knowledge, from installation procedures to where to look when you need to access product information.</p> <h6 id="jaws-exam-categories-1">JAWS Exam Categories</h6> <p>The JAWS certification exam contains a variety of questions from the following categories:</p> <ul> <li>JAWS Features includes in-depth questions on JAWS features and using Braille with JAWS</li> <li>New Features includes questions on the new features in the latest JAWS version</li> <li>Headquarters includes what is available on our web resource pages, along with questions on contacting Technical Support and basic troubleshooting</li> <li>Installation includes all aspects of both typical and custom installation and activation of JAWS</li> <li>Training includes questions on Freedom Scientific’s training resources, JAWS Tandem, and Terminal Services</li> <li>Keyboard Knowledge includes questions on specific desktop and laptop keyboard commands</li> <li>HTML includes questions on all aspects of navigating, reading, and customizing HTML pages</li> <li>Learning JAWS includes the basics of JAWS and customizing an initial JAWS setup</li> </ul> <h6 id="zoomtext-exam-categories">ZoomText Exam Categories</h6> <p>The ZoomText certification exam contains a variety of questions from the following categories:</p> <ul> <li>Installation includes all aspects of both typical and custom installation and activation of ZoomText.</li> <li>ZoomText User Interface the ZoomText User Interface or Toolbar serves a hub for users gaining access to both features and help. This category focuses on the features of the user interface.</li> <li>Visual Enhancements includes in-depth questions on ZoomText visual features such as the pointer (mouse), cursor, color, and focus enhancements, zoom windows, magnification, freeze windows, and tracking.</li> <li>Dual Monitor includes questions pertaining to ZoomText’s popular dual monitor functionality.</li> <li>Speech this category covers speech topics including adjusting speech settings, using speech in the varies AppReader modes, available synthesizers, and other speech settings.</li> <li>Keyboard Knowledge includes questions on specific keyboard commands that allow users to use a key combination to carry out ZoomText functions rather than navigating to the user interface and activating a control there</li> <li>Add-Ons includes questions on tools that can be used in conjunction with ZoomText, such as the ZoomText Large Print Keyboard, Dragon Naturally Speaking, and TypeAbility.</li> <li>Compatibility includes questions about ZoomText compatibility with other commercial and assistive technology products.</li> <li>Help includes what is available on our web resource pages, Built-in Help, Training resources, as well as questions about basic troubleshooting and contacting Technical Support.</li> <li>Settings includes questions pertaining to changing and saving ZoomText settings to meet individual user preferences.</li> <li>Tools includes questions about ZoomText’s tools including: AppReader, SpeakIt, Background Reader, Finder tool, Reading Zones, the Recorder tool.</li> </ul> <h5 id="cost-for-certification-1">Cost for Certification</h5> <p>There is no cost to study the materials and take the exam. Once you complete the exam with a passing score, you will automatically receive a free electronic certificate in HTML format. You will also be given an opportunity to be listed on our website.</p> <p>Passing the JAWS exam entitles your name to be on our list of <a href="https://support.freedomscientific.com/Services/TrainingAndCertification/JAWSCertifiedIndividuals">JAWS Certified Individuals</a>.</p> <p>Passing the ZoomText exam entitles your name to be on our list of <a href="https://support.freedomscientific.com/Services/TrainingAndCertification/ZoomTextCertifiedIndividuals">ZoomText Certified Individuals</a>.</p> <p>In addition, after passing the exam, you will be given an option to purchase an official printed certificate from Freedom Scientific. JAWS certificates are produced in high-quality print and braille while ZoomText certificates are produced in high-quality print. The initial certification is $49 for each product, with a $29 renewal fee if you choose to update your certification later. To qualify for the $29 renewal fee, you must retake the exam and earn a passing score.</p> <h5 id="exam-resources-1">Exam Resources</h5> <p>The study materials are available in the current versions of JAWS and ZoomText, and can also be found on the Freedom Scientific website. If you have a current version of JAWS or ZoomText and a connection to the Internet, then you already have what you need to study for either exam. No additional study materials are required. The exam questions are based on guides, help topics, DAISY training materials, and web resources.</p> <p>The study time for each exam is approximately 10 hours. That time is based on listening to all basic training material and suggested DAISY books (for JAWS), reading the guides and websites, and studying the exact JAWS or ZoomText help topics. Study time will vary with your experience, and you may need to concentrate on some areas more than others. It is recommended that you take your time and become familiar with all the study materials before you take the exam.</p> <p>Below are a list of resources for both JAWS and ZoomText.</p> <h6 id="resources-for-jaws-1">Resources for JAWS</h6> <p>JAWS Tandem Quick Start Guide – available from within the JAWS program window. Open the Utilities menu, open the JAWS Tandem submenu, and then open the Quick Start Guide.</p> <p>JAWS Quick Start Guide – available from within the start menu, Utilities – JAWS 20xx program group, and then open Explore the Manuals. This folder contains the JAWS Quick Start Guide.</p> <p>JAWS Basic Training Materials – the books are in DAISY format and can be reviewed using FSReader. The basic training materials are a collection of books with more than five hours of lessons. If your copy of JAWS is the downloaded version, you may not have the basic training materials.</p> <p>The training books are also available for download in MP3 format. Visit <a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/jaws/getting-started/">Getting Started with JAWS</a> to download either DAISY books or MP3 files.</p> <p>DAISY Books – the books are available to review using FSReader. FSReader can be opened from within the JAWS program window. Open the Help menu and press ENTER on the Training menu item and FSReader opens. If these books are not installed, pressing ENTER on a link in the JAWS Basic Training Table of Contents causes FSReader to download and install them automatically from the Freedom Scientific web site.</p> <p>Web Resources – available from within the JAWS program window. Open the Help menu, then open the Web Resources submenu. It is recommended that you familiarize yourself with the choices in the Web Resources submenu. Spend additional time focusing on JAWS Headquarters, Technical Support pages, Training and Certification pages, and Surfing the Internet.</p> <p>JAWS Help – JAWS Help topics are found in JAWS F1 Help. It is recommended that you become familiar with the JAWS Help topics. Open JAWS Help by pressing F1 from within the JAWS program window. To quickly find a topic, move to the Search tab, and type the topic name in the search field.</p> <h6 id="resources-for-zoomtext">Resources for ZoomText</h6> <p>ZoomText Help – ZoomText Help topics are found in ZoomText F1 Help. It is recommended that you become familiar with the ZoomText Help topics. Providing that are keeping your ZoomText product current by downloading updates, the ZoomText Help within the program may be more current than your printed or downloaded User Guide, as we are providing regular updates that enhance features, and may even provide completely new features. Open ZoomText Help by pressing F1 from within the ZoomText program window. To quickly find a topic, move to the Search tab, and type the topic name in the search field.</p> <p>ZoomText Users Guide the ZoomText Users Guide ships with the ZoomText product. It can also be downloaded from our <a href="https://support.freedomscientific.com/Support/ZoomTextDocumentation/ZoomTextGuides">Product Documentation page</a>. The user guide provides in-depth information about the ZoomText installation, product features and more.</p> <p>ZoomText Large Print Keyboard User Guide – the ZoomText Large Print Keyboard User Guide ships with the keyboard. It can also be downloaded from our <a href="https://support.freedomscientific.com/Support/ZoomTextDocumentation/ZoomTextKeyboardGuides">Product Documentation page</a>. The ZoomText Large Print Keyboard is an optional accessory to the ZoomText program. There may be questions on the exam about the added keyboard functionality so it is good to be aware of the information contained in the Keyboard User Guide.</p> <p>Web Resources – on our website, we provide many tools that may give you greater understanding of ZoomText features. Specific places to look are the <a href="https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLk-npwu4WEBQRbTt4YGaGCfDh3IQzUYtJ">ZoomText videos playlist</a> on YouTube, and help found on the <a href="https://support.freedomscientific.com/support">Technical Support Bulletins page</a>.</p> <h5 id="taking-the-exam-1">Taking the Exam</h5> <p>When you are confident that you have spent adequate time covering all study materials, it is time to take the exam. Be prepared to set aside 60 minutes without interruptions to take the exam. Please note — you will not be able to stop the clock on the exam once you begin.</p> <p>A web page link will take you to the exam log-on page.</p> <p>You must complete your full name and email address in the edit fields, select your country, and then press TAB to move to the Start Test button. Your exam page will load, followed by a dialog notifying you that you have 60 minutes to complete your exam. Press the OK button and begin.</p> <h6 id="exam-navigation-1">Exam Navigation</h6> <p>The exam is a web page, so standard JAWS and ZoomText navigation keys in HTML documents apply. For JAWS, pressing P to move by paragraph moves you between the questions and possible answers</p> <h6 id="during-the-exam-1">During the Exam</h6> <p>At the mid-point of the exam, a dialog will appear to alert you that you are at the halfway point in the exam. You have 30 more minutes from that point. Press the OK button and continue your exam.</p> <p>The time remaining is displayed at the bottom of the testing page. If you are using JAWS to take the exam, you can use the virtual cursor to read the time. Do this by pressing CTRL+END to move to the bottom of the exam page. Before you move from where you are, you can set a temporary PlaceMarker on the question to easily move back to your spot in the exam. Press CTRL+WINDOWS Key+K to set the temporary PlaceMarker or move it to another spot later in the exam. Press K to move back to your spot after checking the time.</p> <p>At the end of each question a Resource for that exam question will be noted. It will appear like this: (Resource: JAWS Help or Resource: ZoomText Help). This is a reference for you.</p> <h6 id="submitting-your-exam-1">Submitting Your Exam</h6> <p>When you submit your exam, the exam page closes and you are taken to another web page with your results. From there, you can read your final score percentage and review your scores in each of the different categories. For passing scores, you may choose the link to download your free electronic certificate, or choose the link to go directly to the online store to purchase your printed certificate. For non-passing scores, you may choose the link in the results page to go back to the Certification page for further review.</p> <p>If you do not finish the exam in the allotted time, a dialog appears at the end of 60 minutes and tells you your time is up. Press OK on the dialog button. Your exam will be submitted automatically.</p> <p>When you submit your exam, the exam page closes and you are taken to another web page with your results. From there, you can read your final score percentage and review your scores in each of the different categories. For passing scores you may choose the link in the results page to go directly to the online store to purchase your Certificate. For non-passing scores you may choose the link in the results page to go back to the Certification page for further review.</p> <p>Do you want to share a success story involving your JAWS Certification? We would love to hear from you. <a href="https://support.freedomscientific.com/Forms/ProductExperience">Submit your comments.</a></p> <h5 id="certification-logo-and-inclusion-on-website">Certification Logo and Inclusion on Website</h5> <p>There are separate exams for JAWS and ZoomText. The exam for the selected software is for both the initial Certification as well as Certification Renewals. Taking an exam is free.</p> <p>When you pass the Certification exam, you will automatically receive an electronic certificate and are entitled to be listed on our JAWS or ZoomText Certified Individuals pages. Further instructions will be provided in an email you will receive after passing the exam. Inclusion on this website helps to enhance exposure of certified individuals as knowledgeable in the features and use of JAWS and ZoomText. If you have not yet taken and passed the exam, visit the Certification information page for full details.</p> <p>After passing the exam, you also have the option to purchase an official certificate from Freedom Scientific. JAWS certificates are produced in high-quality print and braille while ZoomText certificates are produced in high-quality print. Additionally, you are granted the right to use the Certification Logo in your correspondence, email signature, or website. Two options exist when making a purchase:</p> <ul> <li>Initial Certification – $49.00. For first-time certifications, you need to purchase the “Initial Certification.”</li> <li>Certification Renewal – $29.00. For successive certifications, you can purchase the “Certification Renewal” at this lower cost. NOTE: Users who purchase the official printed certificate will be validated to ensure they successfully completed the exam. Only individuals that have previously purchased the Initial Certification are eligible to purchase the Renewal Certification.</li> </ul> <h5 id="faqs-1">FAQs</h5> <h6 id="what-if-i-accidentally-close-my-browser-while-taking-the-exam-1">What if I accidentally close my browser while taking the exam?</h6> <p>If your Internet browser closes, or if you have an equipment failure that interrupts your timed exam session, the portion of the exam you took will not be saved. You will have to start the exam again from the beginning.</p> <h6 id="is-it-okay-to-guess-if-i-am-not-sure-of-an-answer-1">Is it okay to guess if I am not sure of an answer?</h6> <p>Yes. If you do not record an answer for an exam question, then that question will be marked incorrect. If you are not sure, you may try eliminating the choices that you know are wrong. You are then left with choices that could be correct. From the remaining choices, select the choice that you think is the best answer.</p> <h6 id="what-if-i-am-in-the-middle-of-answering-a-question-and-the-60-minutes-are-up-can-i-finish-the-question-i-was-working-on-1">What if I am in the middle of answering a question and the 60 minutes are up, can I finish the question I was working on?</h6> <p>No. When the 60 minutes have elapsed, the focus shifts from the exam question you were working on to a dialog telling you your time is up. You will not be able to go back and finish. Please note – make sure you follow the instructions from that point so that your exam results will be saved.</p> <h6 id="do-i-get-a-reminder-of-how-much-time-has-elapsed-1">Do I get a reminder of how much time has elapsed?</h6> <p>At the halfway point, a dialog will appear letting you know that you have 30 minutes remaining in your exam. The time remaining may show on the status bar in Internet Explorer, depending on your security settings. You can read this by pressing INSERT+PAGE DOWN at any time during the exam.</p> <h6 id="are-there-any-short-answer-or-essay-questions-1">Are there any short answer or essay questions?</h6> <p>No. Exam questions are formatted as multiple choices, true or false, and check all that apply.</p> <h6 id="can-i-go-back-and-change-my-answers-1">Can I go back and change my answers?</h6> <p>During the 60 minutes you can go back and change or review your answers. It is recommended that you go back and review your exam if you finish before the time expires, to ensure that you are satisfied with the choices you made.</p> <h6 id="how-do-i-view-my-results-1">How do I view my results?</h6> <p>Your results are available as soon as you submit your exam. After you submit your results, a web page opens with the results page. You will be given an overall score and shown how you scored in each of the categories.</p> <h6 id="how-do-i-submit-my-exam-1">How do I submit my exam?</h6> <p>When you are ready to submit your exam, you must press the Submit button at the end of the exam web page. Please note – if you do not press the Submit button, your exam results will not be saved.</p> <h6 id="at-the-end-of-each-exam-question-there-is-a-resource.-what-does-that-mean-1">At the end of each exam question there is a resource. What does that mean?</h6> <p>The resource tells you which study materials that exam question was taken from. For example, a resource could be listed like this: (Resource: JAWS Help). This reference tells you that the exam question was taken from one of the JAWS F1 Help topics.</p> <h6 id="the-exam-is-85-questions-but-my-overall-score-showed-that-i-had-118-correct-out-of-147.-why-is-the-number-higher-than-85-1">The exam is 85 questions, but my overall score showed that I had 118 correct out of 147. Why is the number higher than 85?</h6> <p>There are 85 questions. The questions are a random selection of multiple choices, true or false, or check all that apply. The “check all that apply” questions are worth more points. Each correct check box is a point. For example, assume you had one “check all that apply” question in your exam and that question had five check boxes. That exam would be scored out of 89 not 85. Note that the exam will have more than one “check all that apply” question.</p> <h6 id="how-many-times-can-i-take-the-exam-1">How many times can I take the exam?</h6> <p>You may take the exam as many times as you wish.</p> <h6 id="does-a-certification-mean-i-can-train-the-product-1">Does a Certification mean I can train the product?</h6> <p>NO, the JAWS Certification does not mean you are capable of training the product. The certification validates your expertise and knowledge of JAWS, but does not in any way confirm your ability to teach the software to other individuals.</p> <p>If your Internet browser closes, or if you have an equipment failure that interrupts your timed exam session, the portion of the exam you took will not be saved. You will have to start the exam again from the beginning.</p> <p>Yes. If you do not record an answer for an exam question, then that question will be marked incorrect. If you are not sure, you may try eliminating the choices that you know are wrong. You are then left with choices that could be correct. From the remaining choices, select the choice that you think is the best answer.</p> <p>No. When the 60 minutes have elapsed, the focus shifts from the exam question you were working on to a dialog telling you your time is up. You will not be able to go back and finish. Please note – make sure you follow the instructions from that point so that your exam results will be saved.</p> <p>At the halfway point, a dialog will appear letting you know that you have 30 minutes remaining in your exam. The time remaining may show on the status bar in Internet Explorer, depending on your security settings. You can read this by pressing INSERT+PAGE DOWN at any time during the exam.</p> <p>No. Exam questions are formatted as multiple choices, true or false, and check all that apply.</p> <p>During the 60 minutes you can go back and change or review your answers. It is recommended that you go back and review your exam if you finish before the time expires, to ensure that you are satisfied with the choices you made.</p> <p>Your results are available as soon as you submit your exam. After you submit your results, a web page opens with the results page. You will be given an overall score and shown how you scored in each of the categories.</p> <p>When you are ready to submit your exam, you must press the Submit button at the end of the exam web page. Please note – if you do not press the Submit button, your exam results will not be saved.</p> <p>The resource tells you which study materials that exam question was taken from. For example, a resource could be listed like this: (Resource: JAWS Help). This reference tells you that the exam question was taken from one of the JAWS F1 Help topics.</p> <p>There are 85 questions. The questions are a random selection of multiple choices, true or false, or check all that apply. The “check all that apply” questions are worth more points. Each correct check box is a point. For example, assume you had one “check all that apply” question in your exam and that question had five check boxes. That exam would be scored out of 89 not 85. Note that the exam will have more than one “check all that apply” question.</p> <p>You may take the exam as many times as you wish.</p> <p>NO, the JAWS Certification does not mean you are capable of training the product. The certification validates your expertise and knowledge of JAWS, but does not in any way confirm your ability to teach the software to other individuals.</p> <ul> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/certification/certification-details/">Certification Details</a></li> </ul> <h3 id="elbraille-40-v-user-guide">ElBraille 40 V User Guide</h3> <h4 id="elbraille-40-v-user-guide-1">ElBraille 40 V User Guide</h4> <h5 id="introduction-2">Introduction</h5> <p>Welcome to your ElBraille, the twenty-first century, take anywhere replacement for the dedicated notetaker. Running Windows 10 with JAWS, and a braille display with a full Braille keyboard, your ElBraille 40 is a fully accessible compact computer.</p> <p>The ElBraille includes the following key features:</p> <ul> <li>Runs Windows 10 64-bit and JAWS</li> <li>Works with Focus 40 Blue 5th Generation Braille display</li> <li>7th generation Intel® Core™ i5-7Y57 Processor with vPro technology Dual-core (4M Cache, up to 3.30 GHz)</li> <li>8 GB RAM</li> <li>128 GB of internal SSD storage</li> <li>Two stereo speakers and headphone/microphone jack</li> <li>Additional sound and vibration feedback for key functions such as powering on and off or connecting or disconnecting the AC adapter</li> <li>SD card slot supporting SD, SDHC, SDXC up to 2 TB</li> <li>2 USB 3.0 ports and 1 USB C port</li> <li>Wireless WLAN802.11 A/B/G/N/AC networks support (2.4 and 5 GHz)</li> <li>Bluetooth V4.2</li> <li>A built-in 4G LTE modem for cellular connectivity supporting AT&T cellular network services</li> <li>Rechargeable 21.5 Amp Hour battery (Approximately 15 hours on battery)</li> <li>Specially designed apps for performing popular actions such as the creation of voice or text notes, listening to audio content, and more</li> <li>Supports Microsoft Office 365, Office 2019, Office 2016, Office 2013, and Office 2010</li> </ul> <h5 id="whats-in-the-box">What’s in the Box?</h5> <ul> <li>ElBraille 40 V unit</li> <li>ElBraille carrying case with a shoulder strap</li> <li>ElBraille AC adapter and universal plug adapters for use in other regions</li> <li>USB flash drive with ElBraille manual in PDF format</li> </ul> <h5 id="physical-layout">Physical Layout</h5> <p>Position the ElBraille on a flat surface so the opening for the braille display is directly in front of you.</p> <p>On the left side, going from the left front corner to the left back corner, you will find a lever for locking and unlocking the Focus Blue braille display.</p> <p>When you place a Focus Blue braille display into ElBraille, pushing the lever in locks the braille display in place. Pulling the lever out unlocks the braille display so it can be removed from ElBraille.</p> <p>On the right side, going from the right front corner to the right back corner, you will find a headphone jack, SD card and Micro-SIM card slots, two standard USB ports, and a USB C port. The Micro-SIM card slot is located directly under the SD card slot and allows you to insert a SIM card from AT&T and use the built-in 4G LTE modem. The USB C port is used for charging the unit as well as connecting the ElBraille to a PC so you can use the Focus 40 Blue as a braille display over USB with another device.</p> <p>The front part of the unit contains the braille display. The internal microphone is located on the very front closest to the left corner.</p> <p>Above the display are eight buttons. Going from left to right, they are; E1, the Volume Down/Up rocker, E2, E3, E4, E5, E6 (also referred to as the Display Connection Mode button), and E7. A recessed Power button is located directly above E1. The LED indicator is located directly above the Power button. The speakers are located to the far left and far right of the E1-E7 buttons. A fan vent is positioned between the E3 and E4 buttons.</p> <h6 id="led-indication-types">LED Indication Types</h6> <p>The following table lists the available LED indicator types.</p> <p>Color</p> <p>Meaning</p> <p>Green</p> <p>The unit is turned on and running on batter</p> <p>Yellow</p> <p>The unit is turned on and plugged into an outlet using the AC adapter</p> <p>Red</p> <p>The unit is turned off and charging</p> <p>No indication</p> <p>The device is turned off and is not charging. If the unit is plugged in, it can also mean the battery is fully charged.</p> <h6 id="docking-and-undocking-the-braille-display">Docking and Undocking the Braille Display</h6> <p>To dock the Focus 40 Blue with the ElBraille, do the following:</p> <ul> <li>Gently pull the locking lever on the left side of the ElBraille until it is fully retracted. Do not attempt to force the lever beyond the point where it stops.</li> <li>Lower the Focus display until it is resting in the open front section of the ElBraille and make sure the back edge of the Focus is flush with the section containing the ElBraille buttons.</li> <li>Push the locking lever to lock the display in place and establish the USB connection. In most cases, you can leave the Focus docked with the ElBraille as you can use it over Bluetooth or even USB with another device and easily switch back to using it with the ElBraille.</li> </ul> <p>If you need to undock the Focus 40 Blue, do the following:</p> <ul> <li>Remove the ElBraille from its carrying case.</li> <li>Gently pull the locking lever on the left side of the ElBraille until it is fully retracted. Do not attempt to force the lever beyond the point where it stops.</li> <li>Slightly lift the left end of the Focus Blue braille display and slide it to the left to release the right connectors and then lift it away from the ElBraille. Important: It is only necessary to slightly lift the left end of the display to remove it. Lifting the left end too high could increase the risk of damage to the locking connectors on the right side of ElBraille as well as the connection points on the Focus Blue.</li> </ul> <p>If the Focus is not docked, you can still operate ElBraille using a standard USB or Bluetooth keyboard as the ElBraille is a full Windows 10 PC.</p> <h6 id="description-of-focus-blue-controls">Description of Focus Blue Controls</h6> <p>The refreshable braille cells are located toward the front of the unit. There is a Cursor Router button above each braille cell.</p> <p>At each end of the display’s surface are NAV Rockers used for easy navigation. Positioned above each NAV Rocker is a NAV mode button which cycles through different navigation modes.</p> <p>Positioned directly above the Cursor Router buttons is an 8-dot Perkins-style braille keyboard. Going from the center, the left-hand keys contain the following: Dot 1 under the index finger, Dot 2 under the middle finger, Dot 3 under the ring finger, and Dot 7 under the little finger, while the right-hand contains: Dot 4 under the index finger, Dot 5 under the middle finger, Dot 6 under the ring finger, and Dot 8 under the little finger. These keys are used to enter text or perform commands.</p> <p>Between Dots 1 and 4 is a Menu button which is used to access the Focus configuration menu as well as display Focus status information during an active connection.</p> <p>On the front edge, directly under and in the center of the display is a SPACEBAR. This key is used together with the braille keys when entering commands. A command that includes the SPACEBAR is commonly referred to as a chorded command. For example, L CHORD or DOTS 1-2-3 CHORD.</p> <p>On the very front of the display are the following controls, located from left to right: Left Panning button, Left Rocker bar, Left Selector button, Left Shift button, Right Shift button, Right Selector button, Right Rocker bar, and Right Panning button. For more information about the Focus Blue controls, refer to the <a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/braille/focus/focus-user-guide/">Focus 40 Blue user guide</a>.</p> <h5 id="overview-of-jaws-braillein">Overview of JAWS BrailleIn</h5> <p>The JAWS BrailleIn feature allows you to use the Perkins-style braille keyboard on the braille display to control ElBraille. Using the keyboard along with other Focus controls, you can perform all Windows and JAWS commands that you can do from a regular QWERTY keyboard. In addition, you can also enter text using contracted or uncontracted braille. For more information about BrailleIn, refer to the BrailleIn topic in the JAWS Help under the JAWS and Refreshable book. Additionally, go to <a href="https://support.freedomscientific.com/Services/TrainingAndCertification/WebinarDetail/F0109">support.freedomscientific.com</a> to access a free webinar demonstrating how to use the BrailleIn feature.</p> <p>Tip: If necessary, you can also use a USB or wireless QWERTY keyboard with the ElBraille.</p> <h6 id="modifier-keys-1">Modifier Keys</h6> <p>Use the keys on the braille display to simulate key combinations (keystrokes) that include CTRL, ALT, WINDOWS Key, SHIFT, or the JAWS Key (INSERT). To use these modifiers when typing a keystroke, do the following:</p> <ul> <li><p>Hold down DOT 8 CHORD and then press the corresponding modifier keys in the keystroke. Modifier keystrokes are listed below.</p></li> <li><p>After you create the modifier portion of the keystroke, release the keys and press the remaining part of the keystroke. For example, to perform the keystroke CTRL+SHIFT+V, you press DOTS 3-7-8 CHORD, release the keys, and then press V (DOTS 1-2-3-6)</p></li> <li><p>Function Keys (F1 through F12): DOT 1</p></li> <li><p>INSERT: DOT 2</p></li> <li><p>CTRL: DOT 3</p></li> <li><p>WINDOWS Key: DOT 4</p></li> <li><p>JAWS Key: DOT 5</p></li> <li><p>ALT: DOT 6</p></li> <li><p>SHIFT: DOT 7 Instead of memorizing these keys by their dot position, it may be easier to learn the finger with which each key would be associated. When all of your fingers are on the braille keyboard, the layout would be:</p></li> <li><p>Function Keys: Left index finger</p></li> <li><p>WINDOWS Key: Right index finger</p></li> <li><p>INSERT: Left middle finger</p></li> <li><p>JAWS Key: Right middle finger</p></li> <li><p>CTRL: Left ring finger</p></li> <li><p>ALT: Right ring finger</p></li> <li><p>SHIFT: Left little finger Notice that you can create a rather loose correlation between pairs of fingers in this description. For example, the left index finger is Function Keys while the right index finger is the WINDOWS key. A stronger correlation can be made with the left and right middle fingers. The left is the JAWS Key and the right is the INSERT key, both often serving the same purpose in JAWS usage. Finally, the left and right ring fingers are the CTRL and ALT keys respectively, which make these two positions easier to remember.</p></li> </ul> <p>Once this layout is understood, it is easy to grasp that Any time a modifier key, or combination of modifier keys is used as part of a command, DOT 8 CHORD will always be included.</p> <p>Finally, pressing any of these modifier keys with DOT 8 CHORD is the same as pressing and holding any of the equivalent keys on the QWERTY keyboard. The computer is waiting for the key or keys which the modifier keys will modify. So, pressing DOTS 3-8 CHORD is the same as pressing the CTRL key. Windows then waits for the key which will complete the CTRL combination, such as the letter A to make CTRL+A to select all, or the letter C to make CTRL+C to copy the selected text to the clipboard. Repetition of frequently used keystrokes such as the CTRL key combinations already mentioned, Windows commands such as WINDOWS Key+M, and JAWS commands such as INSERT+T should imprint these key associations firmly in your memory.</p> <h6 id="function-keys-1">Function Keys</h6> <p>To simulate the function keys (F1 through F12), press DOTS 1-8 CHORD followed by A through L (which correspond to 1 through 12). For example, to simulate the F6 key, press DOTS 1-8 CHORD, then F (DOTS 1-2-4). If the function key is part of a key combination, add the appropriate modifiers while holding down DOTS 1-8 CHORD. For example, to simulate the keystroke INSERT+F2, press DOTS 1-2-8 C.</p> <h5 id="quick-start">Quick Start</h5> <p>Note: Before turning ElBraille on for the first time, fully charge the battery using the supplied AC adapter. The unit emits two ascending tones and vibrates when the AC adapter is connected and emits two descending tones and vibrates when the adapter is disconnected. When the battery is charging, the LED indicator lights up red. It takes approximately five to seven hours to fully charge the unit. Press E2 while the unit is powered on to check the battery charge level.</p> <h6 id="turning-on-elbraille">Turning On ElBraille</h6> <p>To turn on the ElBraille, press and hold the recessed Power button located directly above E1 until the unit beeps and vibrates. During the startup process, you will hear a series of short beeps and feel occasional vibrations. Once the device has booted, you will hear JAWS speaking and the display will show some text. Finally, you will be placed on the Windows Desktop.</p> <h6 id="turning-off-or-restarting-elbraille">Turning Off or Restarting ElBraille</h6> <p>To put the ElBraille to sleep, completely shut down, or restart, do the following:</p> <ul> <li>Press WINDOWS Key+X (DOTS 4-8 CHORD followed by DOTS 1-3-4-6) to open the Quick Link menu.</li> <li>Press U (DOTS 1-3-6) to open the Shut down or sign out submenu.</li> <li>Use the Left Rocker bar to select an option and then press DOT 8. If you decide to continue working, press Z CHORD (DOTS 1-3-5-6+SPACEBAR) to cancel. You can also press the Power button to put ElBraille to sleep. Press the Power button again to wake the unit up and resume working where you left off.</li> </ul> <p>Note: Shutting down or restarting can take some time. Please wait for the beeps and vibration alerts indicating the device is turned on or turned off.</p> <h6 id="elbraille-rescue-menu">ElBraille Rescue Menu</h6> <p>Sometimes, it may be necessary to shut down or restart if the device is not working correctly. For example, you unexpectedly lost speech or braille output from JAWS. You can easily do this using the ElBraille Rescue menu. This menu provides speech and braille output even if JAWS is not currently working correctly.</p> <p>To open the Rescue menu, press and hold the E1 button. You will hear a beep followed by a menu containing three items: Restart JAWS, Shut Down, and System Reboot. Use the NAV Rockers to navigate the menu and press a NAV Mode button to activate the selected item. To close the menu, press RIGHT SHIFT+DOT 1. Alternatively, you can use the Volume Up/Down rocker to navigate, the E4 button to activate an item, or E1 to close the menu.</p> <p>Note: Use the Rescue menu only when absolutely necessary as shutting down or restarting from this menu will not guarantee anything you are currently working on is saved. In addition, if JAWS speech is currently working, you will hear double speaking as the speech in this menu is independent from JAWS.</p> <h6 id="braille-display-modes">Braille Display Modes</h6> <p>By default, when the Focus 40 Blue is docked, it works as a braille display with ElBraille. However, it can also be used as a stand-alone Focus 40 Blue that can be connected to a PC using the USB C port on the side of the ElBraille or used as a Bluetooth device.</p> <p>To hear the current braille display mode, press E6. To switch between modes, press and hold E6 until you hear a brief tone.</p> <p>When the ElBraille is on, switching the braille display mode will turn the display off.</p> <p>If you connect the ElBraille to a PC using the USB C port on the right side of the unit, the braille display mode automatically switches to the PC connection, and the Focus 40 Blue acts like a stand-alone display. You can then press and hold E6 to toggle the Focus between the ElBraille and PC connection. When you disconnect from USB, the braille display mode automatically switches back to the ElBraille connection.</p> <p>If the ElBraille is off, the display operates as if it was a stand-alone Focus 40 Blue, and the ElBraille buttons do nothing.</p> <p>Note: The ElBraille will charge when connected to a computer through the USB C port as long as the ElBraille is turned off. However, charging time will take longer than with the supplied AC adapter.</p> <h6 id="viewing-device-status-information">Viewing Device Status Information</h6> <p>Use the ElBraille buttons at any time to check the battery status, network connection, or the time and date.</p> <ul> <li>To check the battery status, press E2.</li> <li>To view wireless network status information, press E2 twice quickly.</li> <li>To view the current time, press E3.</li> <li>To view the current date, press E3 twice quickly.</li> </ul> <h6 id="default-elbraille-key-assignments">Default ElBraille Key Assignments</h6> <p>Following is a list of the default assignments for the ElBraille buttons.</p> <ul> <li>E1: Open ElBraille Main menu</li> <li>E1 (press and hold): Open ElBraille Rescue menu</li> <li>E2: Report battery status</li> <li>E2 (twice quickly): Report wireless network connection status</li> <li>E3: Report current time</li> <li>E3 (twice quickly): Report current date</li> <li>E4: Start ElNotes or create a text note</li> <li>E4 (press and hold): Record a voice note</li> <li>E5: Not assigned</li> <li>E6: Report current braille display mode</li> <li>E6 (press and hold): Toggle the braille display mode</li> <li>E7: Not assigned Note: You can modify the default key assignment for each button except for E6.</li> </ul> <h6 id="elbraille-main-menu">ElBraille Main Menu</h6> <p>The ElBraille main menu turns your device into a convenient notetaker. From this menu, you can quickly accomplish many useful daily tasks, such as writing notes or using the calculator.</p> <p>To open the ElBraille main menu, press E1. This menu contains a number of items including:</p> <ul> <li>My Files — opens Windows Explorer.</li> <li>Text Editor — opens Windows Notepad.</li> <li>Office Apps submenu — if you have purchased and installed Microsoft Office, opens a submenu listing the installed Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint).</li> <li>Calculator — opens Windows Calculator.</li> <li>Keyboard Editor — located in the ElBraille Utilities submenu, the ElBraille Keyboard editor is a specially designed application for adding, modifying, and deleting ElBraille keystroke assignments. Use the Rocker bars to navigate through the menu and press DOT 8 to activate an item. Each menu item also offers a corresponding access key you can press to quickly select it. These access keys are announced by JAWS as you navigate.</li> </ul> <p>For example, you can use this menu to create a text file by doing the following:</p> <ul> <li>Press E1, and then press E (DOTS 1-5). The text editor opens.</li> <li>Type in your text.</li> <li>To save the file, press CTRL+S (DOTS 3-8 CHORD, followed by DOTS 2-3-4). The Save File dialog box opens.</li> <li>Type in the file name and navigate to the Save button by using DOTS 4-5 CHORD, and then press DOT 8.</li> <li>To close the text editor, press ALT+F4 (DOTS 1-6-8 CHORD, followed by DOTS 1-4-5). For more information on working in an application, refer to the help for the specific application.</li> </ul> <h5 id="basics-of-working-with-jaws-and-windows-on-elbraille">Basics of Working with JAWS and Windows on ElBraille</h5> <h6 id="windows-basics">Windows Basics</h6> <p>Using Windows with JAWS on the ElBraille is basically the same as using a regular Windows PC. The only difference is that with ElBraille, commands are performed using the ElBraille buttons and the Focus Blue controls. The following describes how to access some of the more frequently used Windows features. For more information, see the help for Windows as well as the JAWS Help.</p> <h6 id="the-start-menu">The Start Menu</h6> <p>To open the Start menu, press RIGHT SHIFT+DOT 4. You will be focused in the Search edit box where you can begin typing the name of an app or setting you want to find. Press a Rocker bar to navigate the list of search results and press DOT 8 to select one.</p> <p>To view the list of frequently used apps, configure your account, view all apps, or turn off the device, press TAB or SHIFT+TAB (DOTS 4-5 CHORD or DOTS 1-2 CHORD) to navigate through the Start menu. Use a Rocker bar to move through list boxes and dropdown menus. Press DOT 8 to activate the selected item or to activate a button.</p> <p>To close the Start menu, press DOTS 1-3-5-6 CHORD.</p> <h6 id="working-with-windows-and-dialog-boxes">Working With Windows and Dialog Boxes</h6> <p>Windows dialog boxes can contain text information as well as various controls including check boxes, radio buttons, buttons, sliders, edit fields, and so on.</p> <p>To read the window title, simultaneously press the top of the Left and Right Rocker bars. To read the status bar, simultaneously press the bottom of the Left and Right Rocker bars. To read the contents of the dialog box, press RIGHT SHIFT+DOTS 1-2.</p> <p>To move between dialog box controls, press TAB or SHIFT+TAB (DOTS 4-5 CHORD or DOTS 1-2 CHORD). You can select a radio button, or select or clear a check box by using the SPACEBAR or a Cursor Router button. To activate a button, press the SPACEBAR, DOT 8, or a Cursor Router button. When focused in an edit field, enter text using the Perkins-style braille keys. To adjust the value in a slider, press a Rocker bar to move by small increments or press a Rocker bar in conjunction with a Selector button to move by larger increments. If the dialog box contains multiple pages (tabs), press DOTS 5-6 CHORD or DOTS 2-3 CHORD to move between the tabs.</p> <p>You can have several applications open at once. The JAWS Window List dialog box enables you to switch quickly between running apps. To open the Window List dialog box, press RIGHT SHIFT+DOT 5. Use the Rocker bars to move through the list of running applications and press DOT 8 to switch to the selected app.</p> <p>For more information, please refer to the JAWS help system.</p> <h6 id="entering-data">Entering Data</h6> <p>Use the Perkins-style braille keyboard to type text on ElBraille. You can enter text in computer braille, or contracted or uncontracted braille. If you choose to type in contracted braille, your input is immediately translated back as normal text in the current email, document, or form. If an application or specific edit box does not support contracted braille, JAWS announces “Computer Braille.” In addition, the computer braille start symbol, dots 4-5-6 followed by dots 3-4-6, is shown on the braille display to indicate when computer braille is required. For more information, refer to the JAWS Help.</p> <p>You can write and edit text not only in text editing applications, but also in edit fields in Windows dialog boxes as well as forms on web pages. In all cases, the commands for editing text are the same. To start a new line, use DOT 8. To backspace and remove the previous character, use DOT 7. To delete the character under the cursor, use LEFT SHIFT+D (DOTS 1-4-5) or DOTS 1-2-3-4-5-6 CHORD.</p> <h6 id="basic-reading-and-navigation-commands">Basic Reading and Navigation Commands</h6> <p>Description</p> <p>Keystroke</p> <p>Say Current Line</p> <p>C CHORD (DOTS 1-4 CHORD)</p> <p>Say Previous Line</p> <p>DOT 1 CHORD</p> <p>Say Next Line</p> <p>DOT 4 CHORD</p> <p>Say Current Word</p> <p>DOTS 2-5 CHORD</p> <p>Say Previous Word</p> <p>DOT 2 CHORD</p> <p>Say Next Word</p> <p>DOT 5 CHORD</p> <p>Say Current Character</p> <p>DOTS 3-6 CHORD</p> <p>Say Previous character</p> <p>DOT 3 CHORD</p> <p>Say Next Character</p> <p>DOT 6 CHORD</p> <p>Say All</p> <p>DOTS 1-2-4-5-6 CHORD</p> <h6 id="windows-explorer">Windows Explorer</h6> <p>To open Windows Explorer, press E1, and then select My Files or press the letter F (DOTS 1-2-4). Use the Rocker bars to navigate the list of files and folders and press DOT 8 to open the selected item. To go back to the previous folder, press DOT 7.</p> <h6 id="other-common-commands">Other Common Commands</h6> <p>Description</p> <p>Command</p> <p>Copy to Clipboard</p> <p>LEFT SHIFT+C (DOTS 1-4)</p> <p>Cut to Clipboard</p> <p>LEFT SHIFT+X (DOTS 1-3-4-6)</p> <p>Paste from Clipboard</p> <p>LEFT SHIFT+V (DOTS 1-2-3-6)</p> <p>Undo</p> <p>LEFT SHIFT+Z (DOTS 1-3-5-6)</p> <p>Delete</p> <p>LEFT SHIFT+D (DOTS 1-4-5)</p> <h6 id="common-qwerty-keyboard-keys-simulated-on-the-braille-display">Common QWERTY Keyboard Keys Simulated on the Braille Display</h6> <p>QWERTY Keystroke</p> <p>Braille Keystroke</p> <p>ESC</p> <p>Z CHORD (DOTS 1-3-5-6 CHORD) or RIGHT SHIFT+DOT 1</p> <p>ALT (activates the menu bar in an application)</p> <p>RIGHT SHIFT+DOT 2</p> <p>APPLICATIONS Key</p> <p>RIGHT SHIFT+DOT 2 CHORD</p> <p>WINDOWS Key (activates the Windows Start menu)</p> <p>RIGHT SHIFT+DOT 4</p> <p>CAPS LOCK</p> <p>RIGHT SHIFT+DOT 7 CHORD</p> <p>BACKSPACE</p> <p>DOT 7</p> <p>ENTER</p> <p>DOT 8</p> <p>TAB</p> <p>DOTS 4-5 CHORD</p> <p>SHIFT+TAB</p> <p>DOTS 1-2 CHORD</p> <p>DOTS 1-3 CHORD</p> <p>END</p> <p>DOTS 4-6 CHORD</p> <p>PAGE UP</p> <p>Selector Button+Rocker Bar Up or DOTS 2-3-7 CHORD</p> <p>PAGE DOWN</p> <p>Selector Button+Rocker Bar Down or DOTS 5-6-7 CHORD</p> <p>DELETE</p> <p>DOTS 1-2-3-4-5-6 CHORD or LEFT SHIFT+D (DOTS 1-4-5)</p> <h6 id="basic-jaws-setup">Basic JAWS Setup</h6> <p>ElBraille users have access to all JAWS features, just like on a standard Windows PC. This section covers some basic information to help you get started. For more information about working with JAWS, refer to the JAWS help system. To open JAWS Help, press RIGHT SHIFT+DOTS 2-4-5 to open the JAWS main window, H to open the Help menu, and then J.</p> <h6 id="jaws-startup-wizard">JAWS Startup Wizard</h6> <p>The JAWS Startup Wizard allows you to customize some of the more commonly used JAWS settings. These include speech rate and verbosity, typing echo, braille translation settings, and more. The Startup Wizard can be accessed at any time by doing the following:</p> <ul> <li>Press RIGHT SHIFT+DOTS 2-4-5 to open the JAWS main window.</li> <li>Use a Rocker bar to navigate to the Help menu and press DOT 8.</li> <li>When the Help menu opens, press Z (DOTS 1-3-5-6) to open the Startup Wizard. The Startup Wizard consists of several pages of options. After making your changes on each page, choose the Next button to move to the next page in the wizard. On the last page, choose the Finish button to save your changes.</li> </ul> <p>Tip: If you do not want to change any options on a particular page, pressing DOT 8 activates the Next or Finish button by default so you do not have to navigate through several options to locate this button.</p> <h6 id="turning-off-speech">Turning off Speech</h6> <p>If you prefer to only use the braille display, you can limit the amount of speech you hear or completely turn it off by using the RIGHT SHIFT+M (DOTS 1-3-4) command.</p> <p>By default, pressing RIGHT SHIFT+M activates Speech On Demand which restricts speech to a limited set of reading keystrokes. Speech On Demand is ideal for braille users who find too much speech overwhelming, but still want speech for certain tasks like reading a window title, checking the time, or speaking the current character, line, sentence, paragraph, or doing a Say All. While Speech On Demand is active, press INSERT+SPACEBAR (DOTS 2-8 CHORD followed by SPACEBAR) and then SHIFT+S (DOTS 2-3-4-7) to completely mute speech. Press RIGHT SHIFT+M again to switch back to full speech.</p> <p>If you want the RIGHT SHIFT+M command to toggle between full speech and completely muting speech, open Settings Center, expand the Speech Options group, and set the Less Speech Options item to Mute Speech. For more information about Speech on Demand, please refer to the JAWS Help.</p> <h5 id="connecting-to-a-network">Connecting to a Network</h5> <p>ElBraille can connect to wireless networks. You can also connect the unit to mobile networks using the built-in LTE modem. The following sections describe how to connect to these networks.</p> <h6 id="connecting-to-a-wi-fi-network">Connecting to a Wi-Fi Network</h6> <ul> <li>Press WINDOWS Key+I (DOTS 4-8 CHORD, DOTS 2-4) to open Windows Settings.</li> <li>Navigate to Network and Internet and press DOT 8.</li> <li>Select Wi-Fi and press DOT 8.</li> <li>Select the Show available networks link and then navigate to the list of available networks.</li> <li>Use the Left Rocker bar to select the network you want to connect to and press DOT 8. The Connect Automatically check box and the Connect button will appear. The check box is selected by default. If you want to connect to the network only once, clear this check box.</li> <li>Press DOTS 4-5 CHORD to navigate to the Connect button and press DOT 8 again. If the network is secure, you are prompted to enter a password.</li> <li>Type in the password and press DOT 8. If the connection is successful, you will see “Connected” near the selected network in the networks list.</li> </ul> <h6 id="connecting-to-a-mobile-network">Connecting to a Mobile Network</h6> <p>Before you can connect to an AT&T cellular network to use its data, you must first turn on the ElBraille’s internal modem by doing the following:</p> <ul> <li><p>Press E1 followed by U to open the ElBraille Utilities menu.</p></li> <li><p>Use the Left Rocker bar to navigate to Settings and press DOT 8.</p></li> <li><p>Select Modem and press SPACEBAR to enable it.</p></li> <li><p>Navigate to the OK button and press DOT 8. In the United States or Canada, most cellular carriers will need the International Mobile Equipment Identification (IMEI) number of your ElBraille to activate the SIM card for use on the carrier’s network. To get the ElBraille’s IMEI number and register the unit on your carrier’s network, do the following:</p></li> <li><p>Press WINDOWS Key+X (DOTS 4-8 CHORD, DOTS 1-3-4-6) to open the Quick Link menu.</p></li> <li><p>Select “Windows PowerShell (Admin)”, making sure to select the Admin one in the list.</p></li> <li><p>Type “netsh mbn show interface | Clip” without the quotes and press DOT 8. The value of the “device ID” parameter is displayed as well as copied to the Windows Clipboard. This is the IMEI of your ElBraille’s modem. Make sure to paste this into a document and save it.</p></li> <li><p>Type “exit” without the quotes and press DOT 8 to close PowerShell.</p></li> <li><p>Provide this IMEI number to your cell carrier in order to register the ElBraille on their network.</p></li> <li><p>Hold the activated SIM card, with the angled corner facing away from you and to the right, and insert it into the Micro-Sim slot on the right side of the unit under the SD card slot until it clicks into place. (The cellular account must have available data.) Once the SIM card is inserted, the ElBraille should automatically switch to your cellular network when a Wi-Fi connection is not available. To make sure the ElBraille can use your cellular network, do the following:</p></li> <li><p>Press WINDOWS Key+I (DOTS 4-8 CHORD, DOTS 2-4) to open Windows Settings.</p></li> <li><p>Navigate to Network and Internet and press DOT 8.</p></li> <li><p>In the Network and Internet list box, navigate to Cellular and press DOT 8.</p></li> <li><p>Verify the name of your cellular provider as AT&T and that ElBraille indicates “Connected”.</p></li> <li><p>Press ALT+F4 (DOTS 1-6-8 CHORD, DOTS 1-4-5) to close Settings.</p></li> </ul> <h5 id="troubleshooting">Troubleshooting</h5> <p>Problem</p> <p>Solution</p> <p>The device will not turn on.</p> <p>Charge the battery using the supplied AC adapter. If the battery is too low, the unit may not boot even when connected to the charger. Wait several minutes and then try turning the unit on again.</p> <p>The battery is not charging or is taking longer to charge than expected.</p> <p>Make sure you are using the charger supplied with the device. If the battery is charging, the LED indicator glows red.</p> <p>Extra dots are appearing on the display and dots are sticking.</p> <p>Clean the display as described in the <a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/braille/focus/focus-user-guide/">Focus 40 Blue user guide</a>.</p> <h5 id="service-and-support">Service and Support</h5> <p>You can contact Technical Support to receive technical assistance.</p> <p>To contact by web, visit www.FreedomScientific.com/Forms/TechSupport, and complete the form to submit questions.</p> <p>To contact by email, send questions to [email protected].</p> <p>To contact by telephone, U.S. customers can call (727) 803-8600, Monday through Friday, from 8:30 AM to 7:00 PM (Eastern Time).</p> <p>When you call, please provide the following information:</p> <ul> <li>Product name</li> <li>Product serial number</li> <li>What you were doing when the problem occurred</li> <li>How you tried to solve the problem</li> </ul> <h6 id="locating-the-elbraille-serial-number">Locating the ElBraille Serial Number</h6> <ul> <li>Press E1 followed by U to open the ElBraille Utilities menu.</li> <li>Use the Left Rocker bar to navigate to About and press DOT 8.</li> <li>Press P until you reach the serial number.</li> </ul> <h6 id="warranty-and-registration">Warranty and Registration</h6> <p>Congratulations on your purchase of the ElBraille.</p> <p>The unit and its accessories come with a two-year warranty against manufacturing defects.</p> <p>Note: These devices have no user-serviceable components. Any unauthorized attempt to service or replace internal components by opening the case will void the product warranty.</p> <p>Please call Technical Support at (727) 803-8600 for assistance in troubleshooting any problems. If necessary, the technical support specialist will issue a Return Materials Authorization (RMA) number that must be referenced on the outside of the package containing your returned unit.
