The unit or its accessory will then be exchanged or repaired as needed.</p> <ul> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/braille/elbraille/elbraille-40-v-user-guide/">ElBraille 40 V User Guide</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/braille/elbraille/elbraille-faqs/">ElBraille FAQs</a></li> </ul> <h3 id="elbraille-faqs">ElBraille FAQs</h3> <h4 id="elbraille-faqs-1">ElBraille FAQs</h4> <h5 id="is-the-elbraille-a-standalone-computer">Is the ElBraille a standalone computer?</h5> <p>The ElBraille is a Windows 10 computer that is designed to seamlessly dock with a Focus 40 Blue 5th generation braille display to provide a compact and portable solution similar in appearance to other braille notetakers.</p> <h5 id="what-makes-the-elbraille-different-from-other-blindness-notetakers-on-the-market">What makes the ElBraille different from other blindness notetakers on the market?</h5> <p>Instead of featuring a heavily customized interface built on top of an operating system, the ElBraille is a complete Windows 10 PC that uses JAWS® for speech and braille output. While the ElBraille does offer some customization, including a special menu providing shortcuts to commonly used Windows apps and a specially designed application for taking notes, you can also run the same Windows 10 applications that you use on a desktop PC.</p> <h5 id="i-do-not-use-braille-at-all-and-rely-entirely-on-speech.-would-i-benefit-at-all-from-an-elbraille">I do not use braille at all and rely entirely on speech. Would I benefit at all from an ElBraille?</h5> <p>If you rely solely on speech and have no plans to learn braille, it may be more cost-effective to purchase an off-the-shelf laptop or tablet computer and install JAWS on it.</p> <h5 id="is-it-worth-getting-an-elbraille-if-i-am-still-learning-to-read-braille-and-use-the-perkins-style-keyboard-on-the-focus-display">Is it worth getting an ElBraille if I am still learning to read braille and use the Perkins-style keyboard on the Focus display?</h5> <p>Even if you do not consider yourself proficient with reading Braille or using the Perkins-style keyboard, having access to a full Windows computer running JAWS that offers the portability of a braille notetaker can be beneficial. The ElBraille will help improve your braille skills.</p> <p>You can choose whether JAWS sends its output as plain text (computer braille), uncontracted, or contracted braille based on your level of expertise. JAWS also offers a feature called Braille Study Mode, which is a tool for learning Braille symbols and contractions.</p> <p>If you are working with a sighted instructor , you can connect to a monitor. This allows you to enter text into an application like Microsoft Word using the braille keyboard, and the instructor can see the text as it is typed to confirm you are entering it correctly. Your instructor can also use the JAWS Braille Viewer, a utility that provides on-screen textual representation of the output received on a refreshable braille display.</p> <h5 id="the-elbraille-seems-expensive-how-can-i-try-to-get-one">The ElBraille seems expensive, how can I try to get one?</h5> <p>Depending on where you live and your employment status, state or federal agencies may be able to assist with the purchase of the ElBraille 40. Also, some companies are willing to help with the purchase to accommodate their employees.</p> <p>If you are a teacher or parent of a student who uses Braille, you could approach your local school district or university about purchasing the ElBraille. Non-profit groups also help obtain assistive technology for qualifying individuals.</p> <p>The ElBraille features a tiered pricing structure, depending on which products you currently own.</p> <ul> <li>If you purchase the full ElBraille 40 package which includes the ElBraille unit, Focus 40 Blue 5th generation braille display, and a JAWS license, the total cost is comparable to other 32 and 40 cell braille notetakers.</li> <li>If you already have a JAWS license, then you only pay for the ElBraille unit and Focus Blue display. This lowers your cost a bit, as you will activate your current JAWS license on the ElBraille.</li> <li>If you already have a JAWS license and a Focus 40 Blue 5th generation braille display, the cost is significantly lower as you only need to purchase the ElBraille itself. Once you receive the ElBraille, you will dock it with your Focus display and activate your JAWS license on the unit.</li> </ul> <h5 id="my-student-currently-has-a-focus-40-blue-5th-generation-braille-display-but-also-needs-a-portable-device-for-taking-notes-in-the-classroom-and-at-home.-would-the-elbraille-be-a-good-solution">My student currently has a Focus 40 Blue 5th generation Braille Display, but also needs a portable device for taking notes in the classroom and at home. Would the ElBraille be a good solution?</h5> <p>Yes, there would be no need to purchase a separate notetaking device. All you need to do is dock your student’s Focus 40 display into the ElBraille, activate a JAWS license on the unit, and your student will have a fully portable computer with access to the same applications as their sighted piers for collaborating in the classroom or completing assignments at home. If assistance is required from a sighted teacher or parent, a USB or wireless keyboard along with a monitor can be connected and the ElBraille used just like any Windows computer.</p> <h5 id="if-i-currently-do-not-have-a-focus-40-blue-5th-generation-braille-display-can-i-still-use-the-elbraille">If I currently do not have a Focus 40 Blue 5th Generation Braille Display, can I still use the ElBraille?</h5> <p>Technically, you could connect a standard USB or wireless QWERTY keyboard to the ElBraille and use it like any Windows computer. However, this would defeat the primary purpose of the ElBraille, which is controlled directly from the Focus display and docks inside the unit for maximum portability. If you are not interested in using a braille display, it would be more cost effective to just purchase an off-the-shelf laptop and install JAWS on it.</p> <h5 id="do-you-have-a-concise-overview-of-the-layout-of-the-ports-and-buttons-on-the-elbraille">Do you have a concise overview of the layout of the ports and buttons on the ElBraille?</h5> <p>See the <a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/braille/elbraille/elbraille-40-v-user-guide/">ElBraille User’s Guide</a> for the location of ports and controls.</p> <h5 id="does-the-elbraille-come-with-a-carrying-case">Does the ElBraille come with a carrying case?</h5> <p>The ElBraille comes with a carrying case and a shoulder strap.</p> <h5 id="can-the-elbraille-be-used-while-in-the-carrying-case">Can the ElBraille be used while in the carrying case?</h5> <p>Yes. All ports and controls on the ElBraille and Focus display can be accessed while the unit is in the carrying case. The only time you need to remove the ElBraille from the case is when you need to undock the Focus display.</p> <h5 id="is-there-an-elbraille-model-that-will-dock-with-the-focus-14-or-focus-80-blue-braille-display">Is there an ElBraille model that will dock with the Focus 14 or Focus 80 Blue braille display?</h5> <p>Not currently.</p> <h5 id="i-have-an-older-focus-40-blue-display-that-is-not-a-5th-generation-model.-can-i-use-it-with-the-elbraille">I have an older Focus 40 Blue display that is not a 5th generation model. Can I use it with the ElBraille?</h5> <p>No. The ElBraille has been specifically designed to dock with the Focus 40 Blue 5th generation Braille Display.</p> <h5 id="what-type-of-processor-does-the-elbraille-use">What type of processor does the ElBraille use?</h5> <p>The ElBraille contains a 7th generation Intel® Core™ i5-7Y57 Processor with vPro technology Dual-core (4M Cache, up to 3.30 GHz).</p> <h5 id="how-much-memory-ram-does-the-elbraille-offer">How much memory (RAM) does the ElBraille offer?</h5> <p>The ElBraille has 8 GB of RAM.</p> <h5 id="how-much-internal-storage-does-elbraille-offer">How much internal storage does ElBraille offer?</h5> <p>The ElBraille includes a 128 GB solid state drive (SSD) for internal storage.</p> <h5 id="can-i-connect-my-elbraille-to-a-wireless-network-or-use-it-with-my-cellular-provider">Can I connect my ElBraille to a wireless network or use it with my cellular provider?</h5> <p>The ElBraille supports wireless WLAN802.11 A/B/G/N/AC networks using both 2.4 and 5 GHz.</p> <p>The ElBraille also includes a built-in 4G LTE modem for cellular connectivity. Currently, only the AT&T cellular network is supported.</p> <p>The <a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/braille/elbraille/elbraille-40-v-user-guide/">ElBraille User Guide</a> contains instructions for connecting to both wireless and cellular networks.</p> <h5 id="can-i-connect-a-monitor-to-elbraille-for-visual-output">Can I connect a monitor to ElBraille for visual output?</h5> <p>You can connect the ElBraille to an HDMI monitor over a Windows Miracast Wi-Fi connection using an optional HDMI dongle (not included).</p> <h5 id="can-i-use-a-standard-wireless-or-usb-keyboard-to-operate-the-elbraille">Can I use a standard wireless or USB keyboard to operate the ElBraille?</h5> <p>Yes. You can use a standard QWERTY keyboard to operate the ElBraille just as you would with any other Windows computer.</p> <h5 id="can-i-connect-the-elbraille-to-bluetooth-devices-such-as-headphones-or-external-speakers">Can I connect the ElBraille to Bluetooth devices such as headphones or external speakers??</h5> <p>The ElBraille supports Bluetooth V4.2 and can be paired with most devices, including a keyboard, mouse, headphones, and external speakers.</p> <h5 id="how-do-i-dock-and-undock-the-focus-40-blue-with-the-elbraille">How do I dock and undock the Focus 40 Blue with the ElBraille?</h5> <p>You can find complete instructions along with pictures on docking or undocking the Focus 40 Blue in the <a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/braille/elbraille/elbraille-40-v-user-guide/">ElBraille User Guide</a>.</p> <h5 id="once-the-focus-40-blue-is-docked-with-the-elbraille-can-i-still-use-the-display-with-other-devices-such-as-my-phone">Once the Focus 40 Blue is docked with the ElBraille, can I still use the display with other devices such as my phone?</h5> <p>There are several ways to do this. One of the fastest is to press and hold the Menu button on the Focus display and then press DOT 1 through DOT 5 to switch to one of the five Bluetooth connections, or press DOT 8 to switch to the USB connection. For example, if you want to switch to displaying information from your iPhone and this is your only Bluetooth device paired with your Focus, press and hold the Menu button and then press DOT 1 to switch to your phone. When you are done, press and hold the Menu button and then press DOT 8 to switch back to the ElBraille connection. For more information, refer to the <a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/braille/focus/focus-user-guide/">Focus User Guide</a>.</p> <p>You can also use the Focus Blue as a braille display for another computer while still docked in the ElBraille. To do this, connect the ElBraille to another computer using the USB-C port located toward the back on the right side of the unit. Once connected to another PC, press and hold the E6 button to toggle the Focus between the ElBraille and the other PC connection. Pressing E6 announces the current braille display connection status. Refer to the <a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/braille/elbraille/elbraille-40-v-user-guide/">ElBraille User Guide</a> for more information.</p> <h5 id="can-i-still-use-focus-blue-features-such-as-the-scratchpad-while-docked-with-the-elbraille">Can I still use Focus Blue features such as the Scratchpad while docked with the ElBraille?</h5> <p>You can activate the Focus Scratchpad at any time by pressing and holding the Menu button and then pressing the letter N (DOTS 1-3-4-5). You can also press the Menu button once to display the Focus status message and once more to open the display’s configuration menu where you can configure Focus specific features. For more information on using the Scratchpad and other functions, refer to the <a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/braille/focus/focus-user-guide/">Focus Blue User Guide</a>.</p> <h5 id="how-do-i-charge-my-elbraille">How do I charge my ElBraille?</h5> <p>Use the included AC adapter to charge the ElBraille. The unit emits two ascending tones and vibrates when the AC adapter is connected and emits two descending tones and vibrates when the adapter is disconnected. It takes approximately five to seven hours to fully charge the unit. If the ElBraille is on, press the E2 button to check the battery charge level.</p> <h5 id="does-the-elbraille-provide-any-feedback-to-indicate-when-it-is-powering-up-or-shutting-down">Does the ElBraille provide any feedback to indicate when it is powering up or shutting down?</h5> <p>Yes. You will receive vibration alerts as well as auditory beeps as the ElBraille boots up or shuts down.</p> <h5 id="how-long-will-the-elbraille-run-before-it-needs-to-be-recharged">How long will the ElBraille run before it needs to be recharged?</h5> <p>From a full charge, you should get approximately 15 hours for typical usage. This would easily get you through a full school or workday.</p> <h5 id="can-i-use-external-storage-such-as-sd-cards-or-external-hard-drives-with-the-elbraille">Can I use external storage such as SD cards or external hard drives with the ElBraille?</h5> <p>You can use the two USB 3.0 ports on the ElBraille to connect a thumb drive or external hard drive. The ElBraille also includes an SD card slot which supports SD, SDHC, and SDXC memory cards up to 2 TB capacity.</p> <h5 id="what-can-i-do-if-i-unexpectedly-lose-speech-and-braille-while-using-the-elbraille">What can I do if I unexpectedly lose speech and braille while using the ElBraille?</h5> <p>The ElBraille offers a Rescue menu, which provides speech and braille output even if JAWS is not currently working correctly. To open the Rescue menu, press and hold the E1 button. You will hear a beep followed by a menu containing three items: Restart JAWS, Shut Down, and System Reboot.</p> <p>Use the NAV Rockers to navigate the menu and press the LEFT NAV Mode button to activate the selected item.</p> <p>To close the menu, press RIGHT SHIFT+DOT 1.</p> <p>Alternatively, you can use the Volume Up/Down rocker to navigate, the E4 button to activate an item, or E1 to close the menu.</p> <h5 id="when-i-first-receive-the-elbraille-will-i-need-to-install-jaws">When I first receive the ElBraille, will I need to install JAWS?</h5> <p>JAWS will already be installed on the ElBraille when you receive it, but it will run in 40-minute mode. You will need to activate your JAWS license on the ElBraille.</p> <p>To activate JAWS, make sure your ElBraille is connected to the Internet, navigate to the JAWS Help menu, expand the License submenu, and then do one of the following depending on your license:</p> <ul> <li>If you have an annual license, select Manage License on Portal to open the Freedom Scientific Licensing Portal where you can log in and activate a license on your ElBraille.</li> <li>If you have a perpetual ILM license, select Update Activation and follow the prompts to activate an ILM license on your ElBraille.</li> </ul> <h5 id="what-is-jaws-braillein">What is JAWS BrailleIn?</h5> <p>BrailleIn™ is a feature that allows you to use the Perkins-style keyboard on your Focus 40 Blue braille display to control the ElBraille. It is the primary method for operating the unit. All Windows and JAWS commands you would typically perform on a regular QWERTY keyboard can be executed using the keyboard and other controls on the Focus.</p> <p>You can also enter text in relevant computer applications using contracted and uncontracted braille. For more information on BrailleIn, refer to the <a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/braille/focus/braille-commands/">Braille Commands web page</a>.</p> <h5 id="what-is-a-chord-command">What is a chord command?</h5> <p>A chord is a command executed by pressing one or more keys simultaneously with the spacebar.</p> <h5 id="is-there-a-keyboard-help-mode-i-can-activate-that-will-help-me-learn-braille-commands">Is there a keyboard help mode I can activate that will help me learn braille commands?</h5> <p>Yes. Press QUESTION MARK CHORD (DOTS 1-4-5-6) simultaneously with the SPACEBAR to turn on JAWS Keyboard Help Mode. You can then press any of the Focus controls or key combinations to learn what they do.</p> <p>You can also use JAWS Command Search to find specific commands. Press INSERT+SPACEBAR followed by J (DOT 8 CHORD, followed by the SPACEBAR, and then J) to run Command Search, then type the command you’d like to find.</p> <h5 id="is-it-possible-to-turn-off-jaws-speech-and-only-use-braille">Is it possible to turn off JAWS speech and only use braille?</h5> <p>By default, pressing RIGHT SHIFT+M activates Speech On Demand, which restricts speech to a limited set of JAWS reading keystrokes. Speech On Demand is ideal for braille users who find too much speech overwhelming, but still want speech for certain tasks like reading a window title, checking the time, speaking the current character, line, sentence, or paragraph.</p> <p>While Speech On Demand is active, press INSERT+SPACEBAR (DOTS 2-8 CHORD followed by SPACEBAR) and then SHIFT+S (DOTS 2-3-4-7) to completely mute speech. Press RIGHT SHIFT+M again to switch back to full speech.</p> <h5 id="how-do-i-use-braille-study-mode-to-practice-my-braille-reading">How do I use braille study mode to practice my braille reading?</h5> <p>When Braille Study Mode is on, press the Cursor Router button directly above a cell for JAWS to announce the current braille character. When you press a Cursor Router button in conjunction with the Left or Right Selector button, JAWS will announce and spell the braille word at that cursor location.</p> <h5 id="how-do-i-navigate-text-in-documents-using-the-braille-display">How do I navigate text in documents using the braille display?</h5> <p>Reading text in documents is done using a series of chorded commands. If you have used other braille notetakers in the past, some of these may look very familiar. Some basic reading commands include:</p> <p>Reading Command</p> <p>Action</p> <p>Say Next or Prior Character</p> <p>DOT 6 CHORD or DOT 3 CHORD</p> <p>Say Character</p> <p>DOTS 3-6 CHORD</p> <p>Say Next or Prior Word</p> <p>DOT 5 CHORD or DOT 2 CHORD</p> <p>Say Word</p> <p>DOTS 2-5 CHORD</p> <p>Say Next or Prior Line</p> <p>DOT 4 CHORD or DOT 1 CHORD or Left Rocker Bar Down/Up</p> <p>Say Line</p> <p>C CHORD (DOTS 1-4 CHORD)</p> <p>Move to Top of File</p> <p>L CHORD (DOTS 1-2-3 CHORD)</p> <p>Move to Bottom of File</p> <p>DOTS 4-5-6 CHORD</p> <p>Say All</p> <p>DOTS 1-2-4-5-6 CHORD</p> <p>For a complete list of commands, visit our <a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/braille/focus/braille-commands/">Braille Commands web page</a>.</p> <h5 id="how-do-i-select-text-using-the-braille-display">How do I select text using the braille display?</h5> <p>Chorded commands can be used to select text in documents. These commands are executed by simultaneously pressing specified braille keys with the SPACEBAR. Here are common selection commands. Additional commands can be found on our <a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/braille/focus/braille-commands/">Braille Commands web page</a>.</p> <p>Selection Command</p> <p>Action</p> <p>Select Prior Character</p> <p>DOTS 3-7 CHORD</p> <p>Select Next Character</p> <p>DOTS 6-7 Chord</p> <p>Select Prior Word</p> <p>DOTS 2-7 Chord</p> <p>Select Next Word</p> <p>DOTS 5-7 Chord</p> <p>Select Prior Line</p> <p>DOTS 1-7 Chord</p> <p>Select Next Line</p> <p>DOTS 4-7 Chord</p> <p>Select from Start of Line</p> <p>K+DOT 7 Chord</p> <p>Select to End of Line</p> <p>DOTS 4-6-DOT 7 Chord</p> <p>Select from Top</p> <p>DOTS 1-2-3-7 Chord</p> <p>Select to Bottom</p> <p>DOTS 4-5-6-7 Chord</p> <h5 id="what-are-the-buttons-along-the-top-of-the-elbraille-used-for">What are the buttons along the top of the ElBraille used for?</h5> <p>The ElBraille buttons offer shortcuts to certain commonly performed actions. Following are the default assignments:</p> <p>Button</p> <p>Action</p> <p>E1</p> <p>Open ElBraille Main Menu</p> <p>E2</p> <p>Report battery status</p> <p>E2</p> <p>wireless network connection status</p> <p>E3</p> <p>Report current time</p> <p>E3</p> <p>Press twice quickly to report current date</p> <p>E4</p> <p>Start ElNotes or create a text note</p> <p>E4</p> <p>Press and hold to record a voice note</p> <p>E5</p> <p>Not assigned</p> <p>E6</p> <p>Report current braille display mode</p> <p>E6</p> <p>Press and hold to toggle the braille display mode</p> <p>E7</p> <p>Not assigned</p> <p>You can assign each button to a different action using the ElBraille Keyboard Editor, which is located under ElBraille Utilities in the Main Menu. Access the Main Menu by pressing E1.</p> <h5 id="can-i-install-and-run-office-365-applications-on-the-elbraille">Can I install and run Office 365 applications on the ElBraille?</h5> <p>Yes. You can install and use Office 365 applications including Word, Outlook, Excel, or PowerPoint on your ElBraille. Once installed, a Microsoft Office submenu will be added to the ElBraille main menu, which is accessed by pressing the E1 button.</p> <h5 id="can-i-install-and-run-office-365-applications-on-the-elbraille-1">Can I install and run Office 365 applications on the ElBraille?</h5> <p>Yes. You can install and use Office 365 applications including Word, Outlook, Excel, or PowerPoint on your ElBraille. Once installed, a Microsoft Office submenu will be added to the ElBraille main menu, which is accessed by pressing the E1 button.</p> <h5 id="what-web-browser-does-the-elbraille-support">What web browser does the ElBraille support?</h5> <p>You can use any Windows-based web browser on the ElBraille. Note that JAWS offers the best support for Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, and Microsoft Edge Chromium.</p> <h5 id="can-i-use-the-elbraille-to-record-class-lectures-meetings-or-other-events-for-audio-playback">Can I use the ElBraille to record class lectures, meetings, or other events for audio playback?</h5> <p>Any recording or audio playback apps you might be using with JAWS on your Windows desktop or laptop PC will also work on the ElBraille. The ElBraille includes an internal microphone or you can use an external mic.</p> <h5 id="can-i-use-the-elbraille-to-access-podcasts-play-content-from-services-like-youtube-or-stream-movies-from-sites-like-netflix">Can I use the ElBraille to access podcasts, play content from services like YouTube, or stream movies from sites like Netflix?</h5> <p>Yes, websites like YouTube and Netflix work well with JAWS. You also can find apps for playing various types of content in the Microsoft Store.</p> <h5 id="can-i-use-the-elbraille-with-facebook-or-other-social-networking-services">Can I use the ElBraille with Facebook or other social networking services?</h5> <p>Yes. You can access your favorite social networking service using your preferred web browser, or you can use their app if it is available for Windows. Most social networks offer a link to download their app on their website.</p> <h5 id="can-i-use-the-elbraille-to-read-books">Can I use the ElBraille to read books?</h5> <p>Yes. For example, you can read DAISY content obtained from sites like Bookshare.org using the FSReader software included with JAWS. You can also use apps such as Adobe Reader or Amazon Kindle for PC with the ElBraille.</p> <h5 id="does-the-elbraille-include-any-specialized-applications">Does the ElBraille include any specialized applications?</h5> <p>The ElBraille includes an application called ElNotes, which is used to create text and voice notes. It can be launched by pressing the E4 button. Pressing and holding the E4 button lets you quickly create a voice note.</p> <h5 id="can-i-use-the-elbraille-to-make-and-receive-phone-calls-as-well-as-send-and-receive-text-messages">Can I use the ElBraille to make and receive phone calls as well as send and receive text messages?</h5> <p>Not currently.</p> <p>The ElBraille is a Windows 10 computer that is designed to seamlessly dock with a Focus 40 Blue 5th generation braille display to provide a compact and portable solution similar in appearance to other braille notetakers.</p> <p>Instead of featuring a heavily customized interface built on top of an operating system, the ElBraille is a complete Windows 10 PC that uses JAWS for speech and braille output. While the ElBraille does offer some customization, including a special menu providing shortcuts to commonly used Windows apps and a specially designed application for taking notes, you can also run the same Windows 10 applications that you use on a desktop PC.</p> <p>If you rely solely on speech and have no plans to learn braille, it may be more cost-effective to purchase an off-the-shelf laptop or tablet computer and install JAWS on it.</p> <p>Even if you do not consider yourself proficient with reading Braille or using the Perkins-style keyboard, having access to a full Windows computer running JAWS that offers the portability of a braille notetaker can be beneficial. Currently, only the AT&T cellular network is supported.</p> <p>The <a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/braille/elbraille/elbraille-40-v-user-guide/">ElBraille User Guide</a> contains instructions for connecting to both wireless and cellular networks.</p> <p>You can connect the ElBraille to an HDMI monitor over a Windows Miracast Wi-Fi connection using an optional HDMI dongle (not included).</p> <p>Yes. You can use a standard QWERTY keyboard to operate the ElBraille just as you would with any other Windows computer.</p> <p>The ElBraille supports Bluetooth V4.2 and can be paired with most devices, including a keyboard, mouse, headphones, and external speakers.</p> <p>You can find complete instructions along with pictures on docking or undocking the Focus 40 Blue in the <a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/braille/elbraille/elbraille-40-v-user-guide/">ElBraille User Guide</a>.</p> <p>There are several ways to do this. One of the fastest is to press and hold the Menu button on the Focus display and then press DOT 1 through DOT 5 to switch to one of the five Bluetooth connections, or press DOT 8 to switch to the USB connection. For example, if you want to switch to displaying information from your iPhone and this is your only Bluetooth device paired with your Focus, press and hold the Menu button and then press DOT 1 to switch to your phone. When you are done, press and hold the Menu button and then press DOT 8 to switch back to the ElBraille connection. For more information, refer to the <a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/braille/focus/focus-user-guide/">Focus User Guide</a>.</p> <p>You can also use the Focus Blue as a braille display for another computer while still docked in the ElBraille. To do this, connect the ElBraille to another computer using the USB-C port located toward the back on the right side of the unit. Once connected to another PC, press and hold the E6 button to toggle the Focus between the ElBraille and the other PC connection. Pressing E6 announces the current braille display connection status. Refer to the <a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/braille/elbraille/elbraille-40-v-user-guide/">ElBraille User Guide</a> for more information.</p> <p>You can activate the Focus Scratchpad at any time by pressing and holding the Menu button and then pressing the letter N (DOTS 1-3-4-5). You can also press the Menu button once to display the Focus status message and once more to open the display’s configuration menu where you can configure Focus specific features. For more information on using the Scratchpad and other functions, refer to the <a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/braille/focus/focus-user-guide/">Focus Blue User Guide</a>.</p> <p>Use the included AC adapter to charge the ElBraille. The unit emits two ascending tones and vibrates when the AC adapter is connected and emits two descending tones and vibrates when the adapter is disconnected. It takes approximately five to seven hours to fully charge the unit. If the ElBraille is on, press the E2 button to check the battery charge level.</p> <p>Yes. You will receive vibration alerts as well as auditory beeps as the ElBraille boots up or shuts down.</p> <p>From a full charge, you should get approximately 15 hours for typical usage. This would easily get you through a full school or workday.</p> <p>You can use the two USB 3.0 ports on the ElBraille to connect a thumb drive or external hard drive. The ElBraille also includes an SD card slot which supports SD, SDHC, and SDXC memory cards up to 2 TB capacity.</p> <p>The ElBraille offers a Rescue menu, which provides speech and braille output even if JAWS is not currently working correctly. To open the Rescue menu, press and hold the E1 button. You will hear a beep followed by a menu containing three items: Restart JAWS, Shut Down, and System Reboot.</p> <p>Use the NAV Rockers to navigate the menu and press the LEFT NAV Mode button to activate the selected item.</p> <p>To close the menu, press RIGHT SHIFT+DOT 1.</p> <p>Alternatively, you can use the Volume Up/Down rocker to navigate, the E4 button to activate an item, or E1 to close the menu.</p> <p>JAWS will already be installed on the ElBraille when you receive it, but it will run in 40-minute mode. You will need to activate your JAWS license on the ElBraille.</p> <p>To activate JAWS, make sure your ElBraille is connected to the Internet, navigate to the JAWS Help menu, expand the License submenu, and then do one of the following depending on your license:</p> <ul> <li>If you have an annual license, select Manage License on Portal to open the Freedom Scientific Licensing Portal where you can log in and activate a license on your ElBraille.</li> <li>If you have a perpetual ILM license, select Update Activation and follow the prompts to activate an ILM license on your ElBraille. BrailleIn™ is a feature that allows you to use the Perkins-style keyboard on your Focus 40 Blue braille display to control the ElBraille. It is the primary method for operating the unit. All Windows and JAWS commands you would typically perform on a regular QWERTY keyboard can be executed using the keyboard and other controls on the Focus.</li> </ul> <p>You can also enter text in relevant computer applications using contracted and uncontracted braille. and guides for detailed procedures for using Focus Blue braille displays.</p> <ul> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/braille/focus/focus-user-guide/">Focus Blue User Guide (online)</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/braille/focus/focus-blue-quick-start-guide/">Focus Blue Quick Start Guide (online)</a></li> </ul> <h5 id="focus-blue-keystrokes-and-commands">Focus Blue Keystrokes and Commands</h5> <p>There are numerous keystrokes available to input braille commands directly from the Focus Blue to type and control the computer.</p> <ul> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/braille/focus/braille-commands/">Focus Blue Braille Commands</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/jaws/hotkeys/">JAWS Hotkeys</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/braille/focus/focus-user-guide/">Focus Blue User Guide</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/braille/focus/focus-blue-faqs/">Focus Blue FAQs</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/braille/focus/braille-commands/">Braille Commands</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/braille/focus/focus-blue-quick-start-guide/">Focus Blue Quick Start Guide</a></li> </ul> <h3 id="focus-blue-faqs-1">Focus Blue FAQs</h3> <h4 id="focus-blue-faqs-2">Focus Blue FAQs</h4> <h5 id="braille-displays-seem-expensive-how-can-i-try-and-get-one">Braille displays seem expensive, how can I try and get one?</h5> <p>Depending on where you live, and your employment status, there may be state or federal agencies that can assist with the purchase of a braille display. Some companies are also willing to help with the purchase of these products to help accommodate their employees.</p> <p>If you are a teacher or parent of a student who uses Braille, you could approach your local school district or university about purchasing the display. There are even non-profit groups that can help with obtaining assistive technology for qualifying individuals.</p> <p>Finally, for those who attend the NFB and ACB national conventions over the summer, we usually offer some good discounts on our hardware and software products including Focus Blue displays, so this might be a good time to purchase one if it is something you are considering.</p> <h5 id="how-will-the-focus-blue-braille-display-benefit-my-family-member-who-is-blind">How will the Focus Blue Braille Display benefit my family member who is blind?</h5> <p>Braille displays can help increase independence and literacy whether at home, school, or on the job. Since the Focus Blue can be connected to any Windows computer running JAWS® as well as Apple or Android devices, users have Braille access to all types of content instead of having to only rely on hard-copy Braille, which can take time to produce when not readily available, which can be the case for textbooks.</p> <p>Additionally, reading Braille can improve a user’s spelling and grammar skills as well as help improve their writing style as you can get a better idea of sentence structure. It can also benefit people in situations where they need to read large blocks of text, such as reading passages aloud in a class, or reading scripts as part of a sales call in customer service positions.</p> <h5 id="im-sighted-and-want-to-learn-about-focus-braille-displays-what-resources-are-available">I’m sighted and want to learn about Focus braille displays, what resources are available?</h5> <p>Check out our free webinar, <a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/webinars/focus-blue-braille-display/">Access at Your Fingertips, the Focus Blue Braille Display</a>. You can also find information on our <a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/products/blindness/focus-blue-family/">Focus product pages</a> as well as on our <a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/">Training page</a>. (update training link to point to the new Focus section when complete)</p> <h5 id="is-the-focus-blue-a-stand-alone-computer">Is the Focus Blue a stand-alone computer?</h5> <p>No. The Focus Blue is intended to provide Braille access to a computer or mobile device. To do this, the display must be connected over USB or Bluetooth and the computer must be running a screen reading application such as JAWS which sends spoken information to the Braille display.</p> <h5 id="what-are-some-of-the-advantages-of-the-different-focus-blue-models-14-40-and-80">What are some of the advantages of the different Focus Blue models (14, 40, and 80)?</h5> <p>While we cannot explicitly say which Focus display model will meet every user’s specific needs, here are some common benefits for each:</p> <ul> <li>Focus 14 – As the smallest and least expensive of the three models, the Focus 14 Blue is a great choice for those who want a display primarily for use with a mobile device as it can slip easily into a purse or bag and is also the least obtrusive when slung over a shoulder or around the neck. It also may be ideal for users who are not heavy Braille readers.</li> <li>Focus 40 – This display can be used comfortably on a desk with a desktop or laptop PC and is also still compact enough where it can be carried with you on-the-go for use with a mobile device. In addition, since 40 cells is the width of a standard braille page, it is ideal for students and other users needing to access books and other reading material as there is much less panning that would be required on smaller displays.</li> <li>Focus 80 – This display is the most expensive and least portable of the three models. It is ideal for users who want the most Braille on one line with the least amount of panning. These displays are found a lot in call center environments such as customer service, help desks, or any situation where large chunks of information need to be quickly accessed at one time.</li> </ul> <h5 id="do-you-have-a-concise-overview-of-what-all-the-controls-on-the-display-do">Do you have a concise overview of what all the controls on the display do?</h5> <p>Our <a href="https://www.youtube.com/freedomscientifictraining">YouTube Training channel offers videos that give a thorough overview of the Focus display and its controls</a>.</p> <h5 id="does-the-focus-blue-braille-display-come-with-a-carrying-case">Does the Focus Blue Braille Display come with a carrying case?</h5> <p>Yes. All Focus Blue displays include a leather carrying case with an adjustable shoulder strap.</p> <h5 id="can-the-focus-blue-braille-display-be-used-while-in-the-carrying-case">Can the Focus Blue Braille Display be used while in the carrying case?</h5> <p>Absolutely. Once the Focus is in the case, you can still access the refreshable braille cells, all controls, and even charge the unit without removing it.</p> <h5 id="im-learning-braille-would-i-benefit-from-using-the-focus-blue">I’m learning braille, would I benefit from using the Focus Blue?</h5> <p>Even if you do not consider yourself proficient with reading Braille, having access to a refreshable braille display where you can continuously try and read the content spoken by JAWS or another screen reader can be very helpful. You can also choose whether JAWS sends its output as plain text (computer braille), Uncontracted, or Contracted Braille based on your level.</p> <p>JAWS also offers a feature called Braille Study Mode which is a tool for helping to learn Braille symbols and contractions. If you are working with a sighted instructor learning to type on the Braille keyboard, you can enter text into an application like Microsoft Word, and the instructor can see the text as it is typed to confirm you are entering it correctly. Your instructor can also use the JAWS Braille Viewer, a utility that provides on-screen textual representation of the output received on a refreshable braille display.</p> <h5 id="can-i-use-the-focus-blue-to-read-books">Can I use the Focus Blue to read books?</h5> <p>Yes. To read books, make sure the Focus display is connected to your computer or mobile device and is communicating with a screen reader such as JAWS. You can then open the book in the appropriate applications like Microsoft Word, Kindle for PC, your web browser, or any other supported application. The Focus also includes a Scratchpad feature which allows you to read Braille formatted files (BRF) and plain text files (TXT) directly on the display.</p> <p>Connectivity</p> <h5 id="can-i-use-my-focus-with-my-apple-or-android-device">Can I use my Focus with my Apple or Android device?</h5> <p>Yes. The Focus Blue can be paired with any Apple Device running at least iOS 11. You can also pair the Focus with the majority of Android powered phones and tablets. For more information, see Using the Focus Blue with iOS or Using the Focus Blue with BrailleBack on Android. (just need to provide links to these documents in the new Focus training section)</p> <h5 id="can-i-connect-the-focus-blue-to-my-mac-computer">Can I connect the Focus Blue to my MAC computer?</h5> <p>Yes. You can use the Focus Blue over USB or Bluetooth with Apple’s iMac and MAC Book line of PCs.</p> <h5 id="how-many-bluetooth-connections-does-the-focus-blue-braille-display-support">How many Bluetooth connections does the Focus Blue Braille Display support?</h5> <p>The Focus Blue supports one USB and five Bluetooth connections. You can switch between active USB and Bluetooth connections on-the-fly.</p> <h5 id="how-do-i-switch-between-using-my-focus-with-my-mobile-device-to-my-computer-using-bluetooth">How do I switch between using my Focus with my mobile device to my computer using Bluetooth?</h5> <p>There are several ways to do this. One of the fastest is to press and hold the Menu button and then press DOT 1 through DOT 5 to switch to one of the five Bluetooth connections, or press DOT 8 to switch to the USB connection. For example, if you are connected to your PC over USB and also paired with your iPhone over Bluetooth, press and hold the Menu button and then press DOT 1 to switch to your phone and when you are done, press and hold the Menu button and then press DOT 8 to resume Braille access to your computer. For more information, refer to “Using the Focus Blue with JAWS” in the <a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/braille/focus/focus-user-guide/">Focus Blue user guide</a>.</p> <h5 id="what-is-braillein">What is BrailleIn?</h5> <p>BrailleIn™ is a feature that allows you to use the Perkins-style keyboard on your Focus Blue braille display to control your computer. All Windows and JAWS commands you would typically perform on a regular QWERTY keyboard can be executed using the keyboard and other controls on the Focus.</p> <p>You can also enter text in relevant computer applications using contracted and uncontracted braille. For more information on BrailleIn, refer to JAWS Help.</p> <h5 id="is-there-a-keyboard-help-mode-on-the-focus-blue-that-will-help-me-learn-braille-commands">Is there a keyboard help mode on the Focus Blue that will help me learn braille commands?</h5> <p>Yes. Press TH CHORD (dots 1-4-5-6) simultaneously with the SPACEBAR for a list of available Focus-specific commands. When the Focus is connected to a computer, you can use JAWS Command Search to find Focus-specific commands. Press INSERT+Space followed by J to run Command Search, then type the command you’d like to find.</p> <h5 id="what-is-a-chord-command-1">What is a chord command?</h5> <p>A chord is a command executed by pressing one or more keys simultaneously with the spacebar.</p> <h5 id="can-i-use-all-the-same-braille-keystrokes-i-use-with-jaws-with-other-screen-reading-applications">Can I use all the same braille keystrokes I use with JAWS with other screen reading applications?</h5> <p>Not all Focus braille commands that are supported in JAWS will work the same in third-party screen reading applications. Please see the screen reader document for Focus commands specific to a given application.</p> <h5 id="how-do-i-use-braille-study-mode-to-practice-my-braille-reading-1">How do I use braille study mode to practice my braille reading?</h5> <p>When Braille Study Mode is on, press the cursor router button directly above a particular cell for JAWS to announce the current braille character. When you press a Cursor Router button in conjunction with the Left or Right Selector button, JAWS will announce and spell the braille word at that cursor location.</p> <h5 id="how-do-i-select-text-using-the-focus-blue">How do I select text using the Focus Blue?</h5> <p>You can use the cursor router buttons on the Focus Blue to select text. Press and hold the Left Shift key on the Focus, then press the Cursor Router button above the first character of text you’d like to select. Release both keys and move to where you want to end the selection. Press the Left Shift plus the Cursor Router button above the last character of text you want to select. Use any navigation commands including the Nav Rockers to move from the beginning point to the end point of the text you are selecting.</p> <h5 id="will-using-the-focus-with-my-computer-help-me-understand-screen-layout-and-computer-concepts">Will using the Focus with my computer help me understand screen layout and computer concepts?</h5> <p>Using the Focus Blue will provide a better understanding of screen layout and computer concepts through navigation of complex web pages and document information such as formatting and page layout.</p> <p>Interacting with these elements using both speech and braille reinforces the speech with a tactile representation of information found in columns, tables, spreadsheets, and regular text. Regularly reading braille on the Focus can also help improve spelling and grammar.</p> <h5 id="will-the-focus-work-with-other-screen-reading-software-besides-jaws">Will the Focus work with other screen reading software besides JAWS?</h5> <p>The focus works with third-party screen readers as well as iOS and Android devices. If you choose to use the Focus display with a third-party screen reading application on a computer or mobile device, refer to the documentation that came with the software as the functions of the controls on the Focus may be different from how they work with JAWS.</p> <p>Hardware Specific</p> <h5 id="how-do-i-charge-my-focus-blue">How do I charge my Focus Blue?</h5> <p>Use the included AC adapter to charge the Focus Blue battery. The unit takes three hours to charge even when the Bluetooth connection is active. Charging time will be less if the battery is not completely discharged when you initially connect the adaptor.</p> <p>The Focus will also charge while connected to a computer using the USB cable, however, charging time will take longer than with the supplied AC adapter. As the Focus charges, the battery charging indicator, a circle of dots, is displayed to the right of the percentage until the unit reaches 100 percent. You can continue using the Focus while it is charging.</p> <h5 id="what-are-the-most-important-settings-i-need-to-know-about-on-the-focus-blue">What are the most important settings I need to know about on the Focus Blue?</h5> <p>The Focus Blue contains many settings to help you customize how you use the device. The first settings to check are those for establishing a USB or Bluetooth connection. If you are connecting via USB using JAWS, the device should be recognized and ready to use automatically. If this doesn’t occur, go to the Braille Basic Settings in the JAWS Options Menu to configure the connection.</p> <p>If you are using a third-party screen reading application, refer to the documentation that came with the software as these procedures might be different.</p> <p>Other important settings in this dialog box include:</p> <ul> <li>Braille language input and output translation</li> <li>Braille mode</li> <li>Panning</li> <li>Flash messages</li> <li>Status cells</li> <li>Cursor</li> <li>Dot firmness You can also access the Configuration Menu directly from the Focus Blue by pressing the Menu Button on the unit while a status message is displayed. Here, you can access settings for Bluetooth ID, the Focus clock, Focus calendar, firmness, and language.</li> </ul> <h5 id="what-is-a-micro-sd-card-and-how-do-i-use-it-with-my-focus">What is a micro SD card and how do I use it with my Focus?</h5> <p>A micro SD card is a type of removable flash memory used for file storage. It can only be used in the Focus when saving or accessing files in the Scratchpad.</p> <p>The micro SD card slot is located on the left side of the device to the right of the power button. To insert the card, Slide it into the slot until it clicks into place.</p> <p>To remove the micro SD card, gently press its exposed edge to eject it, then carefully pull it out of the slot.</p> <h5 id="does-the-focus-offer-any-internal-storage-for-files">Does the Focus offer any internal storage for files?</h5> <p>No, the Focus does not offer internal storage. The micro SD card is used only to save or open files when using the Scratchpad.</p> <h5 id="i-prefer-operating-my-pc-and-typing-text-using-a-standard-qwerty-keyboard.-is-it-possible-to-turn-off-the-focus-keys-so-i-do-not-accidentally-enter-unwanted-characters-or-commands">I prefer operating my PC and typing text using a standard QWERTY keyboard. Is it possible to turn off the Focus keys so I do not accidentally enter unwanted characters or commands?</h5> <p>You can lock the Perkins-style keys on the top of the display to prevent accidentally pressing them and entering unwanted text or commands. This is useful when you want to use the QWERTY keyboard to operate the computer or enter text.</p> <p>You can also lock additional controls so that only very basic display navigation is available. To lock the Perkins-style keyboard, press the Menu button on the device to display the status information. Press and hold a cursor router button while pressing the Left NAV Mode button.</p> <p>To unlock the keyboard, press and hold a cursor router button while pressing the Right NAV Mode Button. Please see the <a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/braille/focus/user-guide/">Focus Blue User Guide</a> for additional information.</p> <h5 id="how-long-will-the-focus-blue-braille-display-run-before-it-needs-to-be-recharged">How long will the Focus Blue Braille Display run before it needs to be recharged?</h5> <p>The Focus Blue contains an internal battery for Bluetooth operation. Typical usage is approximately 20 hours when using the Focus over a Bluetooth connection.</p> <h5 id="will-the-scratch-pad-turn-the-focus-into-a-portable-note-taker">Will the Scratch Pad turn the Focus into a portable note taker?</h5> <p>Though the Scratchpad feature on the Focus Blue does provide some note taking capabilities and the ability to read BRF braille formatted books, it does not include internal storage and is not a full-featured portable note taker.</p> <h5 id="what-file-formats-are-supported-by-scratch-pad">What file formats are supported by Scratch Pad?</h5> <p>Scratchpad supports plain text format (.txt) for saving files and will open both txt and BRF braille files.</p> <h5 id="how-can-i-access-notes-taken-in-the-scratchpad-with-my-pc-or-portable-device">How can I access notes taken in the Scratchpad with my PC or portable device?</h5> <p>If there is currently an active USB or Bluetooth connection between the Focus and a computer or other device, you can export the contents of the currently open file to the edit window of an application on your computer. If your notes are in contracted braille, you must be running a screen reader such as JAWS that supports braille input so the contents will be back translated to text in the document. The braille input settings for the screen reader must also match the braille format you are using when typing in the Scratchpad.</p> <p>To export a file, open the document or application where you want the exported text to appear. Open the Scratchpad file you want to export.</p> <p>Press the Menu button on the Focus Blue and choose Export. The contents of your Scratchpad file will appear in the document on your computer as plain text. You cannot export BRF braille files from the Scratchpad to your computer.</p> <h5 id="can-i-read-braille-book-downloads-from-nls-bard-or-bookshare.org-on-the-focus-blue-braille-display">Can I read braille book downloads from NLS BARD or BookShare.org on the Focus Blue Braille Display?</h5> <p>Yes. You can read BRF braille files from services such as NLS BARD and Bookshare using the Scratchpad feature of the Focus Blue.</p> <h5 id="how-can-i-select-text-in-the-scratchpad">How can I select text in the Scratchpad?</h5> <p>To select a block of text, position the cursor where you want to begin the selection and press Left Shift+M (DOTS 1-3-4) to set a mark at that location. Move the cursor to where you want to end the selection and press Left Shift+S (DOTS 2-3-4) to select all the text between the mark and the cursor location. Once the text is selected, you can:</p> <ul> <li>Copy to clipboard: Left Shift+C (DOTS 1-4)</li> <li>Cut to clipboard: Left Shift+X (DOTS 1-3-4-6)</li> <li>Delete: Left Shift+D (DOTS 1-4-5) To paste text from the clipboard into the currently open file, press Left Shift+P (DOTS 1-2-3-4).</li> </ul> <h5 id="can-i-import-text-files-to-my-focus-from-a-mac">Can I import text files to my Focus from a Mac?</h5> <p>Yes, it is possible to import text files to the Focus from a Mac. Please see Apple’s documentation for instructions.</p> <p>Depending on where you live, and your employment status, there may be state or federal agencies that can assist with the purchase of a braille display. Some companies are also willing to help with the purchase of these products to help accommodate their employees.</p> <p>If you are a teacher or parent of a student who uses Braille, you could approach your local school district or university about purchasing the display. If this doesn’t occur, go to the Braille Basic Settings in the JAWS Options Menu to configure the connection.</p> <p>If you are using a third-party screen reading application, refer to the documentation that came with the software as these procedures might be different.</p> <p>Other important settings in this dialog box include:</p> <ul> <li>Braille language input and output translation</li> <li>Braille mode</li> <li>Panning</li> <li>Flash messages</li> <li>Status cells</li> <li>Cursor</li> <li>Dot firmness You can also access the Configuration Menu directly from the Focus Blue by pressing the Menu Button on the unit while a status message is displayed. Here, you can access settings for Bluetooth ID, the Focus clock, Focus calendar, firmness, and language.</li> </ul> <p>A micro SD card is a type of removable flash memory used for file storage. It can only be used in the Focus when saving or accessing files in the Scratchpad.</p> <p>The micro SD card slot is located on the left side of the device to the right of the power button. To insert the card, Slide it into the slot until it clicks into place.</p> <p>To remove the micro SD card, gently press its exposed edge to eject it, then carefully pull it out of the slot.</p> <p>No, the Focus does not offer internal storage. The micro SD card is used only to save or open files when using the Scratchpad.</p> <p>You can lock the Perkins-style keys on the top of the display to prevent accidentally pressing them and entering unwanted text or commands. This is useful when you want to use the QWERTY keyboard to operate the computer or enter text.</p> <p>You can also lock additional controls so that only very basic display navigation is available. To lock the Perkins-style keyboard, press the Menu button on the device to display the status information. Press and hold a cursor router button while pressing the Left NAV Mode button.</p> <p>To unlock the keyboard, press and hold a cursor router button while pressing the Right NAV Mode Button. Please see the <a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/braille/focus/user-guide/">Focus Blue User Guide</a> for additional information.</p> <p>The Focus Blue contains an internal battery for Bluetooth operation. Typical usage is approximately 20 hours when using the Focus over a Bluetooth connection.</p> <p>Though the Scratchpad feature on the Focus Blue does provide some note taking capabilities and the ability to read BRF braille formatted books, it does not include internal storage and is not a full-featured portable note taker.</p> <p>Scratchpad supports plain text format (.txt) for saving files and will open both txt and BRF braille files.</p> <p>If there is currently an active USB or Bluetooth connection between the Focus and a computer or other device, you can export the contents of the currently open file to the edit window of an application on your computer. If your notes are in contracted braille, you must be running a screen reader such as JAWS that supports braille input so the contents will be back translated to text in the document. The braille input settings for the screen reader must also match the braille format you are using when typing in the Scratchpad.</p> <p>To export a file, open the document or application where you want the exported text to appear. Open the Scratchpad file you want to export.</p> <p>Press the Menu button on the Focus Blue and choose Export. The contents of your Scratchpad file will appear in the document on your computer as plain text. You cannot export BRF braille files from the Scratchpad to your computer.</p> <p>Yes. You can read BRF braille files from services such as NLS BARD and Bookshare using the Scratchpad feature of the Focus Blue.</p> <p>To select a block of text, position the cursor where you want to begin the selection and press Left Shift+M (DOTS 1-3-4) to set a mark at that location. Move the cursor to where you want to end the selection and press Left Shift+S (DOTS 2-3-4) to select all the text between the mark and the cursor location. Once the text is selected, you can:</p> <ul> <li>Copy to clipboard: Left Shift+C (DOTS 1-4)</li> <li>Cut to clipboard: Left Shift+X (DOTS 1-3-4-6)</li> <li>Delete: Left Shift+D (DOTS 1-4-5) To paste text from the clipboard into the currently open file, press Left Shift+P (DOTS 1-2-3-4).</li> </ul> <p>Yes, it is possible to import text files to the Focus from a Mac. Please see Apple’s documentation for instructions.</p> <ul> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/braille/focus/focus-user-guide/">Focus Blue User Guide</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/braille/focus/focus-blue-faqs/">Focus Blue FAQs</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/braille/focus/braille-commands/">Braille Commands</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/braille/focus/focus-blue-quick-start-guide/">Focus Blue Quick Start Guide</a></li> </ul> <h3 id="focus-blue-quick-start-guide">Focus Blue Quick Start Guide</h3> <h4 id="focus-blue-quick-start-guide-1">Focus Blue Quick Start Guide</h4> <h5 id="introduction-3">Introduction</h5> <p>The Focus Blue line of refreshable braille displays provide a tactile interface to your computer or mobile device. Accessing information at your fingertips has never been easier with these compact and portable options.</p> <p>The Focus Blue is available in 14, 40, or 80 refreshable braille cells and requires the use of a screen reader such as JAWS® for Windows. This Quick Start Guide is intended to provide the basic information you need to familiarize yourself with your Focus display and to get you up and running. For more detailed information, see the <a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/braille/focus/focus-user-guide/">Focus Blue User Guide</a>.</p> <h5 id="focus-controls-overview">Focus Controls Overview</h5> <p>Watch a brief video highlighting the Focus 40 Blue’s controls, or continue reading for more details about the three models of Focus Blue braille displays.</p> <p>On the left side of the display, going from front to back, you will find a Micro SD slot which contains a Micro SD card, the Power button, and a micro USB-C port. The USB port allows you to connect the display to a computer using the supplied USB cable, or to the AC adapter.</p> <p>Click to view larger image in new tab.</p> <p>The refreshable braille cells are located toward the front of the unit. A refreshable display creates braille by electronically raising and lowering different combinations of pins in each braille cell.</p> <p>Click to view larger image in new tab.</p> <p>Above each braille cell is a Cursor Router button used for moving quickly to that location.</p> <p>Click to view larger image in new tab.</p> <p>At each end of the display’s surface are NAV Rockers used for easy navigation. Positioned above each NAV Rocker is a NAV Mode button which cycles through the different navigation modes.</p> <p>Click to view larger image in new tab.</p> <p>Positioned directly above the Cursor Router buttons, there are eight keys similar to those on a Perkins-style braille keyboard. These keys are used to enter text or perform commands.</p> <p>Click to view larger image in new tab.</p> <p>Starting center to left, with the left hand:</p> <ul> <li><p>Dot 1: index finger</p></li> <li><p>Dot 2: middle finger</p></li> <li><p>Dot 3: ring finger</p></li> <li><p>Dot 7: little finger Starting center to right, with the right hand:</p></li> <li><p>Dot 4: index finger</p></li> <li><p>Dot 5: middle finger</p></li> <li><p>Dot 6: ring finger</p></li> <li><p>Dot 8: little finger Between dots 1 and 4 is a Menu button which is used to access the Focus configuration menu as well as display Focus status information during an active connection. On the front edge, directly under and in the center of the display is a SPACEBAR. This key is used together with the braille keys when entering commands. A command that includes the SPACEBAR is commonly referred to as a chorded command. For example, L CHORD or DOTS 1-2-3 and the SPACEBAR.</p></li> </ul> <p>On the front edge of the display are the following controls, located from left to right. The layout of these controls is slightly different depending on what model of Focus you have.</p> <p>• Focus 14: Left Selector button, Left Rocker bar, Left Panning button, Left Shift button, Right Shift button, Right Panning button, Right Rocker bar, and Right Selector button</p> <p>Click to view larger image in new tab.</p> <p>• Focus 40: Left Panning button, Left Rocker bar, Left Selector button, Left Shift button, Right Shift button, Right Selector button, Right Rocker bar, and Right Panning button</p> <p>Click to view larger image in new tab.</p> <p>• Focus 80: Left Panning button, Left Rocker bar, Left Selector button, two Left Panning rockers, Left Shift button, Right Shift button, two Right Panning rockers, Right Selector button, Right Rocker bar, and Right Panning button.</p> <p>Click to view larger image in new tab.</p> <p>Note: The following sections describe how these controls work when using the Focus Blue with JAWS. If you choose to use the Focus display with a third-party screen reading application on a computer or mobile device, refer to the documentation that came with the software as the functions of these controls may be different from how they work with JAWS.</p> <h6 id="nav-rockers-and-nav-mode-buttons">NAV Rockers and NAV Mode Buttons</h6> <p>The Focus NAV Rockers allow you to move quickly through files, dialog boxes, lists, and menus. In a file, you can move by line, sentence, paragraph, or pan backward and forward. To switch between the four navigation modes, press the NAV Mode button located directly above each NAV Rocker. In a dialog box, you can move between the available controls, and even interact with them. In a menu, you can move up and down through the menu items. You can also completely turn the NAV Rockers off by simultaneously pressing the Left or Right NAV Mode button and the SPACEBAR. Perform a Left or Right NAV Mode button CHORD once more to turn them back on.</p> <h6 id="panning-buttons">Panning Buttons</h6> <p>The Focus Panning buttons pan left or right one display width each time they are pressed. Press the Left Panning button, the button with a raised double left arrow symbol, to pan left; press the Right Panning button, the button with a raised double right arrow symbol, to pan right. If you are using JAWS, the functions of the Panning buttons can be reversed so that pressing the Left Panning button causes the Focus display to pan right and pressing the Right Panning button causes it to pan left. To enable reverse panning, open JAWS Settings Center, search for “reverse panning”, and select the Reverse Panning Buttons check box.</p> <h6 id="rocker-bars">Rocker Bars</h6> <p>The Rocker bars provide movement up or down by line. Press the top of the Rocker bar to move up one line; press the bottom of the Rocker bar to move down one line. The Rocker bars, in combination with the Panning buttons, move to the beginning or end of the line on which the cursor is positioned. Press a Panning button and the top of a Rocker bar to move to the start of the line. Press a Panning button and the bottom of a Rocker bar to move to the end of the line.</p> <h6 id="selector-buttons">Selector Buttons</h6> <p>Used by themselves, the concave-shaped Selector buttons control Auto Advance. Press both Selector buttons together to toggle Auto Advance on or off. Press the Left Selector button to decrease the Auto Advance speed or press the Right Selector button to increase the Auto Advance speed.</p> <p>When pressed in combination with other controls, the Selector buttons perform multiple functions. For instance, pressing a Selector button and the top or bottom of a Rocker bar performs a page up or page down. You can also press a Selector button and the Right or Left Panning button to move to the top or bottom of a file.</p> <h6 id="panning-rockers-focus-80-only">Panning Rockers (Focus 80 only)</h6> <p>The four Panning rockers on the Focus 80 function as extra panning buttons. However, they move in the same way as the Rocker bars. Press up on either of the Panning rockers to pan left and press down to pan right.</p> <h6 id="shift-buttons">Shift Buttons</h6> <p>The Shift buttons are used in conjunction with the SPACEBAR, braille keys, and other controls to enter commands. For example, when using JAWS, pressing Left Shift+DOT 4 or DOT 1 selects the next or previous line in a document.</p> <h6 id="cursor-router-buttons">Cursor Router Buttons</h6> <p>There is a Cursor Router button located above each braille cell. Press a Cursor Router button to move the cursor to that point, or to select a link in a web page or email message. In line mode, press a Cursor Router button to open a menu or select menu items.</p> <p>Press and hold the Left or Right Panning button while simultaneously pressing a Cursor Router button to simulate a right mouse click at that location.</p> <p>You can also use the Cursor Routers to select text in documents. To select with the Cursor Router buttons, press and hold the Left Shift button, then press the Cursor Router button above the text where you want to begin the selection. Release both keys. Move to where you want to end the selection, and press the Left Shift button plus the Cursor Router button at that location. Use any navigation commands to move from the beginning point to the end point of the text you are selecting, even the NAV Rockers.</p> <h5 id="turning-the-focus-on-or-off">Turning the Focus On or Off</h5> <p>The Focus automatically powers on when you connect it to USB. Otherwise, press and hold the Power button for approximately two seconds to turn the display on and press and hold it for approximately three and a half seconds to turn the display off.</p> <p>Click to view larger image in new tab.</p> <h5 id="charging-the-focus">Charging the Focus</h5> <p>Use the AC adapter supplied with your unit to charge the battery. Charging time is three hours. The display also charges when connected to a PC over USB, however, charging time will be longer. As the Focus charges, the battery charging indicator, a circle of dots, is displayed to the right of the percentage until the unit reaches 100 percent.</p> <p>When using the Focus on battery power, you will get approximately 20 hours for typical usage. To check the battery status while the display is in use, press the Menu button to display the percentage of battery charge used. Press the Left Selector button to return to normal operation.</p> <h5 id="installing-focus-blue-display-drivers">Installing Focus Blue Display Drivers</h5> <p>In Microsoft Windows, JAWS automatically installs the files necessary to use the Focus Blue during the JAWS installation. However, if you choose to use the Focus display with another screen reading application, you must install the Windows driver. Go to the <a href="https://support.freedomscientific.com/Downloads/Focus/FocusBlueBrailleDisplayDriver">Focus Blue Braille Display Driver web page</a> and follow the instructions to download and install this driver.</p> <p>Note: Make sure you do not connect the display to your computer until after the driver is successfully installed.</p> <p>On Apple Mac computers, the VoiceOver screen reader already includes the appropriate drivers necessary to use the Focus Blue.</p> <h5 id="configuring-the-usb-connection-for-jaws">Configuring the USB Connection for JAWS</h5> <p>Watch a brief video describing how to configure your braille display using a USB connection, or continue reading to learn more.</p> <p>Note: If you are using a third-party screen reading application, refer to the documentation that came with the software as this procedure might be different.</p> <ul> <li>Establish a USB connection between the Focus and computer using the supplied USB cable.</li> <li>Close and then restart JAWS. JAWS automatically detects and begins using your Focus Blue braille display.</li> </ul> <h5 id="configuring-the-bluetooth-connection-for-jaws">Configuring the Bluetooth Connection for JAWS</h5> <p>Watch a brief video describing how to pair your braille display with a computer using Bluetooth, or continue reading to learn more.</p> <p>In order to use the Focus Blue wirelessly over Bluetooth, you must first configure a Bluetooth partnership between the Focus and computer.</p> <ul> <li>Make sure that Bluetooth is enabled on the computer running JAWS. If you are using an external USB Bluetooth adapter, insert it and ensure it is detected properly.</li> <li>Power on the Focus. The time and battery status information is displayed.</li> <li>On the computer, go to the Control Panel and type “bluetooth” into the Search edit box.</li> <li>Press TAB to move to Add Bluetooth Device and press ENTER. The computer will begin searching for Bluetooth devices. This may take several seconds. You are placed in the list of devices when the search is complete.</li> <li>Use the ARROW keys to select your Focus display from the list, for example, Focus 14 BT, Focus 40 BT, or Focus 80 BT, and then press ENTER. If the Focus display was not found, make sure it is turned on then select the Retry button.</li> <li>When prompted to enter a pairing code, type 0000 into the edit field, and then press ENTER to finish pairing the display. You must now configure JAWS to use the Bluetooth connection. Note that it is not necessary to first establish a USB connection before using Bluetooth. If you have not yet set up a USB connection with the Focus display, do the following:</li> </ul> <p>Note: If you are using a third-party screen reading application, refer to the documentation that came with the software as these procedures might be different.</p> <ul> <li><p>Press INSERT+J to open the JAWS window.</p></li> <li><p>Press ALT+O to open the Options menu and select Braille to open the Braille Basic Settings dialog box.</p></li> <li><p>Press TAB to move to the Add Braille Display button and press ENTER.</p></li> <li><p>In the list of braille displays, choose Focus and press the SPACEBAR to select it, and then choose Next.</p></li> <li><p>In the Select the output port edit combo box, choose Bluetooth.</p></li> <li><p>Choose next and make sure that the Focus is selected as the primary display.</p></li> <li><p>Select Finish and you are instructed to restart JAWS in order for these changes to take effect. Select OK to close this message and once more to close the Braille Basic Settings dialog box.</p></li> <li><p>Quit and restart JAWS and your Focus Blue is now communicating with JAWS over Bluetooth. If you are currently using the Focus display over USB and you want to switch the connection to use Bluetooth, do the following:</p></li> <li><p>Press INSERT+J to open the JAWS window.</p></li> <li><p>Press ALT+O to open the Options menu and select Braille to open the Braille Basic Settings dialog box.</p></li> <li><p>In the Default Braille Display combo box, make sure Focus is selected then choose Modify Settings.</p></li> <li><p>In the Select the output port edit combo box, choose Bluetooth.</p></li> <li><p>Select OK and you are instructed to restart JAWS in order for these changes to take effect. Select OK to close this message and once more to close the Braille Basic Settings dialog box.</p></li> <li><p>Quit and restart JAWS and your Focus Blue is now communicating with JAWS over Bluetooth.</p></li> </ul> <h5 id="pairing-with-a-mobile-device">Pairing with a Mobile Device</h5> <p>Watch a brief video to learn more about pairing Focus with an iOS device, or continue reading to pair your braille display with iOS or Android devices.</p> <p>You can use the Focus Blue as a Bluetooth display with mobile devices that run Apple’s iOS and Google’s Android operating systems. For more information, refer to one of the following pages.</p> <ul> <li><a href="https://support.freedomscientific.com/Content/Documents/Manuals/Focus/Focus-Blue-iOS-Support.htm">Using the Focus Blue with iOS</a></li> <li><a href="https://support.freedomscientific.com/Content/Documents/Manuals/Focus/Focus-Blue-Android-Support.htm">Using the Focus Blue with BrailleBack on Android</a> Refer to the Focus Blue User’s Guide for more information about managing connections.</li> </ul> <h5 id="setting-the-time">Setting the Time</h5> <p>The time is always displayed as part of the Focus status message. To set the time, do the following:</p> <ul> <li>Press the Menu button to access the display configuration menu.</li> <li>Press DOTS 4-5 CHORD or a Rocker bar to navigate to Clock and press Dot 8 or the Right Shift button.</li> <li>The hours value will be selected when the Clock configuration opens. Use the Rocker bars to set the hour.</li> <li>Press DOTS 4-5 CHORD or the Right Panning button to select the minutes value and use the Rocker bars to set the minute.</li> <li>Press DOTS 4-5 CHORD or the Right Panning button to select the seconds on/off value and use the Rocker bars to toggle the seconds display on or off. When enabled, seconds are shown as part of the time on the status message.</li> <li>Press DOTS 4-5 CHORD or the Right Panning button to select the AM/PM/24-hour value and use the Rocker bars to choose AM, PM, or 24-hour time. The option for 24-hour time is indicated by the number 24 (dots 2-3 and dots 2-5-6).</li> <li>Press DOT 8 or the Right Selector button to save your changes and close the Clock submenu. Press Z CHORD (DOTS 1-3-5-6 CHORD) or the Left Selector button to close the submenu without saving.</li> <li>Press Z CHORD (DOTS 1-3-5-6 CHORD) or the Left Selector button to exit the configuration menu.</li> </ul> <h5 id="scratchpad">Scratchpad</h5> <p>The Scratchpad enables you to take notes as well as read braille formatted (BRF) and plain text (TXT) books. To start the Scratchpad, simultaneously press the Menu button and the letter N (DOTS 1-3-4-5). You are placed in a new blank file where you can immediately begin entering content. To save the file to the included Micro SD card, simultaneously press Right Shift and the letter S (DOTS 2-3-4).</p> <p>To transfer BRF and TXT files for reading in the Scratchpad:</p> <ul> <li>Press and hold the Left Panning button while simultaneously powering on the display. Connect the Focus to your computer using the supplied USB cable, and the display will be recognized as a removable USB drive.</li> <li>Note: If you use a screen reader such as JAWS over USB, it is recommended that you turn on speech or use a Bluetooth connection as braille will currently not work over USB when the Focus is being used as a storage device. You will also not be able to use the Scratchpad while in this mode.</li> <li>On the PC, open the folder containing the files you want to copy, select the files you want, and then press CTRL+C.</li> <li>Navigate to and open the USB drive to display the contents of the Micro SD card.</li> <li>Open FSI, Focus5, Scratchpad, Books, and then press CTRL+V to place the files into this folder.</li> <li>Once you have finished transferring files, press the APPLICATIONS key on your computer while focused on the USB drive, and choose Eject.</li> <li>Power the Focus off and back on and you will once again be able to use the Scratchpad as well as receive braille output from your screen reader over USB. To open a file, simultaneously press Right Shift and the letter O (DOTS 1-3-5). Select the Notes folder to open files you created in the Scratchpad or select the Books folder to open files transferred from your computer.</li> </ul> <p>For more information on using the Scratchpad, simultaneously press Right Shift and the letter H (DOTS 1-2-5) to open Help.</p> <ul> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/braille/focus/focus-user-guide/">Focus Blue User Guide</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/braille/focus/focus-blue-faqs/">Focus Blue FAQs</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/braille/focus/braille-commands/">Braille Commands</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/braille/focus/focus-blue-quick-start-guide/">Focus Blue Quick Start Guide</a></li> </ul> <h3 id="focus-blue-user-guide">Focus Blue User Guide</h3> <ul> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/braille/focus/">Focus Blue Braille Display Training</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/braille/focus/focus-user-guide/">Focus Blue User Guide</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/braille/focus/focus-blue-faqs/">Focus Blue FAQs</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/braille/focus/braille-commands/">Braille Commands</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/braille/focus/focus-blue-quick-start-guide/">Focus Blue Quick Start Guide</a></li> </ul> <h4 id="focus-blue-user-guide-1">Focus Blue User Guide</h4> <p>Welcome to the Focus Blue refreshable braille display user guide. It describes controls, set up, and basic operation of the 14-cell, 40-cell, and 80-cell braille displays.</p> <ul> <li>Introduction</li> <li>What’s in the Box?</li> <li>Focus Controls Overview</li> <li>Turning the Focus On or Off</li> <li>Charging the Focus</li> <li>Connecting the Focus</li> <li>Installing Focus Blue Display Drivers</li> <li>Configuring the USB Connection</li> <li>Configuring the Bluetooth Connection</li> <li>Pairing with a Mobile Device</li> <li>Switching the Active Connection</li> <li>Using the Focus Blue with JAWS</li> <li>Locking the Perkins-style Keyboard and Other Controls</li> <li>The Display Configuration Menu</li> <li>Using Scratchpad</li> <li>Inserting a Micro SD Card</li> <li>Diagnostics Mode</li> <li>Troubleshooting</li> <li>Environmental Considerations</li> <li>Service and Support</li> <li>Warranty and Registration</li> </ul> <h5 id="introduction-4">Introduction</h5> <p>The Focus Blue line of refreshable braille displays provide a tactile interface to your computer or mobile device.
