and Improved Features in JAWS</h4> <h5 id="picture-smart-ai">Picture Smart AI</h5> <p>For a brief introduction to Picture Smart AI™, watch our <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eTWNtEChnt0">video</a> on YouTube.</p> <p>While navigating the digital landscape, you might encounter photos, charts, and other visual elements without an alternative description. This can make it challenging to understand the information provided by the visual content. The JAWS® Picture Smart AI feature allows you to submit a photo to be analyzed and then displays a description of the picture in the JAWS Results Viewer window.</p> <p>This revolutionary update to the original Picture Smart feature, introduced in 2019, integrates with the latest artificial intelligence (AI) technology from services like Chat GPT from Open AI and Claude from Anthropic to offer a whole new level of accessibility to graphical information. Descriptions might offer details such as the number of people in the photo including how they look and what activities they may be performing, recognizable landmarks, landscape details such as the color of the sky, grass, or trees, the layout of information in a visual chart or slide, and much more. Additionally, any text in the picture such as writing on a sign or piece of clothing may also be provided in the description.</p> <p>To use Picture Smart, press INSERT+SPACEBAR followed by P to access the Picture Smart layer, and then use one of the following keystrokes:</p> <ul> <li>A – Opens the Picture Smart dialog box where you can acquire an image from a flatbed scanner or the Freedom Scientific PEARL camera and submit it to be described.</li> <li>F – Describes the currently selected image in File Explorer. Supported image formats include BMP, JPEG, GIF, TIF, PNG, or HEIC.</li> <li>C – Describes any currently selected control. For instance, if focused on a picture in a Word document or on a social media website like Facebook, this command describes the picture. When using this command on a web page, make sure your browser window is maximized for best results .</li> <li>B – Describes the contents of the Windows Clipboard if it contains an image.</li> <li>S – Describes the entire screen.</li> <li>W – Describes the current application window.</li> <li>ENTER – Describes an image based on the current application and context. This eliminates the need to remember multiple keystrokes constantly. For instance: <ul> <li>If someone is presenting in Teams, it describes the current slide.</li> <li>If you are on a web page, it describes the current image or control.</li> <li>If you are in File Explorer, it describes the currently selected file.</li> <li>If playing a video from a source like YouTube, it describes a screenshot from the current position in the video.</li> <li>If a PowerPoint slideshow is running, it describes the current slide.</li> <li>If you are in PowerPoint with a slide selected but not in an active slideshow, it describes the currently visible slide.</li> </ul></li> <li>QUESTION MARK – Displays help for the Picture Smart layer. After running Picture Smart AI, you will also be alerted to any potential problems with an image that may result in poor descriptions. For example, if your browser window is not maximized, images may be clipped, leading to inaccurate descriptions. In this case, an expandable alert is displayed at the top of the Results Viewer prior to the description. Press ENTER on this alert to view the full details. You can then close the Results Viewer, maximize your browser window, and try running Picture Smart AI on the image again.</li> </ul> <p>Once a submitted image finishes processing, Picture Smart AI displays a short description by default. To display more in-depth descriptions, select the Get more details link near the bottom of the Results Viewer. You can also add SHIFT to a Picture Smart command to immediately display the more detailed descriptions. For example, INSERT+SPACEBAR, P, SHIFT+F.</p> <p>To demonstrate the difference in the level of detail, here are a few example photos along with resulting descriptions generated using both the original Picture Smart and Picture Smart AI. You can also try this feature out yourself by pressing INSERT+SPACEBAR, P, C while focused on each photo.</p> <p>Current Picture Smart Sample Description</p> <p>Picture Smart AI Sample Short Description</p> <p>Picture Smart AI Sample Long Description</p> <p>Caption is a group of people sitting on a beach. These tags describe the photo: beach, clothing, girl, group, human face, outdoor, people, person, sky, woman. These tags probably describe the photo: fun, sitting, summer, vacation, water. This tag possibly describes the photo: ground.</p> <p>The image shows a group of six friends sitting on the beach. They are all smiling and laughing, and some of them are singing. One of them is playing the guitar. The sun is setting in the background, and the waves are crashing on the shore.</p> <p>The image depicts a group of friends enjoying themselves on a beach at what appears to be sunset due to the warm, golden lighting. There are five individuals in the foreground, with one more partially seen in the background. The group is casually dressed in summer attire and seems to be engaged in a lively and joyful conversation.</p> <p>In the left part of the image, there’s a man sitting on the sand, wearing a light blue button-up shirt and smiling broadly, evidently amused by the conversation. To his right, a woman is laughing heartily, her head tossed back and her hands raised—she’s wearing a yellow top.</p> <p>Centered in the image, another woman is smiling and appears to be sharing a moment of enjoyment with the man on her left; she has her arm extended as if she is pointing at something or someone outside the frame. Turning clockwise, the next woman is in profile and not fully visible, she’s wearing a red and blue checked shirt, and seems engaged with the person beside her.</p> <p>On the right side, another person is mostly turned away from the camera, wearing a white garment that could be a sweater or jacket; this individual appears to be looking back towards the others with a smile.</p> <p>The beach setting provides a tranquil background with the ocean meeting the horizon. The mood is upbeat and the image exudes a sense of friendship, relaxation, and the simple joys of life. There’s a harmonious mix of motion and stillness, with some individuals in mid-gesture, which adds to the dynamic of a candid and spontaneous moment.</p> <p>Current Picture Smart Sample Description</p> <p>Picture Smart AI Sample Short Description</p> <p>Picture Smart AI Sample Long Description</p> <p>Caption is timeline. These tags describe the photo: display, font, screenshot, text. These tags probably describe the photo: diagram, number.</p> <p>The image is a timeline that spans from September 2024 to May 2025. It is divided into 5 sections, each with a different task and deadline. The tasks are as follows:</p> <p>– September 2024: Synergize scalable e-commerce</p> <p>– November 2024: Disseminate standardized metrics</p> <p>– January 2025: Coordinate e-business applications</p> <p>– March 2025: Foster holistically superior methodologies</p> <p>– May 2025: Deploy strategic networks with compelling e-business needs</p> <p>The image you provided is of a slide with a title “TIMELINE” at the top center. Below the title is a horizontal timeline graphic that spans from September 2024 to May 2025. The timeline is divided into five sections, each with a designated month and year, and an associated objective:</p> <ol type="1"> <li><p>“SEP 2024” with the objective “Synergize scalable e-commerce”</p></li> <li><p>“NOV 2024” with the objective “Disseminate standardized metrics”</p></li> <li><p>“JAN 2025” with the objective “Coordinate e-business applications”</p></li> <li><p>“MAR 2025” with the objective “Foster holistically superior methodologies”</p></li> <li><p>“MAY 2025” with the objective “Deploy strategic networks with compelling e-business needs”</p></li> </ol> <p>Each section is represented by an arrow pointing to the right that starts from the month and extends to the right with the objective contained in the body of the arrow. The colors of the image are mostly shades of blue and grey, with the timeline graphic against a lighter background. At the bottom right corner, there’s a page number or slide number indicated by “11,” and just above it, the year “2024” is written as a note. The overall aesthetic is professional and likely part of a business presentation.</p> <p>Current Picture Smart Sample Description</p> <p>Picture Smart AI Sample Short Description</p> <p>Picture Smart AI Sample Long Description</p> <p>Caption is chart, pie chart. These tags describe the photo: circle, diagram, screenshot, text. This tag probably describes the photo: font. This tag vaguely describes the photo: design.</p> <p>The image is a pie chart that shows the favorite fruits of a group of people. There are four categories: melon, apple, mango, and orange. The melon category is blue and takes up 19% of the pie. The apple category is green and takes up 19% of the pie. The mango category is yellow and takes up 25% of the pie. The orange category is orange and takes up 37% of the pie.</p> <p>The image is a pie chart on a white background with a title at the top that reads “Favorite Fruit.” The chart is divided into four segments, each representing a different fruit with a corresponding percentage, indicating the preference of a group of people.</p> <p>The largest segment is orange, representing oranges, and takes up 37% of the chart. The second largest is yellow, indicating mangoes, accounting for 25%. Two other fruits, melon and apple, each take up 19% of the chart; melon is depicted in blue, and apple in green.</p> <p>Overall, the chart provides a visual representation of the preferred fruits with oranges being the most popular, followed by mangoes, and then melon and apple with equal preference.</p> <h6 id="ai-services">AI services</h6> <p>We are continually refining the offerings of Picture Smart AI. We have made significant advancements thanks to the insights gathered during the Early Adopter program, which included assessments of Google’s Gemini and OpenAI’s ChatGPT.</p> <p>Following further evaluations, we’ve decided to replace Google’s Gemini with Anthropic’s Claude. Claude demonstrated more accurate and reliable image descriptions, with significantly fewer hallucinations. This enhancement is available in the March 2024 release and later.</p> <h6 id="relevance-of-two-services">Relevance of two services</h6> <p>We received great user feedback on the importance of utilizing two services for the image descriptions, mainly because they allow you to spot hallucinations.</p> <p>You can use the alternative service via the Get more details link at the bottom of the results viewer. In addition, both service descriptions can be displayed directly by pressing the SHIFT key along with a Picture Smart command. For instance, the command INSERT+SPACEBAR, P, SHIFT+W will provide you with two descriptions of the current window.</p> <p>Read more on our <a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/picturesmartchallenges">Picture Smart Challenges</a> page.</p> <h6 id="asking-questions-about-a-picture">Asking Questions About a Picture</h6> <p>By popular request, Picture Smart AI offers the ability to send follow-up prompts or questions in order to obtain additional details about a picture that may not have been covered in the initial description.</p> <p>Once you have performed a Picture Smart AI command such as INSERT+SPACEBAR, P, F, and the description is displayed in the Results Viewer, press ENTER on the Ask questions about this image link near the bottom of the window. If you chose the option to get more details or included SHIFT as part of the command to view detailed descriptions from both AI services, then the link is called Ask Chat GPT questions about this image.</p> <p>After selecting the link to ask questions, you are immediately placed in an edit box. Type a prompt and press ENTER. For instance, for a picture of a beach at sunset, you might say, “can you describe the sunset and how it looks going down over the ocean.” After a few seconds, during which JAWS will play a sound to indicate progress, the Results Viewer window updates with the response, and JAWS automatically reads it. Your focus remains in the edit box, so you can type another prompt.</p> <p>In situations where you already have some basic knowledge about an image, you can include ALT with any Picture Smart command to immediately ask a question about specific details.</p> <p>For example, suppose you were shopping on Amazon for a product like an Multicooker or Air Fryer. You already have a basic idea of what the product is, but you may want to know upfront if the product contains physical buttons or a touch activated display. You could press INSERT+SPACEBAR, P, ALT+C, type your question followed by ENTER, and Picture Smart AI attempts to answer the question about the selected image instead of just providing a general description. Once the results containing the response are displayed, you can still use the Ask questions about this image link to ask follow-up questions if needed.</p> <p>Your questions and responses are maintained for the current Results Viewer session until you close the window. To review and copy specific responses for pasting in another application, press ESC to exit Forms Mode, and then use H or SHIFT+H to navigate to the heading that corresponds to the question and response you want to copy.</p> <p>Following is an example picture to demonstrate a question and response.</p> <p>The image displays an organizational chart with various positions and names. The chart is headed by a President, followed by an Executive Assistant and several Vice Presidents (VPs) overseeing departments such as Finance, Technology, Operations, Marketing, and Production. Under the VPs are different managerial and specialist roles like Accounting, Help Desk, Facilities, Project Manager, Production Manager, and Dispatch. The chart uses color-coding to differentiate between national, domestic, and international roles.</p> <p>User Question:</p> <p>Who is marked as international?</p> <p>Response:</p> <p>In the organizational chart, the “Transportation VP” role, held by “Ian Hansson,” is color-coded as international. This is indicated by the blue color of the box associated with that position.</p> <h6 id="providing-feedback">Providing Feedback</h6> <p>Even though Picture Smart AI has transitioned out of the Early Adopter Program and is the new standard for describing pictures, users are still encouraged to provide feedback on there experiences. To provide feedback, use the Give feedback about this feature link at the bottom of the Picture Smart Results Viewer window.</p> <h6 id="voice-assistant-commands-for-picture-smart">Voice Assistant Commands for Picture Smart</h6> <p>For users of the Voice Assistant feature, you can say “Hey Sharky” along with one of the following suggested voice commands to activate Picture Smart AI.</p> <ul> <li>“Describe the screen”</li> <li>“Describe the current window”</li> <li>“Describe the current control”</li> <li>“Describe the current file”</li> <li>“Describe the picture under the camera”</li> <li>“Describe the picture on the clipboard”</li> </ul> <h6 id="accessing-legacy-picture-smart">Accessing Legacy Picture Smart</h6> <p>In situations where you may need to access legacy Picture Smart functionality, add CTRL to a Picture Smart command. Some users have reported that accessing text in images sometimes works better with the older Picture Smart. We are working on further improving the text recognition of Picture Smart AI.</p> <h6 id="mouse-mode-fusion-only">Mouse Mode (Fusion only)</h6> <p>Mouse Mode in Fusion provides an alternative method to access and utilize Picture Smart AI without relying on JAWS hotkeys. By using Mouse Mode, you can bypass the need for keyboard shortcuts, making it easier to access Picture Smart AI if you prefer mouse navigation or if you encounter issues with hotkeys. This method ensures that the feature is accessible to Fusion users with different preferences and needs.</p> <ul> <li>To launch and use Picture Smart AI through Mouse Mode, do one of the following: <ul> <li>On the Tools toolbar tab, select the Picture Smart button.</li> <li>Press CAPS LOCK+CTRL+P.</li> </ul></li> <li>After Fusion announces, “Picture Smart Mouse Mode,” click and drag the mouse pointer over the item you want to have described.</li> <li>Once it is processed, the description displays in the Results Viewer window and is also read aloud. Note: If you press and hold SHIFT just before releasing the mouse button, full AI results from Claude and ChatGPT will display in the Results Viewer window. If you press and hold CTRL just before releasing the mouse button, legacy Picture Smart results will display in the Results Viewer window.</li> </ul> <h6 id="picture-smart-privacy">Picture Smart Privacy</h6> <p>All services we use for Picture Smart follow our AI Privacy guidelines. Freedom Scientific, as well as our AI Service partners, do not store or train on the submitted images, prompts, or associated answers. Read more on our <a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/aiprivacystatement/">AI Privacy Statement</a> page.</p> <h5 id="fscompanion-your-ai-powered-assistant-for-learning-jaws-and-microsoft-applications-2">FSCompanion: Your AI-Powered assistant for Learning JAWS and Microsoft Applications</h5> <p>For a brief introduction to FSCompanion, watch our <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rI3tYR6UdUE">video</a> on YouTube.</p> <p>With so many features and keystrokes available between JAWS, Windows, and the various Office apps, it can be challenging to locate the information you need to perform a specific task or even look up a setting or keystroke you no longer recall. Our AI assistant, FSCompanion, lets you ask questions about JAWS and other applications and quickly provides the information you need without you having to search through multiple documents and web pages to find it. Want to know how a particular JAWS feature works, or the sequence of keystrokes to perform a specific task in Word? Ask FSCompanion, and the AI searches through various help and training resources in a matter of seconds, and provides the key details in a concise step-by-step format.</p> <p>FSCompanion has been trained using JAWS help and training data as well as support content from Microsoft. It is capable of responding to questions about the following, with an emphasis on providing specific keystrokes as answers.</p> <ul> <li><p>JAWS usage</p></li> <li><p>Windows usage and navigation</p></li> <li><p>Web browsing</p></li> <li><p>Microsoft Word</p></li> <li><p>Microsoft Excel</p></li> <li><p>Microsoft Outlook</p></li> <li><p>Microsoft PowerPoint To open FSCompanion, do one of the following:</p></li> <li><p>In JAWS, press the layered command, INSERT+SPACEBAR, followed by F1. FSCompanion is also located in the JAWS Help menu under Web Resources.</p></li> <li><p>Go to <a href="https://fscompanion.ai">FSCompanion.ai</a> from a PC or mobile device using your preferred web browser. Once the FSCompanion page opens, press TAB to move to the edit field and type a question. After typing a question, press ENTER, and JAWS will automatically read the response as soon as it is displayed. Focus remains in the edit field, so you can ask any follow-up questions.</p></li> </ul> <p>To review answers, use H, SHIFT+H, or the ARROW keys. Select the New Conversation button to start a new topic, or select the Feedback button to submit any comments about a response.</p> <p>Here are a few example questions to help get you started.</p> <ul> <li>How do I change the JAWS volume?</li> <li>How do I select cells in Excel?</li> <li>How do I turn off the Preview Pane in Outlook?</li> <li>How do I select text?</li> <li>How do I set a PlaceMarker on a page?</li> <li>How do I create an email signature?</li> <li>How do I use the JAWS Dictionary Manager? Please ask as many questions as you like, and don’t hesitate to give feedback on your experiences. The types of questions you ask and the feedback you provide are very important as it helps our team train the model to be more accurate.</li> </ul> <p>Note: FSCompanion is optimized for English, as it has been trained with English documentation. This means that the answers it gives are based on English keystrokes and terminology. For the best experience, please use it in English. If you ask questions in another language, the keystrokes and descriptions it provides might not be accurate. We are working on supporting additional languages.</p> <p><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/jaws/">Back to JAWS Training</a></p> <h3 id="picture-smart-ai-1">Picture Smart AI</h3> <p>For a brief introduction to Picture Smart AI™, watch our <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eTWNtEChnt0">video</a> on YouTube.</p> <p>While navigating the digital landscape, you might encounter photos, charts, and other visual elements without an alternative description. This can make it challenging to understand the information provided by the visual content. The JAWS® Picture Smart AI feature allows you to submit a photo to be analyzed and then displays a description of the picture in the JAWS Results Viewer window.</p> <p>This revolutionary update to the original Picture Smart feature, introduced in 2019, integrates with the latest artificial intelligence (AI) technology from services like Chat GPT from Open AI and Claude from Anthropic to offer a whole new level of accessibility to graphical information. Descriptions might offer details such as the number of people in the photo including how they look and what activities they may be performing, recognizable landmarks, landscape details such as the color of the sky, grass, or trees, the layout of information in a visual chart or slide, and much more. Additionally, any text in the picture such as writing on a sign or piece of clothing may also be provided in the description.</p> <p>To use Picture Smart, press INSERT+SPACEBAR followed by P to access the Picture Smart layer, and then use one of the following keystrokes:</p> <ul> <li>A – Opens the Picture Smart dialog box where you can acquire an image from a flatbed scanner or the Freedom Scientific PEARL camera and submit it to be described.</li> <li>F – Describes the currently selected image in File Explorer. Supported image formats include BMP, JPEG, GIF, TIF, PNG, or HEIC.</li> <li>C – Describes any currently selected control. For instance, if focused on a picture in a Word document or on a social media website like Facebook, this command describes the picture. When using this command on a web page, make sure your browser window is maximized for best results .</li> <li>B – Describes the contents of the Windows Clipboard if it contains an image.</li> <li>S – Describes the entire screen.</li> <li>W – Describes the current application window.</li> <li>ENTER – Describes an image based on the current application and context. This eliminates the need to remember multiple keystrokes constantly. For instance: <ul> <li>If someone is presenting in Teams, it describes the current slide.</li> <li>If you are on a web page, it describes the current image or control.</li> <li>If you are in File Explorer, it describes the currently selected file.</li> <li>If playing a video from a source like YouTube, it describes a screenshot from the current position in the video.</li> <li>If a PowerPoint slideshow is running, it describes the current slide.</li> <li>If you are in PowerPoint with a slide selected but not in an active slideshow, it describes the currently visible slide.</li> </ul></li> <li>QUESTION MARK – Displays help for the Picture Smart layer. After running Picture Smart AI, you will also be alerted to any potential problems with an image that may result in poor descriptions. For example, if your browser window is not maximized, images may be clipped, leading to inaccurate descriptions. In this case, an expandable alert is displayed at the top of the Results Viewer prior to the description. Press ENTER on this alert to view the full details. You can then close the Results Viewer, maximize your browser window, and try running Picture Smart AI on the image again.</li> </ul> <p>Once a submitted image finishes processing, Picture Smart AI displays a short description by default. To display more in-depth descriptions, select the Get more details link near the bottom of the Results Viewer. You can also add SHIFT to a Picture Smart command to immediately display the more detailed descriptions. For example, INSERT+SPACEBAR, P, SHIFT+F.</p> <p>To demonstrate the difference in the level of detail, here are a few example photos along with resulting descriptions generated using both the original Picture Smart and Picture Smart AI. You can also try this feature out yourself by pressing INSERT+SPACEBAR, P, C while focused on each photo.</p> <p>Current Picture Smart Sample Description</p> <p>Picture Smart AI Sample Short Description</p> <p>Picture Smart AI Sample Long Description</p> <p>Caption is a group of people sitting on a beach. These tags describe the photo: beach, clothing, girl, group, human face, outdoor, people, person, sky, woman. These tags probably describe the photo: fun, sitting, summer, vacation, water. This tag possibly describes the photo: ground.</p> <p>The image shows a group of six friends sitting on the beach. They are all smiling and laughing, and some of them are singing. One of them is playing the guitar. The sun is setting in the background, and the waves are crashing on the shore.</p> <p>The image depicts a group of friends enjoying themselves on a beach at what appears to be sunset due to the warm, golden lighting. There are five individuals in the foreground, with one more partially seen in the background. The group is casually dressed in summer attire and seems to be engaged in a lively and joyful conversation.</p> <p>In the left part of the image, there’s a man sitting on the sand, wearing a light blue button-up shirt and smiling broadly, evidently amused by the conversation. To his right, a woman is laughing heartily, her head tossed back and her hands raised—she’s wearing a yellow top.</p> <p>Centered in the image, another woman is smiling and appears to be sharing a moment of enjoyment with the man on her left; she has her arm extended as if she is pointing at something or someone outside the frame. Turning clockwise, the next woman is in profile and not fully visible, she’s wearing a red and blue checked shirt, and seems engaged with the person beside her.</p> <p>On the right side, another person is mostly turned away from the camera, wearing a white garment that could be a sweater or jacket; this individual appears to be looking back towards the others with a smile.</p> <p>The beach setting provides a tranquil background with the ocean meeting the horizon. The mood is upbeat and the image exudes a sense of friendship, relaxation, and the simple joys of life. There’s a harmonious mix of motion and stillness, with some individuals in mid-gesture, which adds to the dynamic of a candid and spontaneous moment.</p> <p>Current Picture Smart Sample Description</p> <p>Picture Smart AI Sample Short Description</p> <p>Picture Smart AI Sample Long Description</p> <p>Caption is timeline. These tags describe the photo: display, font, screenshot, text. These tags probably describe the photo: diagram, number.</p> <p>The image is a timeline that spans from September 2024 to May 2025. It is divided into 5 sections, each with a different task and deadline. The tasks are as follows:</p> <p>– September 2024: Synergize scalable e-commerce</p> <p>– November 2024: Disseminate standardized metrics</p> <p>– January 2025: Coordinate e-business applications</p> <p>– March 2025: Foster holistically superior methodologies</p> <p>– May 2025: Deploy strategic networks with compelling e-business needs</p> <p>The image you provided is of a slide with a title “TIMELINE” at the top center. Below the title is a horizontal timeline graphic that spans from September 2024 to May 2025. The timeline is divided into five sections, each with a designated month and year, and an associated objective:</p> <ol type="1"> <li><p>“SEP 2024” with the objective “Synergize scalable e-commerce”</p></li> <li><p>“NOV 2024” with the objective “Disseminate standardized metrics”</p></li> <li><p>“JAN 2025” with the objective “Coordinate e-business applications”</p></li> <li><p>“MAR 2025” with the objective “Foster holistically superior methodologies”</p></li> <li><p>“MAY 2025” with the objective “Deploy strategic networks with compelling e-business needs”</p></li> </ol> <p>Each section is represented by an arrow pointing to the right that starts from the month and extends to the right with the objective contained in the body of the arrow. The colors of the image are mostly shades of blue and grey, with the timeline graphic against a lighter background. At the bottom right corner, there’s a page number or slide number indicated by “11,” and just above it, the year “2024” is written as a note. The overall aesthetic is professional and likely part of a business presentation.</p> <p>Current Picture Smart Sample Description</p> <p>Picture Smart AI Sample Short Description</p> <p>Picture Smart AI Sample Long Description</p> <p>Caption is chart, pie chart. These tags describe the photo: circle, diagram, screenshot, text. This tag probably describes the photo: font. This tag vaguely describes the photo: design.</p> <p>The image is a pie chart that shows the favorite fruits of a group of people. There are four categories: melon, apple, mango, and orange. The melon category is blue and takes up 19% of the pie. The apple category is green and takes up 19% of the pie. The mango category is yellow and takes up 25% of the pie. The orange category is orange and takes up 37% of the pie.</p> <p>The image is a pie chart on a white background with a title at the top that reads “Favorite Fruit.” The chart is divided into four segments, each representing a different fruit with a corresponding percentage, indicating the preference of a group of people.</p> <p>The largest segment is orange, representing oranges, and takes up 37% of the chart. The second largest is yellow, indicating mangoes, accounting for 25%. Two other fruits, melon and apple, each take up 19% of the chart; melon is depicted in blue, and apple in green.</p> <p>Overall, the chart provides a visual representation of the preferred fruits with oranges being the most popular, followed by mangoes, and then melon and apple with equal preference.</p> <h5 id="ai-services-1">AI services</h5> <p>We are continually refining the offerings of Picture Smart AI. We have made significant advancements thanks to the insights gathered during the Early Adopter program, which included assessments of Google’s Gemini and OpenAI’s ChatGPT.</p> <p>Following further evaluations, we’ve decided to replace Google’s Gemini with Anthropic’s Claude. Claude demonstrated more accurate and reliable image descriptions, with significantly fewer hallucinations. This enhancement is available in the March 2024 release and later.</p> <h6 id="relevance-of-two-services-1">Relevance of two services</h6> <p>We received great user feedback on the importance of utilizing two services for the image descriptions, mainly because they allow you to spot hallucinations.</p> <p>You can use the alternative service via the Get more details link at the bottom of the results viewer. In addition, both service descriptions can be displayed directly by pressing the SHIFT key along with a Picture Smart command. For instance, the command INSERT+SPACEBAR, P, SHIFT+W will provide you with two descriptions of the current window.</p> <p>Read more on our <a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/picturesmartchallenges">Picture Smart Challenges</a> page.</p> <h5 id="asking-questions-about-a-picture-1">Asking Questions About a Picture</h5> <p>By popular request, Picture Smart AI offers the ability to send follow-up prompts or questions in order to obtain additional details about a picture that may not have been covered in the initial description.</p> <p>Once you have performed a Picture Smart AI command such as INSERT+SPACEBAR, P, F, and the description is displayed in the Results Viewer, press ENTER on the Ask questions about this image link near the bottom of the window. If you chose the option to get more details or included SHIFT as part of the command to view detailed descriptions from both AI services, then the link is called Ask Chat GPT questions about this image.</p> <p>After selecting the link to ask questions, you are immediately placed in an edit box. Type a prompt and press ENTER. For instance, for a picture of a beach at sunset, you might say, “can you describe the sunset and how it looks going down over the ocean.” After a few seconds, during which JAWS will play a sound to indicate progress, the Results Viewer window updates with the response, and JAWS automatically reads it. Your focus remains in the edit box, so you can type another prompt.</p> <p>In situations where you already have some basic knowledge about an image, you can include ALT with any Picture Smart command to immediately ask a question about specific details.</p> <p>For example, suppose you were shopping on Amazon for a product like an Multicooker or Air Fryer. You already have a basic idea of what the product is, but you may want to know upfront if the product contains physical buttons or a touch activated display. You could press INSERT+SPACEBAR, P, ALT+C, type your question followed by ENTER, and Picture Smart AI attempts to answer the question about the selected image instead of just providing a general description. Once the results containing the response are displayed, you can still use the Ask questions about this image link to ask follow-up questions if needed.</p> <p>Your questions and responses are maintained for the current Results Viewer session until you close the window. To review and copy specific responses for pasting in another application, press ESC to exit Forms Mode, and then use H or SHIFT+H to navigate to the heading that corresponds to the question and response you want to copy.</p> <p>Following is an example picture to demonstrate a question and response.</p> <p>The image displays an organizational chart with various positions and names. The chart is headed by a President, followed by an Executive Assistant and several Vice Presidents (VPs) overseeing departments such as Finance, Technology, Operations, Marketing, and Production. Under the VPs are different managerial and specialist roles like Accounting, Help Desk, Facilities, Project Manager, Production Manager, and Dispatch. The chart uses color-coding to differentiate between national, domestic, and international roles.</p> <p>User Question:</p> <p>Who is marked as international?</p> <p>Response:</p> <p>In the organizational chart, the “Transportation VP” role, held by “Ian Hansson,” is color-coded as international. This is indicated by the blue color of the box associated with that position.</p> <h5 id="providing-feedback-1">Providing Feedback</h5> <p>Even though Picture Smart AI has transitioned out of the Early Adopter Program and is the new standard for describing pictures, users are still encouraged to provide feedback on there experiences. To provide feedback, use the Give feedback about this feature link at the bottom of the Picture Smart Results Viewer window.</p> <h5 id="voice-assistant-commands-for-picture-smart-1">Voice Assistant Commands for Picture Smart</h5> <p>For users of the Voice Assistant feature, you can say “Hey Sharky” along with one of the following suggested voice commands to activate Picture Smart AI.</p> <ul> <li>“Describe the screen”</li> <li>“Describe the current window”</li> <li>“Describe the current control”</li> <li>“Describe the current file”</li> <li>“Describe the picture under the camera”</li> <li>“Describe the picture on the clipboard”</li> </ul> <h5 id="accessing-legacy-picture-smart-1">Accessing Legacy Picture Smart</h5> <p>In situations where you may need to access legacy Picture Smart functionality, add CTRL to a Picture Smart command. Some users have reported that accessing text in images sometimes works better with the older Picture Smart. We are working on further improving the text recognition of Picture Smart AI.</p> <h5 id="mouse-mode-fusion-only-1">Mouse Mode (Fusion only)</h5> <p>Mouse Mode in Fusion provides an alternative method to access and utilize Picture Smart AI without relying on JAWS hotkeys. By using Mouse Mode, you can bypass the need for keyboard shortcuts, making it easier to access Picture Smart AI if you prefer mouse navigation or if you encounter issues with hotkeys. This method ensures that the feature is accessible to Fusion users with different preferences and needs.</p> <ul> <li>To launch and use Picture Smart AI through Mouse Mode, do one of the following: <ul> <li>On the Tools toolbar tab, select the Picture Smart button.</li> <li>Press CAPS LOCK+CTRL+P.</li> </ul></li> <li>After Fusion announces, “Picture Smart Mouse Mode,” click and drag the mouse pointer over the item you want to have described.</li> <li>Once it is processed, the description displays in the Results Viewer window and is also read aloud. Note: If you press and hold SHIFT just before releasing the mouse button, full AI results from Claude and ChatGPT will display in the Results Viewer window. If you press and hold CTRL just before releasing the mouse button, legacy Picture Smart results will display in the Results Viewer window.</li> </ul> <h5 id="picture-smart-privacy-1">Picture Smart Privacy</h5> <p>All services we use for Picture Smart follow our AI Privacy guidelines. Freedom Scientific, as well as our AI Service partners, do not store or train on the submitted images, prompts, or associated answers. Read more on our <a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/aiprivacystatement/">AI Privacy Statement</a> page.</p> <p><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/jaws/">Back to JAWS id="software-installation-guide">Software Installation Guide</h3> <ul> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/enterprise/">Enterprise</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/enterprise/activating-software-licenses/">Activating Software Licenses</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/enterprise/installation/">Software Installation Guide</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/enterprise/using-jaws-zoomtext-and-fusion-with-remote-access-software/">Using JAWS, ZoomText, and Fusion with Remote Access Software</a></li> </ul> <h4 id="software-installation-guide-1">Software Installation Guide</h4> <h5 id="installation">Installation</h5> <p>When installing one or two copies of JAWS, ZoomText, or Fusion, the easiest option is to manually run the installer and follow the prompts. In environments where you need to install for many users, such as a university or government agency, manual installation can become tedious and time consuming. To help speed up the installation process in enterprise environments, Freedom Scientific software offers a wide range of options to assist IT personnel with automating the installation process.</p> <h5 id="choosing-a-setup-package">Choosing a Setup Package</h5> <p>The setup packages for JAWS, ZoomText, and Fusion are available as either a Connected or Offline installer.</p> <p>The Connected installer is a small setup package that downloads all necessary components and language files over the internet. The computer you are installing on must be able to access the public internet in order to use this setup type. The latest Connected installer for each product is always available from the following pages.</p> <ul> <li><p><a href="https://support.freedomscientific.com/Downloads/JAWS">JAWS Downloads Page</a></p></li> <li><p><a href="https://support.freedomscientific.com/Downloads/ZoomText">ZoomText Downloads Page</a></p></li> <li><p><a href="https://support.freedomscientific.com/Downloads/fusion">Fusion Downloads Page</a> The Offline installer allows you to install the software when you want to avoid connecting to the internet to access components, or if you will be installing on computers in your organization with limited internet access. The Offline installer is quite large as it contains everything necessary to install the product in a single executable. You can download the Offline installer for each product (JAWS, ZoomText, or Fusion) from the following page.</p></li> <li><p><a href="https://support.freedomscientific.com/Downloads/OfflineInstallers">Offline Installer Page</a></p></li> </ul> <h5 id="customizing-the-installation">Customizing the Installation</h5> <p>Both the Connected and Offline setup packages offer several command line arguments you can use to customize how the software is installed. If your deployment infrastructure supports the use of executable installers, the easiest way to customize the installation process is to run one of the offline installers with the command line options you need. Available command line options are described in the following sections. You can also run the setup package with the /Help or /MoreHelp options to Display a dialog box containing additional information about the available command line arguments. For example,</p> <p>c:.exe /help</p> <h6 id="selecting-a-setup-type">Selecting a Setup Type</h6> <p>Use the /Type argument followed by an option to specify the setup type to use instead of the default. For example,</p> <p>c:.exe /type Silent</p> <p>Available setup types include:</p> <ul> <li>Silent – Silently installs a typical installation without displaying any installation dialog boxes or prompts.</li> <li>Repair – Repairs an existing installation. During the repair, progress dialogs are displayed and a clicking tone is played. At the end, you are prompted to restart the computer.</li> <li>SilentRepair – Silently repairs an existing installation without displaying any installation dialog boxes or prompts.</li> <li>Uninstall – Uninstalls an existing installation.</li> <li>SilentUninstall – Silently uninstalls an existing installation without removing shared components.</li> <li>SilentSharedUninstall – Silently uninstalls an existing installation and the shared components. Note: If you want to install the software without any prompts, you can also use the /silent command line argument instead of /type silent. For example,</li> </ul> <p>c:.exe /silent</p> <h6 id="selecting-languages">Selecting Languages</h6> <p>You can tell the setup package which product languages you want installed, as well as specify the language used by the installer if you want dialogs and prompts displayed during setup.</p> <p>To install specific languages, use the /language command line argument followed by a comma delimited list of the three letter language codes of the product languages to use during a clean install instead of only the Operating System Language. During an install, the first product language specified will be used to determine the language of the shortcuts, the default synthesizers, and the default braille drivers. For example,</p> <p>c:.exe /Language deu,enu,esn</p> <p>The German, English, and Spanish product languages are installed along with the German shortcuts, default synthesizers, and default Braille drivers. For actions like an update or a repair, the previously installed product languages will be used and this option will be ignored.</p> <p>The following language codes are supported:</p> <ul> <li>Arabic: arb</li> <li>Danish: dan</li> <li>German: deu</li> <li>English: enu</li> <li>Spanish: esn</li> <li>Finnish: fin</li> <li>French: fra</li> <li>French Canadian: frc</li> <li>Hebrew: heb</li> <li>Hungarian: hun</li> <li>Italian: ita</li> <li>Belgian Dutch: nlb</li> <li>Dutch: nld</li> <li>Norwegian: nor</li> <li>Brazilian Portuguese: ptb</li> <li>Russian: rus</li> <li>Slovak: sky</li> <li>Swedish: sve</li> <li>Turkish: trk To specify the language used by the installer, use the /InstallerUILanguage command line argument followed by the three-letter language code you want to use for the installer user interface instead of the operating system language. For example,</li> </ul> <p>c:.exe /InstallerUILanguage enu</p> <p>All dialogs and prompts are displayed in English.</p> <h6 id="disabling-external-services">Disabling External Services</h6> <p>When installing JAWS, ZoomText, or Fusion on computers in highly secure environments such as hospitals, banks, or government agencies, administrators can disable product features that connect to the internet. This ensures compliance with security policies while maintaining core product functionality.</p> <p>During installation, you can apply one of the following command line arguments to control which features are enabled or disabled.</p> <h6 id="disableexternalservices">DisableExternalServices</h6> <p>Use this command line argument to turn off all product features that connect to the internet, allowing the product to run fully offline. For example:</p> <p>c:.exe /DisableExternalServices</p> <p>When this option is used, all program files are still installed; however, features requiring Internet access are disabled at startup. This includes:</p> <ul> <li>Automatic updates – Notifications are disabled, the Check for Updates option is unavailable, update settings are grayed out, and script updates are not applied automatically.</li> <li>Voice Assistant – Activation using a wake word or keystrokes is disabled, no icon is displayed, and the Startup Wizard option is removed.</li> <li>Message Center – Notifications and access options are unavailable.</li> <li>Error Reporting – All related settings are disabled, and no prompts are displayed following application crashes.</li> <li>Anonymous Usage Data Collection (Telemetry) – All related settings are disabled, and users are not prompted to opt in during the Startup Wizard.</li> <li>Support Tool – The tool can still be run to collect system details, however only the option to manually send the report is available.</li> <li>Research It – All menu options and keystrokes are unavailable.</li> <li>Add/Remove Voices – All menu options are unavailable.</li> <li>AI Based Features – All menu and keystroke access to AI features (including Picture Smart, AI Labeler, Vispero Companion, and Page Explorer) is disabled. Note that Vispero Companion remains accessible through a web browser.</li> <li>Product Activation – Internet-based activation remains available following installation; however, periodic license verification checks and automatic license updates do not function.</li> <li>JAWS Tandem – Keystrokes and menu options for establishing a Tandem Center session over the internet between two computers running JAWS are not available. Note: Use of the product in remote access or virtual environments remains supported even with external services disabled. Additionally, Tandem Direct is still available for establishing a connection over an internal network between two computers running JAWS.</li> </ul> <h6 id="disableexternalaiservices">DisableExternalAIServices</h6> <p>For environments that restrict the use of AI specifically, use this command line argument to disable only AI-based features. For example:</p> <p>c:.exe /DisableExternalAIServices</p> <p>When this option is used, all program files are installed; however, access to AI-based features (including Vispero Companion, Page Explorer, Picture Smart, AI Labeler, and Voice Assistant) is disabled at startup.</p> <p>All other Internet-connected services remain available.</p> <p>For more information on how AI services handle data, see the <a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/aiprivacystatement/">AI Privacy Statement</a>.</p> <h6 id="advanced-customization-using-additionalsettings.ini-optional">Advanced Customization Using AdditionalSettings.ini (Optional)</h6> <p>For more granular control over installed features, you can use an AdditionalSettings.ini file. This file allows administrators to define detailed installation behavior, including:</p> <ul> <li>Options</li> <li>Individual components</li> <li>Configuration changes</li> <li>ConfigNames</li> <li>Domains</li> <li>Key assignments To extract an AdditionalSettings.ini file from any installer, add the /ExtractAdditionalSettings command line argument along with the folder and file name to extract to. For example,</li> </ul> <p>c:.exe /ExtractAdditionalSettings “c:setup.ini”</p> <p>This generates a sample configuration file with comments that document how to configure specific customizations.</p> <p>IMPORTANT: After making any required customizations, ensure the AdditionalSettings.ini file is located in the same directory as the installer before starting installation.</p> <h6 id="extraction-modes">Extraction Modes</h6> <p>You can extract different versions of the configuration file depending on your needs by adding one of the following types to the /ExtractAdditionalSettings command line argument:</p> <ul> <li>Default – Generates a template file with all options commented out.</li> <li>DisableExternalServices – Generates a configuration file that disables and prevents installation of all Internet-connected features. <ul> <li>This option should not be used together with the /DisableExternalServices or /DisableExternalAIServices command line arguments.</li> <li>It is intended for administrators who require more granular control (for example, enabling Error Reporting while disabling other services).</li> </ul></li> <li>DisableExternalAIServices – Generates a configuration file that disables and prevents installation of AI-based features. <ul> <li>This option should not be used together with the /DisableExternalAIServices or /DisableExternalServices command line arguments.</li> <li>It is intended for administrators who want selective control (for example, enabling Voice Assistant while disabling other AI features).</li> </ul></li> </ul> <h6 id="picture-smart-specific-configuration">Picture Smart Specific Configuration</h6> <p>For additional control over Picture Smart, you can manually add the following settings to the AdditionalSettings.ini file:</p> <ul> <li>IsPictureSmartEnabled – Set to 0 to disable or set to 1 to enable.</li> <li>IsPictureSmartRestricted – Set to 0 to use the default AI functionality or set to 1 to restrict Picture Smart to legacy functionality. For example, If Internet-connected features are disabled but users still require AI-generated descriptions for visual content (such as charts or work-related images), you can enable Picture Smart by adding the following lines to AdditionalSettings.ini:</li> </ul> <p>[AppConfiguration]</p> <p>IsPictureSmartEnabled=1</p> <p>IsPictureSmartRestricted=0</p> <h6 id="using-layout-to-download-installation-files-for-offline-deployment">Using /Layout to Download Installation Files for Offline Deployment</h6> <p>For even greater customization, you can use the /Layout command line option with the Connected installers for JAWS, ZoomText, or Fusion to download the individual MSI files to a specified folder. For example,</p> <p>C:.exe /Layout “C:setup”</p> <p>You can then use scripts or other install automated tools to sequence these files for installation on offline computers.</p> <p>When you use the /Layout command, a dialog box displays with two options: Options and Layout. By default, /Layout extracts files in the same language as the system language. Select the Options button if you want to change the language or extract installers in multiple languages. Select the Layout button to begin downloading files.</p> <p>You can also add the /Language command to automatically download install files for specific languages. For example,</p> <p>c:.exe /Language deu,enu,esn /Layout “c:setup”</p> <p>The installer files for the German, English, and Spanish product languages are downloaded to the c:setupfolder.</p> <p>Finally, the /Layout command creates an “Example MSI scripts” folder, which contains batch files that run the installers in the proper sequence with the necessary flags. These scripts demonstrate how to install using this approach.</p> <p>Note: The /Layout command only works properly with the Connected installers, available by default on the Freedom Scientific Downloads pages. It does not work with Offline installers.</p> <h3 id="student-of-the-month-1">Student of the Month</h3> <h4 id="student-of-the-month-2">Student of the Month</h4> <ul> <li><a id="follow-us-on-these-podcast-apps">Follow Us on These Podcast Apps</h5> <ul> <li><a href="https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/freedom-scientific-training-podcast/id1521340640">Apple <p>Follow the subscription instructions for your device to begin listening to our training content today.</p> <h6 id="ios">iOS</h6> <p>To subscribe to and play an episode of the Freedom Scientific Training Podcast on your iOS device, do the following:</p> <ul> <li>Open the Podcast app on your iPhone.</li> <li>Double tap the Search tab on the app’s home screen.</li> <li>Type “Freedom Scientific Training” in the search box, and double tap Search.</li> <li>Double tap the Freedom Scientific Training Podcast button.</li> <li>Double tap the Subscribe button.</li> <li>Double tap an episode and listen.</li> </ul> <h6 id="android">Android</h6> <p>To subscribe to and play an episode of the Freedom Scientific Training Podcast on your Android device, do the following:</p> <ul> <li>Open the Google Podcasts app on your Android device.</li> <li>Tap Explore, which is located at the bottom of the app’s home screen.</li> <li>Select the Search button at the top left of the screen.</li> <li>Type “Freedom Scientific Training” in the search box, and select Search.</li> <li>Tap Freedom Scientific Training Podcast.</li> <li>Tap the Subscribe button.</li> <li>Tap an episode and listen.</li> </ul> <h6 id="listen-on-an-alexa-or-google-home-device">Listen on an Alexa or Google Home Device</h6> <ul> <li>Say the wake word for your device, followed by, “Play the Freedom Scientific Training Podcast.” The latest episode will play.</li> <li>It is not currently possible to request a specific episode, but you can ask the device to play the previous or next episode.</li> </ul> <h6 id="subscribe-to-the-rss-feed-in-outlook">Subscribe to the RSS Feed in Outlook</h6> <p>To subscribe to the RSS Feed for the Freedom Scientific Training Podcast in Outlook, do the following:</p> <ul> <li>Press SHIFT+F6 to navigate to the folders list in Outlook.</li> <li>Press R to locate the RSS Feeds folder.</li> <li>Press SHIFT+F10 or the APPLICATIONS key to right-click on this folder.</li> Whether you are gathering information for work, school, or personal projects, you may need to compare sources, interpret images and visuals, complete online forms, take notes, and organize information from multiple websites.</p> <p>Join APH’s Passport to Innovation series for our first partner session featuring Elizabeth Whitaker from Vispero. In this practical webinar, Elizabeth will share six JAWS tips designed to help users move through web-based research tasks with greater efficiency and confidence.</p> <h6 id="presenters-1">Presenters:</h6> <p>APH and Elizabeth Whitaker of Vispero</p> <h6 id="help-us-spread-the-word-2">Help Us Spread the Word:</h6> <p>Please feel free to share this with someone you think might benefit from attending.</p> <p>Register for <a href="https://aph.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_bxAYZGlJTGyNJQwniizw-g">Partner Webinar with APH: Six JAWS Tips for Streamlining Web Research Workflows</a>.</p> <h5 id="four-classic-jaws-features-that-can-transform-your-workflow">Four Classic JAWS Features That Can Transform Your Workflow</h5> <p>Thursday, August 27, 2026, 12:00 pm Eastern time (U.S. and Canada)</p> <p>Some of the most useful JAWS features have been around for years, but they aren’t always the ones we talk about most often. In this webinar, we’ll revisit four powerful features that can help you save time, increase productivity, and customize JAWS to better support the way you work with documents and web pages. In this session, you’ll learn how to use:</p> <ul> <li>Skim Reading to quickly locate headings, highlighted text, links, and other important information in documents and web pages.</li> <li>Text Analyzer to identify potential errors beyond spelling and grammar in documents, emails, blog posts, and other text before you share them.</li> <li>Speech and Sound Schemes to customize how JAWS presents information using speech and sounds.</li> <li>Dictionary Manager to customize how JAWS pronounces words, phrases, abbreviations, and symbols.</li> </ul> <h6 id="vispero-presenters-1">Vispero Presenters:</h6> <p>Elizabeth Whitaker and Rachel Buchanan</p> <h6 id="acvrep-credits-1">ACVREP Credits:</h6> <p>ACVREP credits will be available for those who attend the live webinar.</p> <h6 id="help-us-spread-the-word-3">Help Us Spread the Word:</h6> <p>Please feel free to share this with someone you think might benefit from attending.</p> <p>Register for <a href="https://us06web.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_gO29_IL8TrG4WfwVo9roMQ">Four Classic JAWS Features That Can Transform Your Workflow</a>.</p> <h5 id="using-ai-connectors-to-bring-your-everyday-apps-and-information-together-1">Using AI Connectors to Bring Your Everyday Apps and Information Together</h5> <p>Thursday, September 3, 2026, 12:00 pm Eastern time (U.S. and Canada)</p> <p>AI becomes even more powerful when it can work with the apps, files, and information you use every day. Instead of copying and pasting content between applications, AI connectors let you access and interact with information across multiple services from a single conversation.</p> <p>In this webinar, we’ll demonstrate how AI connectors can simplify everyday tasks and help you work more efficiently.</p> <p>You’ll learn how to:</p> <ul> <li>Connect AI to services such as email, calendars, cloud storage, and documents.</li> <li>Find information across connected apps without switching between them.</li> <li>Summarize emails, documents, and meeting information in seconds.</li> <li>Combine information from multiple sources to answer questions and complete tasks.</li> <li>Use practical workflows that save time at work, school, and home. Whether you’re organizing your day, researching a project, or managing documents, AI connectors can help you spend less time searching for information and more time getting things done.</li> </ul> <h6 id="vispero-presenters-2">Vispero Presenters:</h6> <p>Elizabeth Whitaker and Rachel Buchanan</p> <h6 id="acvrep-credits-2">ACVREP Credits:</h6> <p>ACVREP credits will be available for those who attend the live webinar.</p> <h6 id="help-us-spread-the-word-4">Help Us Spread the Word:</h6> <p>Please feel free to share this with someone you think might benefit from attending.</p> <p>Register for <a href="https://us06web.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_UuDbdJbORq-5yMg1jPd_Gw">Using AI Connectors to Bring Your Everyday Apps and Information Together</a>.</p> <h5 id="beyond-the-basics-working-more-effectively-with-pdf-documents-and-jaws">Beyond the Basics: Working More Effectively with PDF Documents and JAWS</h5> <p>Thursday, September 17, 2026, 12:00 pm Eastern time (U.S. and Canada)</p> <p>PDF documents are everywhere, from reports and forms to manuals and online resources. In this webinar, we’ll explore practical ways to make working with PDFs easier and more efficient using JAWS.</p> <p>You’ll learn how to:</p> <ul> <li>Access PDF documents using Adobe Acrobat Reader, your web browser, and other available options.</li> <li>Adjust settings that can improve the reading experience.</li> <li>Navigate PDF documents quickly to find the information you need.</li> <li>Complete and submit PDF forms with greater confidence.</li> <li>Understand reading order and tab order, why they matter, and how they affect accessibility.</li> <li>Create a PDF from a Microsoft Word document while preserving accessibility and document structure.</li> </ul> <h6 id="vispero-presenters-3">Vispero Presenters:</h6> <p>Elizabeth Whitaker and Rachel Buchanan</p> <h6 id="acvrep-credits-3">ACVREP Credits:</h6> <p>ACVREP credits will be available for those who attend the live webinar.</p> <h6 id="help-us-spread-the-word-5">Help Us Spread the Word:</h6> <p>Please feel free to share this with someone you think might benefit from attending.</p> <p>Register for <a href="https://us06web.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_4wH8WJEzSuOGjejA3nwIDg">Beyond the Basics: Working More Effectively with PDF Documents and JAWS</a>.</p> <p>View Webinars On Demand</p> <h3 id="using-jaws-zoomtext-and-fusion-with-remote-access-software">Using JAWS, ZoomText, and Fusion with Remote Access Software</h3> <ul> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/enterprise/">Enterprise</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/enterprise/activating-software-licenses/">Activating Software Licenses</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/enterprise/installation/">Software Installation Guide</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/enterprise/using-jaws-zoomtext-and-fusion-with-remote-access-software/">Using JAWS, ZoomText, and Fusion with Remote Access Software</a></li> </ul> <h4 id="using-jaws-zoomtext-and-fusion-with-remote-access-software-1">Using JAWS, ZoomText, and Fusion with Remote Access Software</h4> <p>It is possible to use JAWS, ZoomText, and Fusion in remote/virtual environments like Remote Desktop, Citrix, VMware Horizon, and Amazon WorkSpaces (AWS). There are a couple ways to deploy Freedom Scientific software for use in these environments.</p> <ul> <li><p>To provide the best experience for blind and low vision users, you must add remote authorization to an existing local or network license of JAWS or Fusion. The software must also be installed correctly on both the client work station as well as the server/remote computers or virtual machines. Once properly authorized, the version of JAWS, ZoomText, or Fusion on the remote computer sends information through a virtual channel which then relays this output on the client computer through speech, braille, or magnification. Note: There is a one-time fee to add this Remote Access authorization option and once purchased, you can use the software in remote access environments for the life of that license. For information and cost to add this remote option to your existing license, contact your Freedom Scientific representative or dealer. For ZoomText only users, please note that you will be required to upgrade to a Fusion license in order to use ZoomText in a remote access session.</p></li> <li><p>You can also choose to install the software only on the remote/server computer or virtual machine and not on the client workstation at all. In this setup, remote authorization is not necessary since nothing is installed on the client. You will experience lower performance as the Freedom Scientific virtual channels are not installed. This means that there will be no braille output on the client and speech will be routed using standard Windows audio and port forwarding. Using JAWS, ZoomText, or Fusion this way is ideal for sighted testers or software developers who just want to remotely connect to a computer or virtual machine where the software is installed and run it to verify functionality.</p></li> </ul> <h5 id="helpful-external-resources">Helpful External Resources</h5> <p>While there are a number of online resources available that cover configuring various remote/virtual environments, a few that may be helpful include:</p> <ul> <li><a href="https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/how-to-use-remote-desktop-5fe128d5-8fb1-7a23-3b8a-41e636865e8c">How to Use Remote Desktop</a></li> <li><a href="https://docs.citrix.com/en-us/citrix-virtual-apps-desktops/install-configure.html">Install and configure Citrix virtual apps and desktops</a></li> <li><a href="https://techzone.vmware.com/quick-start-tutorial-series-vmware-horizon-7">Quick start tutorial for VMware Horizon</a></li> <li><a href="https://aws.amazon.com/workspaces/">Amazon WorkSpaces (AWS)</a></li> </ul> <h5 id="system-requirements">System Requirements</h5> <p>In environments where multiple users may be connecting at once, the minimum system requirements for Freedom Scientific software installed on the server are:</p> <ul> <li>Operating System: Windows Server 2016 or later.</li> <li>CPU: 2 CPU-cores with 1 additional CPU-core every 2 users.</li> <li>Memory: 500 MB per user. The requirements of the operating system and other third party applications must also be taken into account and added to this value.</li> <li>GPU: A virtual or physical GPU. For more information on tuning your server, see <a href="https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/performance-tuning/hardware/">docs.microsoft.com</a>.</li> </ul> <p>For client computers as well as Windows workstations that support a single user connection, the standard system requirements for <a href="https://support.freedomscientific.com/Downloads/JAWS/JAWS-System-Requirements">JAWS</a>, <a href="https://support.freedomscientific.com/Downloads/Fusion/Fusion-System-Requirements">Fusion</a>, and <a href="https://support.freedomscientific.com/Downloads/ZoomText/ZoomText-System-Requirements">ZoomText</a> are fine.</p> <h5 id="expected-behavior">Expected Behavior</h5> <p>The following sections provide an overview of how things should work depending on what software is running on the client and server and whether or not remote access authorization is available.</p> <h6 id="zoomtext-running-on-client">ZoomText Running on Client</h6> <p>License Location</p> <p>Server ZoomText</p> <p>Server JAWS</p> <p>Server Fusion</p> <p>Fusion License including Remote Access installed locally on client or network license server</p> <p>Virtual channels load and magnification works as expected</p> <p>n/a</p> <p>Error message, requires matching products</p> <p>Fusion License including Remote Access installed locally on server</p> <p>If server is a workstation operating system, virtual channels load and magnification works as expected. Running on Client</h6> <p>License Location</p> <p>Server ZoomText</p> <p>Server JAWS</p> <p>Server Fusion</p> <p>Fusion License including Remote Access installed locally on client or network license <h6 id="no-freedom-scientific-software-on-client">No Freedom Scientific Software on Client</h6> <p>License Location</p> <p>Server ZoomText</p> <p>Server JAWS</p> <p>Server Fusion</p> <p>License available locally on server or network license server</p> <p>Provides magnification on the client using Windows port forwarding</p> <p>Provides speech on the client (no braille) using Windows port forwarding</p> <p>Provides speech and magnification on the client (no braille) using Windows port forwarding</p> <p>No license available</p> <p>Runs in 40-minute mode and provides magnification on the client using Windows port forwarding</p> <p>Runs in 40-minute mode and provides speech on the client (no braille) using Windows port forwarding</p> <p>Runs in 40-minute mode and provides speech and magnification on the client (no braille) using windows port forwarding</p> <h5 id="setting-up-standalone-authorizations">Setting up Standalone Authorizations</h5> <ul> <li>Whatever product (Fusion, JAWS, or ZoomText) is going to be running on the client side, must also be installed on the server/virtual environment side. For best results, we highly recommend installing matching versions on both sides if at all possible.</li> <li>You must run the same product on both the client and server. For example, if Fusion is installed on the server but only ZoomText is running on the client, you can only run ZoomText on the server.</li> <li>In order to use the Freedom Scientific virtual channels over a remote access connection, a JAWS or Fusion license with remote authorization support must be available on the client or a network license server. If the server is running a workstation operating system such as Windows 11 Professional, the license with remote authorization can also be installed locally on the server/remote computer.</li> <li>If JAWS, fusion, or ZoomText is only installed on the server/remote computer, it will still work when launched from the client, however, the virtual channels will not load, causing Windows port forwarding to be used to provide speech and magnification on the client. Braille support is not available at all in this mode.</li> <li>Since the Remote Access Flag can only be added to Fusion or JAWS licenses, ZoomText users will be required to have Fusion Authorization.</li> <li>Confirm the Remote Access authorization is enabled for your license by going to the Remote Desktop dialog box located in the Options menu in JAWS or the Fusion or ZoomText menu under Support.</li> </ul> <h5 id="options-to-consider-based-on-each-product">Options to Consider Based on Each Product</h5> <h6 id="zoomtext-5">ZoomText</h6> <p>ZoomText only users should install and authorize ZoomText using the new Fusion Authorization code with the Remote Access authorization that was acquired.</p> <p>Note: If there was previously a ZoomText license installed, please be certain to delete the ZoomText License as described below after updating to a Fusion License. This is the only way to be certain that ZoomText will use the Fusion License with Remote Access Enabled when it starts. If both a Fusion and ZoomText license are on the computer, ZoomText will default to the ZoomText license rather than the Fusion license which will prevent Remote Access from working.</p> <p>To remove the ZoomText license, do the following:</p> <ul> <li>From the ZoomText UI, open the ZoomText Menu (ALT+Z).</li> <li>Open the Help submenu and then open the Technical Support submenu.</li> <li>Select Explore Utilities Folder.</li> <li>When the folder opens, choose Remove ZoomText Activation.</li> <li>Restart ZoomText and it will now use the new Fusion Activation you previously installed.</li> </ul> <h6 id="jaws-4">JAWS</h6> <p>JAWS only users can install JAWS and authorize with either a JAWS or Fusion Authorization, provided the remote access option is enabled for the authorization (license) to be used. Please verify if Remote Access is Enabled or Disabled in the Remote Desktop dialog box located in the JAWS Options menu.</p> <p>Note: If there was previously a JAWS license installed, and you now have a Fusion License with Remote Access enabled, you must first delete the JAWS only License off the client computer as described below and activate with the Fusion License. This is the only way to be certain that JAWS will use the Fusion License with Remote Access Enabled when it starts. If both Fusion and JAWS licenses are on the computer, starting JAWS only will default to the JAWS license rather than the Fusion license preventing Remote Access from working.</p> <p>To remove the JAWS only license, do the following:</p> <ul> <li>From the JAWS UI, open the Utilities Menu (ALT+U).</li> <li>Select Explore Utilities Folder.</li> <li>Choose Remove JAWS Activation.</li> <li>Restart JAWS and it will now use the new Fusion Activation you have installed.</li> </ul> <h6 id="fusion-6">Fusion</h6> <p>Fusion users should install Fusion and activate with the Fusion Authorization with remote access enabled. Please verify if Remote Access is Enabled or Disabled in the Remote Desktop dialog box located in the Fusion menu under Support.</p> <p>Note: In all cases, you should install the same software on the server/remote computer that matches the software running on the client. In other words, if you are only using ZoomText on the client, you only need to install ZoomText on the server.</p> <h5 id="authorizing-the-software-on-the-serverremote-computer">Authorizing the Software on the Server/Remote Computer</h5> <p>If you only intend on using JAWS, ZoomText, or Fusion from client workstations, then it is not necessary to activate a license for the instance of the software installed on the server computer. The software installed on the server/remote computer will get its authorization during the Citrix, Remote Desktop, VMware Horizon, or Amazon WorkSpaces Session from the client-side license that has Remote Access Enabled.</p> <p>If you remote into a computer running a work station operating system like Windows 11 Professional which only supports a single user connection, the software can get its remote authorization from the local license on the remote computer instead of being limited to the license on the client. For example, you use JAWS on a computer at your office which you sometimes need to remote into from home. Your copy of JAWS on your home computer is not authorized for remote access, however, the copy of JAWS on your work computer is. When you establish a remote connection between your home and work computers, JAWS will use the license on your work computer to enable the remote access flag.</p> <p>Since server operating systems like Windows Server support multiple users being connected at one time, the server side JAWS, ZoomText, or Fusion always uses the client side license or a network license to get authorization. In this case, you will not put a local license on the server computer. The only time you might activate a local license on a system running a server operating system is if you ever need to sit down and run the product locally. You will also need to put authorization on the server if you are using Citrix Virtual Desktop or another thin client solution where you remotely connect to a server from a terminal that does not support installing JAWS, ZoomText, or Fusion.</p> <p>Note: Thin client software like Citrix Virtual Desktop only works with JAWS or ZoomText when each product is running by itself. It will not work when both products are running together or as Fusion at this time.</p> <h5 id="network-license-server-authorization">Network License Server Authorization</h5> <ul> <li>In the event the Client version of your product is being Authorized using a Network License Server Key, Remote Access would need to be added to all seats for the Multi User License Server.</li> <li>When this is true, the Remote Desktop dialog box will reflect “Remote Access: Enabled” as it does for standalone licenses.</li> <li>In the event only one person on the network needs the added support, consider purchasing a single standalone license for that client machine.</li> </ul> <h5 id="available-modes-when-running-freedom-scientific-software-on-a-server">Available Modes When Running Freedom Scientific Software on a Server</h5> <h6 id="jaws-5">JAWS</h6> <p>JAWS on the server/remote computer offers the following modes:</p> <ul> <li><p>Server Mode: Requires a JAWS client to be connected in order to output speech and Braille. Authorization is obtained from a local license on the client, a network license server, or a local license on the server if running a workstation operating system.</p></li> <li><p>Dormant Mode: There is no speech or Braille output and JAWS does not look for a license until a JAWS client connects. Consider using this mode when not everyone connecting to the server requires a screen reader. When a client with a running instance of JAWS connects, the dormant instance of JAWS on the server wakes up and begin sending speech and Braille to the client. If JAWS is not running on the client when it connects, then the server instance of JAWS remains dormant and uses a trivial amount of resources. To enable Dorman Mode, launch JAWS on the remote computer with the /WaitForClient command line argument while a client is currently not connected. A JAWS icon appears in the System Tray with the following two options:</p></li> <li><p>Run Standalone: Starts a full instance of JAWS.</p></li> <li><p>Exit: Completely shut down JAWS on the server/remote computer. Once a client JAWS connects, JAWS on the remote computer instantly switches to Server Mode and begins to output speech and braille on the client computer.</p></li> </ul> <p>If a client is currently not connected, you can also set JAWS to always use Standalone Mode by launching JAWS with the /StandAlone command line argument. A license must be installed on the remote computer in order to run JAWS in this mode.</p> <h6 id="zoomtext-or-fusion">ZoomText or Fusion</h6> <p>If you start ZoomText or Fusion with the /WaitForClient command line argument and no client is currently connected, ZoomText or Fusion will display the full UI, however, “Disconnected” will be displayed in the title bar. This will change to “Connected” as soon as a client connects.</p> <p>For remote environments like Citrix where you need to publish applications to the client computer, you can start ZoomText or Fusion with the /PublishedApp command line argument. When using this option, the ZoomText or Fusion UI is displayed on the client side, but no UI is displayed on the server side. Any settings changes that are made using the UI on the client computer will still be applied on the server as expected. This setting prevents two instances of ZoomText or Fusion appearing on the client’s taskbar or in the ALT+TAB order, which could cause confusion.</p> <h5 id="troubleshooting-2">Troubleshooting</h5> <p>You can use the Remote Desktop dialog box to help troubleshoot issues when using JAWS, Fusion, or ZoomText over a remote connection. This dialog box is located in the JAWS Options menu, or in the Fusion or ZoomText menu under Support. From this dialog box, you can:</p> <ul> <li>See whether or not your Freedom Scientific software is authorized for remote access.</li> <li>Check the status for each supported remote channel; Remote Desktop, Citrix, VMware Horizon, or Amazon WorkSpaces (AWS).</li> <li>Test the connection between the client and server/remote computers.</li> <li>Repair any channel that is reported to not be working. For example, if you install the Citrix client software on a computer where JAWS or Fusion is already installed, the Repair option becomes available since the Freedom Scientific remote channel for Citrix was not properly configured. Selecting Repair properly configures the Citrix channel. If the Citrix client is installed before JAWS or Fusion, the channel is set up during the JAWS or Fusion installation and the Repair option is not shown.</li> </ul> <h3
