<p>RIGHT SHIFT+DOTS 1-2-4 CHORD</p> <p>JAWS Find Next</p> <p>RIGHT SHIFT+DOTS 2-5</p> <p>RIGHT SHIFT+DOTS 2-5</p> <h4 id="environmental-considerations-4">Environmental Considerations</h4> <h5 id="storage-4">Storage</h5> <p>Temperature 0 to 45 C (32 to 113 F)</p> <p>Humidity 80% RH non-condensing</p> <h5 id="operating-4">Operating</h5> <p>Temperature 5 to 35 C (40 to 95 F)</p> <p>Humidity 60% RH non-condensing</p> <h4 id="diagnostics-mode-4">Diagnostics Mode</h4> <p>The Focus braille display has built-in diagnostic tests for the cursor router buttons, braille display, NAV Rockers, mode buttons, braille keys, panning buttons, rocker bars, selector Buttons, and panning rockers.</p> <p>Before entering Diagnostics Mode, disconnect the Focus from your computer and make sure it is powered off.</p> <h5 id="entering-and-exiting-diagnostics-mode-4">Entering and Exiting Diagnostics Mode</h5> <p>Simultaneously, press the first two cursor router buttons farthest to the left (above cells one and two) while pressing the power button. The text, “press cr key/nav/panel keys,” is displayed to indicate that Diagnostics Mode has been entered.</p> <p>Press the power button again by itself to exit Diagnostics Mode.</p> <h5 id="routing-button-test-3">routing Button Test</h5> <p>The routing button test ensures that each of the cursor router buttons on the braille display work properly. Press any cursor router button to activate all dots in the cell below the button.</p> <h5 id="display-testclean-4">Display Test/Clean</h5> <p>It is necessary to disconnect the Focus 80 Blue from your computer and make sure it is powered off before beginning this test. The display test is used to ensure that each pin on the braille display can be activated. The display test also allows you to clean the braille display. Press the power button while pressing the rightmost cursor router buttons (above the last two cells) simultaneously. This action causes all cells to be activated for cleaning. Use a soft cloth moistened with isopropyl alcohol. Do not use any other substance to clean the cells.</p> <p>While in this mode, pressing down on either the right or left NAV Rocker will cause all of the cells to be deactivated. Pressing up on either the left or right NAV Rocker will reactivate all cells.</p> <p>Pressing the left or right mode button causes the cells to toggle up and down. To stop this action, press the mode button again.</p> <h5 id="key-and-controls-test-4">Key and Controls Test</h5> <p>The key and controls test ensures that each of the keys and controls operate properly. You can begin the key test after entering Diagnostics Mode by pressing any of the keys or controls listed in the table below. The braille display reflects each key that is pressed. Refer to the following table for the exact dot position for each of the keys. Press each of the keys and controls and verify that the appropriate response is displayed.</p> <p>Key</p> <p>Displays</p> <p>DOT 1</p> <p>1</p> <p>DOT 2</p> <p>2</p> <p>DOT 3</p> <p>3</p> <p>DOT 4</p> <p>4</p> <p>DOT 5</p> <p>5</p> <p>DOT 6</p> <p>6</p> <p>DOT 7</p> <p>7</p> <p>DOT 8</p> <p>8</p> <p>LEFT SHIFT</p> <p>kls</p> <p>RIGHT SHIFT</p> <p>krs</p> <p>SPACEBAR</p> <p>ksp</p> <p>LEFT PANNING BUTTON</p> <p>pl</p> <p>RIGHT PANNING BUTTON</p> <p>pr</p> <p>LEFT SELECTOR BUTTON</p> <p>sl</p> <p>RIGHT SELECTOR BUTTON</p> <p>sr</p> <p>LEFT MODE BUTTON</p> <p>nml</p> <p>LEFT NAV Rocker UP</p> <p>nlu</p> <p>LEFT NAV Rocker DOWN</p> <p>NLD</p> <p>RIGHT MODE BUTTON</p> <p>nmr</p> <p>RIGHT NAV Rocker UP</p> <p>nru</p> <p>RIGHT NAV Rocker DOWN</p> <p>nrd</p> <p>LEFT ROCKER SWITCH UP</p> <p>rlu</p> <p>LEFT ROCKER SWITCH DOWN</p> <p>rld</p> <p>RIGHT ROCKER SWITCH UP</p> <p>rru</p> <p>RIGHT ROCKER SWITCH DOWN</p> <p>rrd</p> <p>LEFT PANNING ROCKER UP</p> <p>blu</p> <p>LEFT PANNING ROCKER DOWN</p> <p>bld</p> <p>RIGHT PANNING ROCKER UP</p> <p>bru</p> <p>RIGHT PANNING ROCKER DOWN</p> <p>brd</p> <h5 id="battery-info-mode-3">Battery Info Mode</h5> <p>Before entering this mode, disconnect the Focus from your computer and make sure it is powered off. Press the power button while simultaneously pressing the cursor router button above cell two. The Focus displays additional information about the internal battery.</p> <h4 id="troubleshooting-5">Troubleshooting</h4> <p>Problem</p> <p>Solution</p> <p>The display will not turn on.</p> <p>Charge the battery using the supplied AC adapter, or by connecting the Focus to a computer using the USB cable. The unit will always power on when connected to USB. If not connected to USB, make sure you press and hold the power button for at least three seconds.</p> <p>The battery is not charging or is taking longer to charge than expected.</p> <p>Make sure you are charging the Focus Blue using the Freedom Scientific supplied AC adapter. The battery takes a maximum of three hours to charge using the supplied AC adapter. If you are charging the Focus using a USB connection to your computer, the battery will take longer to charge. To verify the Focus is charging correctly, press the power button to display the Focus status information.</p> <p>Extra dots are appearing on the display and dots are sticking.</p> <p>Clean the display by activating the Display Test diagnostic mode then use a soft cloth moistened with isopropyl alcohol to clean the cells. Refer to the Display Test/Clean section of this manual for more information.</p> <p>The Focus display is not communicating with the computer.</p> <p>If you are using JAWS 11 or later, make sure JAWS is properly installed on your computer. See the section Adding JAWS Support to the Focus Display for more information on configuring both USB and Bluetooth. If you are using JAWS 10 or earlier, or a third-party screen reading application, you must install the driver from the Focus Companion CD before you can use the display.</p> <h3 id="focus-blue-4th-generation-firmware-downloads">Focus Blue 4th Generation Firmware Downloads</h3> <p>Skip to content</p> <p>Need Support? <a href="tel:+18004444443">1(800) 444-4443</a></p> <h4 id="focus-blue-4th-generation-firmware-downloads-1">Focus Blue 4th Generation Firmware Downloads</h4> <p>IMPORTANT: This update is not intended for use on the Classic Focus 40 Blue braille display (the unit that has WHIZWHEELS®). A Classic unit is any Focus 40 Blue whose serial number begins with 43 and was purchased prior to July 2012. Updating a Classic Focus 40 Blue with this firmware version may result in your unit becoming unusable. The serial number can be found in print and braille on the bottom of the braille display.</p> <p>Use this page to download the latest firmware for your Focus 14 Blue, Focus 40 Blue, or Focus 80 Blue refreshable braille display. For more information on using the Focus Blue, visit the Braille Displays Documentation page.</p> <p>This firmware update adds the Power 1 2 3 feature. Freedom Scientific Focus 14, 40, and 80 Blue braille displays will now have the ability to switch between an active USB connection and a Bluetooth connection with any paired Bluetooth device. If your Focus Blue braille display is connected to your computer using the USB port, you simply press the power button to display the status information, and then press DOTS 1-2-3 from the Perkins-style keyboard on the Focus display. If the Focus has been paired and the device is on, the Focus will immediately begin displaying information from the Bluetooth device. Press the power button and then press DOTS 1-2-3 again to switch back to the USB connection.</p> <p>When initially pairing the Focus Blue with another Bluetooth device, ensure the display is powered on and not connected to USB. Once paired, you can connect the USB cable and then use this feature to toggle the active connection.</p> <p>Android and iOS devices must first be locked before the display is switched from USB to Bluetooth connectivity. Once the display is switched to Bluetooth, unlock your mobile device so that it will find the display and begin using it as usual. Once the connection is established, you can switch back and forth using the Power 1 2 3 command without having to first lock and unlock the device.</p> <h5 id="before-you-begin">Before You Begin</h5> <ul> <li>Review this procedure before attempting to update your unit.</li> <li>Make sure you have the supplied Focus Blue USB cable.</li> <li>Press the unit’s Power button and verify the current firmware version. The unit’s name and firmware version display when the unit turns on.</li> <li>Download the Focus Blue firmware file below and copy it to a location on your computer where you can easily find it later.</li> </ul> <h5 id="updating-the-focus-blue-firmware">Updating the Focus Blue Firmware</h5> <p>IMPORTANT: This update is not intended for use on the Classic Focus 40 Blue braille display (the unit that has WHIZWHEELS). A Classic unit is any Focus 40 Blue whose serial number begins with 43 and was purchased prior to July 2012. Updating a Classic Focus 40 Blue with this firmware version may result in your unit becoming unusable. The serial number can be found in print and braille on the bottom of the braille display.</p> <ul> <li><p>Using the link below, download and save the Focus Blue firmware update file to a location on your computer where you can easily find it, for example, your Downloads folder.</p></li> <li><p>Plug the braille display into your computer’s USB port and wait for the unit to turn on. If the Found New Hardware dialog box appears, follow the messages to locate the driver.</p></li> <li><p>Run the application file (EXE) for your unit and follow the messages to update the firmware. IMPORTANT: Do not disconnect the unit during the update process.</p></li> <li><p>When the update is finished, you may receive a message telling you to close and restart your screen reader before using your braille display.</p></li> <li><p>To verify that the update was successful, press the unit’s POWER button to display firmware information. The firmware version should be 5.71. <a href="https://focus.vfo.digital/Focus/FocusBlueFirmware571.01.exe">Focus 14/40/80 Blue Firmware 5.71 Update</a></p></li> </ul> <h3 id="focus-blue-5th-generation-firmware-downloads">Focus Blue 5th Generation Firmware Downloads</h3> <p>Skip to content</p> <p>Need Support? <a href="tel:+18004444443">1(800) 444-4443</a></p> <h4 id="focus-blue-5th-generation-firmware-downloads-1">Focus Blue 5th Generation Firmware Downloads</h4> <p>Use this page to download the latest firmware for your Focus Blue 5th Generation refreshable braille display. For more information on using the Focus Blue, visit the <a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/braille/focus/">Focus Blue Braille Display Training</a> web page.</p> <p>IMPORTANT: This update is for the Focus Blue 5th generation braille displays. DO NOT install this firmware on older Focus 14 Blue, Focus 40 Blue, or Focus 80 Blue 4th Generation braille displays. The 5th generation Focus Blue braille displays have a Menu button between keys 1 and 4 on the Perkins-style keyboard. If your display has a Menu button, follow these instructions to upgrade the display.</p> <h5 id="changes-in-version-5.83-13">Changes in Version 5.83-13</h5> <h6 id="braille-hid-support">Braille HID Support</h6> <p>The Focus Blue now supports USB and Bluetooth connections using the Braille HID (Human Interface Device) or Serial protocol. Products using HID technology are automatically recognized by the computer or mobile device’s operating system, enabling plug and play functionality for input and output, similar to connecting and immediately being able to use a standard keyboard. If your screen reading software supports HID Braille displays, use the following procedures to change the Focus to use HID.</p> <p>For USB:</p> <ul> <li><p>Make sure the Focus is currently not connected.</p></li> <li><p>Press the Menu button to access the display configuration menu.</p></li> <li><p>Use the Rocker bars to navigate to USB and press DOT 8.</p></li> <li><p>Use the Rocker bars to make a selection and press DOT 8 to return to the main menu. Available choices are USB Serial (selected by default) and USB HID.</p></li> <li><p>Press the Right Selector to exit the main menu. For Bluetooth:</p></li> <li><p>Make sure the Focus is currently not connected.</p></li> <li><p>Press the Menu button to access the display configuration menu.</p></li> <li><p>Use the Rocker bars to navigate to Bluetooth and press DOT 8.</p></li> <li><p>Use the Rocker bars to make a selection and press DOT 8 to return to the main menu. Available choices are Bluetooth Serial (selected by default), Bluetooth HID, and Bluetooth Both. Selecting Bluetooth Both allows you to connect over Bluetooth to a device using the Serial protocol and connect to another device that supports Braille HID.</p></li> <li><p>Press the Right Selector to exit the main menu. Notes:</p></li> <li><p>The first time you connect over Bluetooth to a device over HID, you must first press the Menu button along with DOT 7 to place the Focus into Pairing mode. To confirm HID Pairing Mode is active, dots 2-3-4-5-7-8 followed by dots 1-2-5-6-7-8 is included on the status line near the right end of the display.</p></li> <li><p>It is not possible to simultaneously connect over HID and Serial to the same host device.</p></li> <li><p>USB Serial must be active in order to transfer files between a computer and the Focus SD card for use in Scratchpad. USB Serial is also required when installing firmware updates.</p></li> </ul> <h6 id="other-changes">Other Changes</h6> <ul> <li>The Require Pin option in the display configuration menu has been removed. You will no longert be prompted for a paring code when setting up a Bluetooth connection under any circumstances.</li> <li>Added language support for Icelandic.</li> </ul> <h5 id="changes-in-version-5.82-26">Changes in Version 5.82-26</h5> <ul> <li>Added language support for Kazakh and Hungarian.</li> <li>Improved Scratchpad stability for several languages including Kazakh, Russian, and Hungarian.</li> <li>Addressed an issue with confirmation messages not displaying correctly in Russian.</li> <li>Resolved an issue with the Norwegian Scratchpad help file where special characters were not displayed correctly.</li> <li>Various updates to the SD card contents including updated documentation files for a number of languages, as well as the removal of files no longer needed.</li> </ul> <h5 id="changes-in-version-5.82-20">Changes in Version 5.82-20</h5> <ul> <li><p>When saving a file for the first time in Scratchpad, you are now asked if you want to save using TXT/BRF/BRL/BRA format. If you want to save using one of these formats, press Y, use the Rocker bars, NAV Rockers, or Cursor Routers to select a format (dots 7 and 8 are used to indicate the selected format), and press DOT 8. After choosing the file format, type a name for your file, and then press DOT 8. Files saved in one of these formats can be opened and modified on a PC.</p></li> <li><p>If you do not want to save the file in a specific format, press N, type a name for your file, and press DOT 8. This saves the file with an FNZ extension. FNZ files can only be read and edited in Scratchpad. However, the contents of FNZ files can be exported to any open editing application over an active USB or Bluetooth connection. Note: The BRA format is only available if the Focus language is set to Spanish. Additionally, as you work in your file, make sure to enter content in a way that matches the file type you want to save as. For instance, if you intend to save a file in TXT format, it is suggested that content be written using Computer Braille and not literary or contracted braille. This ensures the file displays correctly when opened on your computer.</p></li> <li><p>When creating a new file in Scratchpad and there is currently content on the clipboard copied from another file, you are now asked if you want to create a file based on the clipboard contents. For example, if the clipboard contains content from a text file, you will be prompted to create a new TXT file. Pressing Y creates a new blank file that will include a TXT extension when saved. Pressing N creates a new blank file using an FNZ extension.</p></li> <li><p>Resolved an issue where the cursor was unexpectedly moved to the beginning of the document instead of remaining at your current location when saving (RIGHT SHIFT+S).</p></li> <li><p>Addressed an issue where BRF files were not displaying properly in Scratchpad If the Focus language was set to French or Polish.</p></li> <li><p>Addressed issues with searching for text in BRF files when the Focus was set to a language other than English.</p></li> <li><p>Resolved an issue where several Scratchpad keystrokes were not working If the Focus language was set to Russian.</p></li> <li><p>When selecting characters that include a dot 7 or 8 such as a capital letter, addressed an issue where the dot 7 or 8 portion of the character was not displayed as part of the selection If Scratchpad was configured to hide dots 7 and 8.</p></li> <li><p>Added language support for Slovenian.</p></li> </ul> <h5 id="changes-in-version-5.82-14">Changes in Version 5.82-14</h5> <h6 id="scratchpad-improvements">Scratchpad Improvements</h6> <ul> <li><p>Scratchpad has been completely reworked to provide improved overall performance when opening, editing, and saving files.</p></li> <li><p>When entering text, files are no longer limited to 32 K before they stop accepting content.</p></li> <li><p>FNZ files, which can only be read and edited in Scratchpad, now offer an approximately 1 MB size limit.</p></li> <li><p>TXT, BRF, BRL, and BRA files up to 10 MB can now be edited. You can also read files as large as 100 MB. Note that BRA files can only be opened when the Focus language is set to Spanish. Note: All files to be edited must be placed in the Notes folder on the SD memory card.</p></li> <li><p>When opening or deleting a file, you can now use DOTS 1-2-3 CHORD or DOTS 4-5-6 CHORD to move to the top or bottom of the files list. You can also use first letter navigation to help you quickly locate a specific file.</p></li> <li><p>Added the following commands based on customer feedback:</p> <ul> <li>Display the title of the currently opened file: LEFT SHIFT+T (DOTS 2-3-4-5)</li> <li>Display the current page and number of pages in the file (requires that files include page break characters which should be available in most formatted books from services like BARD): RIGHT SHIFT+P (DOTS 1-2-3-4)</li> <li>Switch between the current and previously opened file: DOTS 2-4-6 CHORD</li> </ul></li> <li><p>In addition to using RIGHT SHIFT+DOT 4 to find the next occurrence of a word or phrase in a file, you can now press RIGHT SHIFT+DOT 8 CHORD to find the previous occurrence of text. Alternatively, use the new Find Previous option in the Edit menu.</p></li> <li><p>Added a new Advanced menu containing the following options to help improve the reading experience:</p> <ul> <li>Word Wrap – When enabled, Scratchpad does not split a word that is too large to be shown on the braille display and instead shows the entire word when you pan to the next increment. This option is off by default.</li> <li>Reverse Panning – Turn this option on to use the Right Panning button to pan backward and the Left Panning button to pan forward through files. This option is off by default.</li> <li>Hide Cursor – When enabled, the cursor, which is represented by dots 7 and 8, is not displayed. If a Cursor Router is pressed while the cursor is hidden, the cursor briefly flashes at that location. By default, the cursor is always displayed.</li> <li>Hide Dots 7 and 8 – Dots 7 and 8 are used to indicate capitalization and other special symbols. Additionally, formatted braille (BRF) books produced by some agencies in the United States such as Bookshare.org and the National Library Service use characters that include dots 7 and 8. To help reduce distraction while reading, you can enable this option to suppress dots 7 and 8 so they are not displayed as part of the text. This option is off by default.</li> </ul></li> </ul> <h6 id="one-handed-mode-1">One-Handed Mode</h6> <p>The new one-handed mode feature allows users who are unable to enter data using two hands to use the Focus display. To turn this feature on or off, use the One-Handed Mode item in the display configuration menu, or toggle it by pressing LEFT SHIFT+DOTS 1-2-3-7 or RIGHT SHIFT+DOTS 4-5-6-8. Once enabled, one-handed operation works with Focus-specific features such as Scratchpad, or when using the Focus to interact with applications on a computer or mobile device.</p> <p>In one-handed mode, enter commands or Braille characters one key at a time; or enter as many keys together as you find comfortable; then press the SPACEBAR when finished. For example, individually pressing DOTS 1-2-3-5, followed by the SPACEBAR types a letter R. If you are entering data and need to enter the Space character, press the SPACEBAR twice.</p> <p>If you need to enter a chord combination, press the SPACEBAR, then the keys that make up the chord, then press the SPACEBAR again. For example, to go to the beginning of a file, press the SPACEBAR, followed by DOTS 1-2-3, followed once more by the SPACEBAR.</p> <h6 id="bluetooth-pairing-code-no-longer-required-by-default">Bluetooth Pairing Code No Longer Required by Default</h6> <p>When pairing the Focus display with another device over Bluetooth for the first time, you will no longer be prompted to enter a Bluetooth pairing code and the connection is immediately established. If you prefer to be prompted each time you pair the display with a new device, turn on the new Require Pin option in the Focus configuration menu.</p> <h6 id="flash-messages">Flash Messages</h6> <p>The Focus now supports Flash Messages, which are short informational messages that appear on the display for only a few seconds. For instance, Scratchpad displays flash messages in a variety of situations including when confirming a file was saved or deleted. Flash messages disappear automatically after a short time, but you can dismiss one at any time by pressing a Cursor Router. If you need more time to finish reading a message, press one of the Panning buttons to keep the message on the display longer.</p> <p>By default, flash messages are displayed for three seconds. To change this, use the new Flash Msg Time option in the Focus configuration menu to choose a time between 1 and 20 seconds.</p> <h5 id="before-you-begin-1">Before You Begin</h5> <ul> <li>Review this procedure before attempting to update your unit.</li> <li>Make sure JAWS is installed on the computer you will be using for the update. It is not necessary to have JAWS running while updating the unit.</li> <li>Make sure you have the supplied Focus Blue USB cable.</li> <li>When the unit is powered on, press the Menu button (press twice if connected over USB and JAWS is running) and then the top of the left or right Rocker bar to verify the model and current firmware version. When finished, press the right Selector button to exit the menu.</li> <li>Download the Focus Blue firmware file below and copy it to a location on your computer where you can easily find it later.</li> </ul> <h5 id="updating-the-focus-blue-5th-generation-firmware">Updating the Focus Blue 5th Generation Firmware</h5> <ul> <li>Using the link at the end of this procedure, download and save the firmware update file to a location on your computer where you can easily find it, for example, your Downloads folder.</li> <li>Plug the braille display into your computer’s USB port and wait for the unit to power on.</li> <li>Note: If the Found New Hardware dialog box appears, follow the messages to locate the driver.</li> <li>Run the application file (EXE) for your unit and follow the messages to update the firmware.</li> <li>IMPORTANT: Do not disconnect the unit during the update process.</li> <li>When the update is finished, you may receive a message telling you to close and restart your screen reader before using your braille display.</li> <li>Verify that the update was successful by pressing the Menu button (press twice if the USB connection is active) and then the top of the left or right Rocker bar to display the firmware version. <a href="https://vfogroupint.s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com/firmware/Focus/V/Focus5_FW__Update-v5.83-13.exe.zip">Focus Blue 5th Generation Firmware 5.83-13 Update</a></li> </ul> <h5 id="scratchpad-overview">Scratchpad Overview</h5> <p>Scratchpad is a Focus Blue utility. If a Micro SD card (up to 32 GB) is inserted into the display, Scratchpad enables you to enter notes using plain text or contracted braille. No USB or Bluetooth connection is required to use Scratchpad. For example, if you need to quickly write down a phone number, but you do not have immediate access to your PC or mobile device, you can launch Scratchpad on your Focus, write down the phone number using the Perkins-style keyboard, and then save it to a file on the Micro SD card.</p> <p>Scratchpad offers basic file navigation and editing functions including cut, copy, and paste. You can also search for text in the currently open file. Additionally, if the Focus is currently connected to a computer or other device over USB or Bluetooth, you can export the contents of the current file to the edit window of the currently open application.</p> <p>Scratchpad also allows you to open and read braille formatted (BRF) and plain text (TXT) files. When the Micro SD card is inserted, pressing and holding the Left Panning button while inserting the supplied USB cable causes the display to power on and be recognized as a removable drive when connected over USB. Once in this mode, BRF books or TXT files can be transferred directly to the Micro SD card for reading in Scratchpad.</p> <p>See the <a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/braille/focus/focus-user-guide/#scratchpad">Scratchpad documentation</a> for more information on using all of its features.</p> <p>For international users, this firmware supports the following languages for the menus and status messages.</p> <p>Arabic</p> <p>German</p> <p>Portuguese</p> <p>Czech</p> <p>Hebrew</p> <p>Russian</p> <p>Danish</p> <p>Hungarian</p> <p>Slovakian</p> <p>Dutch</p> <p>Italian</p> <p>Spanish</p> <p>Finnish</p> <p>Norwegian</p> <p>Swedish</p> <p>French</p> <p>Polish</p> <p>Turkish</p> <p>Croatian</p> <p>Slovenian</p> <p>Kazakh</p> <p>Icelandic</p> <p>English is selected by default. To switch to a different language, use the Language option located in the display’s configuration menu.</p> <h5 id="preparing-the-micro-sd-card">Preparing the Micro SD Card</h5> <p>Before you can use Scratchpad, you must insert a Micro SD card into the Focus display as files you create are saved directly to the card. BRF books will also need to be copied to the card for reading in the Scratchpad. The Focus supports Micro SD cards up to 32 GB. To insert a Micro SD card, do the following:</p> <p>WARNING: Under no circumstances should you attempt to insert the card in any other position than as described. Damage to the card or the Focus Blue can result if the card is not properly oriented before being inserted.</p> <ul> <li>Make sure the Focus Blue is powered off.</li> <li>Turn the display so the left side is facing you. The Micro SD slot is a narrow opening located to the right of the Power button under the bumper.</li> <li>Hold the card so that the fingernail grip (the raised edge used to grab and remove the card) is pointed toward you and facing down. You will also feel a slight protrusion on the left side as well as a square cutout in the upper left corner. In addition, the printed label on the card should be facing down.</li> <li>Insert the card into the slot until it clicks into place.</li> </ul> <h5 id="downloading-and-transferring-scratchpad-files">Downloading and Transferring Scratchpad Files</h5> <p>Once the card is inserted, do the following to download and transfer the Scratchpad Help to the card so you can access the documentation right on your display from inside the utility:</p> <ul> <li><p>Using the link at the end of this procedure, download and save the Focus5-SDCard file to a location on your computer where you can easily find it, for example, your Downloads folder.</p></li> <li><p>Locate the file and extract its contents. A folder called FSI is created in the same folder where you extracted the file.</p></li> <li><p>On the Focus, make sure the unit is powered off and the supplied USB cable is connected to your PC. Next, press and hold the Left Panning button while simultaneously inserting the USB cable. The display will be recognized as a removable USB drive. Note: If you use a screen reader such as JAWS over USB, it is recommended that you turn on speech or use a Bluetooth connection as braille will currently not work over USB when the Focus is being used as a storage device. Examples are the Microsoft Surface Pro (11th edition) and the Surface Laptop (7th edition).</p> <h6 id="what-operating-system-is-required">What Operating System is required?</h6> <p>Windows 11 is the minimum supported Operating System.</p> <h6 id="what-braille-devices-are-currently-supported">What braille devices are currently supported?</h6> <ul> <li>Freedom Scientific Focus braille displays</li> <li>Humanware braille displays Additional braille display support will be added as we work with our third-party partners.</li> </ul> <h6 id="what-speech-synthesizers-are-currently-supported">What speech synthesizers are currently supported?</h6> <p>Eloquence, Vocalizer Expressive, SAPI 5x, SAPI 5x 64-bit, and Microsoft Mobile synthesizers are supported. Additional synthesizer support will be added as we work with our third-party partners.</p> <h6 id="how-can-i-verify-if-the-arm64-version-of-jaws-zoomtext-or-fusion-is-installed">How can I verify if the ARM64 version of JAWS, ZoomText, or Fusion is installed?</h6> <p>For JAWS, open the About dialog (Help > About JAWS) and the System Type will be ARM64.</p> <p>For ZoomText or Fusion, open the About dialog (ZoomText or Fusion menu > Help > About) and you will see either ZoomText 2025 (ARM64) or Fusion 2025 (ARM64) as your software version.</p> <h6 id="what-features-are-currently-not-available">What features are currently not available?</h6> <p>The following features are still under development:</p> <ul> <li>Citrix remote</li> <li>Convenient OCR from a scanner or camera</li> <li>Dongle authorization</li> </ul> <h6 id="what-applications-are-currently-not-supported">What applications are currently not supported?</h6> <p>ARM64 versions of JAWS, ZoomText, and Fusion do not support 32-bit ARM applications.</p> <h6 id="what-is-the-recommended-version-of-office-365">What is the recommended version of Office 365?</h6> <p>For the best performance, we recommend installing the latest 64-bit version of Office designed specifically for ARM64 devices.</p> <h6 id="for-german-braille-users-is-rtfc-available">For German braille users, is RTFC available?</h6> <p>If you use German braille, you will still receive German braille output when using JAWS on ARM. However, the braille may look slightly different compared to what you see on other computers.</p> <p>So, while both versions provide German braille, the output may not be exactly the same.</p> <h3 id="fusion-system-recommendations">Fusion System Recommendations</h3> <p>Skip to content</p> <p>Need Support? id="international-1">International</h4> <h3 id="introduction-5">Introduction</h3> <h4 id="introduction-6">Introduction</h4> <p>When used with most popular applications, JAWS® screen reading software provides you with screen information for the application you are using. The information that tells JAWS how to behave is contained within a set of “default files.” These default files, created by Freedom Scientific, are provided with JAWS. Unfortunately, not all applications are the same. Therefore, information telling JAWS how to behave in these applications is contained in a set of “application-specific files.”</p> <p>Through the many options available in the JAWS application, changes and adjustments can be easily made to all of the commonly used features, such as Verbosity and Screen Echo. But despite this ability, you may find special situations that require more advanced or specific instructions so that JAWS can properly navigate and provide the correct screen information in the application.</p> <p>A script file contains a variety of scripts and functions. You can think of scripts and functions as small computer programs. Each script or function contains commands that tell JAWS how to navigate and what to speak under different conditions. You can modify existing script files or you can write entirely new commands to make most any application accessible with JAWS. Moreover, you can create scripts that automate many of your daily tasks. In short, your use of the scripting language is endless and is only limited by your imagination and creativity.</p> <p>JAWS is not the only product developed by Freedom Scientific that takes advantage of the powerful scripting language. Both the MAGic® screen magnification application, through the use of the MAGic Pro Scripting edition, and PAC Mate Omni® accessible Pocket PC device take advantage of the power and flexibility offered by the scripting language. With the familiarity gained from writing JAWS scripts, you will be able to easily apply your skills when generating scripts that control magnification and speech functionality found in MAGic.</p> <p>For those of you who ask, “Do I need a programming background to write scripts,” the answer is that while a programming background is helpful, it is not necessary. In fact, many script developers working for Freedom Scientific are self-taught. It is for this reason alone that we have compiled this step-by-step manual in hopes that you will get a good start toward becoming a successful JAWS script developer.</p> <h5 id="basics-of-scripting-table-of-contents">Basics of Scripting Table of Contents</h5> <p>The Basics of Scripting manual contains the following chapters:</p> <p><a href="02-0_TheKeyboardManager.htm">2.0 The Keyboard Manager</a></p> <p><a href="03-0_WhatAreScripts.htm">3.0 What are Scripts?</a></p> <p><a href="04-0_TheScriptManager.htm">4.0 The Script Manager</a></p> <p><a href="05-0_CreatingScripts.htm">5.0 Creating Scripts</a></p> <p><a href="06-0_ReadingInformationWithScripts.htm">6.0 Reading Information with Scripts</a></p> <p><a href="07-0_UsingVariablesAndConstants.htm">7.0 Using Variables and Constants</a></p> <p><a href="08-0_CreatingAndSpeakingMessages.htm">8.0 Creating and Speaking Messages</a></p> <p><a href="09-0_ControllingTheFlowOfScripts.htm">9.0 Controlling the Flow of Scripts with Decision Making</a></p> <p><a href="10-0_PassingKeystrokesAndTypingTextWithScripts.htm">10.0 Passing Keystrokes and Typing Text with Scripts</a></p> <p><a href="11-0_UsingTheVirtualViewer.htm">11.0 Using the Virtual Viewer</a></p> <p><a href="12-0_UnderstandingFunctions.htm">12.0 Understanding Functions</a></p> <p><a href="13-0_WindowsStructure.htm">13.0 Windows Program Structure</a></p> <p>Copyright (c) 2011 Freedom Scientific Inc. All Rights Reserved. From this page, you can discover more about JAWS, quickly and easily navigate to a number of online resources, download updates, and learn valuable tips and tricks for using JAWS.</p> <p>What’s New in JAWS</p> <p><a href="https://fsactivate.freedomscientific.com">Software Activation</a></p> <p>SMA and Upgrade Pricing</p> <p><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/certification/">JAWS Certification Program</a></p> <p><a href="http://www.hartgen.org">J-Say and Leasey</a>, products to enhance the JAWS experience.</p> <p><a href="http://www.yesaccessible.com">TypeAbility</a>, the world’s best typing tutor for users of screen readers and magnifiers.</p> <h5 id="access-to-applications-you-need">Access to Applications You Need</h5> <p>With JAWS, you can work with Microsoft® Office®, including Word®, Excel®, Outlook®, and PowerPoint®; Google Workspace™ apps (Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs, and Sheets); Microsoft Edge™, Google Chrome™, Mozilla Firefox®, Adobe® Reader®, and more. JAWS is compatible with the latest Windows® operating systems, including touch screens and gestures on Windows 10 and later.</p> <h5 id="access-to-mathml-content">Access to MathML Content</h5> <p>MathML is a language for including mathematical content on web pages, enabling browsers to present math and science equations and formulas as they would appear on paper. JAWS provides spoken, natural-language descriptions of MathML expressions in Edge, Chrome, and Firefox using the same terms a teacher would use to explain them in a classroom. Students will benefit from hearing JAWS describe mathematical expressions as their teachers and peers do. If a refreshable braille display is connected, JAWS also shows math expressions on the display using the Nemeth Braille code, a widely used system for reading math in braille. In addition, math expressions are also displayed with highlighting in the Math Viewer as they are spoken, so sighted teachers can assist students who are using JAWS to study math. Once JAWS is installed, you can immediately begin reading math and science content. You do not need to install any additional third-party software applications or plugins to use JAWS MathML support.</p> <p>MathML Examples</p> <p><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/teachers/accessing-math-content-with-jaws-and-fusion">Accessing Math Content with JAWS and Fusion</a></p> <h5 id="tandem-with-jaws">Tandem with JAWS</h5> <p>Tandem® lets you access another JAWS computer via the Internet so that you can provide hands-on technical support, write and distribute scripts from a distance, conduct remote JAWS training, or even just let two JAWS users in different places explore a new program together. Tandem support is included with every JAWS install, even the 40-minute demo.</p> <p>See the JAWS Tandem Quick Start Guide to learn more about Tandem.</p> <h5 id="surfs-up-training">Surf’s Up Training</h5> <p><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/SurfsUp/_Surfs_Up_Start_Here.htm">Surf’s Up</a> - A set of Freedom Scientific web pages that explain how to surf the web with JAWS screen reading software. You will also find many new and updated exercises for practice throughout. You may also access a <a href="https://support.freedomscientific.com/Training/Surfs-Up/ZIP_Surfs_Up.zip">downloadable Surf’s Up version</a> for use when training off line.</p> <h5 id="online-training">Online Training</h5> <p><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/freewebinars/archivedwebinars/">Free Webinars On Demand</a> - Valuable for users at all levels.</p> <p>You can learn to use JAWS - from basic steps to more advanced - in the comfort of your home, office, or school dorm. New webinars eliminate travel expenses, making it easier to get approval to learn at work and to find time to train. Also, check out our <a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/freewebinars">Upcoming Webinars</a> page to see a schedule of upcoming webinars, and sign up to attend for free.</p> <h5 id="international-jaws">International JAWS</h5> <p>Note: A synthesizer that supports the given language is required for reading some of these pages with JAWS.</p> <p><a href="http://www.freedomsci.de">Freedom Scientific European Website</a></p> <p><a href="http://www.extra.co.jp/jaws/index.html">Japanese JAWS Website</a></p> <p><a href="http://www.sightandsound.co.uk">Sight and Sound Technology (UK)</a></p> <p><a href="http://www.karishmaenterprises.com">Karishma Enterprises (India)</a></p> <ul> <li><a href="https://store.freedomscientific.com/">Shop Online in US</a></li> <li>Brochure (PDF)</li> <li>System Requirements</li> <li>JAWS EULA</li> <li>Documentation</li> <li>Success Stories</li> <li>Links and Related Sites</li> </ul> <h3 id="jaws-installation-layout-command-line-options">JAWS Installation Layout Command Line Options</h3> <p>Skip to content</p> <p>Need Support? <a href="tel:+18004444443">1(800) 444-4443</a></p> <h4 id="jaws-installation-layout-command-line-options-1">JAWS Installation Layout Command Line Options</h4> <p>The setup package is a tool used to install or uninstall multiple components, including the main product. The following information is an example of what is available from /Help and /MoreHelp</p> <p>These commands are not case sensitive.</p> <h5 id="help">/Help</h5> <p>Displays this help dialog. The installation process is not performed.</p> <p>Example:</p> <p>c:.exe /help</p> <h5 id="extractsettings">/ExtractSettings </Path-to-file></h5> <p>Outputs the contents of Settings.ini to the output file specified. The installation process is not performed. If the output file already exists, it is overwritten. If there are spaces in the path to the file, the path must be enclosed in quotes.</p> <p>Example:</p> <p>c:.exe /ExtractSettings “c:setup.ini”</p> <h5 id="replacesettings">/ReplaceSettings </Path-to-file></h5> <p>Specifies an initialization file for the setup package engine to use instead of the Settings.ini file stored in the resources. This flag can be used if any of the contents in Settings.ini must be overridden. If there are spaces in the path to the file, the path must be enclosed in quotes.</p> <p>Example:</p> <p>c:.exe /ReplaceSettings “c:setup.ini”</p> <h5 id="log">/Log </Path-to-file></h5> <p>Allows the user to specify the location of the setup package log file. Logging is enabled even if this command line argument is not specified.</p> <p>Example:</p> <p>c:.exe /Log “c:.log” The log file is created under c:.log.</p> <h5 id="layout">/Layout </Path-to-folder></h5> <p>Downloads the non-embedded installer files and creates a copy of the setup package in the folder specified. This allows a user to run the setup package and perform an installation or repair on an offline computer. To do this, the setup package and installer files must be in the same folder.</p> <p>If there are spaces in the path to the folder, the path must be enclosed in quotes.</p> <p>Example:</p> <p>c:.exe /Layout “c:setup” The installer files are downloaded to the c:setupfolder.</p> <h5 id="type">/Type <name></h5> <p>Specifies the setup type to use instead of the default. To view a list of available setup types, use the /MoreHelp command-line option.</p> <p>Example:</p> <p>c:.exe /type Safe The installer files are downloaded to the c:setupfolder.</p> <h5 id="language-1">/Language <LanguageCode></h5> <p>Specifies the three letter language code of the product language to use instead of the Operating System Language. This language is used when performing a clean install or a Layout. For actions like an update or a repair, the previously installed product language will be used and this option will be ignored. To view a list of supported language codes, use the /MoreHelp command-line option.</p> <p>Install Example:</p> <p>c:.exe /Language enu The English version of the product is installed.</p> <p>Layout Example:</p> <p>c:.exe /Language enu /Layout “c:setup” The installer files for the English version of the product are downloaded to the c:setupfolder.</p> <h5 id="installeruilanguage">/InstallerUILanguage <LanguageCode></h5> <p>Specifies the three letter language code of the user interface display language to use instead of the Operating System Language. To view a list of supported language codes, use the /MoreHelp command-line option.</p> <p>Example:</p> <p>c:.exe /InstallerUILanguage enu All dialogs and prompts are displayed in English.</p> <h5 id="morehelp">/MoreHelp</h5> <p>Displays additional help information, if available, about the setup package such as a list of setup types. The installation process is not performed.</p> <p>Example:</p> <p>c:.exe /MoreHelp The log file is created under c:.log.</p> <h5 id="results-of-morehelp">Results of /MoreHelp</h5> <p>These commands are not case sensitive.</p> <h6 id="type-1">/Type <SetupTypeName></h6> <p>Specifies the setup type to use instead of the default. The following is a list of available setup types:</p> <p>Silent Silently installs a typical installation without displaying any installation dialog boxes or prompts.</p> <p>Repair Repairs an existing installation. During the repair, progress dialogs are displayed and a clicking tone is played. At the end, you will be prompted to restart your computer.</p> <p>SilentRepair Silently repairs an existing installation without displaying any installation dialog boxes or prompts.</p> <p>Uninstall Uninstalls an existing installation.</p> <p>SilentUninstall Silently uninstalls an existing installation without removing shared components.</p> <p>SilentSharedUninstall Silently uninstalls an existing installation and the shared components.</p> <h6 id="language-2">/Language <LanguageCode></h6> <p>Specifies the three letter language code of the product language to use instead of the Operating System Language. This language is used when performing a clean install or a Layout. For actions like an update or a repair, the previously installed product language will be used and this option will be ignored. The following is a list of supported language codes:</p> <ul> <li>Arabic: arb</li> <li>German: deu</li> <li>English: enu</li> <li>Spanish: esn</li> <li>French: fra</li> <li>French Canadian: frc</li> <li>Hebrew: heb</li> <li>Dutch: nld</li> <li>Brazilian Portuguese: ptb</li> <li>Russian: rus</li> <li>Danish: dan</li> <li>Hungarian: hun</li> <li>Swedish: sve</li> <li>Italian: ita</li> <li>Norwegian: nor</li> <li>Finnish: fin</li> </ul> <h6 id="installeruilanguage-1">/InstallerUILanguage <LanguageCode></h6> <p>Specifies the three letter language code of the user interface display language to use instead of the Operating System Language. The following is a list of supported language codes:</p> <ul> <li>Arabic: arb</li> <li>Danish: dan</li> <li>German: deu</li> <li>English: enu</li> <li>Spanish: esn</li> <li>French: fra</li> <li>French Canadian: frc</li> <li>Hebrew: heb</li> <li>Dutch: nld</li> <li>Brazilian Portuguese: ptb</li> <li>Russian: rus</li> <li>Hungarian: hun</li> <li>Swedish: sve</li> <li>Italian: ita</li> <li>Norwegian: nor</li> <li>Finnish: fin</li> </ul> <h3 id="jaws-previous-jaws-for-windows-downloads">JAWS Previous JAWS for Windows Downloads</h3> <p>Skip to content</p> <p>Need Support? <a href="tel:+18004444443">1(800) 444-4443</a></p> <h4 id="jaws-previous-jaws-for-windows-downloads-1">JAWS Previous JAWS for Windows Downloads</h4> <p>Make sure to download the correct version (64-bit or 32-bit) for your computer, which we have detected is a -bit computer. Instructions to verify whether you have a 64-bit or 32-bit computer can be found at the bottom of this page.</p> <p>Select Version: Select Language:</p> <p>Non-Tandem builds</p> <p>If your corporate firewall prevents you from downloading files using FTP (File Transfer Protocol), choose the HTTP protocol instead.</p> <ul> <li>Offline Installer for Secure Environments</li> </ul> <h5 id="do-i-need-to-download-the-64-bit-or-32-bit-version-of-software-1">Do I need to download the 64-bit or 32-bit version of software</h5> <ul> <li>Press WINDOWS Key+E to open Windows Explorer.</li> <li>If you are using Windows 7, you should be focused on the OS (C:) drive and can press SPACEBAR to select it, and then ENTER to display the contents on the root of the C drive.</li> <li>If you are in Windows 8, you will have to first press RIGHT ARROW to navigate to the OS (C:) drive, and then proceed to press SPACEBAR and ENTER to open the root of C.</li> <li>Press the letter P until you reach the “Program Files” folder, and then press P once more.</li> <li>If you have 64-bit Windows, you have two folders: one named “Program Files” and another named “Program Files (x86).”</li> <li>If you have 32-bit Windows, you only have one folder named “Program Files.”</li> <li>Please select the appropriate 64-bit or 32-bit version to run on your system.</li> </ul> <h3 id="jaws-system-recommendations">JAWS System Recommendations</h3> <p>Skip to content</p> <p>Need Support? <a href="tel:+18004444443">1(800) 444-4443</a></p> <h4 id="jaws-system-recommendations-1">JAWS System Recommendations</h4> <p>To use JAWS for Windows, we recommend a personal computer running Microsoft® Windows® with the following:</p> <p>Description</p> <p>Specification</p> <p>Operating System (64-bit)</p> <p>Windows® 11, Windows 10, Windows Server® 2025, Windows Server 2022, Windows Server 2019, and Windows Server 2016.</p> <p>JAWS supports the x64 architecture for all operating systems.</p> <p>JAWS provides additional support for the ARM64 architecture on Windows 11 operating systems.</p> <p>Processor speed</p> <p>2.0 GHz i5 dual core or higher processor recommended.</p> <p>Memory (RAM)</p> <p>16 GB or more recommended.</p> <p>Required hard disk space</p> <p>2 GB with more space required for additional voices.</p> <p>SSD drive recommended.</p> <p>Video</p> <p>Video/Graphics card with support for DirectX 9 or later with WDDM 1.0 driver.</p> <p>1024x768 display resolution.</p> <p>Sound</p> <p>Windows compatible sound card (for speech).</p> <p>Note: The <a href="PreviousVersions">Previous JAWS Downloads Web page</a> has older versions of JAWS for computers still running Windows 7 (JAWS 2021 and earlier), Windows Vista (JAWS 17 and earlier), or Windows XP (JAWS 15 and earlier).</p> <h3 id="jaws-tandem-quick-start-guide">JAWS Tandem Quick Start Guide</h3> <p>Skip to content</p> <p>Need Support? <a href="tel:+18004444443">1(800) 444-4443</a></p> <h4 id="jaws-tandem-quick-start-guide-1">JAWS Tandem Quick Start Guide</h4> <p>Use JAWS Tandem™ to access another computer running JAWS to provide hands on technical support, write scripts from a distance, or perform remote JAWS training. This feature consists of a controller system, used by support personnel, distributors, dealers, consultants, and trainers, and a target system, which is the customer’s JAWS application and computer.</p> <p>A JAWS Tandem connection serves as an online meeting between two JAWS users. A meeting can be conducted over the Internet, which is known as a Tandem Center session, or over a private network, known as a Tandem Direct session. The primary connection method is through Tandem Center, a gateway server responsible for creating meeting IDs, verifying proper use of JAWS Tandem, and providing a path between the two systems. After the session is established, the controller can manage and run the target system’s desktop.</p> <p>Tandem Center sessions on both the controller and target computers are free of charge. For Tandem Direct sessions (typically used by corporations within a network) there is a charge for any computer that acts as a controller such as a help desk. There is no charge for target computers, such as workstations, in a Tandem Direct session.</p> <p>Remember to visit the Frequently Asked Questions for more information.</p> <p>Verify the following before you begin:</p> <ul> <li>Internet access</li> <li>JAWS or Fusion 2022 or later (recommended). If you need to connect to a Tandem session using JAWS or Fusion 2020 or 2021, make sure you are running the November 2021 updates for these versions.</li> <li>If you are having issues connecting to the Tandem Center, please make sure that Internet address tandem2.freedomscientific.com and port 443 be given access in the firewall. If you are in a corporate environment, please contact your IT team with this information.</li> </ul> <h5 id="starting-a-jaws-tandem-center-session">Starting a JAWS Tandem Center Session</h5> <p>Note: The controller user provides the target user with a meeting ID. The ID is automatically generated for the controller during the connection process as described in the following procedure.</p> <p>To start a JAWS Tandem Center session on a controller computer, do the following:</p> <ul> <li>Press INSERT+J to open the JAWS application window.</li> <li>Press ALT+U to open the Utilities menu.</li> <li>Select JAWS Tandem from this menu, and then select Tandem Center from the next submenu.</li> <li>Select Get Access to a computer, which then opens the Get Access to a Computer dialog box.</li> <li>Press SPACEBAR to activate the Get Access button.</li> <li>The Meeting ID Created dialog box opens. An alphanumeric ID appears in the Meeting ID read-only edit field. It is not case sensitive.</li> <li>Provide the target user with the meeting ID, and then wait for the connection process to complete on the target system. After successful connection with the target, you have access to the target system’s desktop. Note that once an ID is generated, it is valid for 60 minutes until a connection is made. If you have not made a connection within this period, you must obtain a new ID from the Tandem Center. Note: Instead of having the target user walk through similar menus, just tell the user to press INSERT+ALT+T. This will open the Allow Access to My Computer dialog box, and place focus in the Meeting ID edit box. You can then give the user the meeting ID that was created for you.</li> </ul> <p>On the target computer, do the following:</p> <ul> <li>Press INSERT+ALT+T. The Allow Access to My Computer dialog box opens.</li> <li>Type the meeting ID into the edit box. The ID is not case sensitive.</li> <li>Press TAB, and then SPACEBAR to activate the Allow Access button.</li> <li>After the controller and target successfully connect, the controller has access to the target system’s desktop.</li> </ul> <h5 id="running-a-session">Running a Session</h5> <p>As a controller, you can run the target system using JAWS and braille just as if you are sitting in front of that computer. Use the same JAWS keystrokes and functionality that you are familiar with to control the target system. JAWS keystrokes work no matter which type of keyboard layout is used: Laptop or Desktop.</p> <h6 id="jaws-tandem-keystrokes">JAWS Tandem Keystrokes</h6> <p>Note: When using the Laptop keyboard layout, substitute CAPS LOCK for INSERT when typing a JAWS Tandem keystroke.</p> <ul> <li>INSERT+ALT+T - ends session and can be issued from controller or target systems.</li> <li>Note: You can also use this keystroke to start JAWS Tandem on a target system.</li> <li>INSERT+ALT+TAB - toggles between target system’s desktop and controller system’s desktop. Only available on controller system; cannot be used by target system.</li> <li>INSERT+CTRL+SHIFT+V - toggles video on or off. Video is off by default. When video is on, it lets sighted users watch JAWS Tandem activity. Only available on controller system; cannot be used by target system. Note: If JAWS is running with ZoomText or as Fusion, you must always use INSERT+ALT+T to start or end a Tandem session even when using the Laptop keyboard layout.</li> </ul> <h6 id="remote-clipboard">Remote Clipboard</h6> <p>Use the CTRL+C keystroke to copy text with formatting from the target system, and then use CTRL+V to paste text into a file on the controller system. This is ideal for support personnel who want to copy specific text from a log file on the target system.</p> <p>Note: Remote Clipboard will not transfer files.</p> <h5 id="disconnecting-a-session">Disconnecting a Session</h5> <p>Press INSERT+ALT+T to terminate a session at any time from either the controller system or the target system. Each system regains control of its own desktop.</p> <h5 id="tandem-direct-session">Tandem Direct Session</h5> <p>A Tandem Direct session is used for enterprise networks in a business when two JAWS users are connected to the same network. All functionality and keystrokes previously mentioned for a Tandem Center session are applicable for a Tandem Direct session.</p> <p>Starting a Tandem Direct session is slightly different than a Tandem Center session as outlined in the following list.</p> <ul> <li>Determine which computer will be the controller and which will be the target.</li> <li>The first time you run a Tandem Direct session on a target system, you must unblock the program JTTarget so that it can communicate through Windows Firewall.</li> <li>The target system always initiates the session, and it must provide its meeting ID and its host name to the controller.</li> <li>By default, the target system listens on port 3000. If you change the port setting, remember to configure the controller system for the same port.</li> <li>The controller can turn on video to view JAWS Tandem activity.</li> </ul> <h6 id="starting-a-jaws-tandem-direct-session">Starting a JAWS Tandem Direct Session</h6> <p>A JAWS Tandem Direct session is always launched from the target computer. To start, do the following:</p> <ul> <li><p>Press INSERT+J and then ALT+U to open the Utilities menu in the JAWS application window.</p></li> <li><p>Press T to open the JAWS Tandem submenu, and then R to open the Tandem Direct submenu.</p></li> <li><p>Press A to choose Allow Access to my Computer. A dialog box opens with focus in the Meeting ID edit box.</p></li> <li><p>Type a value into the Meeting ID edit box. The Meeting ID can be letters, numbers, or a combination of both. The maximum ID length is 64-characters, and it is not case sensitive. You will provide this ID to the controller user.</p></li> <li><p>Press TAB to move to the Host Name or IP Address read-only edit box. Provide the controller user with the host name, for example, ABC-DEF001.</p></li> <li><p>Press TAB to move to the Allow Access button, and press SPACEBAR to activate the button. Note: As a target system, a Windows Security Alert dialog box may appear after pressing the Allow Access button. If this happens, choose the Unblock button and press SPACEBAR. (If a User Account Control dialog box opens, choose the Continue button and press SPACEBAR.) This action adds the JTTarget program to an exceptions list in Windows Firewall on the target system.</p></li> <li><p>Wait for the controller user to enter the target information. On a successful Tandem Direct connection, JAWS announces Tandem connection open. The controller system now has access to and can operate the target system. To start a JAWS Tandem Direct session on the controller computer, do the following:</p></li> <li><p>Press INSERT+J to open the JAWS application window, and press ALT+U to open the Utilities menu.</p></li> <li><p>Press T to open the JAWS Tandem submenu, and then R to open the Tandem Direct submenu.</p></li> <li><p>Press G to select Get Access to a Computer. A dialog box opens, and focus is in the Host Name or IP Address edit box.</p></li> <li><p>Type the host name, provided to you by the target user, into the edit box.</p></li> <li><p>Press TAB to move to the Meeting ID edit box, and type the ID provided by the target user.</p></li> <li><p>Press TAB to move to the Enable Video check box. If you are a sighted user and want to watch the JAWS Tandem activity on the target system, select the check box. If you do not need video, clear the check box. Note: By default, the Enable Video check box is cleared; however, if you selected the check box in a previous session, JAWS Tandem remembers this setting and uses it for the next session. Also, video can be toggled on or off at any time during a session using INSERT+CTRL+SHIFT+V.</p></li> <li><p>Press TAB to move to the Get Access button and press SPACEBAR to activate the button. After successfully connecting with the target, you now have control of the target system’s desktop. If the connection fails, verify that Windows Firewall is not blocking JTTarget on the target system. Also verify that host name, meeting ID, and port settings match.</p></li> </ul> <h5 id="configuring-windows-firewall-for-tandem-direct-sessions">Configuring Windows Firewall for Tandem Direct Sessions</h5> <p>Note: The following procedures are only necessary if JTTarget is later blocked on the target system.</p> <p>The target system uses a program named JTTarget. It must be added to an exceptions list on the target system so that the program can communicate through Windows Firewall. (It is not necessary to do this on the controller system.) Windows lets you unblock this program when you first create a Tandem Direct session. Later, if you block the program by deleting JTTarget from the Windows Firewall exceptions list or by clearing the JTTarget check box in the exceptions list, an error message or a Windows Security Alert will appear the next time the target and controller try to connect.</p> <h6 id="adding-jttarget-to-the-exceptions-list">Adding JTTarget to the Exceptions List</h6> <p>If you previously deleted the JTTarget program from the exceptions list in Windows Firewall, use the following steps to add the program:</p> <ul> <li>Open the Windows Control Panel and then select and open Windows Firewall.</li> <li>Navigate to and select the Allow an app or feature through Windows Firewall link. If a User Account Control dialog box opens, choose the Continue button and press SPACEBAR to activate the button.</li> <li>Select Change Settings and then select the Allow Another App button.</li> <li>Choose the Browse button in the Add a Program dialog box, and then type JTTarget.exe in the File name combo of the Browse dialog box.</li> <li>Press ENTER. The program is added to the Programs list in the Add a Program dialog box.</li> <li>Choose OK. JTTarget is added to and selected in the Allowed Programs list.</li> <li>Press TAB to move to the OK button and press SPACEBAR to save the change and close Windows Firewall. The controller system can now connect to the target system.</li> </ul> <h6 id="windows-firewall-exception-for-tandem-direct">Windows Firewall Exception for Tandem Direct</h6> <p>If you previously cleared the JTTarget check box in the exceptions list, do the following to select the check box:</p> <ul> <li>Open the Windows Control Panel and then select and open Windows Firewall.</li> <li>Navigate to and select the Allow an app or feature through Windows Firewall link. If a User Account Control dialog box opens, choose the Continue button and press SPACEBAR to activate the button.</li> <li>Select Change Settings and then select the Allow Another App button.</li> <li>In the Allowed Programs list, use the ARROW keys to move to JTTarget.</li> <li>Press SPACEBAR to select the check box.</li> <li>Press TAB to move to the OK button and press SPACEBAR to save the change and close Windows Firewall. The controller system can now connect to the target system.</li> </ul> <h5 id="connection-audit-logging">Connection Audit Logging</h5> <p>JAWS Tandem maintains a log of session activity using the Windows Event Log service. These events are used to record the beginning and end of a session, the suspension and continuation of a session, and errors triggered before a session starts. The advantage of having such a log is that consultants and trainers now have a record of JAWS Tandem activity which is useful for tracking time for billing purposes and so on. The event log can be set up so that only administrators can delete events. Also, users assigned any privilege level can write events to the event log.</p> <p>Note: JAWS Tandem event logging does not record user activity. It only logs session errors and the start, suspension, restart, and end of a session.</p> <ul> <li>To learn more about events, see JAWS Tandem Events.</li> <li>To learn more about the event properties, see JAWS Tandem Event Properties.</li> <li>To launch the Event Viewer, see Opening the Event Viewer.</li> </ul> <h6 id="jaws-tandem-events">JAWS Tandem Events</h6> <p>JAWS Tandem events and actions trigger an entry in the event log. The following events are available. For event details, see Event Properties.</p> <ul> <li>Event ID 1 - Tandem session error: An error event describing when a session cannot be established. This can be caused by the following: <ul> <li>Meeting ID used by the target does not match the meeting ID used by the controller.</li> <li>Target and controller are unable to find a common voice synthesizer.</li> <li>Meeting ID expired.</li> <li>Network error occurred; can be caused by the target computer not communicating with the Tandem Center.</li> </ul></li> <li>Event ID 2 - Tandem session started: An information event showing when a session is established between a controller and target computer. It appears in both the controller and target event logs.</li> <li>Event ID 3 - Tandem session concluded: An information event showing when a session ended. This can be caused by the target or controller computer closing the session, or by a network error closing the session. It appears in both the controller and target event logs.</li> <li>Event ID 4 - Tandem session suspended: An information event showing when the controller suspended a session. This is done by toggling between the target system desktop and the controller system desktop using INSERT+ALT+TAB. It appears in the target event log.</li> <li>Event ID 5 - Tandem session resumed: An information event showing when the controller resumed the session. This is done by toggling between the controller system desktop and the target system desktop using INSERT+ALT+TAB. It appears in the target event log.</li> </ul> <h6 id="jaws-tandem-event-properties">JAWS Tandem Event Properties</h6> <p>Event properties provide information about a JAWS Tandem event. The amount of detail given depends on the Event ID type. For example, an Event ID 4 logs only the Meeting ID, whereas an Event ID 3 provides details for all of the following event properties:</p> <ul> <li>Meeting ID: The alphanumeric ID that is used to start a session. For a Tandem Center session, this is the value that is automatically generated for the controller computer. For a Tandem Direct session, this is the value entered in the Meeting ID edit box on the target computer.</li> <li>Meeting type: Indicates if the meeting is a Tandem Center or Tandem Direct session.</li> <li>User role: Indicates if the controller or target computer started or ended the session. It also indicates whether the error occurred on the controller side or the target side of the session.</li> <li>Peer machine name - IP address: The machine name of the other computer in the session. For Tandem Direct sessions, the IP address is also included.</li> <li>Peer user name: The user name associated with the other computer in the session.</li> <li>Duration: Indicates the total duration of the session in hours, minutes, and seconds. This value also includes the amount of time the session was suspended.</li> <li>Suspend time: Indicates the duration that the session was suspended by the controller system.</li> <li>Reason: A three-digit code that explains why a session could not be established. The following error codes are available: <ul> <li>001: The controller or target computer could not connect to the Tandem Center.</li> <li>002: The meeting ID expired. This code applies to the controller computer in a Tandem Center session.</li> <li>003: The Tandem Center rejected the meeting ID. This code applies to the target computer in a Tandem Center session.</li> <li>004: The controller computer could not connect to the target computer. This applies to Tandem Direct sessions.</li> <li>005: There is a mismatch between the meeting ID entered for the controller system and the meeting ID entered for the target system. This code applies to Tandem Direct sessions.</li> <li>006: The controller computer and target computer could not agree on a common voice synthesizer to use for the session.</li> </ul></li> </ul> <h6 id="opening-the-event-viewer">Opening the Event Viewer</h6> <p>To open the Event Viewer, do the following:</p> <ul> <li>Press WINDOWS Key+X to open the Quick Link menu, then navigate to Event Viewer and press ENTER. If the User Account Control dialog box opens, choose Continue. The Event Viewer (Local) tree menu opens.</li> <li>Press W to select Windows Logs from the Event Viewer (Local) tree view. If necessary, press RIGHT ARROW to open Windows Logs.</li> <li>Press A to select Application.</li> <li>Press ALT+A to open the Action menu, and choose Filter Current Log. The Filter Current Log dialog box opens.</li> <li>Select the Information and Error check boxes. Clear the Critical, Warning, and Verbose check boxes.</li> <li>Press TAB one time from the Information check box and then press INSERT+3, followed by ALT+DOWN ARROW to open the Event source combo box list.</li> <li>Select JAWS X, where X is the JAWS release number. Make sure the check box is selected by pressing SPACEBAR, and then press ENTER.</li> <li>Choose OK to apply the event filter and close the dialog box.</li> <li>Press F6 to move focus to the Application list. You can now view all JAWS Tandem events. When reviewing audit points, use the meeting ID to make sure that you are viewing all events associated with a single session.</li> </ul> <h5 id="frequently-asked-questions-3">Frequently Asked Questions</h5> <p>Question: What version of JAWS must the controller and target system have?</p> <p>Answer: JAWS 2020 or later. An authorized license is needed if you are going to be a controller. To use 2020 or 2021 as a target or controller, you must be running the November 2021 updates for these versions. Visit the JAWS Previous Versions page to install the latest 2021 or 2020 updates.</p> <p>Question: How responsive is the JAWS Tandem session?</p> <p>Answer: You’ll be amazed! It’s very much like Remote Desktop or Citrix.</p> <p>Question: Can JAWS Demo or JAWS 40-Minute mode be used with JAWS Tandem on either the controller or target system?</p> <p>Answer: Yes, you can use JAWS as a Demo for a target system during Tandem sessions.</p> <p>Question: During a Tandem session, which keyboard layout, laptop or desktop, is used?</p> <p>Answer: The layout used on the controller side of the session is the primary keyboard layout used by both the controller and target systems.</p> <p>Question: Can a sighted user who is using a mouse on the controller computer work with the target computer or is it limited to keyboard use only?</p> <p>Answer: The mouse is also active when running JAWS Tandem provided that you turn on the video output on controller side.</p> <p>Question: What are the main uses of this outside of AT training and tech support? For example, can it be used to work with Web developers for usability testing?</p> <p>Answer: Yes. It can also be used by consultants to help with scripting and debugging issues from a distance.</p> <p>Question: Can JAWS Tandem be used by a JAWS user to remote into computers of sighted colleagues that don’t necessarily use JAWS?</p> <p>Answer: Yes, if the sighted colleagues install JAWS as a demo on their computers.</p> <p>Question: What is the difference between JAWS Tandem and Remote Desktop, Citrix, or terminal services?</p> <p>Answer: JAWS Tandem lets you, the controller, run in the target’s user session while the target user is on the computer at the same time. Remote Desktop/Terminal/Citrix is running on your own desktop on the remote machine, and no one on the other side can see or hear it. For support purposes, JAWS Tandem is perfect.</p> <p>Question: While in a JAWS Tandem session, can the controller use the Task Manager on the target computer?</p> <p>Answer: Yes. To launch Task Manager on the target side, you must use the keystroke CTRL+SHIFT+ESCAPE, or press WINDOWS Key+R to open the Run dialog box, and then type taskmgr and press ENTER. Note that if you try to use CTRL+ALT+DELETE to open the Task Manager, this command will be executed on the controller’s machine.</p> <p>Question: From the controller system, can I hear the target system’s audio?</p> <p>Answer: Yes. During a JAWS Tandem session, events that generate sounds on the target system, such as a Windows program error, entry and exit of Auto Forms Mode, or other JAWS sounds associated with the Speech and Sounds Manager, can be heard on the controller system. This means that when an event occurs on the target system, a notification is sent to the controller system so that the controller computer plays the same or a similar WAV file. This is very helpful to support personnel and trainers running the JAWS Tandem session.</p> <p>Question: Can I change my synthesizer during a session?</p> <p>Answer: No. After a session is established, you can only change the pitch or volume of your synthesizer.</p> <p>Question: Can my English United States (ENU) computer use JAWS Tandem to connect to an English United Kingdom (ENG) or Australian (ENA) computer?</p> <p>Answer: Yes. Systems with different minor languages (dialects) will work in JAWS Tandem.</p> <p>Question: Can my English computer use JAWS Tandem to connect to a computer with a different major language such as French or Spanish?</p> <p>Answer: No. You would first need to switch one of the computers to match the others’ major language before starting the JAWS Tandem meeting.</p> <p>Question: Can a controller temporarily turn off any JAWS user settings on the target computer, in order to troubleshoot a problem that the target computer is having?</p> <p>Answer: Yes. Use the Manage Application Settings dialog box located in the Options menu of the JAWS application window. In this dialog, you can choose to disable all settings, default settings, or selective applications without having to restart JAWS. A restart would end the JAWS Tandem session. This is a great way to troubleshoot a problem by ruling out any user modifications or third party scripts.</p> <p>Question: If either the controller or target computer needs to be restarted, what will happen to the JAWS Tandem session?</p> <p>Answer: You would need to start a JAWS Tandem session again with a new meeting ID after the computer restarts. It is suggested that the controller or target end the JAWS Tandem session with INSERT+ALT+T before rebooting the computer.</p> <p>Question: How many computers can join a JAWS Tandem Meeting?</p> <p>Answer: There can only be two. One controller and one target.</p> <p>Question: If you are using an app such as Teams or Skype to talk between two different computers, can you also use JAWS Tandem without ending the call?</p> <p>Answer: Yes, this can be very useful as well. The controller can explain what is being done and the target user can ask questions during the entire session consequently avoiding a phone call.</p> <p>Question: What if either computer receives a call over Teams or Skype during a JAWS Tandem Session? Can it be answered?</p> <p>Answer: If the call is on the target computer, then either the target user, or controller for that matter, can answer. If the call is on the controller side, then the controller can answer it by toggling back to his or her own desktop by using INSERT+ALT+TAB without having to end the JAWS Tandem session.</p> <p>Question: What is the role of the Tandem Center?</p> <p>Answer: The Tandem Center allows two arbitrary JAWS users anywhere on the Internet to connect to each other. The Tandem Center gets data from one user and passes it to the other user.</p> <p>Question: Who runs the Tandem Center?</p> <p>Answer: The Tandem Center is hosted by Freedom Scientific.</p> <p>Question: How does JAWS Tandem communication work?</p> <p>Answer: JAWS Tandem uses a proprietary protocol to establish a connection and transport data between two computers. To achieve security, it uses the TLS 1.2 cryptographic protocol.</p> <p>Question: Does Freedom Scientific know about what I am doing if all data travels through the Tandem Center?</p> <p>Answer: Freedom Scientific does not record the contents of any session. The session infrastructure is set up so that once a session begins; the data is encrypted so that the Tandem Center server cannot decipher the information.</p> <p>Question: Can the target user disconnect the session if they do not like the controller user’s actions?</p> <p>Answer: Yes. Any user can disconnect at any time by pressing INSERT+ALT+T.</p> <p>Question: My Firewall is blocking the connection to the Tandem Center. What do I do?</p> <p>Answer: The Tandem Center runs at a well-known Internet address and port. The Tandem Center address is tandem2.freedomscientific.com. The port is 443. If Tandem Center is being blocked, configure your firewall to allow access to this address and port.</p> <p>Question: For a Tandem Direct session, what port does the target system listen to for a connection to the controller system? Can I change the port?</p> <p>Answer: For a Tandem Direct session, the target system listens on port 3000 by default. If you need to change the port setting, choose the Options button in the Allow Access to my Computer dialog box, and type a new port number in the Port edit box. Remember to tell the user on the controller side so that JAWS Tandem on the controller system can be configured for the same port. The Options button is in the Get Access to a Computer on the controller system.</p> <p>Question: I use the DECtalk hardware synthesizer. My friend wants to connect to me and help me configure e-mail. He does not have DECtalk and uses Vocalizer Expressive. Can we have a JAWS Tandem session?</p> <p>Answer: Yes, JAWS Tandem will detect that you and your friend have different synthesizers. It will offer to switch both of you to Eloquence for the length of the sessions. You both will connect and work for the length of the session using Eloquence. After the JAWS Tandem session ends, both you and your friend will go back to your synthesizers automatically.</p> <p>Question: My Tandem Direct connection fails and JAWS announces the following message: A connection attempt failed because the connected party did not properly respond after a period of time, or the established connection failed because the connected host has failed to respond. What happened?</p> <p>Answer: On the target system, you must add an exception to the JTTarget program in the Windows Firewall. Refer to Configuring Windows Firewall for Tandem Direct Sessions for more information. After following the steps in this section, make a Tandem Direct connection again. If this still does not work, restart JAWS and try to connect again.</p> <h3 id="jaws-screen-reader-miscellaneous">JAWS ® Screen Reader (Miscellaneous)</h3> <h4 id="jawsscreen-reader-1">JAWS®Screen Reader</h4> <h5 id="the-worlds-most-trusted-screen-reader-for-work-school-and-home.-1">The world’s most trusted screen reader for work, school, and home.</h5> <p><a href="https://vispero.com/lp/download-jaws/">Start free trial</a></p> <p><a href="https://store.freedomscientific.com/collections/jaws">Buy now</a></p> <p>Our screen reader software delivers fast, reliable access for people who are blind or have low vision—trusted by accessibility professionals, governments, and educators worldwide.</p> <h5 id="why-professionals-choose-jaws-screen-reader-software-1">Why professionals choose JAWS screen reader software</h5> <p>As the world’s most trusted and widely used screen reader, JAWS delivers the reliability, security, and performance that modern users and organizations depend on.
