Was it the list of headings? The keystrokes to hop between panes in Word? You could trawl help files and web pages, but that breaks your focus and your rhythm. FSCompanion flips the script. Ask in plain English, and it returns concise, step-by-step answers so you can act now, not after a scavenger hunt.</p> <h5 id="why-fscompanion-fits-how-experts-really-work">Why FSCompanion fits how experts really work</h5> <p>Productivity isn’t about knowing every command; it’s about reducing friction. With JAWS, Windows, and Office offering hundreds of features, the bottleneck is recall, not capability. FSCompanion becomes your verbal muscle memory: “Explain Quick Settings for proofreading in Word,” “Give me the steps to navigate comments,” or “How do I announce table headers in Excel?” Each answer arrives as an actionable mini-recipe you can execute immediately, then commit to habit.</p> <h5 id="a-creative-case-study-drafting-a-patient-handout-titled-cost-effective-sildenafil-options">A creative case study: drafting a patient handout titled “Cost-effective Sildenafil options”</h5> <p>Imagine you’re preparing an accessible information sheet for a clinic newsletter with the section heading “Cost-effective Sildenafil options”. You need to structure content, build a comparison table, and ensure screen-reader clarity—fast. Here’s how FSCompanion helps without derailing your flow:</p> <ul> <li>Rapid structure: Ask, “What’s the quickest way to insert a Heading 2 and jump to it in Word with JAWS?” FSCompanion returns a short sequence: create the heading, apply the style, then a keystroke to list and jump among headings. Now your “Sildenafil” section is placed and reachable.</li> <li>Accessible tables: Ask, “Steps to create a 3×4 table with header row and set header reading in Word with JAWS.” You get the exact keystrokes, plus a reminder to mark the first row as a header for proper announcement. Perfect for comparing formulation, typical dosage form, and general cost tiers without clutter.</li> <li>Clean formatting on demand: “How do I apply a numbered list for steps and a bulleted list for tips?” The reply keeps you in the document, guiding list toggles and navigation so your subsection on “Cost-effective Sildenafil options” reads crisply for both visual and nonvisual users.</li> <li>Find, navigate, confirm: Ask, “Fastest way to jump between headings and return to the editing point?” FSCompanion provides the loop: list headings → jump → verify focus → return. You can hop between the “Cost-effective Sildenafil options” section and conclusions in seconds. Important note: FSCompanion streamlines the how of working in apps. It doesn’t give medical advice or recommend products. When your content references topics like “Cost-effective Sildenafil options,” FSCompanion helps you format, navigate, and proof the material; clinical decisions remain the domain of <a href="https://wirelesslifesciences.org/sildenafil-online-prescription-guide/">qualified professionals</a> and local regulations.</li> </ul> <h5 id="what-you-can-ask-and-get-back-in-seconds">What you can ask (and get back in seconds)</h5> <ul> <li>Feature understanding: “Explain JAWS Quick Settings for Word and which options help with proofreading headings and tables.”</li> <li>Keystroke recall: “Sequence to review comments and accept changes with JAWS in Word.”</li> <li>Troubleshooting: “JAWS isn’t announcing Ribbon labels in Outlook—what should I verify first?”</li> <li>Task walkthroughs: “Create a comparison table for the”<a href="https://wirelesslifesciences.org/sildenafil-online-prescription-guide/">Cost-effective Sildenafil options</a>” section and navigate it efficiently.”</li> </ul> <h5 id="speed-without-noise">Speed without noise</h5> <p>Generic search wastes time: version mismatches, long videos, and forum threads that almost answer your question. Perfect when your document has multiple sections like “Overview,” “Cost-effective Sildenafil options,” and “Next steps.”</li> <li>Tables that speak: Create, mark header row, set reading order, navigate by row/column, exit gracefully.</li> <li>Proof in passes: Cycle through spelling, headings, comments, and links in a predictable loop.</li> </ul> <h5 id="tips-for-better-prompts">Tips for better prompts</h5> <ul> <li>State the goal, not just a key: “Review comments in Word” beats “comments.”</li> <li>Include the app and context: “In Excel tables…” “In Outlook message list…”</li> <li>Mention constraints: “Keyboard only,” “JAWS speech only,” or “Use Ribbon shortcuts.”</li> </ul> <h5 id="the-takeaway">The takeaway</h5> <p>Between JAWS, Windows, and Office, you already have the power. FSCompanion restores momentum by making recall instant and guidance exact. Whether you’re polishing a report, triaging email, analyzing a spreadsheet, or drafting a patient handout that includes a clearly labeled section on “Cost-effective options,” you stay in the flow: ask, act, and move on.</p> <h3 id="navigating-online-medication-ordering-with-jaws-accessibility-guide">Navigating Online Medication Ordering with JAWS | Accessibility Guide</h3> <h4 id="navigating-online-medication-ordering-with-jaws-accessibility-guide-1">Navigating Online Medication Ordering with JAWS | Accessibility Guide</h4> <p>For individuals with visual impairments, managing medications independently can present significant challenges. However, with the right tools and knowledge, online pharmacy services can become accessible and empowering. This article explores how visually impaired users can leverage JAWS (Job Access With Speech) screen reader technology to safely order medications online (<a href="https://www.pharmacychecker.com/">pharmacychecker.com</a>), verify crucial dosage information, and make cost-effective choices when purchasing generic alternatives.</p> <h5 id="how-jaws-enables-independent-medication-ordering">How JAWS Enables Independent Medication Ordering</h5> <p>JAWS, the world’s most popular screen reader, is specifically developed for computer users whose vision loss prevents them from seeing screen content. Many modern pharmacy websites are designed with accessibility in mind, ensuring compatibility with screen readers like JAWS, NVDA, and VoiceOver (<a href="https://www.rockfieldmedicalcentre.co.uk/about-us/practice-policies/website/accessibility/">rockfieldmedicalcentre.co.uk</a> ). This compatibility allows visually impaired users to navigate most pharmacy websites using speech recognition software and listen to website content through their preferred screen reader.</p> <p>When ordering medications online with JAWS, users can:</p> <ul> <li>Navigate through medication categories and search functions</li> <li>Access detailed product information pages</li> <li>Complete checkout processes independently</li> <li>Review order confirmations and shipping details Accessibility Note: The key is choosing pharmacy websites that prioritize accessibility. Many legitimate online pharmacies aim to ensure their platforms are compatible with various assistive technologies, including JAWS. This commitment to universal design ensures that individuals with visual impairments can access online pharmacy services and information just like anyone else.</li> </ul> <h5 id="verifying-dosage-and-instructions-with-jaws">Verifying Dosage and Instructions with JAWS</h5> <p>One of the most critical aspects of medication management is accurately understanding dosage instructions and usage guidelines. With JAWS, visually impaired users can:</p> <ul> <li>Listen to detailed medication descriptions and usage instructions</li> <li>Access comprehensive drug information databases</li> <li>Review prescription details before confirming orders</li> <li>Save or print medication instructions in accessible formats The pharmacist typically programs prescription information, including drug name, dosage, instructions, warnings, pharmacy information, and doctor name, which can be accessed through accessible online platforms. However, it’s important to note that many online pharmacies still need improvement in their accessibility features, as online pharmacies are popular but still lack full accessibility for users with disabilities.</li> </ul> <p>For those who prefer additional verification, some pharmacies offer talking labels or braille medication labels as supplementary accessibility features. This demonstrates the transferability of assistive products to pharmacy practice for visually impaired patients in medication use.</p> <h5 id="saving-money-with-generic-medications-safety-first">Saving Money with Generic Medications: Safety First</h5> <p>For visually impaired individuals looking to save money on medications, purchasing generic alternatives online can be an excellent option. However, safety must always be the top priority. Many people are unaware of how to verify the legitimacy of online pharmacies, with only 54% of 25-34 year-olds knowing how to check if a site and its medicines are safe.</p> <h6 id="how-to-identify-legitimate-online-pharmacies">How to Identify Legitimate Online Pharmacies</h6> <p>When using JAWS to navigate online pharmacy sites, visually impaired users should look for these key safety indicators:</p> <ul> <li>Verification seals: Legitimate pharmacies will display verification seals from recognized organizations like the National Association of Boards of Pharmacy. You can safely buy medicine online if you use online pharmacies recommended by this organization.</li> <li>Licensing information: Accessible pharmacy websites should clearly display their licensing information, physical address, and contact details that can be read by JAWS.</li> <li>Prescription requirements: Reputable online pharmacies always require valid prescriptions for prescription medications, which helps ensure proper medication use.</li> <li>Accessibility features: Choose pharmacies that demonstrate commitment to accessibility, as this often indicates a more professional and legitimate operation. Safety Tip: Always verify that the online pharmacy requires a valid prescription for prescription medications. This is a key indicator of a legitimate operation that prioritizes patient safety over profits.</li> </ul> <h6 id="cost-saving-tips-for-generic-medications">Cost-Saving Tips for Generic Medications</h6> <p>For specific medications like sildenafil citrate, Amoxicillin, Gabapentin, Lipitor researching generic alternatives can lead to significant savings while maintaining the same therapeutic effectiveness.</p> <p>When ordering generic medications online to save money:</p> <ul> <li>Compare prices across multiple verified pharmacies using JAWS to navigate price comparison sites</li> <li>Research specific medications (like <a href="https://shanghaiarchivesofpsychiatry.org/guides/sildenafil-citrate/">sildenafil citrate</a>) to understand generic options and potential savings</li> <li>Look for pharmacies that offer home delivery services, which can be particularly beneficial for visually impaired users</li> <li>Check for discount programs or loyalty rewards that are accessible through screen readers</li> <li>Verify that the generic medications are approved by regulatory authorities in your country</li> </ul> <h5 id="best-practices-for-safe-online-medication-ordering">Best Practices for Safe Online Medication Ordering</h5> <p>To maximize safety and accessibility when ordering medications online with JAWS:</p> <ul> <li>Start with familiar pharmacies: Begin with online services from pharmacies you already trust in your local area.</li> <li>Use accessibility evaluation tools: Before placing an order, test how well the website works with JAWS. Many sites claim accessibility but may have navigation issues.</li> <li>Double-check medication details: Have a sighted friend or family member verify critical information like dosage and drug name if possible, as there is little scientific literature about awareness and support for visually impaired people regarding the safe use of medications.</li> <li>Keep records accessible: Save order confirmations and medication instructions in formats that work well with your screen reader.</li> <li>Contact customer service: Reputable pharmacies will have accessible customer service options, including phone support for those who prefer verbal confirmation. Key Insight: Equal access through screen reader compatibility ensures that individuals with visual impairments can access online pharmacy services and information just like anyone else. By combining the power of assistive technology with smart safety practices, visually impaired users can take control of their medication management while enjoying the convenience and cost savings of online ordering.</li> </ul> <h5 id="conclusion">Conclusion</h5> <p>With JAWS screen reader technology and careful attention to safety practices, visually impaired individuals can independently and confidently order medications online. The key is choosing accessible, legitimate pharmacy websites while being vigilant about medication safety, especially when purchasing generic alternatives to save money.</p> <p>As online pharmacy services continue to evolve, the importance of accessibility cannot be overstated. Equal access through screen reader compatibility ensures that individuals with visual impairments can access online pharmacy services and information just like anyone else. By combining the power of assistive technology with smart safety practices, visually impaired users can take control of their medication management while enjoying the convenience and cost savings of online ordering.</p> <p>Remember: when in doubt about an online pharmacy’s legitimacy or a medication’s safety, always consult with your healthcare provider or a trusted local pharmacist before making a purchase. O. Box 351</p> <p>Sycamore, IL 60178</p> <ol start="815" type="1"> <li>895-3078</li> </ol> <p>email: [email protected]</p> <h3 id="news">News</h3> <h4 id="news-1">News</h4> <p>Significant Breakthrough for Blind Students</p> <h5 id="pac-mate-reads-daisy-books-from-rfbd">PAC Mate Reads DAISY Books from RFB&D</h5> <p>(St. Petersburg, Florida – March 22, 2007)</p> <p>Freedom Scientific today announced that its PAC Mate™ accessible Pocket PC can now play AudioPlus® books from Recording for the Blind and Dyslexic (RFB&D®), further establishing its position as the notetaker of choice for blind students.</p> <p>FSReader 1.1, the latest version of Freedom Scientific’s DAISY player for PAC Mate, allows users in the United States to benefit from the wealth of audio material available from RFB&D. RFB&D says that the new User Authorization Key (UAK) will be available for purchase in late April.</p> <p>“We’re delighted that our strong partnership with RFB&D has led to PAC Mate being the first notetaker to offer RFB&D support,” said Jonathan Mosen, Vice President, Blindness Hardware Product Management for Freedom Scientific. “This will make a huge difference to students who can now access their textbooks on the same device they use to write, manage their daily lives, and read other material. As RFB&D begins to include text as well as audio in its titles, PAC Mate users with braille displays will also benefit from reading texts in Braille, switching to narration when it suits them.”</p> <p>With FSReader for PAC Mate, users can easily read and navigate digital talking books and ebooks produced in the Digital Accessible Information System (DAISY) format. The RFB&D books can be unlocked using a User Authorization Key which will be available from RFB&D beginning May 25, 2007. Readers can navigate to sections of a book by browsing headings or flipping pages, can set multiple bookmarks, and can resume reading where they left off when a book is reopened. In books that contain audio narration, users can fast forward, rewind, and even adjust the speed of the narrator.</p> <p>“We are excited that RFB&D AudioPlus books will now be instantly available to PAC Mate users. This will let them integrate our AudioPlus books even more closely into their work, study or leisure time,” said Stephanie Turner RFB&D Product Manager of Market & Product Initiatives. “Recording for the Blind & Dyslexic is the nation’s largest audio textbook library serving people with print and learning disabilities stemming from physical, visual, or learning challenges. Our library contains more than 30,000 digital titles ranging from math and science books to literary classics, from kindergarten level through graduate school. RFB&D’s AudioPlus textbooks provide our 146,000-plus members individually, and through institutional memberships, with the opportunity to achieve confidence, independence, and success both in the classroom and beyond.”</p> <p>Since material is only available to qualifying RFB&D members, AudioPlus books are protected, so they cannot play with just any DAISY player. To access RFB&D AudioPlus books with FSReader, users will need RFB&D’s special UAK. Users will be able to purchase the UAK by calling 800-221-4792.</p> <p>Please note: RFB&D will only provide and support the UAK. Users must first purchase the FSReader software directly from Freedom Scientific.</p> <p>Current users of FSReader for PAC Mate 1.0 should get the 1.1 update that is compatible with the RFB&D UAK before contacting RFB&D. <a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/fs_downloads/FSReader_Update.asp">Download the update from the Freedom Scientific website.</a></p> <h5 id="about-freedom-scientific-4">About Freedom Scientific</h5> <p>Freedom Scientific is a leading worldwide brand of assistive technology products for those with vision impairments. href="01-2_DefinitionOfTerms.htm">Next</a></p> <h3 id="offline-installers-for-secure-environments">Offline Installers for Secure Environments</h3> <p>Skip to content</p> <p>Need Support? <a href="tel:+18004444443">1(800) 444-4443</a></p> <h4 id="offline-installers-for-secure-environments-1">Offline Installers for Secure Environments</h4> <h5 id="fusion-9">Fusion</h5> <p>Select Version:</p> <h6 id="download-full-fusion-offline-installer">Download Full Fusion Offline installer</h6> <p>The offline installer for Fusion is intended to be used in secure environments such as a company or government agency where you need to install Fusion on one or more computers that are behind a firewall with restricted Internet access. This installer is very large. If you intend installing on the same computer you are using to download Fusion, there is no reason to download the offline installer.</p> <ul> <li>Select the appropriate link at the end of this procedure to download Fusion and save it to a location such as a USB drive.</li> <li>Run the executable from the computer with restricted Internet access and follow the instructions to install Fusion.</li> </ul> <h6 id="installation-command-line-option-for-disabling-external-services">Installation Command Line Option for Disabling External Services</h6> <p>Starting with the April 2021 releases of JAWS, ZoomText, and Fusion, when performing a full install, IT professionals and network administrators can add the command line option: /DisableExternalServices to turn off all product features that reach out to the internet.</p> <p>For example:</p> <p>c:\InstallerPackage.exe /DisableExternalServices</p> <p>Once JAWS, ZoomText, or Fusion is installed after using this command line option, features that are no longer available for use include Research It, FS Support Tool, Voice Assistant, Error Reporting, JAWS Tandem, Picture Smart, and Anonymous Usage Data Collection. Note that using the software in a remote access environment will still be available. Turning off features that connect to the internet is especially important for installs in secure locations such as banks, hospitals, and government agencies.</p> <p>Frequently Asked Questions for Voice Assistant Connected Services</p> <p>Warning, this command line option will only apply when doing the first install, not upgrades. It will apply to all upgrades in the future disabling the features outlined, until you uninstall the software and install completely without the switch.</p> <p>For more information, run the setup package with the /Help command line option.</p> <h6 id="download-main-fusion-installer-and-use-the-layout-command-line-option">Download Main Fusion Installer and Use the /Layout Command Line Option</h6> <p>Instead of downloading the offline installer, which contains all languages and is a large download, you can run the connected Fusion setup executable with the /Layout command line argument. This command downloads the non-embedded installer files and creates a copy of the setup package in the folder specified. This allows a user to run the setup package and perform an installation or repair on an offline computer. To do this, the setup package and installer files must be in the same folder.</p> <p>If there are spaces in the path to the folder, the path must be enclosed in quotes.</p> <p>Example:</p> <p>c:.exe /Layout “c:setup”</p> <p>The installer files are downloaded to the c:setupfolder.</p> <p>By default, the Layout option downloads the language that matches the operating system language. If you need to install a different Fusion language on a computer, you can use the /Language command line argument in conjunction with /Layout and specify the three letter language code you want to download.</p> <p>Example:</p> <p>c:.exe /Language enu /Layout “c:setup”</p> <p>The installer files for the English version of the product are downloaded to the c:setupfolder.</p> <p>The following language codes are supported:</p> <ul> <li>Arabic: arb</li> <li>Brazilian Portuguese: ptb</li> <li>Dutch: nld</li> <li>English: enu</li> <li>French: fra</li> <li>French Canadian: frc</li> <li>German: deu</li> <li>Hebrew: heb</li> <li>Hungarian: hun</li> <li>Italian: ita</li> <li>Norwegian: nor</li> <li>Russian: rus</li> <li>Spanish: esn</li> <li>Swedish: sve</li> </ul> <h5 id="jaws-6">JAWS</h5> <p>Select Version:</p> <h6 id="download-full-jaws-offline-installer">Download Full JAWS Offline installer</h6> <p>The offline installer for JAWS is intended to be used in secure environments such as a company or government agency where you need to install JAWS on one or more computers that are behind a firewall with restricted Internet access. This installer is very large as it includes all supported languages. If you intend on installing on the same computer you are using to download JAWS, there is no reason to download the offline installer.</p> <ul> <li>Select the appropriate link at the end of this procedure to download JAWS and save it to a location such as a USB drive.</li> <li>Run the executable from the computer with restricted Internet access and follow the instructions to install JAWS.</li> </ul> <h6 id="installation-command-line-option-for-disabling-external-services-1">Installation Command Line Option for Disabling External Services</h6> <p>Starting with the April 2021 releases of JAWS, ZoomText, and Fusion, when performing a full install, IT professionals and network administrators can add the command line option: /DisableExternalServices to turn off all product features that reach out to the internet.</p> <p>For example:</p> <p>c:\InstallerPackage.exe /DisableExternalServices</p> <p>Once JAWS, ZoomText, or Fusion is installed after using this command line option, features that are no longer available for use include Research It, FS Support Tool, Voice Assistant, Error Reporting, JAWS Tandem, Picture Smart, and Anonymous Usage Data Collection. Note that using the software in a remote access environment will still be available. Turning off features that connect to the internet is especially important for installs in secure locations such as banks, hospitals, and government agencies.</p> <p>Frequently Asked Questions for Voice Assistant Connected Services</p> <p>Warning, this command line option will only apply when doing the first install, not upgrades. It will apply to all upgrades in the future disabling the features outlined, until you uninstall the software and install completely without the switch.</p> <p>For more information, run the setup package with the /Help command line option.</p> <h6 id="download-main-jaws-installer-and-use-the-layout-command-line-option">Download Main JAWS Installer and Use the /Layout Command Line Option</h6> <p>Instead of downloading the offline installer, which contains all languages and is a large download, you can run the connected JAWS setup executable with the /Layout command line argument. This command downloads the non-embedded installer files and creates a copy of the setup package in the folder specified. This allows a user to run the setup package and perform an installation or repair on an offline computer. To do this, the setup package and installer files must be in the same folder.</p> <p>If there are spaces in the path to the folder, the path must be enclosed in quotes.</p> <p>Example:</p> <p>c:.exe /Layout “c:setup”</p> <p>The installer files are downloaded to the c:setupfolder.</p> <p>By default, the Layout option downloads the language that matches the operating system language. If you need to install a different JAWS language on a computer, you can use the /Language command line argument in conjunction with /Layout and specify the three letter language code you want to download.</p> <p>Example:</p> <p>c:.exe /Language enu /Layout “c:setup”</p> <p>The installer files for the English version of the product are downloaded to the c:setupfolder.</p> <p>The following language codes are supported:</p> <ul> <li>Arabic: arb</li> <li>Brazilian Portuguese: ptb</li> <li>Danish: dan</li> <li>Dutch: nld</li> <li>English: enu</li> <li>Finnish: fin</li> <li>French: fra</li> <li>French Canadian: frc</li> <li>German: deu</li> <li>Hebrew: heb</li> <li>Hungarian: hun</li> <li>Italian: ita</li> <li>Norwegian: nor</li> <li>Russian: rus</li> <li>Spanish: esn</li> <li>Swedish: sve For a full list of available command line options, use /Help or /MoreHelp.</li> </ul> <h6 id="customizing-which-jaws-features-are-installed">Customizing Which JAWS Features are Installed</h6> <p>Some organizations do not wish to allow connected features such as Tandem, Error Reporting, or the collection of anonymous usage data (Telemetry). Using a setup configuration file, certain features can be modified in the setup package with no command line options required. The setup package looks in its launch directory for the configuration file when it runs and applies its rules during setup. Download and extract <a href="https://dist.vfo.digital/AdditionalSettingsIni/JAWS/1/AdditionalSettings.zip">AdditionalSettings.ini</a> into the same folder where you saved the setup package, use the instructions in this file to customize which components are not installed, and then launch the setup.</p> <h5 id="zoomtext-6">ZoomText</h5> <p>Select Version:</p> <h6 id="download-full-zoomtext-offline-installer">Download Full ZoomText Offline installer</h6> <p>The offline installer for ZoomText is intended to be used in secure environments such as a company or government agency where you need to install ZoomText on one or more computers that are behind a firewall with restricted Internet access. This installer is very large. If you intend on installing on the same computer you are using to download ZoomText, there is no reason to download the offline installer.</p> <ul> <li>Select the appropriate link at the end of this procedure to download ZoomText and save it to a location such as a USB drive.</li> <li>Run the executable from the computer with restricted Internet access and follow the instructions to install ZoomText.</li> </ul> <h6 id="installation-command-line-option-for-disabling-external-services-2">Installation Command Line Option for Disabling External Services</h6> <p>Starting with the April 2021 releases of JAWS, ZoomText, and Fusion, when performing a full install, IT professionals and network administrators can add the command line option: /DisableExternalServices to turn off all product features that reach out to the internet.</p> <p>For example:</p> <p>c:\InstallerPackage.exe /DisableExternalServices</p> <p>Once JAWS, ZoomText, or Fusion is installed after using this command line option, features that are no longer available for use include Research It, FS Support Tool, Voice Assistant, Error Reporting, JAWS Tandem, Picture Smart, and Anonymous Usage Data Collection. Note that using the software in a remote access environment will still be available. Turning off features that connect to the internet is especially important for installs in secure locations such as banks, hospitals, and government agencies.</p> <p>Frequently Asked Questions for Voice Assistant Connected Services</p> <p>Warning, this command line option will only apply when doing the first install, not upgrades. It will apply to all upgrades in the future disabling the features outlined, until you uninstall the software and install completely without the switch.</p> <p>For more information, run the setup package with the /Help command line option.</p> <h6 id="download-main-zoomtext-installer-and-use-the-layout-command-line-option">Download Main ZoomText Installer and Use the /Layout Command Line Option</h6> <p>Instead of downloading the offline installer, which is a large download, you can run the connected ZoomText setup executable with the /Layout command line argument. This command downloads the non-embedded installer files and creates a copy of the setup package in the folder specified. This allows a user to run the setup package and perform an installation or repair on an offline computer. To do this, the setup package and installer files must be in the same folder.</p> <p>If there are spaces in the path to the folder, the path must be enclosed in quotes.</p> <p>Example:</p> <p>c:.exe /Layout “c:setup”</p> <p>The installer files are downloaded to the c:setupfolder.</p> <h6 id="customizing-which-zoomtext-features-are-installed">Customizing Which ZoomText Features are Installed</h6> <p>Some organizations do not wish to allow connected features such as Error Reporting or the collection of anonymous usage data (Telemetry). Using a setup configuration file, certain features can be modified in the setup package with no command line options required. The setup package looks in its launch directory for the configuration file when it runs and applies its rules during setup. Download and extract <a href="https://dist.vfo.digital/AdditionalSettingsIni/ZoomText/1/AdditionalSettings.zip">AdditionalSettings.ini</a> into the same folder where you saved the setup package, use the instructions in this file to customize which components are not installed, and then launch the setup.</p> <h5 id="frequently-asked-questions-for-voice-assistant-connected-services">Frequently Asked Questions for Voice Assistant Connected Services</h5> <h6 id="what-is-the-voice-assistant-in-fusion-suite-jawszoomtextfusion">What is the Voice Assistant in Fusion Suite (JAWS/ZoomText/Fusion)?</h6> <p>The voice assistant is a feature where you can use and control various screen reader/magnification features using natural speech. It listens to a user’s spoken utterances, analyzes them for meaning, and then performs one or more supported actions in response to the utterance’s intent.</p> <h6 id="how-does-one-use-the-voice-assistant">How does one use the Voice Assistant?</h6> <p>One can either speak a wake word or activate it using a keystroke. The wake word is the default and most popular.</p> <h6 id="how-does-the-wakeword-mode-work">How does the wakeword mode work?</h6> <p>ZoomText and Fusion listens for “Zoomy” or “Hey Zoomy,” while JAWS listens for “Sharky” or “Hey Sharky.” When the wake word is uttered, the software considers the next five seconds of speech spoken as a request for action.</p> <h6 id="how-does-the-keystroke-mode-work">How does the keystroke mode work?</h6> <p>When the user presses the keystroke, ALT+CAPS LOCK+SPACEBAR, the fusion Suite product listens for the next five seconds of speech spoken as a request for action.</p> <h6 id="how-is-the-speech-recognition-and-utterance-intent-recognition-done">How is the speech recognition and utterance intent recognition done?</h6> <p>We use Microsoft Cognitive Services – an internet connected cloud service which performs speech and intent recognition. (<a href="https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/services/cognitive-services">azure.microsoft.com/en-us/services/cognitive-services</a>)</p> <h6 id="does-it-mean-that-everything-i-speak-is-processed-by-microsoft-cognitive-services-in-the-wake-word-mode">Does it mean that everything I speak is processed by Microsoft Cognitive services in the wake word mode?</h6> <p>No. Wake word recognition happens locally, and no data is sent anywhere until the wake word is uttered. After the wake word is uttered, five seconds work of speech input is sent to the cloud for processing.</p> <h6 id="does-it-mean-one-needs-the-internet-for-the-voice-assistant-to-work">Does it mean one needs the internet for the Voice assistant to work?</h6> <p>Yes.</p> <h6 id="what-are-the-privacy-standards-of-microsoft-cognitive-services">What are the privacy standards of Microsoft Cognitive services?</h6> <p>Microsoft Cognitive services offers strong privacy transparency policies. (<a href="https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/support/legal/cognitive-services-compliance-and-privacy">azure.microsoft.com/en-us/support/legal/cognitive-services-compliance-and-privacy</a>)</p> <h6 id="does-freedom-scientific-or-microsoft-cognitive-services-record-the-voice-of-the-user">Does Freedom Scientific or Microsoft Cognitive services record the voice of the user?</h6> <p>No. The voice data is automatically deleted after processing.</p> <h6 id="does-freedom-scientific-or-microsoft-cognitive-services-record-the-ip-address-from-where-the-user-is-issuing-voice-commands">Does Freedom Scientific or Microsoft Cognitive services record the IP address from where the user is issuing voice commands?</h6> <p>No – neither we nor Microsoft Cognitive services record the IP address of any user or associate any user specific data with a voice command.</p> <h6 id="does-freedom-scientific-know-which-user-asked-for-what-command">Does Freedom Scientific know which user asked for what command?</h6> <p>No. Freedom Scientific does not associate any user specific data with a voice command.</p> <h6 id="what-does-freedom-scientific-record-and-maintain">What does Freedom Scientific record and maintain?</h6> <p>Freedom Scientific records the list of utterances users have requested and the actions the voice assistant took in response. Freedom Scientific uses it to improve the voice assistant.</p> <h6 id="are-calls-to-microsoft-cognitive-services-encrypted">Are calls to Microsoft cognitive services encrypted?</h6> <p>Yes, we use the HTTPS protocol to communicate with Microsoft cognitive services at well-known URLs.</p> <h3 id="omnireader-software-downloads">omniReader Software Downloads</h3> <p>Skip to content</p> <p>Need Support? <a href="tel:+18004444443">1(800) 444-4443</a></p> <h4 id="omnireader-software-downloads-1">omniReader Software Downloads</h4> <p>This page describes how to download, install, and verify installation of omniReader software 2.8.3.</p> <h5 id="changes-in-release-2.8.3">Changes in Release 2.8.3</h5> <p>Below are updates included in this release:</p> <ul> <li>Items in the Menu Voice list are correctly localized when omniReader is configured for Japanese.</li> <li>In the General Settings menu, opening a menu item no longer results in the item above it being opened instead. <a href="tel:+18004444443">1(800) 444-4443</a></p> <h4 id="pac-mate-downloads-1">PAC Mate Downloads</h4> <h5 id="pac-mate-firmware-updates">PAC Mate Firmware Updates</h5> <p>Use these links to download PAC Mate Firmware Updates.</p> <ul> <li><a href="http://www2.freedomscientific.com/downloads/pacmate/pacmate-omni65-update-dl.asp">PAC Mate Omni BX/QX 6.5 Update</a></li> <li><a href="http://www2.freedomscientific.com/downloads/pacmate/pacmate-omni62-update-dl.asp">PAC Mate Omni BX/QX 6.2 Update</a></li> <li><a href="http://www2.freedomscientific.com/fs_downloads/dl_pacmate_omni_60_update.asp">PAC Mate Omni BX/QX 6.0 Maintenance Update</a></li> <li><a href="http://www2.freedomscientific.com/fs_downloads/DL_PACmate_41_Update.asp">PAC Mate BX/QX 4.1 Firmware Update</a></li> <li><a href="http://www2.freedomscientific.com/fs_downloads/DL_PACmate_30_Patch.asp">PAC Mate BX/QX 3.0 Patch</a></li> <li><a href="http://www2.freedomscientific.com/fs_downloads/DL_PACmate_30_Update.asp">PAC Mate BX/QX 3.0 Firmware Update</a></li> <li><a href="http://www2.freedomscientific.com/fs_downloads/DL_PACmate_25_Update.asp">PAC Mate BX/QX 2.5 Firmware Update</a></li> <li><a href="http://www2.freedomscientific.com/fs_downloads/DL_PACmate_22_Update.asp">PAC Mate BX/QX 2.2 Firmware Update</a></li> <li><a href="http://www2.freedomscientific.com/fs_downloads/DL_PACmate_201_Update.asp">PAC Mate BX/QX 2.01 Firmware Update</a></li> <li><a href="http://www2.freedomscientific.com/fs_downloads/DL_PM11DL.asp">PAC Mate BNS/TNS 1.10 Firmware Update</a></li> </ul> <h3 id="picture-smart-ai-feedback-form">Picture Smart AI Feedback Form</h3> <h4 id="picture-smart-ai-feedback-form-1">Picture Smart AI Feedback Form</h4> <p>We appreciate your interest in our new Picture Smart AI feature. Please let us know what you liked or disliked about it in the feedback field below.</p> <h3 id="picture-smart-challenges">Picture Smart Challenges</h3> <ul> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/picturesmartchallenges/feedback/">Feedback</a></li> </ul> <h4 id="picture-smart-challenges-1">Picture Smart Challenges</h4> <p>Article written by Ryan Jones and last updated May 13, 2024.</p> <h5 id="understanding-ai-hallucinations-in-image-descriptions">Understanding AI Hallucinations in Image Descriptions</h5> <p>In the rapidly evolving landscape of artificial intelligence (AI), one of the most promising advancements for those of us who are blind or have low vision is the ability to merge the visual world with the realm of language. Technologies like the JAWS® Picture Smart AI™, which currently leverage AI vision models, are at the forefront of this revolution, offering unprecedented capabilities in image descriptions for users worldwide. While these developments introduce a new era of accessibility and digital interaction, they also bring to light an intriguing phenomenon known as “AI hallucinations.” This post explores the basics of AI hallucinations in image descriptions, exploring their causes, implications, and the ongoing efforts to mitigate their occurrence.</p> <h5 id="the-convergence-of-vision-and-language">The Convergence of Vision and Language</h5> <p>At the heart of Picture Smart AI lies a sophisticated integration of JAWS and leading AI powered vision technology. This combination allows JAWS to not only perceive the contents of an image but also to articulate these observations in detailed, natural language. The vision models analyze visual data, identifying objects, scenes, and activities, while the language models generate coherent, contextually relevant descriptions. This seamless fusion promises to revolutionize how we interact with digital content, particularly for those who rely on technology to interpret the visual world.</p> <h5 id="the-mirage-of-ai-hallucinations">The Mirage of AI Hallucinations</h5> <p>However, as with any new technology, there are challenges. AI hallucinations occur when these systems generate descriptions that include elements not present in the image or misinterpret the visual content. These inaccuracies can range from minor embellishments to significant errors, often resulting from biases in the training data, or the AI’s attempts to fill in gaps in ambiguous information.</p> <p>For example, AI might describe a beach scene with seagulls flying overhead, even if no birds are present in the image. Such hallucinations can stem from the AI’s training, where beach scenes frequently included birds, leading it to infer their presence even when they’re not visually detectable.</p> <h5 id="the-impact-of-hallucinations">The Impact of Hallucinations</h5> <p>The implications of AI hallucinations are directly related to the importance of the image being described. For those of us using AI for image descriptions, these inaccuracies could lead to confusion or misinterpretation. Beyond individual inconvenience, hallucinations raise questions about the reliability and trustworthiness of AI-generated content, highlighting the need for cautious optimism and critical engagement with these technologies.</p> <h5 id="identifying-hallucinations">Identifying Hallucinations</h5> <p>Without being able to visually see the described image, it may be difficult or impossible to tell if hallucinations exist. We may experience a similar challenge when depending on other people to describe graphical information to us. For example, if I ask someone to describe an image or scene to me, it is possible the description will have inaccurate information or maybe a bias towards the life experience of the describer. The following are some ways to help spot description hallucinations.</p> <ul> <li>Context: Use context clues based on what you do know about an image compared with the description. For example, I recently viewed a description of an online image of a concert. I knew the song that the band was playing when the photo was taken was an instrumental. When part of the image description indicated that the crowd was singing along with the music I knew that could not be the case. Maybe the crowd was cheering and the AI assumed they were singing since it was clearly a concert. Based on the description, I did at least know the image contained a portion of the crowd.</li> <li>Common sense and logic: Use common sense and logic to ask yourself if the description really makes sense. For example, if you read a description of an image of a coffee maker you are looking to purchase online and the description indicates the machine is of a different brand, you may want to assume the AI got the brand wrong. This may be less likely to happen if the branding is clearly displayed on the image.</li> <li>Comparison of descriptions: Picture Smart AI currently leverages image descriptions from two different services. If you notice big differences between the descriptions, this is an indicator that one, or maybe both, are providing incorrect information. If you believe the description may not be exactly correct you can always re-run Picture Smart AI again on the same image and compare the results. If it is critical to have a perfectly accurate description, you may wish to rely on someone who can visually review both the image and the description in order to provide validation. Never rely solely on Picture Smart AI for critical topics such as medical information.</li> </ul> <h5 id="charting-a-course-through-the-mirage">Charting a Course Through the Mirage</h5> <p>Addressing AI hallucinations requires a multifaceted approach. Developers and researchers are continuously refining AI models to improve their accuracy and reduce the incidence of hallucinations. This includes diversifying training data to cover a broader range of scenarios and implementing more sophisticated error-checking mechanisms. Additionally, user feedback plays a crucial role in identifying and correcting inaccuracies, underscoring the importance of community involvement in the development process.</p> <p>Moreover, ongoing research into explainable AI seeks to make the decision-making processes of AI systems more transparent, allowing for better understanding and troubleshooting of hallucinations when they occur.</p> <h5 id="conclusion-a-vision-for-the-future">Conclusion: A Vision for the Future</h5> <p>Despite the challenges posed by AI hallucinations, the potential of AI-powered image descriptions is extremely powerful! As we continue to refine these technologies, we move closer to a world where digital content is accessible and comprehensible to all, transcending the barriers between the visual and the verbal. By approaching these advancements with a critical eye and a commitment to continuous improvement, we can ensure that AI serves as a bridge to understanding, rather than a source of confusion.</p> <p>As we cross the horizon into this new world, Vispero is embracing the promise of AI with awareness and responsibility, participating actively in shaping a future where technology enhances our perception of the world in all its richness and complexity.</p> <h3 id="product-solutions-1">Product Solutions</h3> <h4 id="product-solutions-2">Product Solutions</h4> <p>In just a few short months COVID-19 has reshaped our lives in ways never before imagined. From working and learning remotely to carefully managing our public interactions, our daily routines have changed dramatically. Finding integrated solutions to mitigate these changes critical if we are to continue learning, stay productive and remain independent.</p> <p>For over 20 years Freedom Scientific’s mission has been devoted to removing technology barriers for individuals with blindness and low vision. Our innovative software and hardware solutions promote independence, allowing blind and low vision individuals the same access to information as their sighted peers.</p> <p>Whether at home, school, work or out in the community, Freedom Scientific, a Vispero brand, has the technology to create a more accessible environment no matter where you are.</p> <p>Our team is passionate about what we do and committed to the communities that we serve.</p> <h5 id="solution-packages">Solution Packages</h5> <p>We know that each individual situation is unique, and a pre-package solution might not be the right fit for everyone’s needs. We are able to leverage the entire Vispero portfolio of products from Freedom Scientific, Enhanced Vision and Optelec to create a custom solution to fit your needs.</p> <p>Freedom Scientific Low Vision and Blindness products are easily combined into packages or bundles that address many user (or organization) specific software and hardware needs. Whether computer based, stand alone, battery operated or plugged in, our industry leading technology is unmatched in its breadth, versatility, and above all else, its quality and durability.</p> <p>Below are examples of Freedom Scientific products to create a solution to fit a variety of needs.</p> <h5 id="options-for-school-use">Options for school use</h5> <h6 id="elbraille-with-the-focus-40-and-jaws">ElBraille with the Focus 40 and JAWS</h6> <p>The ElBraille combines the flexibility of a modern mainstream computer running the Windows® 10 operating system with JAWS® and a Focus 40-cell Braille display with a full Braille keyboard to offer a fully accessible compact solution.</p> <h5 id="options-for-homeremote-working">Options for home/remote working</h5> <h6 id="topaz-ultra-and-ruby-xl-hd">TOPAZ Ultra and RUBY XL HD</h6> <p>The TOPAZ Ultra’s foldable, lightweight design makes it easy to move from room to room or take from work to home. TOPAZ Ultra comes in two full-HD screen sizes, 15-inch, and 17-inch. The rotating 3-in-1 camera allows you to view objects on a desk, at a distance, and even self-view. The RUBY XL HD has a larger screen and a high-definition camera for the sharpest possible image but is still small enough to carry with you around the house or around town.</p> <h6 id="topaz-ultra-and-a-ruby">TOPAZ Ultra and a RUBY</h6> <p>The TOPAZ Ultra is a portable magnifier with a unique folding design, making it extremely easy to take with you wherever you go. Its 3-1 camera magnifies up close, at a distance for and self-view. The RUBY is the smallest on-the-go magnifier for spot reading and it fits easily in your backpack or pocket.</p> <h6 id="focus-40-with-jaws-and-pearl">Focus 40 with JAWS and PEARL</h6> <p>The Focus 40 is lightweight and rugged with a compact and user-friendly keyboard. You can connect up to 5 Bluetooth devices, such as smartphones, iPads, and tablets. When you combine the Focus 40 Blue with JAWS®, you have the ultimate in speech and Braille access to your computer. The PEARL combined with JAWS, brings users instant access to printed material with an array of human-sounding voices. The folding camera connects to a PC and snaps a picture of the reading material and begins reading it aloud instantly.</p> <h5 id="software-solutions-2">Software Solutions</h5> <p>Freedom Scientific provides software solutions for blind and low vision needs. Whether you are looking for a screen reader, like our world-renowned JAWS software or a magnification software such as ZoomText, or the combination of the two in Fusion.</p> <h5 id="low-vision-solutions-2">Low Vision Solutions</h5> <p>We offer a wide range of powerful desktop and portable video magnifiers designed for people with low vision conditions. Our magnifiers are made to help with all types of daily activities.</p> <h5 id="blindness-solutions-2">Blindness Solutions</h5> <p>With a wide range of refreshable braille displays, we offer many options to fit your needs. Engineered for portability ruggedness and ease of use, our line of Focus braille displays are lightweight, full-featured and designed to fit the needs of your busy lifestyle.</p> <h5 id="request-to-speak-with-somebody-for-your-customized-solution.">Request to speak with somebody for your customized solution.</h5> <h3 id="purchase-orders-and-payments">Purchase Orders and Payments</h3> <h4 id="purchase-orders-and-payments-1">Purchase Orders and Payments</h4> <p>Effective August 30, 2024</p> <p>Please be aware of an important update resulting from the recent merger of our ERP systems.
