id="ruby-7-hd_vpat">RUBY-7-HD_VPAT</h3> <h4 id="ruby-7-hd_vpat-1">RUBY-7-HD_VPAT</h4> <h5 id="voluntary-product-accessibility-template-1">Voluntary Product Accessibility Template</h5> <p>The purpose of the Voluntary Product Accessibility Template is to assist Federal contracting officials in making preliminary assessments regarding the availability of commercial Electronic and Information Technology products and services with features that support accessibility. It is assumed that offerers will provide additional contact information to facilitate more detailed inquiries. <a href="https://www.section508.gov/index.cfm?FuseAction=Content&ID=2/">GSA’s Buy Accessibility.</a></p> <p>The first table of the Template provides a summary view of the section 508 Standards. The subsequent tables provide more detailed views of each subsection. There are three columns in each table. Column one of the Summary Table describes the subsections of subparts B and C of the Standards. The second column describes the supporting features of the product or refers you to the corresponding detailed table, “e.g., equivalent facilitation.” The third column contains any additional remarks and explanations regarding the product. In the subsequent tables, the first column contains the lettered paragraphs of the subsections. The second column describes the supporting features of the product with regard to that paragraph. The third column contains any additional remarks and explanations regarding the product.</p> <p>Date: 01/02/2018</p> <p>Name of Product: RUBY 7 HD Handheld Video Magnifier; RUBY 7 HD+ Handheld Video Magnifier</p> <p>Contact for more Information: Sales at FreedomScientific.com or 888-666-6126</p> <p>Summary Table</p> <p>Voluntary Product Accessibility Template</p> <p>Criteria</p> <p>Supporting Features</p> <p>Remarks and explanations</p> <p>Section 1194.25 Self-Contained, Closed Products</p> <p>Section 1194.41 Information, Documentation, and Support</p> <p>Section 1194.25 Self-Contained, Closed Products – Detail</p> <p>Voluntary Product Accessibility Template</p> <p>Criteria</p> <p>Supporting Features</p> <p>Remarks and explanations</p> <ol type="a"> <li>Self contained products shall be usable by people with disabilities without requiring an end-user to attach Assistive Technology to the product. Personal headsets for private listening are not Assistive Technology.</li> </ol> <p>Yes</p> <ol start="2" type="a"> <li>When a timed response is required, the user shall be alerted and given sufficient time to indicate more time is required.</li> </ol> <p>N/A</p> <ol start="3" type="a"> <li>Where a product utilizes touchscreens or contact-sensitive controls, an input method shall be provided that complies with §1194.23 (k) (1) through (4).</li> </ol> <p>Yes</p> <ol start="4" type="a"> <li>When biometric forms of user identification or control are used, an alternative form of identification or activation, which does not require the user to possess particular biological characteristics, shall also be provided.</li> </ol> <p>N/A</p> <ol start="5" type="a"> <li>When products provide auditory output, the audio signal shall be provided at a standard signal level through an industry standard connector that will allow for private listening. The product must provide the ability to interrupt, pause, and restart the audio at anytime.</li> </ol> <p>N/A</p> <ol start="6" type="a"> <li>When products deliver voice output in a public area, incremental volume control shall be provided with output amplification up to a level of at least 65 dB. Where the ambient noise level of the environment is above 45 dB, a volume gain of at least 20 dB above the ambient level shall be user selectable. A function shall be provided to automatically reset the volume to the default level after every use.</li> </ol> <p>N/A</p> <p>.</p> <ol start="7" type="a"> <li>Color coding shall not be used as the only means of conveying information, indicating an action, prompting a response, or distinguishing a visual element.</li> </ol> <p>Yes</p> <p>The device utilizes colorful buttons with intuitive graphics</p> <ol start="8" type="a"> <li>When a product permits a user to adjust color and contrast settings, a range of color selections capable of producing a variety of contrast levels shall be provided.</li> </ol> <p>Yes</p> <ol type="i"> <li>Products shall be designed to avoid causing the screen to flicker with a frequency greater than 2 Hz and lower than 55 Hz.</li> </ol> <p>Yes</p> <ol start="10" type="a"> <li><ol type="1"> <li>Products which are freestanding, non-portable, and intended to be used in one location and which have operable controls shall comply with the following: The position of any operable control shall be determined with respect to a vertical plane, which is 48 inches in length, centered on the operable control, and at the maximum protrusion of the product within the 48 inch length on products which are freestanding, non-portable, and intended to be used in one location and which have operable controls.</li> </ol></li> </ol> <p>N/A</p> <p>Device is portable</p> <p>(j)(2) Products which are freestanding, non-portable, and intended to be used in one location and which have operable controls shall comply with the following: Where any operable control is 10 inches or less behind the reference plane, the height shall be 54 inches maximum and 15 inches minimum above the floor.</p> <p>N/A</p> <p>(j)(3) Products which are freestanding, non-portable, and intended to be used in one location and which have operable controls shall comply with the following: Where any operable control is more than 10 inches and not more than 24 inches behind the reference plane, the height shall be 46 inches maximum and 15 inches minimum above the floor.</p> <p>N/A</p> <p>(j)(4) Products which are freestanding, non-portable, and intended to be used in one location and which have operable controls shall comply with the following: Operable controls shall not be more than 24 inches behind the reference plane.</p> <p>N/A</p> <p>Return to the top of the page.</p> <p>Section 1194.41 Information, Documentation, and Support – Detail</p> <p>Voluntary Product Accessibility Template</p> <p>Criteria</p> <p>Supporting Features</p> <p>Remarks and explanations</p> <ol type="a"> <li>Product support documentation provided to end-users shall be made available in alternate formats upon request, at no additional charge.</li> </ol> <p>Yes</p> <p>Documentation provided in print format is made available via large print or electronic.</p> <ol start="2" type="a"> <li>End-users shall have access to a description of the accessibility and compatibility features of products in alternate formats or alternate methods upon request, at no additional charge.</li> </ol> <p>Yes</p> <ol start="3" type="a"> <li>Support services for products shall accommodate the communication needs of end-users with disabilities.</li> </ol> <p>Yes</p> <p>Staff is fully trained to address the support needs of persons with disabilities.</p> <h3 id="sect508">Sect508</h3> <ul> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/fs_sect508/jaws_vpat/">JAWS_VPAT</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/fs_sect508/eyepalreader_vpat/">EyePalReader_VPAT</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/fs_sect508/topaz-ocr_vpat/">TOPAZ-OCR_VPAT</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/fs_sect508/topaz-ez-vpat/">TOPAZ-EZ-VPAT</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/fs_sect508/topaz_vpat/">TOPAZ_VPAT</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/fs_sect508/topaz-xl-hd-vpat/">TOPAZ-XL-HD-VPAT</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/fs_sect508/topaz-phd-vpat/">TOPAZ-PHD-VPAT</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/fs_sect508/ruby-7-hd_vpat/">RUBY-7-HD_VPAT</a></li> </ul> <h4 id="sect508-1">Sect508</h4> <h3 id="sharkvember">Sharkvember</h3> <ul> <li><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/sharkvember/sharkvembershortcuts/">Sharkvember Shortcuts</a></li> </ul> <h4 id="sharkvember-1">Sharkvember</h4> <p>Welcome to Sharkvember 2024, our annual month-long celebration of creativity, accessibility, and community at Freedom Scientific. Dive into the exciting events we’ve lined up for you this year and be part of the fun!</p> <h5 id="sharkvember-next-big-thing">Sharkvember Next Big Thing</h5> <p>Event Date: November 19, 2024, Join us for a thrilling showcase of visionary software ideas in our “Next Big Thing” Contest. Discover the future of JAWS and ZoomText as our finalists present their game-changing features.</p> <p><a href="https://us06web.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_DLW6xRfBTj-69HpXn-sHbA#/registration">Register for our Next Big Thing live event</a></p> <h5 id="sharkvember-shortcuts">Sharkvember Shortcuts</h5> <p>Improve Your Proficiency and Productivity with a New Keyboard Command Each Day.</p> <p>Throughout Sharkvember, we’re bringing you bite-sized daily tips showcasing essential JAWS and ZoomText keyboard shortcuts that make navigating the digital world a breeze. From customizing your JAWS or ZoomText software to interacting with websites and mastering document editing, these quick tips will help you ride the accessibility wave with confidence. Stay tuned for daily updates and sharpen your digital skills with <a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/sharkvembershortcuts/">Sharkvember Shortcuts</a>!</p> <h5 id="sharkvember-webinars">Sharkvember Webinars</h5> <h6 id="lets-talk-teams">Let’s Talk Teams</h6> <p>Date & Time: Wednesday, 6th November, at 2:00 pm GMT. 9 AM EST</p> <p>Microsoft Teams is widely used for work and school to communicate with others, share information, and collaborate on projects. Join us and our friends at Sight and Sound Technology on Wednesday, November 6 at 9 AM Eastern for a partner webinar.</p> <p>We’ll dive into features of Microsoft Teams such as chats, calendar, files, and more to help you gain a broad understanding of Microsoft Teams.</p> <p><a href="https://us06web.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_HRKDsyEoRDePhvPyQce7SA#/registration">Register for the Let’s Talk Teams webinar</a></p> <h6 id="onyx-ocr-a-simple-solution-for-students-with-low-vision-6">ONYX OCR: A Simple Solution for Students with Low Vision</h6> <p>Date: November 7, 2024, Learn how the ONYX OCR is a simple magnification and text-to-speech solution for classroom settings and an easy-to-use option for children with low vision.</p> <p><a href="https://us06web.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_YRSMOqLTSDuFBWXrwey9TA#/registration">Register for our ONYX OCR webinar.</a></p> <h6 id="explore-labels-in-gmail-with-jaws-6">Explore Labels in Gmail with JAWS</h6> <p>Date & Time: Nov 12, 2024 07:00 PM Eastern Time (US and Canada)</p> <p>Description: In Gmail, labels enable you to categorize messages. Though they are similar to folders in other email applications, they offer additional functionality for organizing and searching for messages.</p> <p><a href="https://us06web.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_oqUPIOPAQbSJQRTTkgWqOQ">Register for Explore Labels in Gmail with JAWS webinar</a></p> <h6 id="new-features-of-jaws-zoomtext-and-fusion-2025-8">New Features of JAWS, ZoomText, and Fusion 2025</h6> <p>Date: November 21, 2024, Sharkvember would not be complete without training on all the latest features coming to the Fusion suite 2025.</p> <p><a href="https://us06web.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_dTSTast4TIyf7F7TIkZ-Cw#/registration">Register for our Sharkvember software webinar.</a></p> <h5 id="fs-openline">FS OpenLine</h5> <p>Date: November 21, 2024, Connect with our experts during this special edition of FS OpenLine. Get your questions answered, learn about new features, and engage with the Freedom Scientific community.</p> <p><a href="https://blog.freedomscientific.com/fsopenline/">FSOpenLine details.</a></p> <p>Stay Tuned for More Keep an eye on this page as we may add more exciting events and activities throughout Sharkvember. This month is all about coming together, sharing ideas, and making a difference.</p> <p>We can’t wait to celebrate Sharkvember with you!</p> <h3 id="sharkvember-shortcuts-1">Sharkvember Shortcuts</h3> <h4 id="sharkvember-shortcuts-2">Sharkvember Shortcuts</h4> <h5 id="sharkvember-keyboard-command-of-the-day">Sharkvember Keyboard Command of the Day</h5> <h6 id="nov-1-open-fscompanion">Nov 1: Open FSCompanion</h6> <p>Keystroke</p> <p>Description</p> <p>INSERT+SPACE, then F1</p> <p>Opens FSCompanion, the new AI tool for learning how to use JAWS and other applications like Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook.</p> <h6 id="nov-2-zoomtext-command-echo-keyboard-mode">Nov 2: ZoomText Command: Echo keyboard Mode</h6> <p>Desktop Keystroke</p> <p>Description</p> <p>CAPS LOCK+ALT+K</p> <p>Keyboard echo is a feature that lets you hear characters, words, or both as you type. Use this command to cycle through the available options.</p> <h6 id="nov-3-jaws-command-say-font">Nov 3: JAWS Command: Say font</h6> <p>Desktop Keystroke</p> <p>Laptop Keystroke</p> <p>Description</p> <p>INSERT+F</p> <p>CAPS LOCK+F</p> <p>Says the font style name and character size. Also speaks the attributes such as bold, underline, and italics. Hold down the INSERT key and press F twice quickly to virtualize this information in the JAWS Virtual Viewer where you can read it with your arrow keys. Press ESC to exit the Virtual Viewer.</p> <h6 id="nov-4-zoomtext-command-change-zoom-level">Nov 4: ZoomText Command: Change Zoom Level</h6> <p>Command</p> <p>Keystroke</p> <p>Description</p> <p>Increase Magnification</p> <p>CAPS LOCK+UP ARROW</p> <p>When you start ZoomText for the first time, it magnifies the entire screen at 2x magnification. Magnification values range from 1.0x to 60x with incremental steps between 1.0x and 5.0x. Using the keystroke to zoom in increases the magnification level.</p> <p>Decrease Magnification</p> <p>CAPS LOCK+DOWN ARROW</p> <p>When you start ZoomText for the first time, it magnifies the entire screen at 2x magnification. Magnification values range from 1.0x to 60x with incremental steps between 1.0x and 5.0x. Using the keystroke to zoom out decreases the magnification level.</p> <h6 id="nov-5-jaws-command-virtualize-control">Nov 5: JAWS Command: Virtualize Control</h6> <p>Desktop Keystroke</p> <p>Laptop Keystroke</p> <p>Description</p> <p>INSERT+SHIFT+V</p> <p>CAPS LOCK+SHIFT+V</p> <p>This keystroke displays the text of the current control in the Virtual Viewer. You can then select the text and copy and paste it into another application, such as an e-mail message. Press ESC to close the Virtual Viewer.</p> <h6 id="nov-6-zoomtext-command-change-the-voice-rate">Nov 6: ZoomText Command: Change The Voice Rate</h6> <p>Command</p> <p>Keystroke</p> <p>Description</p> <p>Increase Voice Rate</p> <p>CAPS LOCK+ALT+UP ARROW</p> <p>If you are running ZoomText Magnifier/Reader, ZoomText speaks program controls, menus, and dialog boxes, plus reads documents, emails, and web pages. Use this command to increase the voice rate.</p> <p>Decrease Voice Rate</p> <p>CAPS LOCK+ALT+DOWN ARROW</p> <p>If you are running ZoomText Magnifier/Reader, ZoomText speaks program controls, menus, and dialog boxes, plus reads documents, emails, and web pages. Use this command to decrease the voice rate.</p> <h6 id="nov-7-jaws-command-get-screen-sensitive-help">Nov 7: JAWS Command: Get Screen Sensitive Help</h6> <p>Desktop Keystroke</p> <p>Laptop Keystroke</p> <p>Description</p> <p>INSERT+F1</p> <p>CAPS LOCK+F1</p> <p>Describes the current window or control, what it is used for, and what keystrokes can be used at the current location. This information is placed in the JAWS Virtual Viewer where you can read it using standard navigation commands or copy it to the clipboard. If a link has focus, its source URL will be shown so you can responsibly manage possible phishing links in suspicious emails. Press ESC to close the Virtual Viewer.</p> <p>Use this command frequently when learning windows.</p> <h6 id="nov-8-zoomtext-command-toggle-the-zoom-to-1x-magnification">Nov 8: ZoomText Command: Toggle the Zoom to 1x magnification</h6> <p>Command</p> <p>Keystroke</p> <p>Description</p> <p>Toggle the Zoom to 1x magnification</p> <p>CAPS LOCK+ENTER</p> <p>The Zoom to 1x feature allows you to switch between your current magnification level and 1x, which is the size of the screen content when unmagnified. When you Zoom to 1x, all other magnifier and reader features of ZoomText remain active so you can still use them even while the screen is unmagnified. For example, if your magnification level is 3x, pressing this command once will switch to 1x, and pressing it again, will switch back to 3x. This is a handy way of comparing how much of the display you can actually see when it is magnified.</p> <h6 id="nov-9-jaws-command-get-hotkey-help">Nov 9: JAWS Command: Get hotkey help</h6> <p>Desktop Keystroke</p> <p>Laptop Keystroke</p> <p>Description</p> <p>INSERT+H</p> <p>CTRL+SHIFT+CAPS LOCK+H</p> <p>Lists available JAWS hotkeys in the application in focus. These commands are placed in the JAWS Virtual Viewer so you can read them or copy them to your clipboard. Press ESC to close the Virtual Viewer.</p> <h6 id="nov-10-zoomtext-command-launch-the-quick-access-bar">Nov 10: ZoomText Command: Launch the Quick Access Bar</h6> <p>Command</p> <p>Keystroke</p> <p>Description</p> <p>Launch the Quick Access Bar</p> <p>CAPS LOCK+SPACE then Q</p> <p>The Quick Access Bar is a toolbar that can contain up to eight shortcuts of your most used magnification and speech features in one convenient place. For mouse users, the benefits are twofold. First, you no longer have the distraction of leaving your current app to find the ZoomText or Fusion toolbar to perform an action and then returning to and trying to find your previous place in the app. Second, you do not have to memorize keystrokes for all the different things that you can do with ZoomText and Fusion.</p> <h6 id="nov-11-jaws-command-get-windows-keys-help">Nov 11: JAWS Command: Get Windows Keys Help</h6> <p>Desktop Keystroke</p> <p>Laptop Keystroke</p> <p>Description</p> <p>INSERT+W</p> <p>CAPS LOCK+W</p> <p>Press this keystroke for a list of Windows shortcut keys, keyboard help, and other information in the application in focus. These commands are placed in the JAWS Virtual Viewer so you can read them or copy them to your clipboard. Press ESC to close the Virtual Viewer.</p> <h6 id="nov-12-zoomtext-command-cycle-verbosity-level">Nov 12: ZoomText Command: Cycle Verbosity Level</h6> <p>Command</p> <p>Keystroke</p> <p>Description</p> <p>Cycle Verbosity Level</p> <p>CAPS LOCK+ALT+B</p> <p>Verbosity allows you to adjust the amount of information spoken about program controls when they become active or highlighted. Program controls include application and document windows, menus, dialogs, buttons, icons, and more.</p> <p>Three verbosity levels – Low, Medium, and High – allow you to quickly increase or decrease the verbosity. High verbosity provides the most information, while Low verbosity provides the least. Each of these verbosity levels can be fully customized according to your personal needs. Press CAPS LOCK+ALT+B to cycle through the three verbosity levels.</p> <h6 id="nov-13-jaws-command-open-message-center">Nov 13: JAWS Command: Open Message Center</h6> <p>Desktop Keystroke</p> <p>Laptop Keystroke</p> <p>Description</p> <p>INSERT+SPACE, then SHIFT+M</p> <p>CAPS LOCK+SPACE, then SHIFT+M</p> <p>The Message Center is a hub for announcements, tips, and information about updates. It helps maximize your experience with our software by always providing the most recent details. Message topics include: Power tips, New podcast episodes, and Information about new features and updates. Use this command to open Message Center and display a list of messages.</p> <h6 id="nov-14-zoomtext-command-color-enhancements-on-and-off">Nov 14: ZoomText Command: Color Enhancements On and Off</h6> <p>Command</p> <p>Keystroke</p> <p>Description</p> <p>Color Enhancements On and Off</p> <p>CAPS LOCK+C</p> <p>Color enhancements improve the clarity of text and graphics, providing easier viewing and reduced eyestrain. The color enhancement options consist of a variety of filter effects that adjust color, contrast and brightness. You can choose from preset color schemes or create your own custom color settings.</p> <h6 id="nov-15-jaws-command-access-speech-history">Nov 15: JAWS Command: Access Speech History</h6> <p>Desktop Keystroke</p> <p>Laptop Keystroke</p> <p>Description</p> <p>INSERT+SPACE, then H</p> <p>CAPS LOCK+SPACE, then H</p> <p>Speech History enables you to review previous announcements spoken by JAWS. Use this command to open a Results Viewer window containing up to the last 500 announcements spoken by the synthesizer. When the Speech History window opens, you are placed on the line containing the most recent announcement. You can press INSERT+SPACE, followed by CTRL+H in desktop keyboard layout, or CAPS LOCK+SPACE, followed by CTRL+H in laptop keyboard layout to copy the entire Speech History to the Windows Clipboard for pasting into another application such as a Word document or email message.</p> <p>To clear the history, in desktop keyboard layout, press INSERT+SPACE, followed by SHIFT+H. In laptop keyboard layout, press CAPS LOCK+SPACE, followed by SHIFT+H. Press ESC to close the Speech History Results Viewer window.</p> <h6 id="nov-16-zoomtext-command-activate-smoothing-mode">Nov 16: ZoomText Command: Activate Smoothing Mode</h6> <p>Command</p> <p>Keystroke</p> <p>Description</p> <p>Activate Smoothing Mode</p> <p>CAPS LOCK+X</p> <p>Smoothing preferences control how ZoomText smooths and sharpens text and graphics (including photographs) in the magnified view. ZoomText provides two types of smoothing, xFont® and Geometric Smoothing, which can be enabled individually or together. Use this command to Cycle through the different smoothing options to find one that best suits your vision needs.</p> <h6 id="nov-17-jaws-command-adjust-system-or-jaws-volume">Nov 17: JAWS Command: Adjust System or JAWS Volume</h6> <p>Desktop Keystroke</p> <p>Laptop Keystroke</p> <p>Description</p> <p>INSERT+SPACE, V, then S for system or J for JAWS</p> <p>CAPSLOCK+SPACE, V, then S for system or J for JAWS</p> <p>This command enables you to quickly adjust the system or JAWS volume. This is handy when you are in a virtual meeting or listening to a YouTube video. Press INSERT+SPACE in desktop layout or CAPS LOCK+SPACE in laptop layout to enter the command layer. Press V for volume, then S for system or J for JAWS. Press UP ARROW to increase the volume, and DOWN ARROW to decrease it. Press the PAGE UP and PAGE DOWN keys to adjust in larger increments. Press ESC to exit the Volume layer.</p> <h6 id="nov-18-zoomtext-command-toggle-pointer-enhancements-on-and-off">Nov 18: ZoomText Command: Toggle Pointer Enhancements On and Off</h6> <p>Command</p> <p>Keystroke</p> <p>Description</p> <p>Toggle Pointer Enhancements On and Off</p> <p>CAPS LOCK+P</p> <p>Pointer enhancements make it easy to locate and follow the mouse pointer. You can adjust the size and color of the pointer and activate a locator that emphasizes the pointer’s position on the screen. You can choose from preset pointer schemes or create your own custom pointer settings.</p> <h6 id="nov-19-jaws-command-access-notification-history">Nov 19: JAWS Command: Access Notification History</h6> <p>Desktop Keystroke</p> <p>Laptop Keystroke</p> <p>Description</p> <p>INSERT+SPACE, N</p> <p>CAPS LOCK+SPACE, N</p> <p>Displays a list of recent Windows or application-specific notifications. Recent means either the last 500 notifications, or notifications sent within the last 24 hours. From that dialog, you can create rules to govern how JAWS announces notifications, either in speech or braille.</p> <h6 id="nov-20-zoomtext-command-cursor-enhancements-on-and-off">Nov 20: ZoomText Command: Cursor Enhancements On and Off</h6> <p>Command</p> <p>Keystroke</p> <p>Description</p> <p>Cursor Enhancements On and Off</p> <p>CAPS LOCK+R</p> <p>Cursor enhancements make it easy to locate and follow the text cursor. A choice of high visibility locators marks the cursor’s position without obscuring the surrounding text. You can choose from preset cursor schemes or create your own custom cursor settings.</p> <h6 id="nov-21-jaws-command-say-color">Nov 21: JAWS Command: Say Color</h6> <p>Desktop Keystroke</p> <p>Laptop Keystroke</p> <p>Description</p> <p>INSERT+5 (on the number row)</p> <p>CAPS LOCK+5 (on the number row)</p> <p>This keystroke says the foreground and background color of the text at the location of the active cursor.</p> <h6 id="nov-22-zoomtext-command-toggle-speech-on-and-off">Nov 22: ZoomText Command: Toggle Speech On and Off</h6> <p>Command</p> <p>Keystroke</p> <p>Description</p> <p>Toggle Speech On and Off</p> <p>CAPS LOCK+ALT+ENTER</p> <p>Enables and disables speech output for screen reading, and allows you to open the Voice Settings dialog box where you can select and customize different voices.</p> <h6 id="nov-23-jaws-command-toggle-the-face-in-view-feature-onoff">Nov 23: JAWS Command: Toggle the Face in View feature on/off</h6> <p>Desktop Keystroke</p> <p>Laptop Keystroke</p> <p>Description</p> <p>INSERT+Space, F, O</p> <p>CAPS LOCK+SPACE, F, O</p> <p>Video calls have become a standard form of communication in the workplace, in schools, and in personal relationships. Before joining a video call, you want to make sure your setup is right and the camera is correctly focused on you. The new Face in View feature helps with this by alerting you to key visual details like: knowing whether your face is centered in the view, whether you are looking directly at the camera, If the lighting is adequate, and if there are additional items in the view. This command toggles Face in View on/off. Once you have entered the Face in View layer by pressing INSERT+SPACE, F in desktop layout or CAPS LOCK+SPACE, F in laptop layout, press ? (question mark) for a list of all available Face in View commands</p> <h6 id="nov-24-zoomtext-command-focus-enhancements-on-and-off">Nov 24: ZoomText Command: Focus Enhancements On and Off</h6> <p>Command</p> <p>Keystroke</p> <p>Description</p> <p>Focus Enhancements On and Off</p> <p>CAPS LOCK+F</p> <p>Focus enhancements make it easy to locate and follow the control focus when you press TAB and the arrow keys to navigate through menus, dialogs, tool bars, and other application controls. When enabled, a choice of high visibility locators marks the position of the control with focus without obscuring any surrounding text. You can choose from preset focus schemes or configure your own custom focus settings.</p> <h6 id="nov-25-jaws-command-append-selected-text-to-clipboard">Nov 25: JAWS Command: Append Selected Text To Clipboard</h6> <p>Desktop Keystroke</p> <p>Laptop Keystroke</p> <p>Description</p> <p>INSERT+WINDOWS+C</p> <p>CAPS LOCK+WINDOWS+C</p> <p>The FSClipboard allows you to append text to the clipboard without replacing the content each time text is appended. This feature removes all formatting from text that you copy, Making it useful in programs like Microsoft Word when you do not want to include styles, numbering, and other formatting information when pasting text into a document. Using a Copy To Clipboard command instead of an Append To Clipboard command erases any previous clipboard content and replaces it with the new content.</p> <h6 id="nov-26-zoomtext-command-say-current-time-or-date">Nov 26: ZoomText Command: Say Current Time Or Date</h6> <p>Command</p> <p>Keystrokes</p> <p>Description</p> <p>Say Current Time Or Date</p> <p>Keystrokes for time, press CAPS LOCK+SPACE, Y, T</p> <p>Keystrokes for date, press CAPS LOCK+SPACE, Y, D</p> <p>Use these layered commands to have ZoomText speak the current time or date.</p> <h6 id="nov-27-jaws-command-open-quick-settings">Nov 27: JAWS Command: Open Quick Settings</h6> <p>Desktop Keystroke</p> <p>Laptop Keystroke</p> <p>Description</p> <p>INSERT+V</p> <p>CAPS LOCK+V</p> <p>Use the Quick Settings dialog to adjust JAWS settings for the application currently in use.</p> <h6 id="nov-28-zoomtext-command-open-message-center">Nov 28: ZoomText Command: Open Message Center</h6> <p>Command</p> <p>Keystrokes</p> <p>Description</p> <p>Open Message Center</p> <p>CAPS LOCK+M</p> <p>Message Center is your hub for timely announcements from Freedom Scientific to help maximize your experience with ZoomText. The messages cover various topics, including: product specific training tips to explore key features, information about new features and changes in updates, details about upcoming webinars and additional training opportunities, and notifications about new FSCast podcast episodes.</p> <h6 id="nov-29-jaws-command-access-jaws-command-search">Nov 29: JAWS Command: Access JAWS Command Search</h6> <p>Desktop Keystroke</p> <p>Laptop Keystroke</p> <p>Description</p> <p>INSERT+SPACE, J</p> <p>CAPS LOCK+SPACE, J</p> <p>Once in Command Search, type in a word or phrase to find a JAWS keystroke for a specific feature or task such as List Headings or Say Selected Text. Each command has a description and related keystroke. Press enter on the command to perform it from within the Search Commands window.</p> <h6 id="nov-30-zoomtext-command-use-freeze-view">Nov 30: ZoomText Command: Use Freeze View</h6> <p>Command</p> <p>Keystrokes</p> <p>Description</p> <p>Use Freeze View</p> <p>CAPS LOCK+N: Creates a Freeze View window.</p> <p>CAPS LOCK+CTRL+x: Toggles in or out of a Freeze View window. The value “x” is a number—1, 2, 3, or 4—that represents which Freeze View window you are entering or leaving.</p> <p>With this feature, you can draw a window around the area of the screen that you want to monitor. After you make your selection, the Freeze View displays on top of the full zoom window, which continues to operate normally. The Clock and Start menu are on opposite sides of the screen, for example, so you can select one as a Freeze View and see both simultaneously.</p> <p>The magnification level of the Freeze View is not affected by changes to the full zoom window. You can create up to four Freeze Views and place them anywhere on the screen. CAPS LOCK+A Adjusts the size and position of a Freeze View window. ESC Closes the Freeze View tool.</p> <h3 id="speak-with-a-product-specialist">Speak with a product specialist</h3> <h4 id="speak-with-a-product-specialist-1">Speak with a product specialist</h4> <p>To request a demo or to speak with somebody please</p> <p><a href="https://support.freedomscientific.com/Forms/ContactInternationalSales">Contact Our International Sales Team</a></p> <h3 id="speech-and-sounds">Speech and Sounds</h3> <h4 id="speech-and-sounds-1">Speech and Sounds</h4> <h4 id="submit-your-own-jaws-speech-and-sound-scheme">Submit Your Own JAWS Speech and Sound Scheme!</h4> <p>It’s a contest! Create a unique speech and sound scheme for JAWS and submit it to be considered for a $100 Amazon gift card and a chance to have your scheme added to JAWS 2022.</p> <p>Three finalists will be chosen, and everyone will have the chance to try out the schemes and vote!</p> <p>Speech and sound schemes let you use voices, spoken text, or sounds to identify elements of Web pages, dialog boxes, and documents. For example, you could use different notes from a piano to indicate different heading levels. You can also assign speech or a sound to specific text attributes in a word processing document. Alternatively, you might want JAWS to identify bold text in a document by reading it in a deep voice. When you use speech and sounds to alter the way JAWS reads information, you can store your associations as a scheme that you can apply at any time. You can easily switch between schemes.</p> <p>For more information about speech and sound schemes, visit and listen to the references below.</p> <p>All submissions will become the property of Freedom Scientific, see official rules for details.</p> <h5 id="speech-and-sounds-scheme-tutorials-and-references">Speech and Sounds Scheme Tutorials and References</h5> <ul> <li><p><a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5VNzKJYhxqM">Speech and Sounds Video Tutorial</a>: In this demonstration, Ryan Jones from TPGI describes how Speech and Sounds schemes work, explores some of the default schemes included with JAWS and how to switch between them, and walks you step-by-step through creating your own scheme.</p></li> <li><p><a href="https://blog.freedomscientific.com/fscast-194-braille-transcriber-matthew-horspool-and-duxbury-creator-joe-sullivan/">FSCast 194</a>: This episode features an interview with JAWS user Matthew Horspool who shows how he uses Speech and Sounds schemes. This page includes links to listen as well as read the text transcript.</p></li> <li><p><a href="https://www.freedomscientific.com/SurfsUp/Speech_Sounds_Schemes.htm">Speech and Sounds Schemes on Surf’s Up</a>: This section of the Surf’s UP internet navigation tutorial walks you through creating Speech and Sounds schemes for use on web pages. In addition, the JAWS help contains information on using Speech and Sounds schemes. To access these topics, do the following:</p></li> <li><p>From the JAWS main window, press F1 to open Help.</p></li> <li><p>In the Contents tree view, navigate to the Settings Center book and press RIGHT ARROW to expand it.</p></li> <li><p>Navigate to Speech and Sounds Schemes and press ENTER to display this topic.</p></li> <li><p>Press F6 to move focus to the topic window to review the contents.</p></li> </ul> <h5 id="more-contest-details">More Contest Details</h5> <p>After you have reviewed the speech and sound references on this page, follow these instructions to create your own speech and sounds scheme:</p> <p>(You must use JAWS 2021 to create the scheme.)</p> <ul> <li>Consider a set of sounds or voices that you have applied or want to apply to enhance an application you use with JAWS.</li> <li>Spend time creating your speech and sound scheme and making sure it works as you intend.</li> <li>When you think it’s complete and ready for submission, make sure you are connected to the Internet.</li> <li>From the JAWS application window, press ALT+H to open the Help menu and choose FS Support Tool.</li> <li>When the tool opens, press ENTER to begin gathering information. Note that this process may take several seconds.</li> <li>Enter your email address and then select Send report to upload the report containing your speech and sounds scheme file to Freedom Scientific. Be sure to use the same email address here and in the submission form.</li> <li>When your file is uploaded, complete the submission form to provide additional details about your scheme. Submissions will not be accepted after June 30, 2021.</li> <li>We will announce finalists and instructions on how to vote after all submissions have been entered and evaluated.</li> </ul> <h5 id="official-contest-rules">OFFICIAL CONTEST RULES</h5> <p>Official Contest Rules and Legal Disclaimer</p> <h6 id="introduction-7">Introduction</h6> <p>By entering into the Freedom Scientific, Inc’s. Please take a minute to complete the form below.</p> <h3 id="synthesizers-downloads">Synthesizers Downloads</h3> <p>Skip to content</p> <p>Need Support? <a href="tel:+18004444443">1(800) 444-4443</a></p> <h4 id="synthesizers-downloads-1">Synthesizers Downloads</h4> <p>Use this page to download the appropriate synthesizer that works with the version of Freedom Scientific software you are running.</p> <ul> <li>Vocalizer Expressive Voices Version 2 for Fusion 2018 or later, JAWS 2018 or later, ZoomText 2018 or later, and MAGic 14. (Version 2 voices also support Fusion 11 and JAWS 18.)</li> <li>Note: JAWS, Fusion, and ZoomText 2020 versions and later offer support for the Japanese Voices on this page when you select VE 2.</li> <li>Vocalizer Expressive Voices Version 1 for JAWS 15 to JAWS 17 and MAGic 13.1</li> <li>Vocalizer Direct Voices for JAWS 14 and MAGic 12</li> <li>RealSpeak Solo Direct Voices for JAWS 10, MAGic 11, OpenBook 9, and WYNN 6 or later</li> <li>RealSpeak Solo Language Installers for PAC Mate Omni</li> <li>RealSpeak Eloquence Language Installers for PAC Mate Omni To get more information about the synthesizer along with the download links, select your preferred synthesizers and language below.</li> </ul> <p>Synthesizer:</p> <p>Language:</p> <h5 id="realspeak-solo-and-eloquence-languages-for-pac-mate-omni">RealSpeak Solo and Eloquence Languages for PAC Mate Omni</h5> <p>To use any of the RealSpeak voices, you must be running PAC Mate Omni release 6.5 or later. The Eloquence language modules can be installed on any version of PAC Mate Omni as well as older PAC Mates running a release no earlier than 2.5.</p> <p>These voices are available at no charge. The RealSpeak Solo voices can be installed into main memory or on a CompactFlash® card. If you intend to install more than one voice, it is recommended that you install them onto a CompactFlash card, as each voice requires at least 10 megabytes of storage space. Additional Eloquence languages are always installed to main memory, and each language will occupy between 1.5 and 2 MB of space. Once a voice is installed, you can open the Voice Settings dialog box, move to the Secondary page, and configure it as your secondary voice, which is active when you use INSERT+S, L on the QX or S CHORD, L on the BX to toggle between the primary and secondary voice. For more information on configuring the secondary voice, refer to the PAC Mate Omni documentation.</p> <h5 id="realspeak-solo-voices">RealSpeak Solo Voices</h5> <p>You can choose to download each voice as either an EXE or CAB installer. Select the EXE file to install the voice onto the PAC Mate Omni from your computer using ActiveSync or Windows Mobile Device Center. Choose the CAB file to perform the installation directly from the PAC Mate Omni.</p> <p>To install a voice using the EXE installer, do the following:</p> <ul> <li><p>Locate the voice you want and choose the link to download the EXE file. Save the downloaded file in a location on your computer you can easily remember, such as the Desktop.</p></li> <li><p>Establish a Standard or Guest connection between your PAC Mate and computer using Active Sync or Windows Mobile Device Center.</p></li> <li><p>Locate the downloaded file and press ENTER. This will begin the installation process. Follow the prompts.</p></li> <li><p>After installation has completed, press ENTER on the QX or DOT 8 on the BX when prompted to perform a warm reset. To install a voice using the CAB file, do the following:</p></li> <li><p>Locate the voice you want and choose the link to download the CAB file.</p></li> <li><p>Transfer the CAB file to a location on your PAC Mate Omni. You can run the file from main memory or a CompactFlash card.</p></li> <li><p>Use File Explorer to locate the CAB file and press ENTER on the QX or DOT 8 on the BX to begin the installation, then follow the prompts.</p></li> <li><p>Once the installation completes, press ENTER on the QX or DOT 8 on the BX when prompted to perform a warm reset.</p></li> </ul> <h5 id="vocalizer-direct-voices">Vocalizer Direct Voices</h5> <h5 id="vocalizer-expressive-voices-version-1">Vocalizer Expressive Voices Version 1</h5> <p>Vocalizer Expressive version 1 voices are available for use with JAWS 15, JAWS 16, JAWS 17 and MAGic 13.1. These voices offer many benefits including pitch adjustment, improved performance, especially in the areas of latency and speech quality, as well as support for a variety of languages. Each voice can be downloaded as high premium or premium. The high premium voices are large files, but offer the highest quality speech. The premium voices offer very good speech quality and a smaller file size. Both high premium and premium versions of a voice can be installed on the same computer so they can be compared.</p> <h5 id="vocalizer-expressive-voices-version-2">Vocalizer Expressive Voices Version 2</h5> <p>Vocalizer Expressive version 2 voices are available for use with Fusion 11, JAWS 18, ZoomText 2018, and MAGic 14 (or later for each application). These voices are offered in two forms: compact voices and individual high premium voices. The compact voices are smaller files and take up less disk space on your computer. As a result, you can download a single file that contains all voices and dialects for a selected language. These voices offer very good speech quality at fast speech rates. The high premium voices are larger files, but offer the highest quality speech.</p> <p>Note: When you install a version 2 voice, any version 1 voices installed on your computer are no longer available in your voice profiles for use with JAWS 18 or later and MAGic 14 or later. To restore the version 1 voices, you must first uninstall all version 2 voices.</p> <h5 id="realspeak-solo-direct-voices">RealSpeak Solo Direct Voices</h5> <h5 id="eloquence-languages">Eloquence Languages</h5> <p>Eloquence languages can be installed on PAC Mate or PAC Mate Omni. training</p> <p><a href="https://training.vispero.com/">Training Blog</a></p> <h3 id="using-the-focus-blue-refreshable-braille-display-with-talks">Using the Focus Blue Refreshable Braille Display with Talks</h3> <h4 id="using-the-focus-blue-refreshable-braille-display-with-talks-1">Using the Focus Blue Refreshable Braille Display with Talks</h4> <p>The Focus 14, 40, and 80 Blue braille displays can provide braille access over a Bluetooth® connection to any cell phone running the Symbian operating system using the Talks screen reader from Nuance. This document describes how to install the Talks support for the Focus and lists the commands that can be performed directly from the Focus display to control Talks and various other phone functions.</p> <p>For more detailed information on the Focus, refer to the Focus Blue User’s Guide. Refer to your Talks documentation for more information on using Talks.</p> <h5 id="installing-and-configuring-the-focus-in-talks">Installing and Configuring the Focus in Talks</h5> <p>Make sure Talks is installed and running on your phone before continuing.</p> <p>To add support for the Focus Blue in Talks, do the following:</p> <ul> <li>Establish a connection between your phone and a computer running the Nokia PC Suite software.</li> <li>Insert the Focus Blue Companion CD. When the Freedom Scientific Focus Setup dialog box opens, choose Install Talks driver. If your phone is connected to your computer and the Nokia PC Suite is installed, choose OK to continue.</li> <li>Choose OK again when asked if you are sure you want to install the application to your phone. The remainder of the installation is now performed from the phone.</li> <li>Follow the prompts on your phone to complete the installation. Press the Left Soft key to move to the next screen. If you have a mmemory card inserted, you are asked if you want to install to your phone’s main memory or the card. Select the option to install to main memory.</li> <li>Once the Focus driver is installed, you must establish a Bluetooth partnership between the display and the phone. Refer to the documentation that came with your phone for instructions on pairing with other Bluetooth devices. When prompted to enter a passkey to complete the bonding process, type 0000 on the phone keypad. Once the driver is installed and the Bluetooth partnership is established, Talks immediatly begins communicating with your Focus.</li> </ul> <h5 id="focus-blue-talks-commands">Focus Blue Talks Commands</h5> <p>The following sections list the commands that can be performed directly from the Focus display. Refer to the Focus Blue User’s Guide for a more in-depth description of the various controls.</p> <p>Note: When used with Talks, the Focus NAV Rockers only support panning. You can not move by line, sentence, or paragraph as you can when using the display with JAWS.</p> <h6 id="braille-commands-8">Braille Commands</h6> <p>Description</p> <p>Command</p> <p>Grade 2
